roles.description: Operate or control an entire process or system of machines, often through the use of control boards, to transfer or treat water or wastewater.

tasks.label: Collect and test water and sewage samples, using test equipment and color analysis standards.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine in-plant process-control sampling at a municipal water or wastewater plant: the operator walks the process train (indoor galleries, outdoor catwalks over open basins, all weather), dips a bottle or sampler pole at influent, aeration basins, clarifiers, filters and chlorine contact chamber, and runs spot tests (chlorine residual by DPD color comparator, DO, pH, turbidity) at the point of collection or a nearby bench.

Bench analyses in the plant/utility laboratory on collected bottles: pH, conductivity, turbidity, true/apparent color against color standards, alkalinity titration, DPD colorimetry, TSS filtration and filter weighing, BOD/COD setup and reading, settleometer, with logging of results to sheets/LIMS.

Permit compliance sampling at the plant: setting and servicing a flow-proportional 24-hour composite sampler at the influent and final effluent, retrieving and preserving bottles, plus permit grab samples (pH, DO, chlorine residual, fecal coliform) at the outfall, with chain-of-custody paperwork for in-house or contract-lab analysis.

Distribution-system / small-system field sampling route: driving to dedicated sample stations, hydrants, well houses, storage tanks and customer taps; flushing the tap, measuring chlorine residual, pH and temperature on the spot, and collecting monthly bacteriological (total coliform) bottles for the certified lab.

Collection-system, lift-station and industrial pretreatment sampling: grab or composite samples at manholes, wet wells, pump stations and industrial discharge points, often in the street or on an industrial customer's site, with traffic, odor and confined-space conditions.

Source-water and receiving-water sampling: raw-water intake and reservoir profiles at a surface-water plant, or upstream/downstream stream stations required by an NPDES permit, reached by boat or by walking down a stream bank, with in-situ probe readings and bottles for lab work.

tasks.label: Operate and adjust controls on equipment to purify and clarify water, process or dispose of sewage, and generate power.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Steady-state process control over a shift from the control room of a mid/large instrumented water or wastewater plant: watching SCADA trends and analyzer readings and adjusting setpoints and equipment states — blower/aeration DO and ammonia setpoints, pump and VFD speeds, flow splits between trains, RAS/WAS rates, starting and stopping units.

Field round through the plant to physically operate equipment that is not remotely actuated: cracking open or closing manual valves and handwheel slide gates, setting stroke/speed on a chemical feed pump at a local panel, initiating a filter backwash or sludge withdrawal at a local HMI, starting a standby pump at the MCC, swapping a chemical tote.

Chemical dose adjustment for water quality at a drinking-water plant: raw-water turbidity/temperature/pH changes prompt jar tests or analyzer trends, then coagulant, pH-adjust, fluoride and chlorine feed rates are changed and the settled/filtered/residual results verified and re-trimmed.

Wet-weather and upset/alarm response at a wastewater plant: storm inflow or an equipment alarm at night requires diverting flow to storage or a bypass, bringing additional trains, pumps or blowers online, throttling headworks and primary flows, and holding permit compliance while conditions change rapidly.

Solids handling and power generation: operating sludge/scum pumps and digester feed, running the dewatering centrifuge or belt press (polymer dose, torque, feed rate), and operating digester gas handling and the biogas cogeneration engine to make plant power.

Small or remote systems: a package plant, well/booster site or sewage lift station visited by a circuit-rider operator, who sets pump controls and level setpoints, adjusts the hypochlorite feed, resets or restarts equipment, and returns the site to automatic.

sources.title: South Bend Reduces Combined Sewer Overflow by 80% and Saves $400 Million | Xylem US
sources.claim: A deployed real-time control system operates instrumented gates and storage in a municipal combined sewer system, automatically moving wet-weather flows to available capacity, with operators able to override; it cut CSO volume sharply.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: wet-weather flow management. The same control actions the operator performs (throttling/diverting flow, using storage, protecting the plant) are executed automatically on actuated gates and pumps.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: field operation of manual valves and local controls in a plant. This is the closest commercial capability, and it is human-triggered, so it cannot support autonomous field control rounds.

tasks.label: Add chemicals, such as ammonia, chlorine, or lime, to disinfect and deodorize water and other liquids.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: At a municipal water or wastewater plant, holding the disinfectant dose on target: watching flow, chlorine-residual/ORP/pH analyzers and CT, and setting or trimming the hypochlorite, chlorine-gas, ammonia or lime feed rate at the feeder/SCADA station as demand and water quality swing; verified against grab samples and permit limits.

Chlorine gas supply changeout in the plant chlorine room: isolating and disconnecting an empty 150-lb cylinder or one-ton container, moving/rigging and securing the full one, fitting a new lead gasket and yoke or flexible connector, opening the valve, ammonia-swab leak check, returning to service.

Liquid chemical replenishment at the plant: receiving a bulk tanker of 12.5% sodium hypochlorite, aqueous ammonia or ferric (verify placard/COA, open fill-line valve, couple and uncouple hose, watch tank level and containment), or moving drums/carboys and filling day tanks and priming/calibrating metering pumps.

Dry chemical charging: hoisting and dumping 50-lb bags or supersacks of hydrated lime, soda ash or polymer into the feeder hopper/bag-dump station and keeping the volumetric or gravimetric feeder and slaker charged through the shift, in the plant's chemical building.

Remote satellite disinfection sites owned by the utility (well house, booster pump station, finished-water reservoir): setting and verifying the chlorine/ammonia feed so the target residual is held at the unmanned site as flows vary, checking the on-site analyzer and adjusting the feed pump.

Collection-system odor/corrosion control: managing chemical dosing (calcium nitrate, magnesium hydroxide, pH-shift solution) at a lift station or force-main injection point — setting the dose curve to sewage flow, checking H2S and pH readings, and re-optimizing the feed rate; chemical delivered in bulk by the supplier.

sources.claim: Hach's RTC-C/DC control module is a commercial off-the-shelf closed-loop controller that automatically sets disinfectant dose to hold a user-defined CT value in the contact tank using influent flow and measured total residual chlorine, actuating the plant's chemical feed equipment.

tasks.label: Inspect equipment or monitor operating conditions, meters, and gauges to determine load requirements and detect malfunctions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine indoor operator round at a municipal water or wastewater treatment plant: walking a fixed route through pump galleries, blower rooms, chemical feed rooms and electrical/motor control rooms; reading local pressure/flow gauges and panel displays, checking pump seals and piping for leaks, listening for abnormal bearing or cavitation noise, checking motor temperature and vibration, logging readings and flagging abnormal conditions for maintenance.

Outdoor process-unit checks on plant grounds in all weather: headworks screens and grit, aeration basins (mixing pattern, foam, DO reading), secondary clarifiers (weirs, scum arm, sludge blanket), filters, digesters and chlorine contact basins; visual and olfactory assessment of process condition plus local gauge/flowmeter readings to judge loading and spot failed equipment (stalled scum arm, plugged diffuser, broken weir).

Control-room monitoring shift: watching SCADA screens, trends and alarms plus local panels and indicator lights; comparing influent flow, levels, pressures, turbidity/DO/chlorine residual against setpoints to determine how many pumps, blowers or filters must be in service (diurnal and wet-weather load swings) and to detect instrument or equipment malfunctions.

Check of a remote, normally unstaffed satellite facility owned by the utility (sewage lift station, booster pump station, well house, storage tank site): drive to the fenced site, inspect pumps and motors, read local gauges and run-hour/amp meters, check wet-well level and alarm panel, look for leaks, overheating or odor, and report faults.

Investigating an abnormal indication to localize a malfunction: e.g., a high-amperage or vibrating pump, a drifting analyzer, a plugged sample line, a tripped breaker or a false level signal — opening cabinets and covers, hand-checking valves and piping, comparing local instrument readings with SCADA, and deciding whether to shift load to standby equipment.

tasks.label: Clean and maintain tanks, filter beds, and other work areas, using hand tools and power tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine floor cleaning of finished indoor plant areas (control building, chemical building corridors, lab, shop, gallery walkways with sealed concrete floors): sweeping, scrubbing, mopping, emptying trash on a daily/weekly housekeeping round.

Washdown/housekeeping of wet process areas: hosing floors, grating and stairs around pumps, blowers, belt press and chemical feed rooms; squeegeeing to drains, wiping equipment surfaces, cleaning polymer/chemical spills, clearing floor sumps with hand tools.

Cleaning in-service clarifier/aeration basin appurtenances from the walkway: hosing and brushing algae, grease and rags off effluent launders, weirs, scum baffles and tank walls at the waterline with fire hose or pressure washer, on a recurring (often weekly, summer-heavy) schedule.

Cleaning a drained tank/basin/wet well: after dewatering, shoveling and vacuuming grit, rags and sludge, scraping and pressure-washing floor and walls, often as a permit-required confined-space entry with a partner and blowers.

Filter maintenance in a drinking-water plant: after backwash, inspecting the media surface, breaking up and removing mudballs, raking/leveling sand or anthracite, cleaning wash-water troughs, walls and the surface-wash arms with brushes and hoses.

Screen, channel and wet-well debris work: raking rags and debris off bar racks, clearing jams in screw conveyors and screening compactors, hosing grit channels and hoppers, cleaning wet-well float switches and walls with rakes, poles and hoses.

tasks.label: Maintain, repair, and lubricate equipment, using hand tools and power tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine preventive-maintenance lubrication round through the plant: operator walks pump galleries, blower rooms and outdoor basin walkways with a grease gun and oil cans, greases motor/pump bearing zerks, checks and tops up gearbox oil on clarifier and mixer drives, changes gear oil, wipes and re-checks sight glasses. Installed machinery, some running, varied access (ladders, catwalks, wet floors).

Bench service/rebuild of small removable equipment in the plant shop: chemical metering pump heads (diaphragms, check valves, tubing), small valves and actuators, sample pumps, analyzer probes and membranes. Unit is carried to a bench, torn down with hand tools, worn parts replaced from a kit, reassembled, bench-tested and calibrated.

In-place corrective repair of installed process equipment: replacing mechanical seals or repacking a centrifugal pump, changing blower belts, replacing couplings and checking alignment, swapping a burned-out motor, replacing a flanged valve or gasket in piping, freeing seized/corroded fasteners with power tools, rigging and re-commissioning.

Clearing clogs, jams and fouling on wet equipment: pulling rags and debris off submersible/sludge pump impellers, unjamming bar screens and grinders, rodding out plugged sludge and chemical lines, hosing down and re-greasing after the clean-out. Wet, slippery, odorous, sometimes confined-space entry.

Field maintenance at remote lift stations, well houses, booster stations and outlying valve vaults: pulling and servicing submersible pumps, replacing check valves and float switches, exercising valves, servicing standby generators and chemical feed skids. Sites differ from one another, outdoors, weather-exposed, often overgrown or cramped.

tasks.label: Draw samples of products and conduct quality control tests to monitor processing and to ensure that standards are met.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine grab sample from a fixed sample station/tap on a process line in an operating unit: the operator walks a multi-level process area in PPE, purges/flushes the sample line, fills and caps a labeled bottle or sample bomb of hot/pressurized/flammable product, restores the valves, logs the sample and carries it to the lab (or runs a quick field check such as pH or density).

Sampling a storage tank, day tank, reactor or dryer: climbing stairs/platform to a gauge hatch or elevated sample valve, drawing a thief/level or bomb sample outdoors in whatever weather, sealing and labeling it, sometimes with gas testing and hot-work-style precautions.

Bench quality-control tests on collected samples in the plant or satellite laboratory: titration, Karl Fischer moisture, pH/conductivity, specific gravity/density, viscosity, color, particle size, GC or XRF; comparing results to specification, entering them in the log/LIMS and flagging off-spec material.

Product-release sampling at loading/packaging: sampling a tank truck, railcar, tote, drum or bagged product during or after transfer at the loading rack or warehouse, then running release tests and confirming the certificate-of-analysis specification before shipment.

Non-routine sampling during process upsets or off-spec investigations: the operator judges where and when to sample, uses unusual or temporary take-off points, handles hot, viscous, corrosive or plugged streams, repeats or re-runs tests, and coordinates results with the lab and board operator under time pressure.

instances.label: Routine scheduled field round inside a multi-level chemical process unit: the operator walks a fixed route through pipe racks, up stairs and across grating, checking sight glasses, local level indicators and open tank/trough levels at a set of known points, logging readings and radioing the board operator if a level is trending high.

Outdoor round of a tank farm / open process area (day or night, rain, heat or cold): checking tank level gauges, overflow lines and sumps on gravel and paved areas, climbing external stairs to tank platforms, confirming no vessel is approaching high level during a transfer.

Round through a congested or temporarily disrupted area (turnaround or maintenance work in progress): hoses, scaffolding, laydown material and contractors block parts of the usual route, and the operator improvises a path to still verify levels in the affected tanks and troughs.

Alarm- or upset-driven check: a high-level alarm, a suspected plugged outlet or an in-progress transfer prompts the operator to walk out, verify the level locally, and take immediate physical action at the equipment — throttle or close a manual feed valve, crack a drain, reposition a fill hose, start a transfer pump locally — to keep the tank from overflowing.

Patrol of open troughs, sumps and pits at floor level in a plating, finishing or wastewater/neutralization area: spotting foaming, splashing, debris or a plugged screen that is backing liquid up, and clearing the obstruction or hosing down the spill on the spot.

tasks.label: Regulate or shut down equipment during emergency situations, as directed by supervisory personnel.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Control-room/board operator, on the shift supervisor's direction during a process upset (high pressure, loss of cooling, runaway exotherm, compressor trip), regulates the unit from the DCS console - cutting feed, dumping to flare, pulling rates back - or initiates a unit emergency shutdown; final elements are already actuated and interlocked.

Outside/field operator dispatched during the emergency into the live process unit to locally isolate equipment: closing manual handwheel or chain-operated block valves on a leaking pump, exchanger or line, tripping a local motor switch, or hitting a field ESD/kill station; congested piperack layout, stairs, PPE, minutes matter.

Emergency with an active release or fire: shut down and isolate equipment under degraded conditions - vapor cloud, smoke, spilled product, alarms sounding, possible SCBA - including activating deluge/water spray and ESD stations while moving toward muster.

Transfer/loading emergency at a truck rack, railcar spot, or marine dock (hose failure, overfill, drive-away): operator activates the ESD station, stops transfer pumps, closes loading-arm and tank block valves as directed.

Plant-wide utility emergency (power failure, instrument-air loss, cooling-water loss, freeze or storm): supervisor directs a coordinated, staged shutdown of several units over hours - sequencing trips, managing flare load, purging and verifying each unit is left in a safe state.

tasks.label: Start pumps to wash and rinse reactor vessels, to exhaust gases or vapors, to regulate the flow of oil, steam, air, or perfume to towers, or to add products to converter or blending vessels.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Continuous unit, control room: operator executes routine flow moves from the DCS — starts a feed/transfer/reflux pump, lines up and ramps oil, steam or air flow to a tower, adjusts setpoints and confirms flows, pressures and levels respond. Equipment is instrumented with control valves and remote-start motors.

Field lineup and local pump start in an operating unit: outside operator walks the unit, opens manual suction/discharge block valves and vents, checks seal flush/lube oil, primes and starts the pump at the local starter, verifies discharge pressure and absence of leaks. Congested piping, stairs and mezzanines, ladders, all weather, hazardous area.

Wash and rinse a reactor/blend vessel between product grades: route wash water/solvent, start the wash pump through spray devices, run wash and rinse steps for set times/temperatures, drain to waste or recovery, verify cleanliness before the next charge (sometimes hooking a hose to a wash connection).

Charge products/additives to a converter or blending vessel: dump 25–50 lb sacks or a bulk bag of powder through a manway/charge hopper, or line up drums/day-tank and start a metered liquid additive transfer to recipe weight, then confirm the charge amount.

Exhaust gases or vapors: start vacuum pump/blower or open vent valves to flare or scrubber, run a nitrogen purge/inerting sequence on a vessel before or after a batch, monitor pressure and gas readings until the vessel is clear.

sources.transferJustification: Directly the task: pump starts, valve line-ups and flow ramps are executed by the plant's motor starters and control valves under sequence control rather than by an operator.

tasks.label: Turn valves to regulate flow of products or byproducts through agitator tanks, storage drums, or neutralizer tanks.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outside/field operator on rounds in a covered or outdoor process unit lines up flow to or from an agitated reactor or storage drum: walks the pipe rack and grade level, identifies the correct 2-8 in gate/ball block valves by tag, opens/closes them (multi-turn handwheels, sometimes a valve wrench), works at ladders/platforms and around insulation, tracing and other piping, then confirms flow on a local gauge or by radio with the board operator.

Local throttling to a target: operator hand-throttles a globe or needle valve to set a feed rate into an agitator or neutralizer tank (reagent, caustic, acid, product), adjusting in small increments while watching a local flow indicator, level sight glass or pH reading, and holding the rate until the board operator confirms the target is met.

Indoor batch/specialty chemical building: operator on a mezzanine operates a cluster of hand valves on a reactor/agitator tank manifold - charging raw materials, transferring product to drums or totes, then flushing/CIP lines - in full PPE, with hoses and portable equipment sometimes in the aisle, following a written batch sheet with valve line-up steps.

Wastewater/neutralization and utility area: operator opens and closes valves on neutralizer tanks, sumps and caustic/acid header lines; many are corroded or infrequently stroked, stick and need extra force or a cheater bar, and some sit in pits, behind other equipment, or in wet, splash-prone spots.

Console/remote operation: from the control room the operator strokes motor-operated block valves and adjusts control-valve output/setpoints to regulate flow through storage tanks and neutralizer tanks, checking flow and level trends and valve position feedback rather than physically handling the valve.

tasks.label: Gauge tank levels, using calibrated rods.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine shift gauging of a large outdoor atmospheric storage tank in the plant tank farm: climb the spiral stairway to the roof, open the gauge hatch, lower a calibrated gauge tape with plumb bob to the datum plate, read innage/outage to 1/8 in, close the hatch and log the reading; wind, rain, night, flammable vapors, full PPE.

Verification/custody-transfer gauge on a product storage tank: multiple tape readings, water-finding paste to find the free-water bottom, temperature at depth, reading cross-checked against the automatic gauge and converted to volume with the tank strapping table; result must fall within transfer tolerance and be documented.

Rounds inside a process building or covered process area: dip a series of small day tanks, mix/charge tanks, additive drums and sumps with a calibrated rod or stick through hatches at grade or on platforms, compare with sight glasses, record on the round sheet; contents may be viscous, crusting or hot.

Gauging a tank truck, rail tank car or IBC at the loading rack: climb the rack platform/cage, open the dome or hatch, dip the compartment with a calibrated stick before and after transfer to confirm loaded quantity and heel.

Non-routine gauging: the automatic gauge is out of service or suspect, or the tank is a temporary/uncommon vessel, a floating-roof tank at an awkward leg position, or is being checked during an upset, spill investigation or turnaround; the operator improvises access, judges an uncertain reading and reconciles it against process data.

tasks.label: Repair or replace damaged equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Swap small modular in-line components in the operating unit: filter/strainer elements and baskets, spray nozzles, sight glasses, hoses. Operator isolates, drains/depressurizes, opens the housing, removes the fouled part, cleans sealing faces, fits new gasket/element, closes and leak-checks.

Rotating-equipment repair: replace a leaking mechanical seal or gland packing on a process pump, replace a coupling element, or change out a small pump/motor - decoupling, unbolting corroded fasteners, cleaning the shaft, setting the seal, reassembling and aligning.

Replace or repair field instruments and control devices: pressure/level transmitters, gauges, thermowell elements, solenoid valves, control-valve positioners and actuators - disconnect tubing/wiring, remove, mount replacement, reconnect, calibrate and verify the loop.

Stop leaks on piping and valves: re-torque flange bolting in sequence, replace a blown flange gasket, repack a valve gland, replace a small block valve or fitting, sometimes on hot/insulated or awkwardly located lines.

Replace wear parts on ancillary and material-handling equipment: conveyor belts and idlers, bagging/packaging machine parts, screens and sieves, agitator blades/seals, dust-collector bags - typically diagnosis plus hand-tool disassembly of a fouled machine.

Major or emergency repairs coordinated with maintenance crews and contractors: pulling a heat-exchanger tube bundle, changing out a large motor or agitator, temporary clamps on a failed line - rigging, scaffolding, permits, multi-person work.

tasks.label: Supervise the cleaning of towers, strainers, or spray tips.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine strainer/filter service on an operating process unit: operator swaps flow to the spare basket strainer or Y-strainer, breaks the housing open, pulls the fouled basket, has it cleaned (hosed, soaked, hydroblasted or ultrasonically cleaned) by a helper or contractor, inspects the screen for holes and residual solids, reinstalls with a new gasket, vents and returns to service. Indoor/outdoor process unit, hot piping, hazardous fluids, permits.

Spray tip/nozzle cleaning: scrubber spray headers, spray-dryer atomizer nozzles, quench or wash nozzles, CIP spray balls. Operator schedules the work, oversees removal of plugged tips, cleaning by soaking/ultrasonics/soft probes (no drilling of orifices), checks spray pattern and flow, and verifies reinstallation and torque. Done in the unit or in the maintenance shop.

Turnaround cleaning of a distillation/absorption tower: operator preps the column (block, drain, steam/nitrogen purge, blind), issues confined-space and hot-work permits, gas-tests, acts as attendant while a hydroblast crew cleans trays, packing and downcomers, then inspects internals and signs off before box-up. Congested scaffolded work area, many contractors.

In-place chemical cleaning / CIP circulation of a tower, vessel or exchanger circuit: operator lines up temporary or permanent cleaning circuits, starts the cleaning recipe (caustic/acid/solvent, spray heads or fill-and-circulate), monitors temperature, flow and concentration, samples or watches conductivity/turbidity endpoints, verifies cleanliness and returns the equipment to service.

Cooling tower cleanout: cell taken out of service, basin sludge vacuumed, fill and distribution deck pressure-washed or chemically cleaned, screens and nozzles cleared, disinfection for Legionella control. Operator directs the contractor crew, checks water treatment, inspects fill and drift eliminators, and returns the cell to service. Outdoor, wet, biologically fouled.

tasks.label: Defrost frozen valves, using steam hoses.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Winter outdoor round in a process unit: operator finds a frozen small-bore valve at grade (drain, sample point, instrument tap, seal-flush line), walks to the nearest steam station, drags/uncoils a steam hose, connects it, cracks the steam header valve, plays the jet over the valve body and adjacent piping for several minutes, works the handwheel until it frees, drains it, then blows down, disconnects and stows the hose.

Frozen valve at an elevated or congested location: on a pipe rack, tower platform, or under insulation reached by stair or ladder. Operator hauls the steam hose up, works in wind and ice with poor access, keeps steam off nearby transmitters, wiring and painted surfaces, and frees the valve.

Large frozen block or control valve, or an ice plug in a process line: extended steaming (30+ minutes), repositioning the hose along the line and around the bonnet/actuator, judging where the ice sits, avoiding thermal shock and damage to seals, positioner and steam tracing, then stroking the valve and confirming flow before returning the line to service.

Truck or railcar loading rack: frozen valve on a transfer/unloading line or a frozen car bottom-outlet valve must be thawed with a steam hose before the transfer can start, under time pressure with a carrier waiting, in an area with vehicle traffic and hose/arm connections.

Indoor pump house, utility area or process building: frozen valve on a utility line (cooling water, condensate, instrument-air drain, vaporizer) in congested piping; operator brings a steam hose from a nearby utility station, thaws the valve, and mops up condensate afterward.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated hose-fed jet cleaning of process plant equipment. tasks.label: Monitor equipment functioning, observe temperature, level, and flow gauges, and perform regular unit checks to ensure that all equipment is operating as it should.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine outside-operator round at a staffed gas processing/treating plant: operator walks a fixed route through process units (compressors, dehydrators, amine/glycol units, coolers), reads local pressure/temperature gauges, level sight glasses and flow meters, looks/listens/feels for leaks, vibration and hot bearings, checks running equipment against normal ranges, and logs readings and exceptions. Indoor and outdoor areas with stairs, grating and Ex-classified zones; access controlled by the operating company.

Control-room console watch: operator at the DCS/SCADA boards monitors temperature, pressure, level and flow indications and trends for the whole plant, acknowledges and screens alarms, records shift-log readings, and directs field checks by radio. Physical activity limited to working the console in a clean, fixed control room.

Hands-on unit checks requiring manipulation: draining condensate from filter separators/knockout pots, checking and topping up lube-oil levels on compressor packages, greasing points, checking or swapping filters/strainers, pulling routine oil or gas samples, physically verifying valve line-ups and resetting local devices during the round.

Checks at remote or normally unmanned gas facilities (compressor stations, gate/metering stations, wellsite and offshore gas installations) under adverse conditions: once- or twice-daily rounds outdoors in wind, rain, night or salt spray, no permanent staff on site, readings taken from local gauges and equipment and reported to a central operations center.

Abnormal-condition investigation: a deviating reading or alarm sends the operator to the field to compare the local gauge with the board indication, decide whether it is an instrument fault or a real process upset, find the cause (leak, plugged filter, sticking valve, high vibration), and either correct it locally or escalate before the unit trips.

tasks.label: Distribute or process gas for utility companies or industrial plants, using panel boards, control boards, and semi-automatic equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine board work in the control room of a gas processing/treating plant: over a shift the operator watches the DCS/panel board and trims setpoints (inlet pressure, tower temperatures, amine circulation, refrigeration, flows) to keep the train on spec and at target throughput under normal, steady-state conditions.

Controlling compressors and station pressures to move gas into transmission/distribution mains: from a control board or station panel the operator starts, loads, unloads and stops compressor units and shifts pressure/flow setpoints as demand, nominations and ambient conditions swing, holding specified main-line pressure.

Field execution of the switching the board calls for: walking the plant or station to open/close manual block valves, line a dehydration, filtration or amine unit into or out of service, operate local semi-automatic equipment panels, swap filters/strainers and reset tripped equipment.

Non-routine board-plus-field work: starting up or shutting down a processing train or compressor unit, and responding to upsets (compressor trip, high-pressure or high-H2S alarm, feed swing) with coordinated panel actions and local verification, under time pressure.

Small or legacy facility (propane-air peak-shaving plant, LPG vaporizer, city-gate/odorization station) with hard-wired panel boards and semi-automatic equipment: hand-valve throttling, odorizer adjustment and odorant drum changes, manual gauge reading and log-keeping, local start/stop of pumps and vaporizers.

tasks.label: Control operation of compressors, scrubbers, evaporators, and refrigeration equipment to liquefy, compress, or regasify natural gas.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Console/steady-state control of a gas processing or LNG train from the plant control room: holding suction/discharge pressures, refrigerant levels and chiller/cold-box temperatures on target by adjusting compressor speed, recycle, guide vanes and refrigeration setpoints as feed rate and ambient conditions drift.

Field-side control actions inside the operating plant or station yard during rounds: manually lining up or throttling block/bypass valves on a compressor or refrigeration circuit, cracking scrubber drains and blowdowns, topping up seal/lube oil, resetting local panels, locally starting or stopping a unit.

Operating an unattended or lightly attended field gas-compressor station (gathering/wellhead or transmission booster): the unit must start, load, unload and stop on pipeline suction/discharge pressure setpoints to keep the line at contract pressure, with one operator covering several sites.

Start-up or planned shutdown of a large compressor or liquefaction/refrigeration train: pre-start checks and valve lineups in the field, purging/pressurizing, sequenced start of driver and compressor, loading against pressure, bringing the propane/mixed-refrigerant loop and chillers into service, then controlled ramp-down.

Abnormal-condition response: approach to surge, high vibration or discharge temperature, liquid carryover from a scrubber, hydrate/freeze-up or fouling in a chiller or evaporator, unit trip - diagnose the cause from panel data and field checks, take corrective action and restore the train to service.

Regasification/send-out control at an LNG peak-shaving, satellite or import facility: bringing vaporizers online, controlling send-out pressure, temperature and odorization into the distribution system as demand swings, and switching vaporizer trains.

tasks.label: Control equipment to regulate flow and pressure of gas to feedlines of boilers, furnaces, and related steam-generating or heating equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine shift operation in a gas plant / utility area: operator holds fuel-gas (or process gas) pressure and flow to boiler and fired-heater feedlines within spec as steam demand swings, working from a control room console — trimming controller setpoints, putting loops on/off auto, watching header pressure, flow and burner firing rate, with actuated control valves in the piping doing the throttling.

Boiler / furnace startup, shutdown or fuel changeover: line up and pressurize the gas feedline, purge, light off burners, ramp firing rate up to load and hold header pressure, or bleed down and isolate the gas feedline on shutdown, in the plant's boiler house.

Station- and plant-level pressure regulation feeding the heating/steam equipment: setting and holding compressor discharge / fuel-gas header / regulator-station outlet pressure so downstream feedlines stay in band, including at unattended compressor and pressure-regulating stations supervised from a gas control center.

Field rounds in the process area and at regulator skids: reading local gauges, throttling manual hand valves and block/bypass valves, adjusting mechanical regulator pilots or loading pressure, cutting a standby regulator run in or out — climbing stairs and platforms, outdoors and in weather, in an operating plant with other trades present.

Abnormal conditions: pressure excursion or low supply pressure, regulator freeze-off or failure, relief valve lifting, burner trip on gas pressure — operator diagnoses the cause, isolates or swaps equipment, and restores gas flow and pressure to the feedlines using both console and field action under time pressure.

tasks.label: Record, review, and compile operations records, test results, and gauge readings such as temperatures, pressures, concentrations, and flows.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Determine causes of abnormal pressure variances, and make corrective recommendations, such as installation of pipes to relieve overloading.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Adjust temperature, pressure, vacuum, level, flow rate, or transfer of gas to maintain processes at required levels or to correct problems.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Board/console operator in the control room of a natural gas processing plant makes routine adjustments during steady operation: trimming amine contactor/regenerator, dehydration, chiller and fractionation setpoints (tower temperature, separator and column levels, inlet pressure, product flow) on the DCS as feed gas rate, composition and ambient conditions drift, so products stay on spec.

Compressor-station / gas-control operator sets and adjusts suction and discharge pressures, unit loading, recycle and station throughput to maintain mainline pressure, line pack and contracted transfer/nomination rates, working from a station control panel or a central gas control console.

Outside/field operator inside the plant is dispatched to make hands-on adjustments: throttling or opening/closing manual block, bypass and drain valves on congested piping racks and stairs, adjusting a local regulator, loader or pump recycle, blowing down a vessel, then reporting the process response by radio.

Abnormal event or upset: high-pressure alarm, compressor surge/trip, hydrate or freeze-up, level runaway, or off-spec product. Operator diagnoses the cause, adjusts several variables at once, reroutes or flares gas, coordinates field intervention, and brings the unit back to required levels (including startup/shutdown ramping).

tasks.label: Monitor transportation and storage of flammable and other potentially dangerous products to ensure that safety guidelines are followed.

instances.label: Routine safety surveillance rounds through the plant's storage and product-transfer areas (LPG/NGL bullets and spheres, cryogenic/LNG tanks, condensate and odorant tanks, transfer piping, compressors): looking, listening and sniffing for leaks, taking portable gas readings, reading local level/pressure/temperature gauges, checking relief devices, frost/ice, spills, ignition sources and housekeeping; logging findings and reporting deviations from safety guidelines. Outdoors and in process structures, all weather, day and night shifts.

Shift-long monitoring of storage vessel conditions and hazardous-gas detection status while product is being received or shipped (tank levels, pressures, temperatures, LEL/H2S alarms, verifying storage stays inside safe operating limits), combining console/board readings with physical verification checks in the field whenever a reading or alarm deviates.

Attending a bulk transfer of flammable product to or from a tank truck or rail car at the loading rack: checking placards and paperwork, verifying bonding/grounding clamp, wheel chocks and correct hose or loading-arm connection, watching the transfer for leaks, static, venting or overfill, standing by to stop the transfer, and verifying disconnection and valve closure before the vehicle departs.

Enforcing safety guidelines on other people in and around the hazardous product areas: gas testing and standby fire watch for contractor hot work or confined-space entry near storage vessels, checking PPE and ignition-source rules, vehicle entry permits, and correct labeling/placarding of drums and containers.

Investigating a gas alarm, odor report or suspected leak in a storage or transfer area: proceeding to the area, confirming and localizing with a gas detector, assessing extent and hazard, and alerting the control room and personnel.

Responding to a leak, spill or unsafe transfer that requires hands-on intervention: closing a manual block valve, stopping and disconnecting a truck transfer, isolating a leaking hose or flange, or deploying spill containment.

Emergency or upset shutdown: high-high pressure, gas detection, fire or equipment trip leads to shutdown of the unit or station, closure of shutdown valves, isolation and blowdown/flaring, sometimes initiated by the operator hitting ESD and sometimes tripped automatically, followed by securing the equipment.

Start/stop of equipment at an unattended satellite facility (gathering or mainline compressor station, gate station, dehydration skid) dispatched from the plant control room or gas control center over SCADA, to follow pipeline pressure and flow demand.

instances.label: Routine leak-detection walk-down of the operating plant: operator carries a portable combustible-gas/H2S monitor (and/or laser methane detector or soap solution) through the compressor building, amine/dehydration units, pipe racks and tank area, checking flanges, seals, valves and connections, then logs and tags any leak found. Live hazardous-area plant, noise, stairs and grating, all weather.

Monitoring and verifying installed online analyzers that test gas during processing (process gas chromatograph for composition/BTU, water and hydrocarbon dew-point/moisture analyzer, H2S and O2 analyzers): comparing readings against process conditions, running zero/span calibration gas, purging and clearing sample-conditioning lines, changing filters/desiccant in the analyzer shelter, reporting off-spec gas. Plant analyzer house / control room.

Spot checks with portable instruments at sample taps: connecting a portable dew-point meter or portable analyzer, drawing a Draeger/stain tube or lead-acetate H2S check at a sample point on the inlet, treated-gas or residue line; purge the tap, take the reading, record and act. Field location in the plant, pressurized small-bore fittings.

Collecting a grab/spot gas sample per API 14.1 into a sample cylinder for laboratory or GC analysis of composition, moisture and H2S: purge cylinder and line, open sample valve, fill, close, label and transport to the lab; inlet, product and flare streams. Field sample points in the plant.

Bench tests of process chemicals in the plant lab: amine strength and acid-gas loading titration, glycol purity/water content and pH, filter and lube-oil checks; measuring out sample, adding reagents, titrating or running a bench analyzer, recording results and recommending chemical make-up. Plant quality-control lab with glassware, balance, titrator.

Checks at unmanned outdoor/remote points: gas quality and odorant verification and leak sniffing at gate/meter/odorizer stations and along above-ground piping in publicly accessible right-of-way; variable terrain, weather, no fixed layout, uncontrolled surroundings.

tasks.label: Clean, maintain, and repair equipment, using hand tools, or request that repair and maintenance work be performed.

instances.label: In-plant equipment cleaning/housekeeping at a gas processing or compression plant: wiping oil and grease off compressor skids, pumps and engines, blowing down and washing fouled coolers/exchanger surfaces, pulling and cleaning strainer baskets and filter housings, cleaning sight glasses and gauges, cleaning up spills and debris after a job. Congested live piping, hoses, solvents, hand tools.

Routine preventive maintenance with hand tools inside the plant: greasing bearings, changing compressor/engine lube oil and filter elements, replacing belts, gaskets and packing, tightening fittings and valve packing to torque, replacing sight glasses and small instrument parts. Requires isolating and locking out the machine, removing guards, handling dirty degraded hardware in place.

Minor troubleshooting and repair with hand tools: tracing a leaking flange, seal or valve, repacking or rebuilding a small valve, swapping a pressure gauge, transmitter or instrument tubing fitting, replacing a small pump or motor component. Fasteners are corroded, access is awkward, and the fault must be diagnosed before the repair.

Operator round through the plant to check running equipment (thermal, vibration/noise, leaks, levels, gauge readings), detect an abnormal condition on a compressor, pump, cooler or motor, and initiate a maintenance request/notification to the maintenance department, then track it to completion.

Outdoor/remote field equipment serviced by truck: metering and regulator stations, odorizer units, dehydrators and remote compressor skids in fenced yards or well pads. Layouts vary site to site, footing is gravel/mud with vegetation, weather is whatever it is; the operator cleans, services, makes minor repairs with hand tools, or calls in a repair crew.

tasks.label: Calculate gas ratios to detect deviations from specifications, using testing apparatus.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Control room of a gas processing plant or transmission/metering station: operator pulls continuous online analyzer data (chromatograph composition, moisture, H2S), computes/verifies heating value, relative density, Wobbe and component ratios, compares against pipeline tariff specification, and flags a deviation for action.

Field grab/spot sample: operator walks to a sample point in the plant or at a station, purges the sample line, fills a sample cylinder or bomb at line conditions, labels it and carries it to the on-site lab for analysis. Outdoors, all weather, classified area.

On-site plant laboratory: operator connects a sample cylinder to the bench chromatograph inlet, runs the analysis, calculates component mole percents, BTU/GPM and specific gravity per GPA methods, compares with contract specification and logs the result.

Routine verification of the testing apparatus: run certified calibration/validation gas through the analyzer, check response factors and repeatability against tolerance, record the as-found/as-left results in the analyzer log.

Analyzer trouble call: readings have drifted or a stream failed validation; operator diagnoses the cause (plugged filter, sample line leak, moisture in the line, spent carrier or cal-gas bottle, degraded column), corrects it and re-runs the check.

Remote station check: portable/handheld testing at an odorizer, city-gate or wellhead site — odorant sniff/odorometer test or H2S/O2 spot check with detector tubes or a portable analyzer, results compared with the minimum odorization/contaminant spec.

instances.label: Open-route trenching for a new gas main or service: digging the trench run with a backhoe/excavator/trencher in a subdivision under construction, a rural road shoulder, or an open easement/cross-country route. Ground is largely clear of congested existing utilities, the route is staked/surveyed, spoil is windrowed alongside, trench cut to spec depth and grade; site access controlled by the contractor.

Trenching in an established paved street or road for main replacement or a new service tap: saw-cutting pavement, digging a narrow trench between marked water/sewer/electric/telecom crossings, working within a coned lane with live traffic and pedestrians a few feet away, stacking spoil in a confined workspace.

Repair or emergency dig: excavating a bell hole with the backhoe to expose a live, pressurized main or service for a leak repair, tie-in or valve replacement; feathering the bucket within inches of the pipe and of unmarked utilities, finishing by hand or vacuum, under time pressure and gas-in-the-ground conditions.

Backfilling and restoring after the pipe is laid: pushing/placing select bedding and spoil back into the trench without damaging the coated pipe, compacting in lifts with a plate or trench roller, grading, and restoring the surface (asphalt/concrete patch, gravel or topsoil and seed).

Equipment operation inside the plant, gate station or utility yard fence: excavating open ground for new station piping or a valve pit, loading and hauling spoil, moving pipe joints, valves and pallets with a loader or forklift, grading and maintaining the yard. Premises fenced, mapped and access-controlled.

Trenchless installation: setting up and running a boring machine or horizontal directional drill to push/pull a service line under a driveway or road, steering the head to a locator, reaming and pulling in the pipe between entry and exit pits in a residential street.

tasks.label: Change charts in recording meters.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine round inside a gas processing plant or compressor station: operator opens the hinged case of 8"/12" circular chart recorders on meter runs and panel-mounted recorders in the control building, lifts the pen arms, unscrews the knurled chart hub nut, removes the completed chart, writes station/meter number, date, time, static and differential settings and initials on it, installs a fresh chart indexed to the correct time arc, re-seats the pens, closes the case and files/logs the chart.

Unmanned metering/regulator or custody-transfer station reached by truck: fenced gravel pad or small shelter, recorder mounted on a 2-inch stand or in a weather enclosure; operator unlocks the gate/enclosure, performs the same chart swap and annotation outdoors in heat, cold, wind or rain, checks clock and ink, and returns the chart for integration.

Wellhead or field gathering measurement point on a lease: dirt access road, uneven ground, mud/snow/vegetation/livestock, recorder head on a stand next to an orifice meter run; operator changes and annotates the chart, verifies pen travel against the time arc, and carries the used chart back.

Industrial or commercial delivery meter on customer premises (plant yard, building alcove, meter vault/pit): operator gains access, kneels or reaches into the meter set, changes the recorder chart, notes the index reading and customer/account data on the chart, and leaves a receipt/log entry.

Chart change complicated by a recorder problem: dry or dragging pen, ink starvation, stopped or slow clock drive, chart torn or slipping on the hub, pen off zero, frozen linkage; operator diagnoses the fault, re-inks or replaces the pen, winds/replaces the clock or adjusts pen zero against the line pressure, then installs and annotates the new chart so the record remains defensible for billing.

tasks.label: Maintain and repair equipment, or report malfunctioning equipment to supervisors so that repairs can be scheduled.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Scheduled outside-operator round through a refinery process unit (pumps, compressors, exchangers, furnaces, drums): the operator looks and listens for leaks, hot bearings, seal weeps, vibration and abnormal gauge/level readings, logs readings, and raises a maintenance notification to the supervisor for any equipment found malfunctioning. Nothing is repaired on the spot.

Ad-hoc discovery and diagnosis while doing other hands-on operating work: a valve handwheel binds while lining up a pump, a sample line is plugged, a local pressure gauge reads suspect, a field alarm is investigated. The operator manipulates the equipment to confirm the fault, may make a small on-the-spot adjustment, and then reports it for repair.

Minor first-line maintenance performed by the operator in the field: greasing/lubricating pumps and fans, swapping filter or strainer elements, tightening a leaking fitting or adjusting a packing gland, replacing a gauge glass or a small hose, steaming out or rodding a plugged line, cleaning equipment.

Preparing failed equipment for the maintenance crew and returning it to service: switch to the spare pump, isolate, depressure, drain, purge, install blinds, apply lockout/tagout, walk the permit with the craft crew, then reinstate, refill, vent and test-run the repaired machine.

Tank farm, marine dock, truck loading rack or pipeline pump station (largely unmanned, weather-exposed, fenced company property): find and report faulty tank gauges, level transmitters or meters, and repair or replace small components such as loading hoses, sample valves, gauge tapes and strainers.

instances.label: Refinery board/console operator in the control room: starts charge and product pumps, opens motor-operated block valves and adjusts flow/level controllers on the DCS to route feed and product into and out of intermediate and product tanks, holding rates and levels within spec during a shift.

Pipeline/terminal control-center operator: from a SCADA console starts mainline or booster pumps at remote stations, opens remotely actuated valves, switches receipt tanks on level, and runs a scheduled batch receipt or delivery into and out of terminal tankage.

Terminal operator/gauger at a truck or rail loading rack: lines up tank-to-rack valves, authorizes and sets the preset batch, starts the loading pump, monitors the meter and flow rate, and shuts the valve/pump at the preset volume.

Marine dock/barge transfer: operator lines up jetty and tank-farm manifold valves (many manual on the dock and on the barge), starts shore pumps for a ship or barge load, ramps rate and monitors, then closes valves at completion.

Non-routine work: unit startup/shutdown lineups, upsets and emergency tank swings, stuck or leaking valves needing a wrench/cheater bar, temporary hose or bypass lineups, degraded instrumentation requiring manual field control.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine shift round through a refinery or terminal metering area: the operator walks the meter runs, LACT/loading skids and pump manifolds, reads local totalizers and rate displays, checks strainer differential-pressure and line pressure gauges, looks and listens for leaks, vibration and hot bearings, and compares field readings against control-room values. Fixed plant layout, plant-controlled access, outdoor process structures with stairs and grating.

Verifying the flow path for a recurring, standard movement (scheduled pipeline receipt into a designated tank, unit rundown, routine delivery): confirm the assigned meter run is lined up and its bypass shut by checking valve position indicators along a known route, then confirm the correct meter's totalizer/rate is advancing and the other runs are static once flow starts.

Verifying metering for a non-standard or ad hoc movement — marine dock, truck or rail rack, temporary hose connections, tank-to-tank transfer, or a lineup involving car-sealed/locked valves — where the required path differs each time, the operator checks each valve against a written lineup and transfer paperwork and signs off the custody-transfer routing.

Proving/accuracy verification of a custody-transfer meter: line the meter through a fixed prover or hook up a mobile prover truck, run the required proof runs at operating rate, confirm repeatability and meter-factor shift are within API MPMS tolerance, and accept/enter the new meter factor.

Reconciling a completed movement to confirm the meter is reading true: record opening and closing meter readings and tickets, climb the tank and hand-gauge or verify the automatic tank gauge, compare metered volume with tank movement, and flag a meter that is drifting, slipping or not registering.

Responding to a suspect meter during a movement: erratic or zero flow indication, high strainer differential, leaking meter seal or failed pulse output; the operator switches flow to the spare meter run by turning manifold valves, clears or cleans the strainer basket, resets/reboots the flow computer, and confirms the substitute run registers correctly.

instances.label: Board/console operator in the refinery control room establishes and maintains circulation: sets pump flow and pressure targets, strokes control valves and motor-operated valves, routes feed, rundowns and recycle between units and tanks on the DCS, and holds rates against unit constraints for a shift.

Field operator lines up a manifold in the tank farm or pump house for a transfer or circulation: walks the route, verifies tag numbers, cracks and opens/closes manual gate and globe block valves (handwheels, chain and gear operators), checks for closed drains/blinds, and confirms the lineup with the board before flow is started.

Field operator starts, swaps, or stops a centrifugal transfer/charge pump locally: checks lube oil and seal flush, opens suction and vents/primes the casing, starts the motor at the local station, verifies discharge pressure and flow, throttles the discharge, and feels/listens for cavitation, vibration and seal leakage.

Surveillance rounds while liquid is circulating: walking the pump rows, manifolds and lines to read local pressure/flow gauges and tank levels, check pump seals and bearings for leaks, heat and noise, spot spills or gas releases, and report abnormalities to the board.

Abnormal-condition response during circulation: pump loses suction or cavitates, strainer plugs, seal or flange leaks, line plugs or freezes; operator diagnoses the cause, isolates and switches to the spare pump, clears or bypasses the restriction, and safely stops or restores the movement.

instances.label: Console/board operator on shift in the unit control room of an operating refinery: holds a crude/vacuum distillation or treating train at target rates and product specs during normal operation by moving setpoints and outputs that regulate control valves, pump flows, reflux, furnace firing and compressor loads across two or more coupled units.

Planned transition across console and field: crude or feed switchover, charge-rate or product-grade change, swapping a running pump/exchanger/filter to its spare. Console moves must be paired with field lineups - opening and closing manual block, bypass and drain valves on the unit, priming and locally starting the spare, then confirming flows.

Outside (field) operator during normal operation in a live process unit: walking the unit and physically moving controls - handwheels and chainwheel-operated block valves, local bypass and drain valves, local pump and blower start/stop stations, strainer and filter swaps, sample and drain points - on congested, weather-exposed piperacks and grating, in hot/hydrocarbon-service areas.

Auxiliary/utility systems supervised from the console: boiler and fired-heater firing rates, steam header pressures and letdowns, cooling water and air compressor loading, flare and fuel gas balance - adjusted by setpoint moves as unit demand changes.

Abnormal condition across multiple units: compressor trip or surge, column flooding, pump cavitation or seal failure, power dip or heavy rain causing multiple alarms. Operator must diagnose, cut rates, reroute or block in equipment through both console and field actions, and restore stable operation.

tasks.label: Collect product samples by turning bleeder valves, or by lowering containers into tanks to obtain oil samples.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine round at a refinery process unit: operator walks to a designated sample point/bleeder valve at grade or on a platform, purges the dead leg to a slop container, fills and caps a labeled bottle or can of hot or warm hydrocarbon stream (naphtha, gas oil, treated water), logs it, and carries it to the unit lab. Fire-retardant PPE, hot/pressurized lines, several points per shift.

Pressurized / hazardous-stream sample at a closed-loop sample station: LPG, light ends, sour (H2S) or benzene-bearing product drawn into a purge-and-fill sample cylinder or septum bottle, following purge, vent-back and bonding procedures; exposure control and emission limits govern acceptance of the sample.

Custody-transfer sampling at a pipeline station, meter skid, marine dock or truck/rail loading rack: operator draws a spot sample from a sample valve on the transfer line during a batch, or retrieves, mixes and decants the composite from an automatic sampler receiver, for BS&W and quality determination on a shipment.

Manual thief/running sample from an atmospheric storage tank in a tank farm: climb the stairway to the tank roof, open the gauge hatch, lower a weighted bottle or thief on a bonded cord to specified upper/middle/lower or bottom levels, retrieve, decant into a labeled container, close the hatch. Wind, weather, static and vapor hazards.

Non-routine and adverse-condition sampling: troubleshooting an upset unit at a point with no permanent sample station, drains, sumps and slop lines, barge/vessel cargo tanks, unmanned lease tank batteries or temporary tie-ins, often at night, in rain, ice or heat, with makeshift access and improvised containers.

instances.label: Board/console operator or pipeline controller in a refinery control room or pipeline control center reads automatic tank-gauge levels and meter flow rates off DCS/SCADA screens at scheduled intervals (e.g., hourly) and enters them in the shift log; no travel, purely screen-based reading of telemetered gauges.

Outside operator on a refinery process-unit round: walks a fixed route through the unit at specified intervals, reading local flow indicators, level gauges/sight glasses on drums and day tanks, meter counters and pressure gauges, climbing stairs and platforms, recording readings on a tablet or log sheet in all weather.

Gauger/terminal operator on a tank-farm round at a refinery or products terminal: travels the tank farm, reads automatic tank gauge boards/local ATG displays and manifold meter registers on 20-60 tanks, tracks level change to determine receipt/delivery rates, records inventory readings outdoors day or night.

During an active transfer (truck loading rack, marine dock/barge, or pipeline receipt), operator checks meter flow rate readouts and shore-tank automatic gauges every 15-30 minutes while trucks/vessels and other workers move around the rack or dock, to verify rate and remaining ullage.

Gauger at a remote, normally unattended pump station, metering station, or lease tank battery: reads the automatic tank gauges and meter registers on site at the scheduled interval and reports volumes/rates; fixed but sparsely equipped outdoor site with no permanent staff.

tasks.label: Inspect pipelines, tightening connections and lubricating valves as necessary.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Refinery / gas-plant outside operator walks the unit's process piping on a shift round with no defect requiring hands-on correction: looks and listens along pipe racks, flanges, pump seals, instrument tubing and drains for weeps, drips, corrosion, insulation staining, abnormal temperature or vibration; records readings and writes up findings. Congested live unit, stairs and grating, hot/hazardous fluids.

Same refinery/plant round, but a minor defect is found and corrected on the spot: snugging a weeping tubing compression fitting or a flange bolt with a wrench, taking up a valve packing gland, or putting a shot of grease on a valve stem/gear operator, then re-checking that the weep has stopped.

Tank farm, truck/marine loading rack or pipeline pump-station round by a gauger/pump system operator: inspect manifold piping, strainers, pump seals and meter runs for leaks and corrosion, and carry out the scheduled valve lubrication program (injecting sealant/grease through fittings on plug and ball valves, greasing valve gear operators), tightening packing and loose fittings as found.

Post-maintenance or turnaround start-up line walk: as piping is pressured up, walk the reassembled joints, instrument tubing and small-bore connections hunting for leaks, tighten leaking fittings and flange bolts within operator limits, and hand off anything needing torque work to maintenance before the unit is put in service.

Field pipeline patrol: drive/walk the right-of-way and remote mainline block valve, launcher and meter sites in open country — mud, snow, tall grass, uneven ground, no fixed layout — inspecting exposed piping, risers and valve stations for leaks, damage or erosion, and greasing valve operators and tightening fittings as needed.

tasks.label: Perform tests to check the qualities and grades of products, such as assessing levels of bottom sediment, water, and foreign materials in oil samples, using centrifugal testers.

instances.label: Custody-transfer BS&W shake-out at a crude pipeline terminal or truck unloading station: the gauger draws a spot/automatic-sampler sample, shakes crude 50/50 with water-saturated toluene plus demulsifier into two graduated cone centrifuge tubes, heats them in a 60 C bath, spins 10 minutes, reads the water-and-sediment volume, re-spins to a constant reading, and records BS&W on the run ticket. Done in a small sample/test room at the terminal.

Refinery unit operator on rounds: purges a live unit sample point and fills a labeled bottle of hot, volatile product (naphtha, gasoil, LPG bomb), then runs quick quality checks at the unit's satellite test bench (visual/color, water by centrifuge, density by hydrometer) and re-samples or adjusts the unit if the stream is off-spec.

Tank thief sampling and testing at a tank farm: climbs the external stairway of a crude storage tank in all weather, opens the thief hatch (vapor/H2S exposure), lowers a weighted thief to upper/middle/lower levels, draws and composites the sample, takes temperature, then runs hydrometer API gravity and a centrifuge BS&W test.

Loading rack or marine dock quality check: samples each truck/barge/ship parcel at the loading arm sample point or by thief on deck, checks appearance and free water (water-finding paste, centrifuge shake-out), verifies grade and density against the product spec, and accepts or rejects the load under time pressure.

Bench test battery in the site quality lab: a rack of delivered, labeled samples is worked through on the bench with standard apparatus (centrifuge water/sediment, Karl Fischer or density meter, distillation, flash point, color), results compared to spec and entered in the LIMS; lab is a normal human lab shared with technicians.

tasks.label: Clean interiors of processing units by circulating chemicals and solvents within units.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Turnaround/shutdown chemical decontamination of a whole process unit (crude/vacuum unit, hydrotreater, coker): operator works the unit with a chemical-cleaning crew — blinds/de-blinds, lines up dozens of manual and control valves, hooks temporary hoses and spool pieces to a decon header, injects degreaser/solvent, circulates hot solution through columns, exchangers and piping for many hours while monitoring flow, temperature, LEL/H2S, pulls samples, then drains, neutralizes and hands the unit over gas-free. Outdoor refinery unit, hazardous (Class I Div 2) area, elevated platforms.

In-service or between-run chemical/solvent circulation through one equipment circuit — a fouled preheat exchanger train, filter/coalescer, amine or slurry circuit, or a plugged pump and strainer — using existing plant pumps and permanent piping. Circuit isolated and lined up in the field, chemical dosed from a tote/drum, circulation run and monitored largely from the DCS, with hourly field checks, sampling and titration to judge endpoint, then flush and drain to slop.

Storage tank interior cleaning/sludge removal at a refinery tank farm or terminal: circulating cutter stock, recovered oil or solvent through tank mixers/jet nozzles to re-liquefy bottoms, running the circulation pump loop for days, monitoring level/temperature/vapor, then transferring recovered oil and slop out and confirming the tank is fit for entry or return to service.

Pipeline pump station / terminal manifold and header flushing between product batches or before maintenance: gauger/operator lines up the manifold, circulates flush stock or solvent through pumps, meters, strainers and loading headers, drains low points to slop, and verifies cleanliness by sample before the next product movement.

Small equipment cleaning at grade: circulating solvent or cleaning chemical through a knockout drum, filter housing, sample/analyzer system, seal flush pot or small skid using a portable pump and hoses rigged by the operator, running for an hour or two, then draining, rinsing and returning the item to service.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: cleaning the interiors of process vessels, exchangers and piping by circulating cleaning chemicals without disassembly — the same physical operation (dose, heat, circulate, monitor concentration, rinse, drain) that a refinery operator performs, on comparable closed pressure equipment; the difference is the fluid handled and the plant, not the manipulation or precision required.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: interior cleaning of process vessels and lines by circulating chemicals. tasks.label: Clamp seals around valves to secure tanks.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Refined-products terminal truck loading rack: after bottom-loading a tank trailer, the operator/gauger applies numbered tamper-evident plastic or cable seals to each compartment's loading-valve adapter cap, dome cover and vapor cap, then records every seal number on the bill of lading. Outdoors under a rack canopy, on and around a parked trailer, in all weather.

Refinery or terminal process area 'car sealing': operator installs wire or pull-tight seals on critical block valves (relief-valve isolation, drain, bypass) to lock them car-sealed open/closed, threading the seal through handwheel spokes or a chain lug and crimping it, then logging the number in the car-seal register. Valves are at grade, on platforms and at height in congested piping.

Crude-oil gauger at a lease tank battery or crude unloading point: breaks and later re-applies numbered seals on the tank's sales/outlet valve and thief hatch and on the trailer's outlet valve, recording seal-off and seal-on numbers on the run ticket. Remote unfenced pads, layout differs site to site, mud, wind, night work.

Rail tank car rack at a refinery or terminal: after loading, operator secures and seals the bottom outlet valve handle/cap, the manway cover lugs and vent valves with numbered bolt or cable seals and records the numbers for the shipping papers. Work is done from a fixed rail platform alongside the car.

Marine dock: before a barge or tanker departs, the dockman/gauger applies numbered seals to the vessel's cargo manifold valves, ullage hatches and sea-suction valves and records the numbers on transfer documents. Work is on a fixed dock and on the vessel deck, with vessel movement and marine weather.

It is the same act as the rated task - fitting a tamper-evident seal around a container's valve to secure the vessel - on comparable objects (industrial valve bodies, plastic seals/caps) at comparable precision, in a flammable-hydrocarbon (ATEX Zone 1/2) atmosphere; it works only because the cylinder arrives fixtured on a conveyor, i.e. an E1 purpose-built line.

tasks.label: Lower thermometers into tanks to obtain temperature readings.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Refinery or products-terminal shore tank: gauger climbs the stairway to the tank top, grounds and opens the gauge hatch, lowers a portable electronic thermometer (or cup-case thermometer) on a graduated line to required depths in a large fixed- or floating-roof tank of gasoline, diesel or crude, waits for the reading to stabilize, records upper/middle/lower temperatures for volume correction on an inventory or custody-transfer ticket, and closes the hatch.

Crude oil lease / production tank battery: pumper-gauger climbs the stairway of a stock tank, opens the thief hatch, and lowers a thermometer (often with a thief and tape) to obtain product temperature at required depths for the run ticket before a truck haul; outdoors in all weather, with vapor/H2S exposure and a layout that varies battery to battery.

Marine transfer at a dock: gauger or independent inspector boards a tank barge or tanker and takes cargo-tank temperatures before and after transfer, lowering a portable thermometer/UTI probe through the gauge hatch or a vapor-control (closed-gauging) valve on deck, at multiple depths in several compartments.

Heated or viscous product tank (asphalt, residual fuel, heavy crude, heated chemical) at a terminal or refinery: temperature checks at several depths through the gauge hatch to verify heating/blending and confirm the product is within the shipping temperature window; the instrument comes out coated and must be wiped, and the hatch releases hot vapor.

Tank truck compartment or rail tank car at a loading rack, or a small day/process tank: operator lowers a thermometer through the dome or gauge hatch to get product temperature for the bill of lading or a process check, working from a rack platform or a ground-level tank top.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated in-tank gauging. The servo gauge performs under machine control the same physical act the gauger performs by hand - lowering an instrument on a line through the tank's gauge nozzle into the product - and the same installation reports the product temperature used for volume correction.

tasks.label: Monitor batch, continuous flow, or hybrid biofuels production processes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine shift monitoring of a continuous dry-mill ethanol plant: technician watches DCS/SCADA trends and alarms (cook, liquefaction, fermenters, beer column and rectifier, molecular sieves, DDGS dryers, thermal oxidizer) and makes hourly walk-throughs of the process building to verify local gauges and sight glasses, confirm pumps/compressors/agitators are running normally, look and listen for steam/ethanol/CO2 leaks, and log readings and flag drift.

Dedicated outside-operator field rounds through the tank farm, loadout and utilities: reading local level, pressure and temperature gauges, checking pump seals, motor heat and vibration, boiler and cooling-tower conditions, checking for leaks and spills, recording readings on a rounds sheet and escalating anything out of range to the board operator.

Batch fermentation monitoring: following each fermenter from fill to drop - temperature profile and cooling response, pH, level, CO2 evolution and foaming, verifying yeast/enzyme/urea/antimicrobial dosing pumps ran, comparing inline and lab solids/ethanol trends against the expected curve, watching for stuck or infected ferments, confirming the batch is on profile and ready to transfer.

Abnormal condition or upset during monitoring: an alarm or deviation (fermenter foam-over, plugged heat exchanger, distillation column flooding, cavitating pump, dryer temperature excursion) that the technician investigates at the equipment, diagnoses by hands-on inspection, and corrects physically (manual valves, bypasses, clearing plugs, restarting equipment) to bring the process back on spec.

Monitoring a smaller batch or hybrid facility - biodiesel transesterification plant, biogas/RNG upgrading skid, or pilot cellulosic/SAF unit: partially instrumented, hands-on checks at local panels and gauges of reactor temperature and pressure, methanol recovery, glycerin/phase separation, gas quality, with manual logging and more variable equipment and layout.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: operator/maintenance inspection rounds in an oilseed crush and oil refinery plant - the same class of pumps, vessels, heat exchangers, dryers and local gauges found in a biofuels plant, and the same output (logged readings, trends, alerts) that monitoring a production process produces.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine equipment and process-area inspection rounds in a large fermentation plant (brewery). Fermenters, CIP lines, CO2 systems, pumps and local instruments are directly comparable to an ethanol plant's fermentation and utilities areas.
