tasks.label: Operate valves, pumps, engines, or generators to control and adjust biofuels production.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Control-room/HMI adjustment of the continuously running production train at a corn-ethanol or biodiesel plant: trimming slurry/feed rates, fermenter temperature and enzyme dosing, distillation reflux and steam, evaporator/dryer loads by moving control-valve positions and pump/VFD speeds to hold yield and quality.

Field round through the process area: locating and turning manual handwheel/lever block, bypass, drain and sample valves; lining up a spare pump; starting/stopping pumps at local panels; venting and confirming flow by gauge, on stairs and catwalks in an operating plant.

In-plant liquid movements through fixed piping: beer well to distillation, whole stillage to centrifuges, ethanol to day/shipping tanks, denaturant blending — selecting a path, opening the lineup, starting the transfer pump, watching levels and stopping on target.

Truck or rail loadout / chemical unloading at the rack: spotting and grounding the vehicle, connecting hose or loading arm, opening the loadout valves, running the transfer pump to a preset quantity, then draining and disconnecting.

Utility and auxiliary equipment: starting, stopping and adjusting the boiler/thermal oxidizer firing rate, standby generator or engine, air compressors, cooling-tower and CIP pumps to keep steam, power and utilities matched to production.

Abnormal-event response: reacting to a fermenter foam-over, cavitating or tripped pump, plugged line or fouled exchanger by diagnosing the cause, cutting or rerouting flow, swapping to spare equipment and physically restoring service under time pressure.

tasks.label: Collect biofuels samples and perform routine laboratory tests or analyses to assess biofuels quality.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine process round at a corn-ethanol plant: technician walks the plant, purges and draws samples from mash/liquefaction, several fermenters, beer well and distillation sample valves into labeled bottles, carries them to the on-site lab, checks solids/Brix, pH and temperature, centrifuges/filters aliquots and runs HPLC for sugars, ethanol, glycerol and organic acids, then logs results and flags off-spec fermenters. Hot, piped, congested plant floor; several rounds per shift.

Finished-product specification testing: technician pulls a sample from the denatured-ethanol day/shipping tank or biodiesel finished tank and runs spec tests in the plant lab - water by Karl Fischer, acidity/acid number titration, density/specific gravity, pHe, visual appearance, sulfate by ion chromatography; for biodiesel free and total glycerin by GC, methanol, cloud point - then records results and issues the certificate of analysis for the load.

Receiving and loadout sampling: sampling incoming feedstock (corn, distillers corn oil, used cooking oil, tallow, methanol) from trucks or railcars at the scale/receiving pit, and sampling outgoing ethanol or biodiesel at the loading rack; taking composite and retain samples, sealing and labeling them, and running quick acceptance tests (grain moisture/NIR, water and sediment, appearance). Outdoor rack, ladders and hatches, weather.

Utility and environmental stream sampling and testing: cooling tower, boiler feedwater, condensate, RO/softener water, process water and stillage/wastewater; measuring pH, conductivity, hardness, chlorides, alkalinity, iron and residual chemical levels with test kits, meters and titrations; logging results and adjusting chemical dosing.

Microbiological and yeast monitoring: sampling fermenters/propagators, plating broth on selective media for lactic acid bacteria, gram staining, doing microscope yeast cell counts and viability (methylene blue/hemocytometer), incubating and counting colonies, and reporting infection and cell-count trends.

Non-routine troubleshooting sampling during upsets: sampling from ad hoc points chosen on the spot (heat exchanger drains, centrifuge cake, dryer discharge, tank bottoms, syrup line, a leaking pump seal), often hot, viscous or solids-laden material requiring valve and hose manipulation, then deciding which analyses to run and interpreting them against the upset.

tasks.label: Process refined feedstock with additives in fermentation or reaction process vessels.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Corn dry-mill fuel ethanol plant, routine batch: technician sets up and runs a fermenter cycle - fill the vessel with saccharified mash to target level, dose glucoamylase, yeast slurry, urea/nutrient and antimicrobial at recipe ratios via metering pumps, hold the temperature/pH profile over ~50-60 hours, monitor from the DCS with field rounds, then drop the batch to the beer well. Inputs arrive by pipe from upstream cook/liquefaction; vessels, pumps and automated valves are fixed plant.

Field charging of dry or drummed additives: weighing and dumping 25-50 lb bags or supersacks of dry yeast, nutrient salts or antimicrobial into a hydration/mix tank hopper, or connecting hoses and pumping from IBC totes into a day tank, on the plant floor and mezzanines around the fermenters.

Yeast propagation batch: CIP and steam-sterilize the propagator, fill with cooled mash/water, add nutrient and pitch yeast, aerate and hold temperature, draw samples for cell count/viability, then pitch the propagated yeast into the fermenter. Mix of skid/vessel operation and hygienic hands-on steps in the propagation area.

Biodiesel or renewable-fuel reaction vessel batch: charging measured refined oil feedstock plus methanol and sodium-methoxide catalyst in a fixed ratio to a heated, agitated transesterification reactor, running the reaction to completion under temperature/agitation control, checking conversion, and transferring to separation.

Off-normal batch: sluggish or bacterially infected fermentation, excessive foaming, a plugged additive line or failed dosing pump, or out-of-spec pH. Technician samples the vessel, works with the lab, diagnoses the cause, adds corrective chemistry manually, clears or repairs the line/pump, and salvages or reroutes the batch.

Dispatched to investigate an abnormal condition or alarm (odd noise from a pump, high temperature, tripped motor, suspected leak): locating the fault, diagnosing the mechanical problem at close range, and reporting it with enough detail to generate a work order.

Liquid feedstock receiving at a biodiesel/renewable diesel plant: tanker truck or railcar of soybean oil, distillers corn oil, used cooking oil or animal fat; draw a representative sample (hatch/thief or unloading-line sampler), run free fatty acid/acid value titration, Karl Fischer moisture and MIU/insolubles in the plant lab, verify received quantity by meter or tank gauge, accept the load and log results.

Continuous monitoring of feedstock rate and inventory from the control room: watch weigh-belt/flow-meter and bin/tank level readings on the DCS, trend against targets, log hourly readings, reconcile inventory, and walk out to verify a suspect level indicator or local gauge when readings deviate.

Routine plant-floor round through feedstock handling and storage areas: check grind/hammermill operation, look for bridging or plugging in bins, chutes and conveyors, spot leaks and spills, and read local level, temperature and pressure gauges on feedstock tanks. Congested piping, stairs and ladders, 24/7 operation.

Pull an ad-hoc grab sample at a process point (ground corn at the hammermill discharge, slurry, oil from a day tank) and run a quick moisture/solids/particle-size check on the bench, then report or adjust.

Outdoor feedstock storage yard and silos: measure pile or bin inventory volume, check moisture and internal temperature of stored biomass or grain, and spot spoilage, molding, heating or contamination; report the results for inventory and quality records.

tasks.label: Preprocess feedstock in preparation for physical, chemical, or biological fuel production processes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Corn dry-mill ethanol plant: preprocess incoming corn — probe/sample and grade delivered loads, dump and convey grain, scalp/clean it, run hammermills to a target grind particle size (changing screens, adjusting feed rates), then slurry the meal with water/backset in the slurry tank, dose alpha-amylase and adjust pH/solids ahead of cook and liquefaction. Continuous 24/7 operation, DCS-monitored, with field rounds to clear plugged chutes and check grind.

Biodiesel / renewable diesel plant: prepare fats, oils and greases (used cooking oil, tallow, distillers corn oil, soybean oil) — connect and sample truck/railcar deliveries, heat and settle, dewater, filter out solids/MIU, dose acid/caustic or enzyme for degumming, bleach and filter, and transfer on-spec feedstock to a reaction-ready day tank; handle spent filter cake/bleaching earth.

Anaerobic digestion / RNG or organics-to-fuel facility: prepare wet feedstock — depackage food waste and grocery returns, screen and remove contaminants (film plastic, metal, glass, grit), macerate and blend with liquids to a target solids concentration, and dose the digester feed system; clear rags, jams and grit from screens, pumps and augers.

Feedstock yard / bulk solids handling at a biomass, cellulosic, or pellet fuel operation: move woodchips, stover, silage, or bagged/bulk additives from a stockpile or delivery truck into a receiving hopper or grinder with a front-end loader, keep the hopper fed at rate, break bridging in bins, and clean up spillage — outdoors or in an open reception building, in weather.

tasks.label: Calculate, measure, load, or mix refined feedstock used in biofuels production.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

Manual additive make-up inside the plant: technician hauls 50-lb sacks or drums/IBC totes of nutrient, urea, antimicrobial, antifoam or enzyme to a mix/day tank, weighs out the calculated amount on a floor scale, slits and dumps bags into an open hopper or hooks a tote to a transfer pump, lines up manual valves and mixes.

Biodiesel plant: technician titrates the refined oil/fat feedstock for free fatty acids and checks moisture, calculates the methanol and sodium methylate catalyst charge for the batch or continuous reactor, then sets and verifies the metered charging of oil, methanol and catalyst into the reaction vessel and confirms mixing.

Receiving and loading refined feedstock at the plant rack: gauging a tank truck or railcar of refined corn oil, tallow, methanol or denaturant, calculating net volume with temperature correction, grounding the vehicle, connecting the hose/loading arm, opening valves and pumping the measured quantity into the designated storage tank and on into process.

Small-scale, pilot or non-routine batch: at a small biodiesel producer, pilot/demo unit or during a trial, the technician hand-measures liters of refined oil, methanol and catalyst with graduated vessels and a bench scale, lines up manual valves, charges a batch reactor and adjusts the recipe from titration results.

tasks.label: Monitor stored biofuels products or secondary by-products until reused or transferred to users.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine shift monitoring of finished-product storage (denatured ethanol or biodiesel day/shipping tanks) at a plant: check levels, temperatures and pressures on local and control-room indicators, confirm available capacity before the next batch is transferred, watch for alarms and out-of-range trends, and log readings. Plant premises, fixed piping and tankage.

Outdoor tank-farm and pump-area walkdowns while product sits in storage: look for leaks, drips, stains and vapor odor around tank shells, seals, valves and pump packing; check vents, floating roofs/seals, thermal condition of pumps and motors; note anything abnormal and report/log it. Weather, noise, hazardous (Class I Div 1/2) area.

Physical gauging and sampling of a stored liquid product batch: climb the tank stairs, open the thief hatch, gauge level/temperature or verify against the automatic gauge, draw a sample with a bacon-bomb/zone sampler, carry it to the on-site lab, run proof/density/water/denaturant checks, and record results before releasing the tank for transfer.

Monitoring bulk by-product storage — DDGS/wet cake in flat storage buildings or silos: check pile temperature and hot spots, moisture and crusting, level and inventory, spillage and dust, and pull samples for moisture/protein/fat spec before the load is sold and hauled out.

Monitoring liquid secondary by-product tanks (distillers corn oil, syrup/CDS, crude glycerin, recovered methanol) held until reuse or sale: level and temperature checks, watching for settling/layering, heat-trace and agitation status, leaks around fittings, until the tank is pumped out to a truck or recycled back into the process.

Attending a transfer of stored product out of the plant: monitor the tank level and rack meter while denatured ethanol, corn oil or DDGS is loaded to a tank truck, railcar or hopper trailer; watch hoses/spouts and grounding for spills or overfill, verify quantity, and seal and release the shipment.

tasks.label: Assess the quality of biofuels additives for reprocessing.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Plant QC lab: bench wet-chemistry assessment of an additive sample already in hand (catalyst/methoxide strength or alkalinity titration, acid value, Karl Fischer water, density/specific gravity) against the additive spec; result decides whether the lot is usable or must be reworked. Glass beakers, balance, autotitrator, hazardous solvents, results logged to LIMS/log sheet.

Plant QC lab: instrumental assessment of an additive or additive-bearing sample (GC/HPLC purity of recovered methanol or denaturant, FTIR/NIR identity, refractive index). Technician preps the vial, loads the autosampler/instrument, runs the method, compares the chromatogram/spectrum to the reference spec and judges pass/fail or reprocess.

Recovered/recycled additive stream (recovered methanol from the stripper, recycled denaturant, recovered catalyst solution): technician walks out into the process area, opens a sample point or tank valve, draws a representative sample into a bottle, returns to the lab, tests water/purity/strength and decides whether the stream can be returned to the process.

Receiving of a delivered additive lot (tote, drum, or tank truck of enzyme, antifoam, denaturant, caustic, or methanol): technician breaks the seal, thief- or valve-samples the container in the receiving bay/tank farm, checks appearance and identity plus one or two spec parameters, and accepts, rejects, or routes the lot for rework.

Judgment call on heterogeneous off-spec or partly used additive material (slop/recovered tank contents, returned drums, phase-separated or contaminated material): appearance, phase separation, sediment and odor checks plus a quick water/sediment measurement, deciding reprocess versus dispose.

tasks.label: Clean biofuels processing work area, ensuring compliance with safety regulations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine end-of-shift housekeeping of open floors inside plant buildings (grain receiving/DDGS building, warehouse, loadout building, control-building corridors and shop bays): sweeping/scrubbing grain dust, DDGS fines, tracked-in mud and water from broad, mostly clear concrete floors while forklifts and staff move about.

At-grade housekeeping in congested process areas: sweeping and hosing spilled corn mash, syrup, yeast and chemical drips in narrow aisles between pumps, hammermills, centrifuges, hose stations and sumps; squeegeeing wash water to floor drains so no slip hazard remains.

Removing accumulated dust and residue from elevated and non-floor surfaces: catwalk gratings, stair treads, pipe ledges, motor and conveyor tops, beams and handrails, using vacuum or low-pressure blowdown at height for combustible-dust housekeeping compliance (NFPA 61/OSHA), plus wiping down equipment exteriors.

Cleaning process vessel and line interiors between batches: circulating caustic/acid wash through fermenters, beer well, mash lines and heat exchangers so the vessel interior is free of residue and returned to service on the batch schedule.

Spill and waste response: containing and cleaning a methanol/denaturant, glycerin, lube-oil or caustic spill with booms and absorbents, neutralizing, collecting into labeled waste drums, restocking the spill kit and recording the event per SPCC/RCRA and plant safety procedure.

Outdoor housekeeping of the plant yard: sweeping spilled grain and DDGS at the truck receiving pit and loadout pads, clearing debris from tank-farm containment areas, roadways and rail spur so the paved areas stay clean and unobstructed.

tasks.label: Perform routine maintenance on mechanical, electrical, or electronic equipment or instruments used in the processing of biofuels.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Mechanical preventive-maintenance route inside an ethanol/biodiesel plant: greasing dozens of zerk fittings on pumps, motors, conveyor and bucket-elevator bearings; checking and topping gearbox oil; checking/tensioning V-belts and chain drives; inspecting couplings and packing. Work is spread over hot, dusty, multi-level installed equipment; requires lockout/tagout and ladders/platforms.

Component service and replacement: changing filter cartridges, strainer baskets and inline screens; replacing mechanical seals, gaskets and pump packing; swapping hammermill screens and hammers; rebuilding or replacing valves, actuators and small pumps. Involves disassembling fouled, corroded used hardware with hand and power tools, either in place or on the shop bench.

Instrument and electrical PM: calibrating/verifying flow, level, pressure and temperature transmitters and control-valve positioners with a documenting calibrator and loop checks; cleaning and inspecting MCC buckets and control panels, torqueing lugs, replacing contactors, relays and fuses, megger-testing motors and checking VFD cooling fans.

Analytical probe maintenance on fermenters, beer well and process lines: retracting pH/ORP/DO electrodes, rinsing off mash/solids fouling, running buffer calibration, adjusting or replacing the electrode, and returning the sensor to service with documented calibration records.

Cleaning-based maintenance at scheduled outage: heat-exchanger/evaporator tube bundles pulled and cleaned by high-pressure lancing at the plant wash pad to restore heat transfer, with post-clean inspection before reinstallation.

Condition-monitoring PM rounds through the plant: logging local gauge and sight-glass readings, taking thermal images of motors, bearings and electrical gear, taking vibration/acoustic readings on rotating equipment, checking for leaks and abnormal noise, and recording results in the CMMS for follow-up work orders.

tasks.label: Calibrate liquid flow devices and meters, including fuel, chemical, and water meters.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In-situ calibration/verification of a process flow transmitter (Coriolis or magnetic meter on mash, beer, syrup or ethanol line) at an ethanol plant: technician isolates the loop, connects a documenting calibrator/HART communicator, checks and trims zero and span against a reference, compares totalizer to tank gauging, records results in the CMMS. Hot, piped, walk-up process area inside the plant.

Calibration of chemical additive flow meters (sulfuric acid, caustic, ammonia, enzyme, denaturant lines) on dosing skids: small-line liquid meters checked against a reference volume/mass, correction factor adjusted, results logged. Corrosive/hazardous fluids, small flows, plant chemical feed area.

Calibration of a mechanical diaphragm chemical metering pump's output: draw-down test with a graduated calibration column over a timed interval, manual adjustment of the stroke-length knob or stroke frequency, retest until delivered volume matches setpoint, log the pump curve.

Proving the custody-transfer fuel load-out meter (positive-displacement or Coriolis) at the truck/rail rack with a small-volume prover (often a contractor's prover trailer): hoses and cables connected, several prove runs at rack flow rates, meter factor computed and entered into the preset/flow computer, proving report filed for weights-and-measures compliance. Outdoor loading rack controlled by the plant.

Bench calibration in the plant instrument shop or an outside accredited lab: meter removed from the line, mounted on a test stand/master-meter or gravimetric rig, run at several flow points, K-factor or calibration factor written to the transmitter, calibration certificate produced and filed.

Verification/calibration of water meters (city water intake, process and cooling-tower makeup, boiler feed): totalizer comparison against a reference meter or bench test of a removed meter, error checked against tolerance, meter adjusted or replaced, readings recorded for water-use reporting.

tasks.label: Rebuild, repair, or replace biofuels processing equipment components.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pump/driver work in an ethanol or biodiesel plant: a mash, beer, slurry or caustic-service centrifugal pump is locked out, drained, uncoupled from piping, and either rebuilt in place or hauled to the maintenance shop for mechanical-seal, impeller, bearing and coupling replacement, then reinstalled, aligned and test-run.

Piping-system component replacement: swapping leaking butterfly/gate/check valves, actuators, hoses, sight glasses, strainer baskets and steam traps; breaking flanged joints, scraping and re-gasketing faces, re-torquing studs, sometimes at height in congested pipe racks or on hot lines.

Feedstock handling and rotating equipment in dusty grain-receiving/milling areas: replacing conveyor belts and chains, screw-conveyor flighting, hammermill hammers and screens, V-belts, sprockets, gearboxes, bearings and drive motors, then re-tensioning and alignment.

Process/separation equipment overhauls: plate-and-frame heat exchanger gasket replacement, shell-and-tube tube plugging or bundle work, decanter centrifuge scroll/bearing rebuild, filter-press cloth and filter-media change-outs, molecular sieve and dryer internals, agitator seals in fermenters (often confined-space entry).

Instrumentation, electrical and control component replacement: swapping level probes, pressure/flow/temperature transmitters, solenoid valves, positioners, proximity switches, small motors and VFD components, followed by wiring, calibration and loop check.

In-place metal repair of worn or cracked equipment surfaces: grinding out and weld-repairing erosion or cracks on chutes, wear plates, agitator blades, impeller faces, hoppers or vessel walls, then grinding back to profile and inspecting the repair.

roles.title: Chemical Equipment Operators and Tenders
roles.description: Operate or tend equipment to control chemical changes or reactions in the processing of industrial or consumer products. Equipment used includes devulcanizers, steam-jacketed kettles, and reactor vessels.

tasks.label: Observe safety precautions to prevent fires or explosions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: During a batch or continuous run in a chemical plant, the operator watches process conditions (temperature, pressure, level, cooling, agitation, vent/relief status) on the panel and at local gauges for signs of a developing exotherm, overpressure, overheating or vapor release, and acts (cut feed, add cooling, vent, trip the unit) to keep the process out of the flammable/overpressure regime.

Field surveillance round through the process unit or tank farm: metering for combustible gas, checking flanges, pumps and seals for leaks, looking for hot bearings and hot surfaces, spotting combustible spills or accumulations, and verifying fire equipment and gas detectors are in place and unobstructed.

Charging or transferring flammable material (solvent drums, totes, powders) to a kettle or reactor: bonding and grounding drum, hose and vessel, inerting the vessel headspace, controlling addition rate to limit static and vapor generation, keeping ignition sources out, using non-sparking tools, closing up afterwards.

Preparing equipment for maintenance or hot work: purging/inerting the vessel or fired heater, verifying atmosphere with oxygen/LEL measurement, isolating and blanking lines, draining and de-pressuring, and confirming the safe condition before any ignition source (burner light-off, welding) is introduced.

Ignition-source and PPE discipline while working in a classified (Zone 1/Division 1) area: flame-resistant clothing and face protection, no phones or spark-producing tools, permits observed, static-dissipative footwear, so that the operator's own presence and actions do not create an ignition source.

Abnormal event: a gas detector or high-temperature alarm sounds, or a small solvent spill/incipient fire occurs. The operator locates the source, isolates the leak, initiates emergency shutdown or suppression, uses an extinguisher on an incipient fire, and clears/evacuates the area and notifies emergency response.

tasks.label: Patrol work areas to detect leaks or equipment malfunctions or to monitor operating conditions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine indoor round through the process area of a continuous chemical or consumer-products plant: fixed route past reactors, pumps, heat exchangers, filters and compressors; read local gauges and sight glasses, look for drips/puddles/seal leaks, listen for abnormal pump or motor noise, check for hot spots, log readings and report anomalies to the board operator.

Outdoor round of a process unit, tank farm or pipe rack at a petrochemical/large chemical plant: stairs, grating and weather; carrying a portable gas detector through electrically classified (Ex) areas; checking flanges, pump seals, vents, tank levels and steam traps for leaks and malfunctions.

Monitoring loop during a batch run on a small/mid-size batch plant floor (kettles, reactors, blend tanks): frequent circuits of a cluttered area with drums, totes, temporary hoses, forklift traffic and mezzanine stairs; watching temperature/pressure gauges, agitator seals, jacket steam and hoses, and calling out deviations.

Round that includes hands-on verification and immediate minor intervention: feeling bearings and lines for heat/vibration, checking gearbox oil levels, cracking a drain valve on a trap or sight glass, tightening a weeping fitting or closing a valve on a small leak, wiping/containing a drip before reporting it.

Hard-access checks prompted by an alarm, odor or suspected leak: climbing a vertical ladder to a tank top or elevated platform, crawling under vessels, opening an equipment enclosure or checking a roof/pipe-bridge location, in PPE, to locate the source and confirm the malfunction.

tasks.label: Inspect equipment or units to detect leaks or malfunctions, shutting equipment down, if necessary.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine scheduled field round in an outdoor/semi-outdoor continuous process unit (refinery, petrochemical or gas-processing plant): operator walks a fixed route past pumps, compressors, heat exchangers, tanks and piping, looking for gas or liquid leaks, reading local gauges and sight glasses, checking for overheating, abnormal noise or vibration, logging readings and reporting anomalies to the control room. No shutdown needed on the great majority of rounds.

Routine round inside a multi-floor indoor chemical or consumer-product production building: operator checks reactors, steam-jacketed kettles, agitators, pumps, filters and transfer piping for drips, weeping gaskets and seal leaks, verifies liquid levels, valve/lever positions, jacket temperatures and motor condition, and logs/reports deviations. Shutdown not required in most passes.

Continuous tending of a running batch unit: while operating a kettle/reactor the operator notices a developing malfunction (leaking pump or agitator seal, leaking hose or gasket, overheating drive, foaming/overpressure) and must immediately shut the equipment down in the field — stop the agitator and feed pump, close steam and product hand valves, isolate and lock out, and drain or vent as needed before calling maintenance.

Alarm or upset response: control board shows an abnormal reading or an alarm sounds, and the operator goes to the unit to investigate hands-on — opens a panel, feels a bearing housing, checks a strainer or seal pot, cracks a drain, traces an odor — diagnoses the cause of the malfunction and shuts the equipment down if warranted.

Post-maintenance or pre-startup leak check: after a repair or during startup, the operator brings the equipment up on pressure/steam and checks flanges, packing glands, gaskets, hose couplings and seals close-up (visual, soap solution, sniffer), tightens or re-isolates and shuts the unit back down if a leak or malfunction appears, before releasing the unit to service.

tasks.label: Measure, weigh, and mix chemical ingredients, according to specifications.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Batch chemical/coatings/resin production run: operator follows a batch sheet to charge major ingredients — bulk solvents and resins metered from storage tanks through flowmeters/load cells, plus totes and drums pumped in — into a reactor or mixer, then starts and times the agitator and logs actual weights. Plant process area with piping, pumps and hose connections.

Minor/micro-ingredient weigh-up: operator takes the batch card to a weigh room or warehouse rack, scoops or pours catalysts, pigments, biocides and additives (grams to tens of pounds) from as-received sacks, fiber drums and pails onto bench and floor scales to tight tolerance, labels each container and stages the kit for the batch.

Hand-charging of powders and solids: operator lifts 25 kg / 50 lb sacks and pail contents from pallets, slits and dumps them through a charging port or dump station into a mixer/kettle per the formula count and weight, working under a dust hood with hoist assistance, then runs the mix cycle.

In-process adjustment: after a lab/QC check (viscosity, color, pH, solids), the operator computes and weighs out a make-up addition — colorant, solvent, thickener — adds it to the batch in the tank or into pails/drums/IBCs, re-mixes and has the batch re-tested until it meets spec.

Small-scale preparation in a pilot/QC/lab area of the plant: weighing gram- to kilogram-quantities of reagents into flasks, vials or small vessels to make premixes, standard solutions or trial batches, dissolving/mixing them per a written procedure.

tasks.label: Open valves or start pumps, agitators, reactors, blowers, or automatic feed of materials.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Continuous or large batch chemical unit: from the control room console the operator executes a lineup/startup — opens motor-operated and control valves, starts feed pumps, blowers and agitators through the DCS, watches pressures/levels and confirms equipment picked up. Instrumented, actuated equipment; institution-controlled plant.

Field lineup in an operating process unit: the operator walks the unit with a checklist, opens/closes manual handwheel, gate and ball valves (some stiff, elevated on platforms, needing a wrench or valve key), racks in and starts local pumps/agitators at motor starters, cracks vents and checks for leaks while coordinating with the board operator. PPE, congested piping, weather.

Raw-material feed setup at a batch/compounding plant: stage drums, supersacks or silo lines, connect transfer hoses or couplings, open discharge/rotary valves and hopper or manway feeds, then start the screw feeder, blower or pneumatic conveying so the reactor is charged automatically; verify feed rate.

Small specialty, food-grade or cosmetics plant with a steam-jacketed kettle or small reactor: at a local panel the operator starts the agitator, cracks the steam valve, starts a transfer pump to charge liquids, and adjusts by hand and by eye during the charge.

Non-routine or upset conditions: swing to a spare pump or blower, open a bypass around a plugged exchanger/filter, or restart feed after a trip — actions taken under time pressure and requiring judgment about sequence and safety.

tasks.label: Test product samples for specific gravity, chemical characteristics, pH levels, concentrations, or viscosities, or send them to laboratories for testing.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Mid-batch spot check at the unit: operator opens a sample valve/cock on a reactor, kettle or tank in the production area, purges and draws a bottle of hot, pressurized or corrosive liquid in PPE, then runs a quick pH (meter or strip) and specific-gravity (hydrometer/portable density meter) check at the sampling station or on-unit bench, logs the value and calls for an adjustment.

Bench testing in the plant or satellite QC lab: a sample bottle already delivered to the lab is aliquoted and run on standard benchtop gear - pH meter, oscillating-tube density meter, titration for concentration/assay - results keyed into LIMS/batch sheet and the batch released or held.

Collecting and dispatching samples for outside testing: draw the routine end-of-batch or shift sample, fill and cap sample bottles, label and log them, complete the request/chain-of-custody, and get them to the central plant lab or a contract lab (drop station, tube station, courier).

Viscosity/consistency check on a viscous or non-Newtonian product (paint, adhesive, resin, food slurry) in a mixing kettle: dip a sample, run an efflux/Zahn cup or spindle viscometer at temperature, judge against spec, add solvent/thickener and re-check.

Sampling in the tank farm or loading area: climb to a tank top or reach a drum, tote or railcar, open the hatch, use a thief/bomb sampler or bottom valve, then check specific gravity with a hydrometer and concentration/pH; done outdoors in weather, at height, on institution-controlled plant grounds.

tasks.label: Adjust controls to regulate temperature, pressure, feed, or flow of liquids or gases and times of prescribed reactions, according to knowledge of equipment and processes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Batch reactor / process vessel run in a specialty chemical or pharmaceutical plant: operator works from an HMI at a local console, setting and trimming jacket temperature ramps, reactor pressure, catalyst/monomer feed rates and hold times through the prescribed reaction profile, watching for exotherm and holding the batch on the recipe until endpoint.

Continuous process unit controlled from a DCS console/control panel in a chemical, polymer or gas-processing plant: operator adjusts temperature, pressure, level and flow setpoints on distillation columns, reactors and heat exchangers as feed composition, ambient weather and downstream demand change, and responds to alarms and quality lab results.

Field adjustment at the equipment during a run: operator walks the unit and throttles manual hand valves, steam and cooling-water valves, rotameters, pressure regulators and local flow controllers to hit the flows and temperatures called for by the panel operator or the batch sheet, reading local gauges on stairs, platforms and outdoors.

Semi-manual or older equipment with a local panel (steam-jacketed cook kettle, devulcanizer, dryer, coating/curing line) in a food, rubber or consumer-products plant: operator sets dials/timers and then adjusts heat, steam and feed by observing the product itself (viscosity, color, smell, pull samples) rather than from instrumented setpoints.

Startup, shutdown, grade transition or upset recovery: operator ramps temperatures, pressures and feeds along a written procedure, coordinates panel and field actions, and deviates from normal control to bring the unit back inside limits after a deviation, trip or equipment problem.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Batch reactor or steam-jacketed kettle campaign in a specialty chemical / consumer-products plant (resins, latex, adhesives, paints, soaps, personal care): operator charges piped liquid raw materials by valve/pump, starts agitation and jacket heating, follows the batch sheet through exotherm, hold, cool and neutralization steps, watches temperature/pressure, and transfers the finished batch. Instrumented vessel, DCS/PLC HMI, institution-controlled plant floor.

Tending a continuous reaction/treatment unit over a shift (polymerization train, hydrogenation, esterification, gas treating/absorption): monitoring the DCS, trimming flows, temperatures and valve positions to hold product on spec, responding to alarms and process disturbances, coordinating with the field.

Field/manual work that feeds and services the reaction: dumping 25 kg bags, drums or totes of solid or minor ingredients into a charge port or hopper, connecting and blowing transfer hoses, cracking manual valves and hatches, pulling grab samples for the lab, clearing plugged lines. Walkways, ladders, mess, variable equipment condition inside a controlled plant.

Turnaround between products and unit startup/shutdown: washing out or CIP-cleaning the kettle/reactor and lines, blowing down and purging, lining up valves, re-establishing heating/cooling and inerting, and bringing the reaction system back to steady operating conditions.

Bench/kilo-lab or pilot-scale reaction work in an R&D, QC or small-custom-batch setting: running small reactors, flasks and hot plates or a pilot kettle to a written procedure, dosing reagents, timing and sampling the reaction, adjusting conditions, and handing off product for analysis. Ordinary human-scale laboratory built for people.

Abnormal events during a reaction: runaway exotherm or pressure excursion, failed agitator/pump, off-spec result mid-batch, instrument failure - diagnosing the cause and physically intervening (emergency quench, dumping to a catch tank, switching to backup equipment) under time pressure.

Batch reactor, mix tank or kettle with no CIP circuit: operator opens the bottom drain valve to a waste drum/sump, hooks a hose from a water or solvent line, pumps flush solution through the vessel and transfer piping with the agitator running, drains again, opens the manway to inspect and wipe residue, then closes up.

Portable equipment cleaning at a wash bay: IBC totes, drums/pails, filter housings, pump heads, hoses and fittings are drained, moved to the wash station, flushed with water/detergent/solvent, drained and inspected before reuse.

Tank trailer, ISO container or railcar interior wash at a tank-wash rack: residual heel drained, spinner/lance inserted through the manway, hot water and caustic pumped through, tank drained, dried and inspected for a food-grade or chemical-grade release.

Heavily fouled equipment: after draining and a first flush, stubborn polymer, scale or sludge remains, requiring high-pressure water lancing of the vessel interior, heat-exchanger tube bundles, or de-sludging of a storage tank, with confined-space controls.

Powder, pellet or slurry product handling (pigments, catalysts, polymers, dried chemicals): operator examines colour, texture and flow of the discharged solids against retained standard samples, compares with lab results for particle size, moisture and colour, and decides to pack, hold or rework.

tasks.label: Implement appropriate industrial emergency response procedures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Instrumented process emergency (reactor exotherm/runaway, overpressure, loss of cooling or agitation) in a chemical plant: operator implements the emergency procedure largely from the control room/panel — trips feeds and heat input, initiates emergency cooling/quench or inhibitor injection, depressures to flare/scrubber, closes remote-operated isolation valves, confirms the unit is in a safe state and notifies the shift team.

Loss of containment or equipment emergency requiring field response: operator dons PPE, enters the process area, hits the local stop on a pump/agitator, hand-closes suction/discharge or block valves, applies a leak clamp or blind, drains/depressures the segment and locks it out, in congested piping on multiple levels.

Chemical spill in the unit, drumming/packaging area or loading rack: operator sizes up the material, dons PPE, stops the source, dikes and contains with booms/absorbent pads, neutralizes or absorbs, shovels/collects into waste drums, decontaminates the floor and equipment, and documents the release.

Incipient fire (pump seal fire, small solvent or dust fire, electrical panel fire): operator pulls the alarm, isolates the fuel source, applies a portable extinguisher, hose reel or fixed monitor/deluge, cools surrounding equipment and hands over to the plant fire brigade.

Personnel emergency and site alarm: operator activates the evacuation/gas alarm, clears and evacuates the area, walks to the muster point for accountability, assists an exposed or injured co-worker to the safety shower/eyewash and renders first aid, and briefs the arriving emergency responders on the process and hazards.

Emergency drills, mock incidents and readiness checks: participation in quarterly evacuation and spill/fire drills, donning SCBA and Level B suits, practicing emergency shutdown steps on the unit, testing eyewash/showers and verifying spill-kit and extinguisher readiness.

tasks.label: Make minor repairs, lubricate, and maintain equipment, using hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine lubrication round in the process area: operator walks the unit with a grease gun, oil can and rags, greases bearing fittings on transfer pumps, agitator drives, blowers and conveyors, checks and tops up gearbox/reducer oil levels, oils chain drives and valve stems, wipes up excess. Fittings are at varying heights, in pipe racks and under equipment; some equipment is running and hot.

Minor mechanical repair in place to stop a leak or restore service: replace a flange or manway gasket, tighten or repack valve packing, snug leaking tube fittings and unions, swap a cracked hose, clamp or quick-disconnect coupling on a transfer line, using wrenches, sockets, screwdrivers and pliers after isolating and draining the line. Residues, awkward access, torque-to-spec.

Replacing consumable and wear parts on process equipment: change filter cartridges or bags and clean strainer baskets, replace spray nozzles and screens, swap drive belts on a pump or agitator, replace small pump seals/impellers, sometimes at a shop bench with the component removed, sometimes at the unit.

Cleaning and servicing kettle/reactor internals and heat-transfer surfaces: scrape or wash out product buildup in a steam-jacketed kettle or reactor, rod out plugged nozzles, drain lines and condenser tubes, service the agitator shaft seal/packing, reinstall covers and gaskets with hand tools. Confined, fouled, permit-controlled work.

Minor instrument, actuator and utility upkeep: pull and replace a plugged pH probe, thermocouple or level float, remake compressed-air tubing and fittings on a control-valve actuator, lubricate and adjust actuator linkages and limit switches, replace a gauge, tighten conduit and mounting hardware.

tasks.label: Flush or clean equipment, using steam hoses or mechanical reamers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Between-batch flush/rinse of a reactor vessel, steam-jacketed kettle, or mixing tank and its associated transfer lines in a batch chemical/consumer-products plant: operator lines up valves, connects a water/solvent/steam hose or starts the wash cycle, circulates or steams out the vessel and lines, drains to waste, and verifies the vessel is clean before the next charge.

Open-plant washdown of equipment exteriors, pump skids, filter housings, drum-filling stations, floors and drains in the process area with a steam or hot-water hose and foaming chemical, done at end of shift or after a spill in a wet, congested but institution-controlled production room.

Clearing plugged or fouled small-bore items: rodding out a plugged transfer line or drop leg, reaming a crusted spray nozzle, backflushing/cleaning strainers, screens and filter elements with mechanical reamers, rotary brushes or a hand lance, often after breaking the line and taking the part to a wash station.

Cleaning the interior of a vessel, dryer, kettle or filter press with hardened/baked-on product residue: opening the manway, high-pressure lancing or inserting a wash head, scraping stubborn deposits, sometimes under a confined-space entry permit with hazardous residue.

Turnaround/shutdown cleaning of heat exchanger, condenser or cooler tube bundles: pulling or isolating the bundle, lancing tube IDs and blasting the shell side with high-pressure water or driving mechanical reamers through the tubes until flow is restored, in a laydown area or in situ at the plant.

tasks.label: Inventory supplies received and consumed.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Periodic/cycle physical count of packaged raw materials in the plant's chemical warehouse or storeroom: walk (or drive) the racking and floor-stack areas, count and scan labelled drums, totes, sacks and pails on pallets, note lot numbers and empty locations, and reconcile the counts against the ERP/inventory system.

Verifying and logging an incoming delivery at the plant receiving dock: count pallets/drums/cases coming off the truck, match labels, lot numbers and quantities to the packing slip/BOL and COA, note obvious damage or leakage, and enter the receipt into the inventory system.

Determining on-hand quantities of bulk raw materials in the process area: reading tank and silo level gauges, sight glasses and load-cell/level indicators on a set round (including elevated platforms and Ex-classified areas), and recording the readings in the shift log/inventory sheet so bulk receipts and consumption can be tracked.

Recording material consumed during production: weighing or metering each charge of raw material into the reactor/kettle, capturing the lot numbers of bags, drums or totes used, and entering the quantities consumed into the batch record and inventory system on the production floor.

Counting small consumables and supplies held in the maintenance crib, storeroom cabinets and QC lab: filters, gaskets, hoses, PPE, sample bottles and reagent containers on shelves and in bins; count on-hand units, note what has been drawn down, and update the stock list/reorder trigger.

tasks.label: Inspect machines or equipment for hazards, operating efficiency, malfunctions, wear, or leaks.

instances.label: Routine shift walk-through of the process area in a dairy/food, beverage, or chemical plant: operator walks the separators, centrifuges, filter presses, pumps and seal-water lines, heat exchangers and valve stations, looking for drips, weeping flanges and product/oil leaks, listening for abnormal noise, checking for hot bearings, vibration and spills; findings are logged and abnormalities reported.

Local instrument and efficiency check: reads analog pressure/temperature gauges, sight glasses, rotameters and differential-pressure indicators across filters and screens, checks still/evaporator temperatures and vacuum, compares readings with target ranges and logs them, flagging fouling, blinding or declining separation efficiency.

Hands-on close inspection of equipment internals and consumables at changeover, CIP or shutdown: opens the filter press and checks cloths and plates for tears, blinding and worn edges; inspects shaker screens for holes; checks centrifuge bowls/scrolls, gaskets, O-rings, drive belts and bearings by sight and touch before restart.

Outdoor and elevated plant inspection: climbs stairs and platforms around tank farms, scrubbing towers, condenser banks, distillation columns and evaporators to look for leaks, steam plumes, corrosion, damaged insulation and mispositioned valves, in weather and sometimes in classified (explosive-atmosphere) areas.

Pre-start and safety hazard walkthrough of the machine area: confirms guards, interlocks and e-stops are in place, hoses and cords are not tripping hazards, no chemical/product spills or slick floors, exits are clear, fire extinguishers and eyewash stations present, and documents hazards found before starting equipment.

instances.label: Dairy plant: operator sets up and adjusts an HTST pasteurizer / cream separator / standardizer line — selects product recipe, sets flow rate and pasteurization temperature, trims separator cream flow and back-pressure, watches divert valve and pressure differential during a run and after a product changeover. Indoor food-grade processing hall.

Chemical or pharmaceutical plant: operator sets up and adjusts a filter press, decanter or disc centrifuge run — sets feed pump pressure ramp and flow, cycle/wash times, bowl differential speed or pond depth, and adjusts as cake builds and differential pressure rises. Indoor/outdoor process area of a controlled plant.

Distillation: still operator adjusts steam rate, reflux, column temperature profile, vacuum/pressure and draw-off flows on a batch still or continuous column to hold product on spec through feed and ambient disturbances. Chemical plant or distillery process structure.

Beverage/juice/brewery: operator sets up and adjusts a clarification or membrane/DE filtration skid — sets crossflow velocity, transmembrane pressure, feed flow and temperature, adjusts during the run and triggers backflush/CIP as differential pressure climbs. Indoor filtration room of a controlled plant.

Scrubbing tower, precipitation or clarification duty: operator sets and trims chemical/coagulant dosing rates, recirculation flow, pH setpoint, blowdown and tower liquid/gas flows to hold effluent or product quality as loading varies. Industrial or municipal treatment facility, largely outdoor tank/tower area on controlled premises.

Legacy or small-scale equipment (small dairy, craft distillery, rendering or specialty plant): setup is largely hands-on — hand-throttling manual valve trains and steam valves, hooking up hoses, hanging filter cloths/screens, setting mechanical stops and timers on non-instrumented equipment scattered around the plant floor.

instances.label: Dairy/food-and-beverage plant: on a fixed schedule the operator draws liquid samples (raw-milk intake bay, separator/HTST pasteurizer outlet, filtrate, finished product) from sanitary sample valves into sanitized bottles, labels and logs them, and walks them to the plant QC lab.

Chemical / petrochemical / refinery unit: operator collects process liquid or gas samples at designated sample stations (fast-loop, sample cylinder/bomb, cooler), flushes/purges the line, wears PPE, seals and labels the container, and routes it to the plant lab.

Solids/slurry operation (mineral processing, cement, sugar, starch, coal prep): operator cuts slurry from a launder or pipe, takes filter cake from a filter-press or centrifuge discharge, or screen underflow, into buckets/bags, labels and sends to the lab.

Fermentation/bioprocess (brewery, distillery, biotech, pharma): operator takes an aseptic sample from a fermenter or bioreactor sample valve (sterilize/steam, purge, fill sterile vial) for cell count, titer, gravity or micro testing.

Extra unscheduled samples during a process upset or QA hold, taken at existing equipped sample points (extra grab from a sample cock, effluent outfall sampling point, tank sample valve) and rushed to the lab.

Ad-hoc sampling where no sample point exists: thieving from an open vat or tote through a hatch reached by ladder or platform, scraping cake from an opened filter-press plate, sampling a tanker compartment from the top hatch.

Small or legacy operation (craft distillery batch still, small cheese plant vat pasteurizer, rendering or recycling plant): mostly manual equipment - operator hand-lines valves, drags hoses, fires and cuts a batch still or holds a vat pasteurizer cycle by hand, and records the legally required temperatures and times.

tasks.label: Test samples to determine viscosity, acidity, specific gravity, or degree of concentration, using test equipment such as viscometers, pH meters, or hydrometers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Dairy plant: during a pasteurizing/separating/evaporating run the operator opens a sample cock on the line or vat, draws milk, cream or condensed product into a beaker, and at an at-line bench measures pH with a probe and titratable acidity by titration, plus specific gravity/total solids with a lactometer or density meter; logs results and adjusts the process.

Food/beverage concentration or distilling (juice or syrup evaporator, sugar pan, ethanol or spirits still): operator draws a hot sample at the sample valve, cools it, pours it into a cylinder and floats a hydrometer (or uses a refractometer/density meter) to check degree of concentration or proof, checks pH, and trims steam or feed rate.

Chemical/petrochemical batch still, solvent recovery, scrubber or filtration unit: operator collects product or filtrate at a sampling station in PPE (hot, flammable or corrosive liquid), cools/settles it, and runs specific gravity/density, viscosity and acidity (pH or acid number) at a satellite lab bench before releasing the cut.

Minerals, pigment or wastewater-type clarification: operator collects slurry, thickener underflow or filtrate in a bucket/cylinder, checks pulp density/specific gravity (Marcy scale or hydrometer) and pH at a plant bench, often in a dusty, wet, partly outdoor process building; results drive flocculant or filter-press settings.

Pharma/biotech/personal-care fermentation, centrifugation or filtration under GMP: operator pulls a sample through an aseptic sample port at set intervals, tests pH, density and sometimes viscosity in a controlled/clean area, and records results against batch documentation with signature and audit trail.

Small craft operation (craft distillery, small creamery, small juice or water bottler): a single operator uses a glass hydrometer in a cylinder plus a handheld pH meter on a crowded, non-standardized bench next to the still or tank, calibrating the meter and correcting readings for temperature by hand.

tasks.label: Clean or sterilize tanks, screens, inflow pipes, production areas, or equipment, using hoses, brushes, scrapers, or chemical solutions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: End-of-run clean-in-place (CIP) of process circuits in a dairy, beverage, brewery or chemical plant: operator sets up the circuit (swing bends/valve routing), starts the caustic/acid/sanitize program on the CIP skid, circulates solutions through tanks, pipes, pumps, plate heat exchangers and spray devices, monitors temperature/conductivity/return, drains and rinses, and signs the circuit off as clean.

Routine open-plant washdown of the production area between runs or on the sanitation shift: rinse floors, drains, walls, conveyor frames and tank/machine exteriors with a hose, apply foam detergent, rinse again and apply sanitizer over defined zones of a food or beverage plant.

Detail hand cleaning of complex equipment on the same sanitation shift: scrubbing with brushes and pads and scraping product residue off filler heads, guards, conveyor belts, gaskets and other awkward surfaces the hose alone will not clean, then inspecting for residue before sanitizing.

Clean-out-of-place work: dismantling removable parts - shaker screens, filter press cloths and plates, strainer baskets, centrifuge/filter internals, pump heads, valve seats, hoses and gaskets - hand-brushing or soaking them in chemical solution, rinsing and sanitizing, then reassembling and checking the machine.

Periodic deep cleaning of a heavily fouled vessel interior: fermenter, evaporator, settling/precipitating tank or still bottom with scale, sludge or hardened residue; confined-space permit, entry with hose, scraper and brushes, chemical descale, hose-out and inspection.

Cleaning inflow screens, strainers and intake piping at a water/wastewater or process-water intake: raking and hosing debris off bar screens, pulling and washing strainer baskets, back-flushing or rodding inflow lines, and hosing down the headworks area.

tasks.label: Examine samples to verify qualities such as clarity, cleanliness, consistency, dryness, or texture.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Dairy/beverage plant: operator draws a sample of milk, cream, juice or process water from a line sample valve into a beaker or vial, holds it to the light to check clarity, sediment and body/consistency, and either passes the batch or pulls it for lab test. Wet, warm, CIP-cleaned plant floor.

Chemical, petrochemical or pharma plant: operator collects liquid from a still, filter, scrubber or centrifuge sample port into a bottle, checks clarity, colour, haze and visible particulates/carryover before the batch is released or the sample is sent to the QC lab. Piping, hot lines, PPE.

Filter press / centrifuge cake check: operator inspects the discharged cake at the press or scroll, breaks or squeezes a handful to judge dryness, crumbliness and consistency, and adjusts the cycle if the cake is wet or poorly formed. Messy, variable cake positions.

Dry bulk product after dryer, screen or classifier (sugar, starch, salt, powdered milk, minerals): operator scoops a sample, rubs it between fingers for grit, lumps, texture and dryness, and eyes it for foreign matter or discoloration before it goes to packing.

Water/wastewater or utility treatment works: operator collects clarifier, filter-effluent or thickener sample in a jar, checks clarity/turbidity against the light and watches floc settle to judge whether the separation step is performing. Part indoor gallery, part outdoor basin deck.

Bench measuring for process control in the plant's QC/lab area: weighing out a small measured mass of sample, reagent or additive (grams to milligrams) and measuring liquid volumes to set dose rates or verify solids content before the material is processed.

tasks.label: Dump, pour, or load specified amounts of refined or unrefined materials into equipment or containers for further processing or storage.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Sack/bag dumping: in a food, chemical, water-treatment or pharma plant, the operator breaks down a pallet of 25-50 lb bags (filter aid/diatomaceous earth, salt, sugar, lime, polymer, resin), cuts each open at a bag-dump station or open tank hatch, dumps the specified count into the hopper/vat, and disposes of the empty bags; dusty, repetitive, count logged against the batch sheet.

Bulk containers: using a forklift or hoist, the operator lifts super sacks (FIBC), drums or totes of raw material, hangs/positions them on a bulk-bag discharge frame or drum tipper over a hopper feeding the separation equipment, opens the spout, and empties the specified quantity; plant floor traffic and mixed container types.

Measured additions of liquids and minor ingredients: pouring/weighing out specified amounts of coagulant, acid/caustic, enzymes, cultures, antifoam, or precoat slurry from pails, jugs or carboys into a vat, day tank, or mix tank, verifying quantity on a scale or sight glass before starting the batch.

Filling containers with refined product for storage/shipment: filling drums, IBC totes, carboys, or bins with recovered product, filtrate, or concentrate to a specified net weight or level, closing/labelling them, and staging them for storage.

Charging solids into separation equipment and discharging cake: feeding slurry/wet solids into a filter press, centrifuge basket, or screen, precoating filters, then shovelling or dumping the discharged cake/crystals into bins, totes or carts for further processing or disposal.

Yard/outdoor bulk loading: a loader or dump truck delivers bulk unrefined material (stone, grain, sludge, lime, ore) and dumps a specified load into a receiving hopper, pit, or crusher at the plant yard; outdoors, weather exposed, plant-controlled traffic routes.

tasks.label: Assemble fittings, valves, bowls, plates, disks, impeller shafts, or other parts to prepare equipment for operation.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Dairy/beverage plant: after CIP or scheduled maintenance, the operator reassembles a disc-stack centrifugal separator/clarifier — mounts the impeller/paring disc and shaft, restacks ~100 conical discs on the distributor in order, seats O-rings and gaskets, sets the bowl hood and torques the large lock ring to spec, then remounts the bowl in the frame and reconnects product lines. Heavy (50-300 kg) sanitary parts, hoist-assisted, wet floor, plant-standard layout.

Chemical, pharma, food or water-treatment plant: prepare cartridge/bag filter housings and strainers — insert new elements into the tube sheet or basket, seat and lubricate O-rings/gaskets, position the cover or head, and tighten swing bolts/eye nuts in sequence; verify seating and leak-tightness on start-up.

Mining, chemical or wastewater plant: prepare a plate-and-frame filter press — hang or shift heavy filter plates onto the rails in the correct order, dress new filter cloths onto plates (barbed necks, tie strings, retaining rings), align gasketed sealing faces, and close the pack.

Any process plant: set up the flow path for the run — bolt or thread pipe fittings, install and orient valves, place sanitary gaskets in tri-clamp ferrules and close clamps, connect flexible hoses/couplings between tanks, pumps, filters and the separator, and fit screens/strainers/sight glasses before start-up.

Distillation still, evaporator, condenser or scrubbing tower: install internals and closures — spray nozzles, packing supports or trays, demister pads, condenser tube-bundle covers and head gaskets — insert bolts through flanges and torque in a cross pattern, sometimes at height on an outdoor process structure.

Sanitizing separation equipment before startup or after a run: turning valves to pump sanitizer and rinse water through centrifuges/separators, membrane filtration skids, filter housings/presses, screens and condenser tubes, including hose-connected units and equipment that must be flushed at set flow and pressure.

Pharmaceutical/biotech, chemical or specialty plant: CIP/SIP of stills, columns, evaporators, scrubbing towers, precipitation vessels and fermenters — sequencing valves to pump cleaning solution and WFI/rinse water through the system, with cycle parameters recorded for the batch record.

tasks.label: Remove clogs, defects, or impurities from machines, tanks, conveyors, screens, or other processing equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Food/dairy/chemical plant: an unexpected plug or jam in a wet-process line - curd or fiber plugging a transfer pipe or separator bowl, a foreign object jamming an auger or valve, a plugged pump or spray nozzle. Operator diagnoses the location, shuts down and isolates/locks out, opens unions or hatches with hand tools, rods/hoses/digs the obstruction out, reassembles and restarts.

Blinded or clogged filtration media: a plugged basket strainer, a fouled cartridge or bag filter, a blinded shaker/vibratory screen, or filter-press cloths and plates caked with solids. Operator takes the unit offline (or switches duty/standby), removes the accumulated solids by backflushing, scraping, or washing, and returns it to service when differential pressure recovers.

Removing impurities and defective material from the product stream itself on a moving conveyor, chute, or screen deck - pulling out rocks, wood, plastic, metal, stems, off-color or off-spec pieces, and tramp material at a picking station in a food, minerals, or waste-recovery line, continuously for a shift.

Fouled vessels and heat-transfer surfaces: sludge, scale, or hardened residue accumulated in a settling/precipitating/fermenting tank, clarifier, evaporator body, or condenser/heat-exchanger tube bundle. Removal by lancing, hydroblasting, spray cleaning, or desludging during a scheduled shutdown or between batches.

Bulk-solids buildup in a minerals, aggregate, sugar, or cement-type processing plant: material bridging or rat-holing in a hopper, wet fines packing a transfer chute, carryback and spillage building up on conveyor belts and rollers, often outdoors on plant structures. Operator pokes, air-lances, vibrates, or scrapes the buildup free.

Waste/wastewater processing facility: rags, plastics, and coarse debris blinding an inlet bar screen or trash rack, or fouling channels, grinders, and pumps. Debris must be raked/removed continuously as flow varies so downstream separation equipment keeps running.

tasks.label: Start agitators, shakers, conveyors, pumps, or centrifuge machines.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Continuous-process plant (refinery, chemical, water/wastewater, large dairy or edible-oil plant): operator at the control-room DCS/HMI checks permissives and initiates start of feed/transfer pumps, tank agitators, and disc-stack or decanter centrifuges as a unit is brought online, then watches motor amps, flow, and vibration and trims speeds.

Local start-up at the machine on the plant floor: operator walks the unit, checks lube/seal water/guards and drain valves, opens suction and discharge valves, presses the local start pushbutton at the motor starter or VFD keypad, confirms rotation, priming, flow and absence of unusual noise/vibration, and adjusts.

Batch sanitary food/dairy/beverage processing: after a vat or silo is filled, operator starts the agitator, then the transfer pump and the conveyor feeding a shaker screen or press, many times per shift on a fixed, standardized sanitary line with CIP.

Small or legacy facility (small creamery, winery, rendering plant, small mineral or juice processor): crowded, non-standard layout with manual controls - cord/lever starters, belt shifters, handwheel valves, local drum switches on shakers and conveyors - started by hand and watched until steady.

Portable/engine-driven equipment at an outdoor field site (construction dewatering, lagoon or tank cleanout, remediation, temporary bypass): operator sites and primes a mobile pump or dewatering skid, starts the diesel engine and pump, verifies prime and discharge, and sets speed; ground and layout as found.

tasks.label: Install, maintain, or repair hoses, pumps, filters, or screens to maintain processing equipment, using hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Dairy/beverage processing plant: operator changes clogged filter cartridges or bag filters in in-line housings and swaps worn sanitary hoses, gaskets and tri-clamp fittings between tanks, pumps and fillers; wet washdown floor, product-contact hygiene rules, wrenches/clamp tools, work at floor level and on tank platforms.

In-place process pump work: isolate and lock out a centrifugal or positive-displacement pump, remove coupling guard and casing bolts, replace mechanical seal, packing or worn impeller, reinstall, re-align coupling, reconnect piping/hose and leak-check; confined pump room, corroded fasteners, hand and torque tools.

Chemical/pharma/refinery filtration unit: replace filter press cloths or plates, pull and clean basket strainers, change flange gaskets and flexible process hoses on piping; PPE, hazardous residues, lockout/tagout, some work on elevated platforms or in tight pipe racks.

Water/wastewater or mineral-processing separation equipment: unbolt and replace blinded vibrating/shaker screen panels or intake screens, patch or replace slurry hoses and clamps, rebuild a small transfer pump; wet, gritty, partly sheltered areas inside the plant fence.

Centrifuge, separator or still overhaul: disassemble bowl/discs or column internals, replace seals, nozzles and screens, clean scale, reassemble to torque spec and test-run; heavy precision parts, sequence-dependent teardown in plant maintenance bay or in place.

Small craft operation (winery, small dairy, cannabis/botanical extraction): set up and break down portable pumps and hose runs, change pad/lenticular filter media and screens, tighten clamps and fix leaks; layout varies batch to batch, mixed improvised fittings, hand tools only.

sources.system: AutoFuel autonomous truck refuelling robot
sources.title: Autonomous Truck Refuelling with Universal Field Robots
sources.claim: Autonomous truck refuelling robot positions itself at a purpose-built fuelling station, removes the fuel cap and connects a fuel nozzle to a haul truck without an operator - the closest commercial analogue to robotic hose/coupling connection, but it performs no hose installation, clamping or repair.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = coupling a fluid line to a fixed port at a dedicated station. It does not transfer: the robot handles one engineered nozzle/cap geometry at a station built for it, and never removes, routes, clamps or repairs hoses, filters or pumps with hand tools.

sources.system: Robotized bolting control framework and robotic bolting setup
sources.title: Improving dependability in robotized bolting operations
sources.claim: Robotized bolting for industrial assembly and facility maintenance remains a research problem; the authors propose a control framework precisely because autonomy and fault-detection reliability in bolting operations are still limited.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = threaded-fastener make/break, the core motor skill in removing pump casings, filter housing lids and screen hold-downs. Dependable autonomous bolting is unsolved even in a laboratory setup with known bolt locations, so it cannot substantiate whole maintenance jobs.

sources.system: Robotic unscrewing and screw-collection cell for EV battery disassembly
sources.title: Robotic Removal and Collection of Screws in Collaborative Disassembly of End-of-Life Electric Vehicle Batteries
sources.claim: Robotic removal of fasteners from used assemblies is demonstrated only as semi-automated human-robot collaborative disassembly in a laboratory cell on one known product family.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = disassembly of a used, fouled assembly, as in pump rebuilds and filter/screen changeouts. Performance does not carry over: the work is fixtured, product-specific, human-assisted, and no reassembled, leak-tight accepted result is shown.

sources.system: Single-arm deformable-linear-object harnessing pipeline
sources.title: Harnessing with Twisting: Single-Arm Deformable Linear Object Manipulation for Industrial Harnessing Task
sources.claim: Robotic manipulation of flexible hoses and cables (deformable linear objects) is still an open research challenge; harnessing and routing tasks are not reliably automated.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = routing and securing flexible lines, the core of installing or replacing process hoses. It shows the capability is at lab-demo level even in fixtured settings, so it cannot substantiate hose installation or repair at worker quality.

sources.system: Agility Robotics Digit (with comparable humanoids Apollo, Figure)
sources.title: Humanoid Robots in Industrial Manufacturing: What They Can (and Can't) Do in 2026
sources.claim: Documented 2026 humanoid deployments in industry are limited to material handling and machine tending in defined cells, not tool-based maintenance or repair of process equipment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = general-purpose mobile manipulation in a human work facility. The demonstrated envelope (tote transfer in a defined cell) is far below multi-step disassembly and reassembly of pumps, filter housings and hoses with hand tools, so no transfer is supported.

tasks.label: Connect pipes between vats and processing equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Dairy/beverage processing plant: between batches or after CIP, the operator hooks up 2–4 inch flexible sanitary hoses (tri-clamp ferrules, gaskets, wing-nut clamps) between silo/vat outlets, pumps, separator/pasteurizer and filler manifolds; wet warm floor, hoses stored on wall racks, connections must be leak-tight and hygienic and are checked before transfer starts.

Chemical or pharmaceutical batch plant: connecting flexible transfer hoses or drop lines (camlock, flanged or sanitary fittings, bonding/grounding straps) between reactors/vats and a filter press, centrifuge, evaporator or dryer; product-specific hose selection, valve line-up, solvent/ATEX area, full PPE.

Brewery, winery or small food plant cellar: dragging and connecting hoses between fermenters, transfer pump, filter and bright tank; tank locations, hose lengths and routings vary batch to batch, floor drains and hose reels, some connections made from platforms or step ladders.

Tanker or railcar bay at a plant/terminal: connecting the transfer hose or loading arm between a road tanker or rail tank car and the plant's receiving line/storage vats — API or camlock coupler, vapour-return line, grounding clamp, outdoors at a loading rack in all weather.

Hard-piped change in refinery/still or plant process piping: making up a flanged spool piece, jumper or swing elbow between a vessel and equipment with a new gasket and bolts torqued in a pattern, sometimes at elevation or in a confined space, with a hoist or come-along to align flanges.

Fixed transfer/flow-plate panel: moving jumper hoses or swing bends on a standardized matrix panel (or docking a hose into fixed hose stations on a skid) to route a given vat to a given piece of processing equipment; ports fixed, identical fittings, done many times a shift.

tasks.label: Remove full containers from discharge outlets and replace them with empty containers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Chemical/specialty-liquid or food plant: operator swaps 55-gal drums or 5-gal pails at a liquid discharge/filling outlet on the plant floor - rolls or jacks the full drum off the fill scale, positions an empty drum squarely under the spout/lance with the bung aligned, caps the full one.

Processing plant solids discharge: exchanging plastic/steel bins, totes, or wheeled carts under a centrifuge, filter press, or shaker-screen cake chute - full bin pulled out with a pallet jack or forklift and an empty bin repositioned under the chute, in a wet, indoor, institution-controlled plant.

Bulk powder/granule plant: swapping FIBC bulk bags or sacks at a discharge/bagging outlet - untie and remove the filled bag on its pallet, hang a limp empty bag's loops and spout on the fill head, set a fresh pallet.

QC/pilot laboratory attached to the process: swapping small receiving vessels, sample jars, and fraction receivers at a bench still, evaporator, or filter discharge, indoors in a controlled lab shared with technicians.

Craft distillery / essential-oil or pilot-scale still: swapping 5-gal buckets, jugs, or carboys at the still's discharge (spirit safe, parrot, condenser outlet) at cut points, handling hot or volatile liquid on a wet floor in a small production room.

Outdoor plant yard: exchanging a large container at a dewatering/screenings discharge - dewatering box, roll-off container, or hopper - which must be hauled out with a truck, loader, or hook lift and an empty one spotted precisely beneath the chute, in weather.
