tasks.label: Observe operation of equipment to ensure continuity of flow, safety, and efficient operation, and to detect malfunctions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Aggregate/stone crushing and screening plant at a quarry: operator watches jaw/cone crushers, screens and conveyors from a control booth and by walking the plant — checking belt tracking, chute plugging, oversize/spillage, unusual noise or vibration, hydraulic leaks, dust suppression — outdoors, dusty, 8-12 hour shifts.

Cement, lime or minerals grinding plant: operator/tender monitors raw mills, ball/vertical roller mills, separators and crushers from a control room plus periodic field rounds — mill amperage and feed flow, bearing and gearbox temperatures, dust collector and chute condition — hot, dusty, multi-level plant.

Grain, feed, flour or oilseed milling plant: operator observes hammermills, roller mills, sifters, presses and pneumatic/chain conveying — watching for choked spouts, belt slip, motor amp swings, bearing hotspots (fire/dust-explosion risk) and product flow rate — indoor, continuous 24/7 operation.

Other food/consumer or chemical processing plant grinding (coffee, spices, sugar, cocoa refiners, pharmaceutical mills): operator watches grinders/mills and product flow in a sanitary indoor plant, listening for changes, watching feed uniformity and looking for leaks, spills, or clogging.

Machine shop / precision grinding and polishing: operator tends one or several surface, centerless, or CNC grinders (or buffing/lapping machines) for metal or glass parts, watching the cycle for coolant flow, wheel loading or breakage, chatter, burn marks and part surface finish, and stopping the machine on any abnormality.

Portable/mobile crushing and screening at a demolition, concrete-recycling or road-construction site: operator monitors a track-mounted crusher and stacking conveyors set up on as-found ground, watching feed, metal in the feed, blockages, and machine noise amid changing site traffic and weather.

tasks.label: Clean, adjust, and maintain equipment, using hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Shift-end or between-batch cleaning of the crushing/grinding/polishing machine itself: opening covers and doors, removing product residue, sludge, swarf, flour or dust from chambers, hoppers, chutes and work surfaces; brushing, scraping, vacuuming, hosing or blowing out; wiping down. Occurs on a food/grain mill, mineral processing line, or shop grinder inside a plant the employer controls.

Changing worn consumables and wear parts with hand tools and hoists: grinding wheels, abrasive belts/discs and polishing pads; screen panels; crusher jaw or cone liners; mill liners; hammers and cutters. Bolts must be broken loose, parts aligned and torqued, guards refitted. Plant floor or quarry crushing plant.

Adjusting the machine so output meets spec: closed-side setting or roll gap, feed rate and gate position, belt tension and tracking, wheel dressing and truing, guard/deflector alignment, checking with feeler gauges and rules, tightening lock nuts. Plant floor.

Routine lubrication and preventive maintenance route: greasing bearing fittings, checking and topping oil, replacing filters, seals and drive belts, retightening fasteners, swapping small worn components, tagging faults for millwrights. Plant floor, often in tight or elevated spaces around the machine.

Housekeeping and washdown around the equipment: sweeping and scrubbing floors and platforms, hosing down surfaces, removing spilled material and accumulated dust in the machine area of a processing plant or quarry.

tasks.label: Tend accessory equipment, such as pumps and conveyors, to move materials or ingredients through production processes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Aggregate/mineral crushing plant (quarry or mine): tender keeps feeders, belt conveyors and water/slurry pumps moving rock through crushers and screens — sequence-starts the plant, adjusts feed rate to keep the crusher choke-fed without plugging, walks the plant to check belt tracking and spillage, bars out a plugged chute, hoses down, restarts. Dusty, semi-outdoor, noisy; institution-controlled site.

Grain elevator / feed or flour mill: tender routes grain through pits, bucket-elevator legs, drag/screw conveyors and distributor gates to the right bin or grinder, starts equipment in interlocked sequence, watches bin levels and leg amperage, shuts down and unplugs a choked leg or spout, and keeps pneumatic conveying/aspiration running. Multi-floor indoor mill controlled by the operating company.

Food, pharma or chemical ingredient milling/grinding line: tender starts transfer and metering pumps, opens/closes valves to route liquid ingredients between totes, tanks and mills, connects and swaps hoses, dumps bagged or bulk-bag powders into feed hoppers, watches screw/pneumatic conveying into the mill, and runs CIP/flush cycles. Sanitary indoor plant.

Cement, coal-fired power or industrial minerals plant: operator tends the belt conveyors, screw/rotary feeders, air slides and slurry/ash pumps that move raw meal, coal or slurry through the grinding circuit — starts and stops equipment from an HMI/control room, responds to level, plug and belt-drift alarms, and makes field checks and local resets. Large institution-controlled plant.

Small polishing/grinding or finishing shop (stone fabrication, tumbling/deburring, small mineral or glass work): tender runs a coolant/slurry recirculation pump, a dust collector, and a small vibratory or belt conveyor moving parts and media, tops up compound and water, moves hoses, cleans filters and settling tanks, and loads/unloads bins. Small employer-controlled shop floor.

tasks.label: Move controls to start, stop, or adjust machinery and equipment that crushes, grinds, polishes, or blends materials.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Fixed aggregate/sand-and-gravel crushing plant in a quarry: operator in the control booth or at the plant starts the circuit in sequence (feeders, jaw, cone, screens, conveyors), adjusts feed rate and crusher closed-side setting as feed and product gradation change, and stops units for plugs, belt issues and at shift end.

Portable/mobile crushing or grinding on a jobsite (demolition, C&D recycling, land clearing tub grinder): operator starts the machine train on ground taken as found, adjusts feeder speed and crusher setting to varying dirty feed, and stops on overload or when the excavator stops feeding.

Grain, flour or animal-feed mill: operator at an HMI/panel starts and stops hammer mills, roller mills, mixers/blenders and transfer conveyors per recipe, adjusts roll gap, feed rate and mixing time, and shuts equipment down between batches.

Cement or mineral grinding plant control room: operator starts the ball/SAG mill and auxiliaries, adjusts fresh feed, water addition, separator speed and mill load setpoints to hold fineness, and stops the mill for product changes or upsets.

Polishing/fine-grinding shop (stone slab polishing line, glass edger, ophthalmic Rx lens surfacing lab, metal finishing): operator loads or presents the workpiece, starts the machine on the correct program, adjusts head pressure, spindle and belt speeds or abrasive feed, and stops the cycle.

Chemical, plastics, rubber or pigment grinding and blending: operator starts a pulverizer/media mill and blender for a batch, adjusts speed, screen/feed and blend time to spec, and stops and discharges at end of batch.

tasks.label: Weigh or measure materials, ingredients, or products at specified intervals to ensure conformance to requirements.

instances.label: Grain, flour or feed mill: every hour or two the operator draws a sample of ground product from a spout, chute or bagging line, weighs it on a bench scale, runs a sieve/particle-size and moisture check, compares results with the spec sheet and adjusts the mill. Dusty mill floor plus a small in-plant QC bench.

Aggregate/stone crushing and screening plant: each shift the operator collects crushed product from a belt discharge, bin or stockpile, weighs the sample and runs a sieve gradation test, recording conformance to the product spec. Outdoor/semi-enclosed plant, dust, weather, heavy traffic.

Food/ingredient grinding and packing (spice, coffee, cocoa, pet food): operator weighs ingredient batches charged to the mill on a floor/platform scale and, at set intervals, pulls finished packs or portions off the line to verify fill weight against target and label declaration. Sanitary production line.

Precision grinding/polishing of parts (metal components, glass, optical blanks, stone slabs): every Nth part the operator measures diameter, thickness or finish with micrometer, caliper, snap gauge or comparator, checks it against tolerance and compensates the machine. Production shop floor.

Cement, coal or mineral grinding plant: on a scheduled hourly/shift routine the operator takes raw meal, clinker, coal or finish-cement samples from process points, weighs the sample and runs fineness (Blaine/residue) and chemistry checks in the plant QC lab, reporting conformance for mill control.

Portable crushing/screening spread on a construction, demolition or road job: technician samples crushed recycled concrete or millings from the belt discharge or stockpile, splits and weighs it, and sieves it in a field trailer lab against gradation spec. Site layout changes daily, no fixed infrastructure.

tasks.label: Reject defective products and readjust equipment to eliminate problems.

instances.label: Grain/food ingredient milling plant (flour mill, corn mill, coffee/spice grinding): tender draws samples from spouts, checks granulation, color and contamination, diverts or scraps off-spec product, then resets roll gap, feed rate or sifter screens to bring the grind back to spec.

Fixed aggregate/mineral crushing and screening plant (quarry, sand & gravel, cement raw grinding): operator watches product gradation and belt/stockpile samples, pulls or recirculates oversize and contaminated material, and readjusts closed-side setting, feeder speed or screen deck when product goes off gradation or the crusher chokes.

Precision grinding of metal or ceramic parts in a production machine shop (centerless, OD/ID, surface grinding): operator gauges ground parts, scraps out-of-tolerance or burned/chattered pieces, and corrects wheel offsets, dress cycle, feed or coolant to stop the drift.

Glass, optical or stone polishing operation (lens/glass polishing line, granite slab or edge polishing, buffing): operator inspects surface finish for scratches, haze or chipped edges, rejects defective pieces to scrap/rework, and readjusts polishing head pressure, speed, slurry/abrasive feed.

Plastics, rubber or chemical pulverizing/powder plant: tender screens or samples powder for mesh size and contamination, rejects off-spec lots and oversize, and adjusts classifier speed, mill screens or feed rate to correct particle size.

Portable/mobile crushing or grinding at a demolition, C&D recycling or road-construction site: operator on a track-mounted crusher spots oversize or contaminated (rebar, wood, dirt) output, pulls it out or recirculates it, and readjusts crusher setting and feeder while the site layout and feed vary hour to hour.

tasks.label: Inspect chains, belts, or scrolls for signs of wear.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine operating-shift walkaround in a fixed indoor processing plant (cement plant, coal prep plant, oilseed crush/grain mill, food processing): operator walks the line while equipment runs, looking and listening at conveyor belts, drive V-belts, chain drives, idlers and sprockets for fraying, cracking, mistracking, glazing, hot or squealing components; logs findings for maintenance.

Scheduled shutdown / lockout-tagout inspection in the same plant: operator opens or unbolts guards and trough covers, pulls the chain to measure elongation with a wear gauge or tape over a span of pitches, flexes and turns the belt by hand to check for cracks, cuts and cord exposure, checks sprocket tooth hooking, and inspects screw-conveyor flighting (scrolls) for thinning; decides repair/replace.

Outdoor aggregate/quarry or coal crushing-screening plant: walk the plant checking long conveyor belts and splices, skirting, drive V-belts on crusher and screen, apron-feeder chains and mill drive chains; heavy dust, weather, uneven ground, noise; findings recorded on a pre-shift checklist.

Machine-level check at setup or changeover on an individual grinding/polishing/granulating machine (surface grinder, belt polisher, rubber grinder, roller mill): open the machine's guard or access panel, inspect the spindle or feed drive belt, timing belt, abrasive belt and small drive chain for wear and correct tension inside the enclosure, replace if worn.

Portable crusher, grinder or screening plant working at a construction, demolition or land-clearing site: pre-shift walkaround of the machine as found on rough ground, checking conveyor belts, feeder chains and drive belts for wear and damage before start-up.

tasks.label: Dislodge and clear jammed materials or other items from machinery and equipment, using hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Quarry or mine primary crushing station: oversize rock bridges the grizzly or the jaw/gyratory feed opening and stops the feed. Operator stops the feeder and dislodges/breaks the bridged rock, using a pedestal boom breaker plus pry bar, sledge or scaling bar for wedged pieces; dusty, noisy, outdoor or underground tipping point.

Aggregate/mineral processing plant: plugged transfer chute, blinded screen deck, packed crusher discharge or buried conveyor skirt. Operator locks out, climbs to a catwalk or access hatch in a confined, wet/dusty space and digs out compacted material with pry bar, shovel, sledge, rod or air/water lance, then restarts.

Grain, feed or flour mill: hammermill, roller mill, screw conveyor or spout plugged with compacted grain, dust-cake or a foreign object (bolt, wire, stone, corn cob). Operator de-energizes, opens inspection doors/end plates, and knocks, pries and rakes the material out with hammer, bar, hooks and vacuum, watching for dust hazards.

Food processing plant (meat grinding, sugar, coffee, cocoa, spice): grinder/mill/pulverizer jammed by bone, gristle, packaging film or clumped product. Operator shuts down, partially disassembles the head, auger or feed screw with hand tools, clears the obstruction under sanitary rules and reassembles.

Grinding/polishing shop (glass, stone slab, ceramics, optics, metal parts, tumblers/lappers): a workpiece wedges in feed rollers, chuck, belt or between abrasive heads, or slurry/abrasive buildup blocks the feed path. Operator stops the machine, pries or taps the part free without damaging it or the tooling, clears the nip and resets.

Plastics, rubber or wood size-reduction: granulator, shredder or chipper jammed by a foreign object or a fused/wrapped mass on the rotor. Operator locks out, opens the housing or removes screens, and uses bars, wrenches and cutters, sometimes partially disassembling the rotor area, to free it.

tasks.label: Test samples of materials or products to ensure compliance with specifications, using test equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Aggregate/stone quarry or ore crushing plant: operator scoops a sample of crushed rock from a belt discharge, chute or stockpile, carries it to the on-site plant lab, splits/dries it, runs a sieve gradation and moisture check against product spec, records results and signals a crusher setting change. Dusty, wet material, coarse and fine fractions.

Cement, lime or industrial-mineral finish grinding: operator pulls a powder sample from the mill/separator sampling point, tests fineness (Blaine, 45 µm residue or laser particle size) and chemistry (XRF), compares to spec and adjusts the mill. Plant quality lab adjacent to the mill.

Food/grain milling and powder processing (flour, corn, sugar, coffee, spices): operator draws a sample from a spout or hopper, runs moisture, particle size (sieve shaker) and composition (bench NIR) tests, checks against product specification and adjusts roll gap or grinder settings. Clean but food-safe, GMP plant lab.

Precision grinding, lapping or polishing shop (metal, glass, optics, ceramic parts): operator measures the just-finished workpiece with micrometers, gauges, thickness or surface-roughness testers, verifies dimensional and finish tolerances against the print, and adjusts wheel dress or feed. Shop floor with a bench gauging station or nearby inspection room.

Rubber/plastics compounding (mill, mixer, granulator): operator takes a slab or pellet sample from the mixing line, cuts specimens and runs Mooney viscosity, rheometer cure and density tests for batch release against specification. QC lab beside the mixing floor.

Paint, ink, pigment or specialty chemical milling: operator draws a sample from the bead/roller mill, draws it down on a Hegman grind gauge and reads fineness of grind by eye, checks viscosity with an efflux cup or viscometer, and decides whether to keep milling. Small batch lab bench with judgment-based visual grading.

Small job shop or specialty operation (stone/glass polishing shop, small feed mill, lab-scale grinding): cramped variable layout, mixed unpalletized stock — slabs, crates, buckets, drums — moved by hand truck, overhead hoist and a small forklift through narrow, cluttered aisles.

Sanitary indoor plant, fixed layout.

Mineral processing or coal preparation plant: operator collects slurry, cyclone-overflow, tailings or clean-coal product samples from launders, pipes and product belts into buckets/bottles for assay and size analysis; wet, slippery walkways inside the plant.

Discrete-product grinding/polishing line (glass, ceramic, stone, metal or rubber parts): operator pulls finished pieces off the line at set intervals, marks them with lot/machine ID, and carries them to the measurement room or lab for dimensional, surface-finish or composition testing.

Outdoor yard sampling: operator walks to a stockpile, truck bed or railcar at the quarry/mill yard and takes composite increments with a shovel or probe, combines and quarters them, labels the bag and brings it to the lab; uneven footing, weather, piles that change shape day to day.

Precision grinding/polishing shop (metal parts, ceramics, optics): operator loads workpieces into chucks, magnetic tables, collets or fixtures on a surface/cylindrical/centerless grinder or lapping machine using wrenches, mallets and clamps, indexes them, and loads abrasive wheels/compound. Indoor machine shop, parts staged in trays and racks.

Stone/glass fabrication shop: operator lifts slabs, tiles or glass sheets from an A-frame onto the polishing/edging machine bed using a vacuum lifter, clamps or hoist, aligns and blocks them with shims and hand tools, then starts the machine. Indoor shop, wet, heavy pieces.

Chemical, paint, ink, ceramic or rubber batch milling: operator charges a ball mill, attritor or two-roll mill with powders, pigments, resin, grinding media or rubber slabs using scoops, drum dollies, hoists and bag-dump chutes, then secures the lid or guard with hand tools. tasks.label: Turn valves to regulate the moisture contents of materials.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Flour/grain mill tempering: operator checks incoming grain moisture (lab or in-line meter) and turns/sets the dampening water valve on the conditioning line ahead of the roller mills to hit a target temper moisture; indoor mill, fixed piping, standard equipment.

Aggregate/stone/coal crushing and screening plant: operator opens and throttles water spray and wash valves at crushers, screens and transfer points to wet material for dust suppression and to keep product moisture in spec; fixed outdoor plant on a quarry or prep-plant site, dusty and weather-exposed.

Cement, clay, gypsum or ceramic grinding/mixing: operator turns the water valve feeding a pug mill, raw mill or mixer to bring the ground mix to target moisture for pelletizing, extrusion or briquetting; indoor/covered plant with fixed equipment.

Feed or food plant grinding line: operator adjusts steam/water valves on the conditioner or mixer ahead of the hammermill or pellet mill so meal moisture is right for grinding and pelleting; sanitary indoor plant, washdown conditions.

Portable crushing/screening spread at a construction, demolition or C&D recycling site: operator opens and adjusts the water-tank/spray-bar valves on the mobile crusher by eye, judging dust and material wetness; as-found outdoor site, layout different each job, weather and feed material vary.

tasks.label: Set mill gauges to specified fineness of grind.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Commercial wheat/corn flour mill: at a product changeover the miller sets the grinding gap on break and reduction roller-mill stands to the fineness specified for the flour grade, pulls samples at the mill's sampling points, checks granulation on a sieve/plansifter, and re-adjusts until the stock meets spec. Indoor multi-floor mill, fixed layout, dusty, standard roller-mill stands.

Feed mill, ethanol plant or brewery: operator sets roll gap (and roll speed differential) on a roller grinder to hit a specified mean particle size in microns for a recipe (e.g. swine feed at 600 microns, brewer's malt crush), takes a discharge sample for sieve/particle analysis, and trims the setting. Indoor mill room with catwalks, standard equipment, company-controlled premises.

Cement, lime or industrial-mineral plant: operator sets finish-mill/separator gauges and setpoints (classifier speed, mill feed, air) to the specified fineness (Blaine or d50) for the product being run, using online analyzer or lab results, and re-trims as clinker hardness and feed change. Control room plus plant floor, fixed circuit, institution-controlled site.

Aggregate/mineral crushing and grinding plant: operator sets the crusher/mill gauge (closed-side setting, gap, screen deck) to produce the specified product gradation, checks samples against the gradation spec, and resets as liners wear. Fixed plant in a quarry or processing yard, outdoor but company-controlled, dusty and noisy.

Food or pharma specialty grinding (coffee, cocoa/chocolate refiner, spice, sugar, corn masa): operator selects the recipe and sets the mill's gap/gauge to the specified fineness, runs a sample for particle-size check (sieve or micrometer), and adjusts. Sanitary indoor production room, recipe-controlled modern machine with HMI.

Older or small-scale operation: mill has hand-crank/handwheel gap adjusters with dial gauges, hammer-mill screens that must be swapped to change fineness, or coal-pulverizer classifier vanes cranked by hand; operator walks to the machine, physically turns the adjusters or changes hardware, hand-collects a sample and runs a bench sieve shaker, and repeats. Cramped, dusty legacy plant floor with no actuators on the machine.

tasks.label: Verify quality of finished workpieces by inspecting them, comparing them to templates, measuring their dimensions, or testing them in working machinery.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Machine/fab shop: after hand deburring, grinding or finishing machined and sheet-metal parts, the worker checks the piece — measures critical dimensions with calipers, micrometers or gauges, checks edge break and burr-free condition — and accepts or sends it back for rework.

Foundry/weld shop: after chipping and grinding gates, risers, flash, parting lines or weld spatter from castings and weldments, the worker inspects the cleaned part for remaining protrusions, undercut, gouges and cracks, and compares contours to a profile template or gauge. Parts are heavy, dirty, high-mix.

Cosmetic polish/buff work (stainless trim, plated hardware, aluminum, automotive/appliance parts): worker inspects the polished surface under strong light for scratches, swirl marks, burn-through, dull spots and uneven gloss before the part passes to plating/assembly.

Wood furniture/cabinet plant: worker checks hand-sanded panels, doors, lamellas and profiled components by sight and touch for scratches, cross-grain marks, swirl, raised grain and sand-through before finish is applied.

Small precision or craft items (jewelry, dental/medical components, optics, small ceramics/plastics): worker inspects the polished piece under magnification, measures with micrometer or gauge, and sometimes test-fits it into a mating assembly or runs it in the machine it belongs to.

Stone/countertop shop: worker checks the polished slab, edge profile and cutout for gloss uniformity, scratches, chips and lippage, and lays the piece against the customer's template to verify dimensions before shipping.

tasks.label: Grind, sand, clean, or polish objects or parts to correct defects or to prepare surfaces for further finishing, using hand tools and power tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Metal fabrication shop: dressing and blending weld seams, spatter and high spots on large fabricated steel/aluminum weldments (tank shells, frames, trailers) with hand-held angle grinders, flap discs and belt files; parts sit on stands/turning rolls on the shop floor.

Foundry / machine shop finishing room: cleaning castings and machined parts — knocking off gates, riser stubs, parting-line flash, burrs on bench grinders, backstands and with pneumatic die grinders; parts arrive in bins, sizes vary within a few families.

Wood furniture / cabinet plant: orbital and block hand-sanding of chair parts, doors and panels — knocking down raised grain, removing mill marks and correcting defects between finish coats, judging the surface by touch.

Stone / solid-surface countertop fabrication shop: grinding and polishing countertop edges, sink cutouts, chips and seams through progressive diamond pad grits with wet hand polishers to a uniform gloss.

Plastics / composites plant (marine, RV, tub-shower): deflashing molded parts and sanding gelcoat or laminate on large contoured composite panels and shells, then buffing to a finish before paint or assembly.

Small precision items: buffing and polishing jewelry, dental/orthopedic implants, surgical instruments, faucet and hardware castings on buffing wheels and belt heads, holding tight cosmetic and dimensional standards.

tasks.label: Measure and mark equipment, objects, or parts to ensure grinding and polishing standards are met.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Metal fabrication / weld-finishing shop: worker checks a ground weld bead, machined face or deburred edge with calipers, radius/fillet gauges and a straightedge against a print, then marks high spots, undercut or areas needing more grinding with soapstone or paint marker. Parts arrive on carts and benches amid other workers.

Stone / solid-surface countertop fabrication shop: worker measures a slab, seam edge, cutout or profiled edge with tape, square and template, checks thickness and edge polish against shop standard, and pencil/marker-marks layout, seam and rework lines on the slab before edge polishing.

Foundry or weld-shop casting cleaning room: worker gauges gate stubs, parting lines and flash on rough castings against templates and go/no-go gauges, chalk-marks areas to chip and grind, and re-checks after grinding for flushness.

Wood furniture / cabinet or millwork finishing shop: worker inspects and measures sanded panels, profiles and edges (thickness, flatness, profile match), and chalk-marks glue spots, sand-throughs, dents and defect areas for further sanding or buffing.

Precision small-part finishing (optical glass, dental/jewelry pieces, turbine blades, hardware): worker measures with micrometer, thickness gauge or surface-finish comparator to close tolerance and marks or tags parts needing more polishing, or sorts pass/fail.

On-site finishing work: concrete floor polishing, installed stone or field-welded structural steel — worker measures the as-found surface (flatness, joint alignment, weld profile) and marks areas to grind on a jobsite taken as found.

sources.system: GrayMatter Robotics Scan&Blast / Scan&Inspect autonomous cell
sources.title: 26025 – GrayMatter Robotics – NCMS
sources.claim: GrayMatter Robotics' Scan&Blast autonomous cell scans arbitrary part geometry, inspects the surface inline, maps non-conforming areas in 3D ... uses robot-mounted laser profilometry to measure and record surface roughness against a written finishing standard, triggering selective rework without human intervention.
sources.transferJustification: The task is measuring a workpiece against a finishing standard and recording/marking where the standard is not met; this system performs that measurement on steel components in a self-contained cell and maps the non-conforming areas that a hand worker would chalk-mark.

sources.claim: GrayMatter's Scan&Sand cells scan each incoming part and adapt sanding in real time to part ... across metal, composite and wood parts; a dual-arm autonomous sanding cell has been deployed in production at a composites manufacturer.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (robotic sanding): the cell must first measure each as-presented part's geometry and surface condition to decide where material must be removed — the same measure-against-standard judgement the hand worker records with a chalk mark, on comparable parts in a shop cell.

tasks.label: Trim, scrape, or deburr objects or parts, using chisels, scrapers, and other hand tools and equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Bench deburring of machined metal parts in a machine shop: worker takes milled/turned parts from a bin or cart, breaks edges and removes burrs from holes, slots and profiles with hand deburring blades, files, scrapers and small powered tools, inspects by touch, and returns parts to a tote. Mixed batches, repeat part numbers.

Foundry / die-cast cleaning room: chipping and scraping gates, risers, flash and parting-line fins off sand or die castings with pneumatic chisels, chipping hammers, cut-off wheels and scrapers; heavy dirty parts moved on pallets and conveyors, hearing and vibration hazards.

Trimming molded plastic, rubber or composite parts: cutting sprues and gates, knife-trimming parting-line flash and degating edges on injection/blow/compression molded and layup parts, at a bench next to the presses in a molding plant.

Fettling clay/ceramic ware in a pottery or sanitaryware plant: scraping mold seams off green ware, cleaning up functional holes, removing excess slip/glue and sponging surfaces with knives, scrapers and sponges, on delicate unfired pieces.

Dressing large fabricated weldments in a fab shop, shipyard or heavy-equipment plant: knocking off slag and spatter, scraping and grinding weld beads and burrs on structures too large to fixture in a cell, with the worker climbing over/around the piece where it sits.

Field/on-site trimming and scraping: deburring, scraping or chipping installed or one-off items at a customer site or outdoors (repair rework, in-place structures, monuments), varying layout, no institutional control of the setting.

tasks.label: Mark defects, such as knotholes, cracks, and splits, for repair.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Wood products plant (furniture, cabinet, millwork, plywood): after sanding a part or panel at a bench or line station, the worker inspects the surface under shop light, then chalks/crayons circles around knotholes, checks, splits, tearout and glue spots so a repair worker can fill and re-sand them.

Foundry cleaning room or metal fabrication shop: after chipping/grinding a casting or weld seam, the worker inspects the ground surface and marks cracks, porosity, cold shuts, sand inclusions and gouges with soapstone or a paint marker so a welder can excavate and repair them.

Stone, terrazzo or engineered-countertop fabrication shop: after honing/polishing a slab or countertop, the worker wets and eyes the surface, feels hairline fissures with a fingernail, and marks pits, chips and cracks with a crayon or tape flag for epoxy fill and color matching.

Glass, plastic or composite part finishing: the buffer inspects flat or lightly curved transparent/molded parts on a bench or conveyor and marks scratches, bubbles, chips or delamination with a washable marker or grease pencil for rework.

One-off or low-volume custom work in a shop (architectural metalwork, sculpture, restoration pieces, large custom furniture): the finisher inspects an item of unfamiliar geometry and marks assorted flaws for the repair or fill step; no two pieces alike, no standard part program.

On-site/field finishing: marking defects on installed or immovable work — installed stone tops and floor slabs, monuments, boat hulls, large weldments in place — using chalk or tape while working around other trades and variable lighting.

tasks.label: Study blueprints or layouts to determine how to lay out workpieces or saw out templates.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Move controls to adjust, start, or stop equipment during grinding and polishing processes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Metal fabrication/machine shop: worker finishes small-to-medium metal parts at a pedestal grinder, belt sander, or deburring station — flips the switch to start, adjusts belt speed/tracking and tool rest, dresses/changes the wheel, stops the machine between parts.

Hand-held power tool finishing of large workpieces or assemblies (auto body panels, welded assemblies, composite/fiberglass parts): pulls trigger on angle grinder/random-orbit sander/polisher, changes variable-speed setting, adjusts air pressure or backing pad pressure mid-job, releases trigger and stops.

Buffing/polishing wheel or lathe work on plated hardware, jewelry, dental/orthopedic or medical items: starts the buffing spindle, changes speed, rakes/recharges the wheel with compound, stops the spindle for inspection.
Stone, countertop or glass shop: operates wet grinder/edge polisher or hand polisher — starts machine, sets and adjusts water flow and spindle speed for each grit step, stops between passes.

Semi-automated finishing equipment in the shop (vibratory/tumbling barrel, wide-belt or drum sander, robotic-assist finishing cell): loads media/part, sets or recalls parameters on the panel, presses cycle start, monitors, stops or e-stops the cycle.

On-site/field finishing away from the shop: concrete floor grinding/polishing in a building under construction, polishing installed stonework, dressing welds on erected structures — starting, throttling and stopping portable grinding/polishing equipment on the jobsite.

tasks.label: Load and adjust workpieces onto equipment or work tables, using hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: High-volume production finishing station in a metal parts plant: the worker repeatedly takes the same part type (castings, stampings, machined parts, a few pounds each) from a rack, tote or conveyor, seats it in a dedicated nest/fixture or jig at a grinding, deburring or buffing station, and locks it down before finishing. Same part all shift, standard containers.

Job-shop / small fabrication shop setup: each batch is a different part, so the worker clamps varied castings, weldments or machined pieces in a bench vise, angle plate or clamp fixture on the work table, shims and squares them, and tightens with wrenches, C-clamps and screwdrivers; fixtures and stops are changed between jobs.

Foundry cleaning room or heavy fabrication: 100-1,000 lb castings or weldments are rigged with a hoist/jib crane, set onto a grinding stand, floor table or positioner, blocked and clamped by hand before chipping and swing-frame grinding. Irregular, hot/dusty conditions, parts arriving on pallets and carts.

Stone, glass or tile fabrication shop: the worker moves slabs and cut countertop/glass pieces onto polishing benches or machine work tables, sets them on rails, suction pads or supports, and levels/secures them for edge polishing and hand finishing.

Woodworking / furniture plant or cabinet shop: the worker places panels, doors, frames or turned parts onto sanding tables, jigs or vacuum pods, adjusts stops and clamps them before hand or power sanding.

Small precision or decorative work (jewelry, dental, optical, plumbing hardware, cutlery, medical implants): the worker mounts small workpieces onto polishing fixtures, mandrels, chucks or holding blocks, tightening and adjusting them with hand tools before buffing or lapping.

sources.transferJustification: Same act as the task: taking a metal workpiece from its presentation point and positioning/holding it at grinding equipment; parts (4-14 kg castings) match the metal-finishing instances.

sources.transferJustification: Loading and orienting wood panels/parts onto a machine table is the wood-shop version of this task; the sanding/CNC table is the equipment the workpiece is placed and held on.

sources.system: Figure 02 humanoid robot at BMW Group Plant Spartanburg
sources.title: Humanoid Robots Complete Trial Project at BMW Assembly Plant | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: Two Figure 02 humanoids ran 10-hour shifts for ten to eleven months in BMW Spartanburg's body shop, picking sheet-metal parts from racks or ... placing them on a welding fixture to a 5 mm tolerance; targets were 99% placement success per shift and zero human interventions.

tasks.label: Repair and maintain equipment, objects, or parts, using hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In a metal-finishing / fabrication / woodshop bay, the worker swaps spent abrasive consumables and accessories on hand-held power tools and bench machines — hook-and-loop sanding discs, belts, flap wheels, buffing wheels, mounted points — using spanners, wrenches and belt-tension levers, then re-checks the tool runs true before resuming work.

The worker dresses, trues or rakes a grinding or buffing wheel that has loaded up or gone out of round, using a dressing stick, star dresser or diamond dresser held by hand, restoring wheel geometry and cutting surface, then re-sets the tool rest gap.

Routine housekeeping maintenance on shop equipment: blowing down and wiping compound and dust off a buffing lathe or sander, emptying/clearing dust-collection bags and hoses, oiling or greasing spindles and slides, checking and tightening guards, hoses and fittings, and re-adjusting work rests and fences with hand tools.

The worker repairs or reworks the object or part itself with hand tools — blending a weld or casting flaw, deburring an edge, sanding and polishing out a scratch or paint/finish defect, filling a chip and re-finishing — to bring a rejected or damaged piece back to accepted quality.

The worker troubleshoots a malfunctioning machine and replaces worn or broken components: drive belts, bearings, motor brushes, damaged cords, air hoses and fittings, platens or contact wheels, using screwdrivers, wrenches, pullers and allen keys, then tests the repair.

Off-site/field work (stone or terrazzo restoration crew, marine hull polishing, monument work): maintaining and repairing the crew's grinders, polishers, generators and water-feed gear on the customer's premises, with only a hand-tool kit and no fixed layout.

tasks.label: Select files or other abrasives, according to materials, sizes and shapes of workpieces, amount of stock to be removed, finishes specified, and steps in finishing processes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Metal fabrication shop, foundry or machine shop: worker sizes up a welded steel/aluminum weldment or a rough casting on a bench or fixture stand, judges material, weld bead size and stock to remove, and picks a grinding wheel, flap disc, fiber disc, carbide burr or hand file of the right type and grit, mounts it on an angle grinder or die grinder, then steps down to finer media for the specified finish.

Wood furniture, cabinet or millwork shop: worker chooses the abrasive form (belt, orbital disc, sanding sponge, hand block) and grit progression for raw-wood leveling, edge/profile sanding and between-coat scuff sanding of sealer or primer, per the finish schedule, loading discs onto a random-orbit sander.

Auto body / paint finishing bay or OEM paint repair area: worker selects abrasive grade and pad/compound for shaping filler, block-sanding primer, denibbing topcoat defects and buffing to gloss, changing discs on a DA sander and swapping polishing pads and compounds as the repair progresses.

Stone, quartz or solid-surface countertop shop: worker selects the diamond pad or wheel grit progression (e.g., 50 through 3000) matched to the material and edge profile, swapping pads on a wet polisher to profile and polish edges, seams and cutouts to the specified sheen.

Industrial precision-part bench: implant, mold/die, aerospace or machined-part finishing where the worker picks needle files, mounted points, structured abrasive belts, buffing wheels and compounds sized to small radii, pockets and contours, sequencing from stock removal to cut-buff to color-buff against a written finish spec.

Artisan or one-off bench work: jewelry, art glass, custom restoration or on-site touch-up, where the piece is unique, irregular and often held in the hand, and the worker chooses among needle files, emery sticks, small buffs and compounds by feel and inspection with no repeatable recipe.

tasks.label: File grooved, contoured, and irregular surfaces of metal objects, such as metalworking dies and machine parts, to conform to templates, other parts, layouts, or blueprint specifications.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Production machine shop: filing/deburring grooves, slots, keyways, chamfers and contoured edges on machined metal parts (housings, brackets, valve bodies) so edge breaks and contours meet blueprint callouts; parts arrive in batches on carts or trays, inspected against print and gauges.

Tool-and-die room bench work: hand-filing and stoning grooved and contoured die/mold cavity detail, radii and parting-line areas to match a template, a layout, or the mating die half, using spotting blue and repeated try-fit cycles until the contour and fit are accepted.

Fabrication shop or foundry finishing area: filing/grinding weld seams, gate and riser stubs, parting-line flash and irregular as-cast contours on medium and large steel/iron parts so the surface blends into the specified contour; heavy dust, part moved by hoist or cart.

Job shop, batch of one or two: precision filing of small metal parts to scribed layout lines or a print dimension (slot widening, contour blending on a machined detail), programmed from a print or CAD model, checked with gauges/calipers.

Job shop, batch of one or two: filing a small part 'to fit' another part or a gauge — easing a slot, key, bushing or pin until the mating piece seats with the right feel/clearance, judged by repeated hand assembly rather than a dimension.

Field or in-plant maintenance/assembly: filing a part in place or at a nearby bench so it fits an installed assembly (bracket hole, keyway, burred shaft, misaligned mating face), with the reference being the installed machine and no fixed layout.

tasks.label: Sharpen abrasive grinding tools, using machines and hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Metal fabrication shop or foundry: worker dresses the wheel of a bench/pedestal or swing-frame grinder, holding a star-wheel or hand diamond dresser against the free-running wheel, removing glaze and loading, squaring the face and breaking the corners, judging progress by sound, sparks and feel, then checking the face with a square.

Machine shop: worker trues and dresses a wheel mounted on a surface, cylindrical or tool-and-cutter grinder using a single-point diamond, dressing stick or rotary form roll — mounting the dresser, setting infeed, running the dressing passes, and reprofiling form wheels between jobs.

Metal-finishing/polishing department: worker rakes and trues cloth, sisal and flap buffing wheels on polishing lathes — removing loaded compound and frayed cloth with a buff rake, evening the face, and recharging the wheel with bar compound between parts.

Wood, composite or plastics finishing shop: worker deglazes and cleans loaded abrasive belts, sanding drums and flap wheels with rubber cleaning sticks or a cleaning device, and trues drum/contact-wheel faces so the abrasive cuts evenly again.

Stone, tile or glass fabrication shop: worker dresses diamond abrasive tooling — CNC profile wheels, cup wheels, glass edging/seaming wheels — with a soaked dressing stick or brick to reopen closed diamond and remove high spots, running the tool on a spindle while applying the stick.

Job site (concrete polishing crew, monument setting, field weld dressing): worker opens/dresses metal-bond diamond segments, cup wheels or grinding stones in the field using dressing blocks or abrasive plates, under uncontrolled conditions with no fixed layout.

tasks.label: Transfer equipment, objects, or parts to specified work areas, using moving devices.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Metal fab shop / machine shop production floor: the hand grinder moves loaded totes, wire baskets or wheeled racks of small-to-medium parts (a few lb to ~100 lb each) between the grinding bench and adjacent operations — wash, deburr, inspection, plating dock, assembly — pushing a cart or tugging a rack across aisles shared with forklifts and people.

Palletized or skidded loads: using a hand/electric pallet jack or forklift, the worker brings pallets, skids and bulk containers of raw or ground parts from staging racks to the work area and takes finished loads to the next department or shipping, in a manufacturing plant with marked aisles and standard 48x40 pallets or plant-standard containers.

Foundry cleaning room / heavy fabrication: individual heavy castings, weldments or plate sections (100–3,000 lb) are slung and lifted with a chain hoist, jib crane, or overhead bridge crane from the cooling/staging area onto the grinding stand or into the chipping booth, and the finished piece is lifted off again; also dragging the grinder, hoses and stands to the piece.

Stone/countertop or architectural glass shop: slabs (300–900 lb) and cut pieces are moved with A-frame carts, clamp/vacuum lifters, forklift slab booms or a monorail hoist from slab storage or the saw to the polishing/edge-finish station and then to the loadout rack.

Bench-scale shops (dental laboratory, jewelry shop, optical, small custom finishing): trays, pans and racks of small pieces are carried or wheeled on a small cart between benches, the buffing/polishing room, ultrasonic cleaner, and plating or packing, in a room-sized shop with crowded benches.

tasks.label: Remove completed workpieces from equipment or work tables, using hand tools, and place workpieces in containers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: High-volume production shop (foundry finishing room, stamping/fab plant): a hand grinder finishes the same repeated metal part all shift, lifts the completed piece off the bench or out of a simple holding jig, and drops it into a tote, wire basket or rack beside the station. Parts a few pounds each, consistent geometry, hundreds per shift.

High-mix job shop bench: each job is a different part (weldments, brackets, castings, machined pieces). The completed workpiece is clamped in a vise, toggle jig, magnetic chuck or bolted fixture and must be released with hand tools (wrench, clamp lever, mallet, pry) before being carried to whatever crate, cart or bin the traveler calls for, on a cluttered bench shared with tools, abrasives and coolant.

Heavy or bulky workpieces: large castings, weldments, stone slabs or big glass panels ground/polished at a floor stand or table. Removal requires a hoist, jib crane, vacuum lifter or two-person lift, with the piece set onto a pallet, A-frame rack or roll cart rather than a hand-carried container.

Delicate high-finish items: polished/plated metal, optical or decorative glass, ceramics, jewelry and similar. Finished surfaces must not be marred, so the piece is handled with gloves/cloth or soft tongs and set into padded, divided or interleaved containers, sometimes with orientation and count requirements for the next operation.

Wood, plastic or composite parts after hand sanding (furniture components, fiberglass/plastic housings): light but awkward, dusty station, parts stacked with spacers into carts, bins or dollies for finishing/assembly.

tasks.label: Clean brass particles from files by drawing file cards through file grooves.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Machine/fab shop bench: hand finisher filing brass or bronze parts stops when the file loads up, holds the file in one hand (or braces it on the bench) and draws a wire file card along the grooves in the direction of the tooth cut, several passes each side, inspects for remaining pins, resumes work. Standard flat/half-round mill files, cut 1-3.

Foundry / casting cleaning room or heavy fabrication finishing area: coarse files, rasps and riffler files loaded with soft-metal (brass, bronze, aluminum) debris after dressing castings or weld areas; vigorous carding at a bench near grinding stations, dusty environment, gloves and PPE, occasional tapping of the file to shed particles.

Jewelry, instrument, mold or die shop: fine needle, escapement and Swiss-pattern files (cut 4-6, very fine tooth pitch) pinned with brass/silver; cleaned with a fine file card or brass brush plus a pick/scorer to lift individual embedded pins out of single grooves without dulling or bending the delicate teeth.

Mid-job cleaning at the workstation while the workpiece stays clamped in the vise: worker pauses every minute or two of filing, cards the file two or three strokes and resumes; the file is never set down or transported, cleaning is interleaved with the filing cycle and must not disturb the setup.

End-of-shift or tool-crib maintenance: a set of assorted files (flat, round, half-round, rasps) is carded one after another, inspected for remaining pinning and worn teeth, wiped/chalked or lightly oiled, and racked for storage.

tasks.label: Weigh or measure materials, ingredients, or products to ensure conformance to requirements.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Weigh-up (dispensary) room of a food, feed, cosmetic or pharmaceutical plant: operator scoops minor/micro ingredients (spices, colors, additives, actives) out of sacks, drums and bins into tared bags or tubs on a bench scale to gram-level tolerances, checks the readout against the batch sheet, labels the kit with lot numbers and stages it for the mixer.

Bulk/major ingredient charging in a plant: operator brings 50-lb sacks, bulk bags or totes to a dump station or hopper scale, slits and empties them, watches the hopper/floor scale or silo weigh readout, tops off or removes material to hit the target weight, and records the verified weight for the batch record.

Liquid measurement in a chemical, coatings, adhesive or beverage plant: operator meters solvents, resins, syrup, water or colorant into a mix tank or portable vessel by pump/valve, verifying quantity on a flow meter, tank load cells or a scale/graduated vessel, and adds tint or additive to bring the batch to the recipe.

In-process and finished-batch conformance checks: operator draws a sample from the mixer, blender or line, and measures viscosity, density/specific gravity, moisture, pH, particle size or Brix on bench or at-line instruments, compares to the spec sheet, and either adjusts the batch or releases it.

Mobile/field mixing at a job site or customer site (volumetric concrete or grout mixer, on-site chemical or fertilizer blending rig): operator proportions cement, aggregate, water, admixtures or chemicals at the site from truck bins and drums, adjusting proportions to conditions and documenting the delivered mix.

tasks.label: Observe production or monitor equipment to ensure safe and efficient operation.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Chemical, coatings, adhesive or plastics-compounding plant: operator watches batch mixers/agitated vessels from an HMI and walks routine rounds through the process area — checking pump and agitator seals for leaks, motor/bearing temperature and noise, tank levels, local gauges, valve and lever positions — and reports or escalates anomalies. Fixed piping and process structure, controlled access.

Food, beverage or animal-feed blending plant: operator monitors continuous blending/mixing and packaging lines — flow and level readouts, conveyor and mixer condition, air leaks, product spills, hygiene and safety conditions on the floor — during a shift in a sanitary, institution-controlled facility with fixed layout.

Pharmaceutical, nutraceutical or cosmetics blending in a GMP-controlled production room: operator monitors V-blenders/high-shear mixers and liquid compounding vessels, verifies run parameters against the batch record, watches for dust escape, seal leaks, overheating or unusual noise, and logs observations. Gowned, cleanliness-controlled but human-scaled room.

Minerals/construction-materials or rubber plant (cement or dry-mix mill, concrete or asphalt batch plant, Banbury rubber mixer): operator monitors mills, mixers, hoppers, conveyors and dust collectors in a hot, dusty, noisy multi-level plant, watching for buildup, plugging, belt misalignment, overheating and spillage.

Hazardous-material blending (explosives/propellants, solvent-based inks or pigments, flammable chemicals): operator monitors mixing in classified/Ex-rated or barricaded areas, checking for leaks, static/heat build-up, gas or vapor release and equipment abnormality, with restricted occupancy and strict safety rules.

Close continuous attendance at a single mixer during critical batch steps in a small, lightly instrumented shop (small paint/ink toll blender, bakery or sauce kitchen): operator stands at the machine watching the mix through the hatch or sight glass, judging consistency, color and texture, listening for motor strain, and stopping or calling the batch the moment it foams over, lumps or binds.

tasks.label: Mix or blend ingredients by starting machines and mixing for specified times.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Food/beverage plant, in-line batch mixing: operator selects the recipe at an HMI on a fixed-vessel mixer (liquefier, kettle, ribbon blender, dough mixer) fed by piped liquids and conveyed/augered dry ingredients, starts the agitator, mixes for the recipe-specified time at set speed/temperature, watches for alarms, then discharges to the next stage.

Chemical/paint/coatings/adhesive/resin batch plant: operator charges fixed tanks via pumps and manual adds, starts a high-speed disperser or reactor agitator per the batch sheet, holds the specified mixing time at specified speed and temperature, pulls a sample for QC, and re-mixes or adjusts if the sample is off spec.

Pharmaceutical/nutraceutical/cosmetic GMP suite: gowned operator docks a bin/IBC on a tumble blender (or charges a V-blender or high-shear mixer), sets the specified number of revolutions or blend time and speed, starts the cycle, monitors, then undocks and signs the batch record.

Concrete/asphalt/dry-bulk batch plant: operator in the control booth calls up the mix design for the ticket and initiates the batch; aggregates, cement, water and admixtures are weighed and charged and the mixer runs the specified mixing time before discharging into the truck; operator watches slump/moisture feedback and re-runs or adds water as needed.

Rubber/plastics compounding or feed/pet-food mill: operator initiates an internal (Banbury) mixer or ribbon/paddle mixer cycle from a control station; the batch mixes to a specified time, temperature or power endpoint with ram-down stages, then dumps to the mill/extruder or next bin.

Small-batch or non-automated equipment on a human work floor (small bakery, specialty compounder, pilot/sample batches, or a portable agitator clamped to a tote or drum): operator starts the machine, times the mix by clock and eye, adjusts speed, and stops at a visual endpoint; equipment and layout vary and people work around the machine.

Smaller or older plant (specialty chemical, cosmetics, sauces, adhesives, ag chemicals): after judging the batch by viscosity cup, look/feel or a lab result, the operator physically walks the tank, closes manual butterfly/ball valves, couples a hose to a portable transfer pump or drum/tote filling head, primes it and starts the pump, watching for leaks and stopping at level.

Field or mobile mixing (grout, slurry, drilling fluid, on-site coatings or ag chemical mixing at a jobsite or plant yard): the batch is mixed in a portable mixer or tank, consistency judged by eye or a field test, then valves are opened and a pump started to move the mix to a tanker, hopper or point of use, over hoses run across the site in outdoor conditions.

instances.label: Food, beverage, pet-food or animal-feed plant: operator works a batch sheet, stages majors from silos/bulk bags and hand-weighs minor ingredients out of 25-50 lb sacks and totes at a scale, dumps them into the ribbon blender/mixer in the specified order, runs the mix cycle, pulls a sample and adjusts (e.g., moisture, seasoning) before discharge. Rubber, plastics or masterbatch compounding: operator assembles the cure package and fillers per compound recipe - carbon black, oils, sulfur, accelerators, pigments in gram-to-kilogram quantities from sacks and totes - and charges the Banbury internal mixer or extruder hopper in sequence; hot, dusty mixing room in a tire or rubber-goods plant.

Bench/lab-scale small-batch formulation inside a plant's lab or pilot area: making gram-scale trial or QC batches in vials, beakers and small jars per a written formula - weighing solids on an analytical balance, adding liquids, capping, agitating/dissolving, and handing off for test. tasks.label: Examine materials, ingredients, or products visually or with hands to ensure conformance to established standards.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In-process batch check at the mixer/blender on the production floor: operator pulls or observes a sample of the batch (powder blend, slurry, liquid, rubber compound), judges color, uniformity, lumps, viscosity/consistency against the batch standard, and decides to keep mixing, adjust, or release. Plant floor, standard equipment, institution-controlled.

Finished/blended product inspection before or during packing: visually scanning the discharged product stream or packed units for off-color material, defects, contamination or foreign matter, and pulling nonconforming product. Occurs at the discharge chute, conveyor, or packing station of a food, chemical, or pigment plant.

Incoming raw material and ingredient inspection at receiving/staging: checking bags, drums, totes or bulk deliveries for the correct material, damage, caking/clumping, off-color, moisture, or foreign matter before charging into the mixer. Warehouse/receiving bay of the plant.

Hands-on sensory examination: rubbing powder between fingers for grit or lumps, squeezing granulation or paste for moisture and tack, smelling material for off-odor, feeling temperature and texture of a compound — subjective judgments made by hand at the machine.

Visual check of material inside the process during the run: looking into an open mixer, hopper, ribbon blender or tank (sometimes from a platform or ladder) for unmixed streaks, dead spots, buildup, or a dropped foreign object, and reporting/removing what is found.

tasks.label: Tend accessory equipment, such as pumps or conveyors, to move materials or ingredients through production processes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Liquid-ingredient transfer in a chemical, paint, or beverage plant: operator lines up valves and starts/stops transfer pumps to move liquids from bulk tanks, totes or day tanks into the mixer, watches flow meters, tank levels and pressures at a local panel or DCS, trims pump speed, and switches to the standby pump on alarm.

Dry-ingredient conveying: operator charges hoppers by cutting open and dumping 25-50 kg sacks or discharging bulk bags, tends the screw/belt/pneumatic conveyors and feeders that carry powder to the blender, and corrects bridging or rat-holing in bins so flow to the mixer continues.

Flushing and washdown of transfer equipment between batches or at product changeover: circulating water/caustic through pumps, hoses and piping, rinsing hoppers and tanks, verifying the line is clear before the next recipe.

Fault clearing on accessory equipment: unplugging jammed chutes and clogged conveyors, poking out compacted material, cleaning pump strainers and filters, swapping worn hoses, gaskets and screens, cleaning up spills in the plant aisle.

Bulk transfer hookups at a loading rack or dock: connecting and disconnecting hoses/couplings to tanker trucks, rail cars, IBC totes and drums, opening hatches, grounding and purging, opening manual valves, then running the pump-down transfer to the storage tank or mixer.

Surveillance rounds along the transfer line in the plant: walking to pumps, motors and conveyors to check for leaks, overheating, unusual noise/vibration and belt mistracking, reading local gauges and sight glasses, logging readings and flagging problems for maintenance.

tasks.label: Transfer materials, supplies, or products between work areas, using moving equipment or hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Using a sit-down forklift or powered pallet jack, bring palletized raw ingredients (pallets of 50-lb sacks, drums of resin/pigment, cases of additives) from the receiving dock or warehouse racks to the staging spot beside the mixer; plant floor with shared aisles, pedestrian traffic, and a mix of pallet conditions.

Move blended output away from the mixer: palletized drums/pails, filled totes, or cases off the packout line, taken by pallet jack or lift truck to staging, warehouse racking, or the shipping dock inside the same plant.

Hand-carry or hand-truck individual sacks, boxes, and pails of ingredients from the staging pallet to the mixer charging platform (often up steps to a mezzanine), then slit and dump them into the mixer hopper.

Move palletized IBC totes, portable mix tanks, and wheeled bins/buggies of in-process material between mixing, holding, and filling areas of the plant, through doorways and sometimes on wet washdown floors.
Single-container handling with hand tools: use a drum truck or hoist to take one drum off a pallet, walk it to the mixer or a fill head, and position/tip it for decanting.
Errand-type transfers: fetch hand tools, cleaning supplies, spare parts, labels or empty containers from a crib or supply room, and carry sample cups of the batch across the plant to the QC lab.

tasks.label: Clean and maintain equipment, using hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Food/beverage plant: after a production run, the mixer operator washes down the blender/mixer, hoppers, chutes and surrounding surfaces — pre-rinse with a high-pressure hose, apply foam chemical, scrub/scrape stubborn product with brushes and hand scrapers, final rinse and sanitize; result verified by ATP swab. Wet, slippery, warm, plant controls access during the sanitation shift.

Batch-changeover cleanout of a mixing vessel/tank interior and agitator without major teardown: drain and flush, spray or solvent-wash the interior, scrape/brush caked product off walls, baffles and blades, wipe the lid and manway, dispose of rinsate. Typical in paint, coatings, adhesive, chemical and liquid-food batch plants.

Cleanout that requires hand-tool disassembly: using wrenches, sockets, hex keys and clamps, the operator removes agitator blades, screens/sieves, discharge valves, product hoses and gaskets, carries them to a wash sink/COP tank, scrubs them, then reinstalls with new gaskets and correct torque and checks for leaks before the next batch.

Scheduled preventive maintenance round with hand tools per checklist: grease bearings and seals, check and adjust belt/chain tension, change filters and screens, tighten loose fasteners, replace worn seals, packing or wear liners, top off gearbox oil, and log the work — judgment about wear and fit is part of the job.

Dry housekeeping of powder-handling blending equipment (pharma, plastics compounding, tobacco, dry food): vacuum and blow dust off ribbon blenders, bins, sifters and dust-collector housings with compressed air and industrial vacuums, wipe exterior surfaces, clear plugged chutes and screens, and sweep the area — no water permitted.

tasks.label: Dislodge and clear jammed materials or other items from machinery or equipment, using hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Coarse, visible blockage at an open bulk-solids transfer point feeding a batch mixer (concrete/asphalt batch plant, aggregate or feed mill): an oversized lump or clumped material bridging over a grate/bin opening; operator breaks it up with a bar or sledge from a platform, then restarts flow.

Powder, granular or sticky material bridged/packed inside an enclosed hopper, rotary airlock, or screw feeder serving a blender; operator locks out, opens an access door or poke port, and rods, hammers and scrapes in a confined, poorly visible space until flow is restored.

Caked or set product inside the mixer vessel, on ribbon/paddle agitator blades or at the discharge gate, stalling or overloading the machine; operator locks out, opens the cover, and chips/scrapes the buildup out with scraper, chisel and mallet before reassembly.

Foreign object or tramp material (bag scrap, glove, string, wood, bolt, hardened lump) wedged in the machine — screw conveyor, slide gate, screen, valve or mixer seal — usually requiring removal of a guard or access panel and pliers, pry bar and wrenches to extract it without damaging the equipment.

Jam in the ancillary conveying/packaging equipment on the blending line (bag packer, bucket elevator, drum/container filler, belt conveyor): jammed bags, cartons or containers pulled free with hand tools, misaligned parts reset, line restarted.

Plugged liquid transfer line, pump, strainer or spray nozzle in a liquid/paint/chemical blending system; operator isolates and drains, breaks unions or flanges with wrenches, rods and flushes the line or cleans the strainer, then reassembles and leak-checks.

tasks.label: Test samples of materials or products to ensure compliance with specifications, using test equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Paint/ink/adhesive or specialty-chemical blending plant: operator draws a sample from a batch mix tank (sample valve or dip cup), carries it to the in-plant QC bench, and runs viscosity (Brookfield/rheometer), weight-per-gallon/density, pH and fineness-of-grind or a color drawdown against a standard, logs results and passes or holds the batch.

Food/beverage blending operation: operator pulls a sample from the blend tank, syrup line or filler, tests Brix/density, alcohol, dissolved CO2/O2, pH and titratable acidity on at-line lab instruments, records against the recipe spec and signals adjustment or release.

Dry bulk / mineral / cement raw-mix / animal-feed blending: operator collects powder samples from the blender, belt or silo, then determines moisture, sieve residue or particle size, and chemical composition (e.g., XRF, Blaine fineness) in the plant process laboratory and feeds the result back to the blending set-points.

Plastics/rubber compounding: operator takes a sample of compound from the mixer or pelletizer and runs melt flow index, specific gravity, Shore hardness, dispersion or cure rheometry (MDR) on lab test equipment, comparing results with the customer specification.

Pharmaceutical, nutraceutical or cosmetic blending under GMP: operator takes thief/in-process samples from a powder blender or liquid mixing vessel, performs in-process checks (loss-on-drying moisture, pH, viscosity, appearance) or submits vials for assay, and documents every step in the batch record.

Concrete, asphalt or explosive-ingredient batch plant: operator tests fresh batches at or beside the mixer — slump/air content/temperature for ready-mix, or aggregate gradation and moisture — sometimes in an open-sided or outdoor batch-plant lab under variable weather.

tasks.label: Open valves to drain slurry from mixers into storage tanks.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Automated/DCS- or PLC-controlled batch plant (chemicals, coatings, food, beverage): at the end of a batch the operator confirms the destination storage tank has room and the route is lined up, initiates the discharge from an HMI, an actuated outlet valve drains the slurry from the mixer to the tank, and the operator watches level/flow, confirms the mixer is empty, closes the valve and runs a line flush.

Semi-automated plant floor: operator walks to the mixer, checks the destination tank and hose/pipe line-up, hand-operates a butterfly or knife-gate discharge valve (lever or handwheel) under the mixer, watches the slurry drain, throttles to avoid splash/overflow, then closes the valve and flushes the line.

Abrasive/viscous slurry service (mineral processing, ceramic slip house, pulp and paper stock prep, cement/lime): thick or settling slurry, valve seats pack with solids and outlets plug; operator opens a large knife-gate slowly, may rod or hose out the outlet, takes a sample, and manages residue and spills before closing.

Small-batch hygienic or hazardous production (food flavors, cosmetics, pharma, explosive/energetic slurries): mixer discharged through a sanitary or dedicated valve into a portable tote, drum or holding tank; operator connects and disconnects hoses, follows PPE/sanitation and grounding rules, samples, and cleans the valve after transfer.

Field/mobile mixing at a site taken as found (grout or bentonite plant at a construction or tunneling site, drilling-fluid mixing at a rig, mobile slurry unit): operator opens valves to drain mixed slurry from the mixer into agitated holding/storage tanks outdoors, in weather, with hoses and tanks positioned differently at each site.

roles.title: Cutters and Trimmers, Hand
roles.description: Use hand tools or hand-held power tools to cut and trim a variety of manufactured items, such as carpet, fabric, stone, glass, or rubber.

tasks.label: Mark or discard items with defects such as spots, stains, scars, snags, chips, scratches, or unacceptable shapes or finishes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Apparel/home-textile cutting room: worker inspects fabric as it is unrolled or spread on the cutting table, spots stains, holes, snags, slubs and shade bands, and chalks/tapes/stickers the flaw or pulls the flawed length out of the spread so cut panels avoid it. Standard rolls, indoor plant lighting, production pace.

Leather/hide cutting operation (auto seats, furniture, footwear): worker lays a whole hide on a lit table, judges natural scars, brands, insect bites, veins and grain flaws against grade rules, marks each with colored chalk/pen, and rejects hides that are unusable.

Molded rubber/plastic/foam parts bench: worker deflashes/trims parts and checks each for flash, chips, tears, short shots and surface blemishes, tossing bad parts in a scrap bin and setting borderline ones aside for rework, at press-side cycle rates.

Glass, mirror, tile or stone fabrication shop: worker checks cut lites, mirrors or slabs for chips, scratches, inclusions, bad edges or off-size shapes, grease-pencils the flaw location or moves the piece to the cullet/scrap rack.

Carpet, rug and upholstery goods shop: worker inspects carpet or upholstery web and cut pieces for stains, streaks, pile/high-low lines, snags and pattern faults, flags the flaw or rejects the piece before it goes out.

Paper, paperboard, film, label and printed-sheet converting: worker inspects sheets/blanks being hand-trimmed for spots, stains, scratches, misprints and ragged edges, marks the flaw with a slip/tape or throws the sheet into waste.

tasks.label: Separate materials or products according to size, weight, type, condition, color, or shade.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Plastics/rubber/foam/gasket or printed-goods plant: after deflashing or trimming at a bench or line, the worker culls parts with flash, tears, discoloration or bad edges and drops good pieces into labeled totes by size and type. Apparel/textile-product cutting room: after cutting plies, the worker separates cut panels and stacks into bundles by size and by shade lot (keeping same-dye-lot plies together), pulls miscut or flawed panels, and matches tickets. Limp fabric pieces on cutting tables and carts.

Separating usable material from scrap after cutting: pulling reusable remnants and offcuts back to stock and sorting waste into gaylords or bins by material type and color (e.g., PET vs. PVC film, foam vs. fabric, cullet by color) for recycling.

tasks.label: Fold or shape materials before or after cutting them.

instances.label: Apparel/home-textile cutting room: before cutting, the worker spreads and folds fabric off a roll into a multi-ply lay on the cutting table — folding face-to-face at each end, aligning selvages, smoothing wrinkles so the stack can be cut as one. Factory floor, standard tables, roll goods delivered on carts.

Same cutting room, after cutting: the worker picks cut panels of varied shapes and fabrics (knit, woven, slippery linings) off the table, folds them, and stacks/bundles them by size and shade for the sewing department. Pieces lie unfixtured in loose piles.

Soft-goods, shoe, upholstery or composites plant: the worker shapes a cut flexible piece — drapes fabric/prepreg/leather/foam over a form or into a mold, folds edges over a frame or into corners, tucks and creases before or after trimming excess. Bench or layup station inside the plant.

Glass, stone or tile shop: after cutting, the worker dresses and shapes the piece — seaming/grinding a cut glass edge, profiling or arrising a stone/tile edge — and turns or repositions the heavy piece on the bench or rack. Wet, dusty shop floor with standard equipment.

Rubber, plastic or foam sheet-goods plant: the worker bends, rolls or forms sheet and strip stock before or after cutting — wrapping a cut ply or strip around a form/drum, rolling or folding cut sheet, curling gasket stock — so it takes its finished shape.

Converting/packaging or rolled-goods area: the worker folds trimmed paperboard blanks or sheets into their finished form, or rolls/folds cut carpet, vinyl or padding lengths for finishing, binding and packing.
