tasks.label: Replace or sharpen dulled cutting tools such as saws.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Production floor of a carpet/fabric/foam/rubber plant: the hand cutter's utility knife, snap-off blade or rotary cutter has dulled mid-run. Worker retracts/unscrews the holder at the bench or on the cutting table, discards the old blade in a sharps bin, seats and locks a fresh blade, and test-cuts to confirm a clean edge.

Stone, glass or plastics fabrication shop: a hand-held power tool (circular saw, angle grinder cut-off wheel, jigsaw, oscillating multi-tool, wet-saw diamond blade) has a worn blade. Worker unplugs the tool, opens the guard, holds the arbor, loosens the nut with a wrench, seats the new blade on the flange in the correct rotation, torques the nut and runs a test cut.

Shop bench: worker restores the edge on a reusable hand cutting tool - trim knife, shears, scissors, hook blade or leather/glass knife - using a bench grinder, belt sander, whetstone or honing steel, holding the correct bevel angle, deburring, and checking sharpness by feel or a test cut on the material.

Shop tool room: worker sharpens or resets the teeth of a dulled circular saw or band saw blade with a file, tooth setter, or a bench sharpening machine (or mounts it on a sharpening machine), returning the blade to service on the plant's saw.

Plant maintenance of stationary equipment supporting the hand work: replacing a band saw blade (uncoil, thread through guides and wheels, tension and track), swapping a guillotine/shear knife or slitter knives, or changing die-press blades - heavy, awkward, sharp parts needing alignment and torque checks.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: replacing a dulled blade held by a flange/nut on a cutting spindle. It transfers because the physical act - detecting wear, unfastening, removing a thin circular blade, seating and torquing a fresh one, and verifying cut quality - matches the hand worker's blade swap, at finer precision, though on a machine-held rather than hand-held tool.

tasks.label: Adjust guides and stops to control depths and widths of cuts.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Apparel/textile cutting room: before cutting a spread or stack, the worker sets the guide bar/gauge and the blade depth (and notch depth) on the cutting equipment — straight knife, band knife, or die press — so parts are cut to the correct width and the knife penetrates the lay without scoring the table.

Print shop, bindery or board-converting plant: the worker positions the back gauge (stop) and sets clamp/cut settings on a guillotine or board cutter so trimmed sheets come out to a specified width, then re-sets the stop for each successive trim in the job.

Glass or stone fabrication shop: the worker sets guide rails/fences and depth stops on a cutting table or saw — score-wheel penetration for the glass thickness, blade drop depth for a slab — so the cut is to correct depth and the piece to correct width.

Rubber, foam or plastics plant: the worker sets fences, side guides and thickness/depth stops on splitting, skiving or slitting equipment (including repositioning slitter knife holders for new slit widths) at each product changeover.

On-site carpet, resilient flooring or countertop trimming: at a house or commercial jobsite the worker sets the depth guide/roller and width guide on a hand-held trimmer, loop-pile cutter, wall trimmer or laminate router so trims are cut to the wall line at the right depth over varying subfloor and substrate conditions.

tasks.label: Count or weigh and bundle items.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Apparel/soft-goods cutting room: after a spread is cut, the worker separates cut parts at a bundling table, counts plies per size/shade, ties or tapes each stack into a bundle, and attaches a numbered bundle ticket before it goes to sewing. Limp, similar-looking pieces of many shapes; mixed sizes on one table.

Small cut items in a fabricator (rubber gaskets, foam pads, plastic/leather blanks, cut trim): the worker counts a set quantity or weigh-counts on a bench scale, then bags, bands or boxes the batch and labels it with part number and count.

Paper, board and printed-goods trimming/finishing room: the worker counts trimmed sheets, labels, blanks or die-cut pieces into lifts of a set quantity and bands/straps each lift, stacking bundles on a skid.

Long or rigid cut stock (extruded rubber/plastic profile, cut glass strips, stone/tile pieces, moulding, cut metal trim): the worker counts pieces into a bundle, aligns them, straps or wires the bundle, and sometimes weighs it for shipping papers.

Heavy or awkward finished goods (cut carpet/vinyl rolls, large slabs, rolls of cut goods): the worker weighs the piece on a floor or conveyor scale, tags/labels it with weight and order data, and wraps or bands it for shipment.

tasks.label: Clean, treat, buff, or polish finished items, using grinders, brushes, chisels, and cleaning solutions and polishing materials.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Stone/solid-surface fabrication shop: after sawing a granite or quartz countertop, the worker hand-grinds and polishes cut edges and sink-cutout radii with a variable-speed wet polisher, chisels off chips, washes slurry off the slab and wipes/seals it before it goes on the delivery rack. Wet, dusty shop floor; parts on A-frames and benches.

Metal fabrication shop, machine shop or foundry: finished cut, stamped or cast parts are deburred with a die grinder and wire brush, parting-line flash is chiselled off, surfaces are buffed to a satin or bright finish on a wheel, then wiped or washed with cleaner before packing. Batches arrive on carts and benches.

Glass/mirror shop: edges of cut glass, mirror or tabletop pieces are seamed/ground and polished on a belt or wheel, chips stoned off, then the piece is washed with cleaning solution and wiped to a spot-free finish before crating.

Rubber, molded plastic or composite goods plant: residual flash, gates and whiskers on trimmed molded parts are chiselled/knifed off, parting lines buffed on a wheel or with abrasive brushes, and parts washed/blown clean before inspection.

Soft-goods plant (carpet, fabric, foam, leather): trimmed pieces are brushed and vacuumed free of loose fibers, lint and cutting dust, leather edges are buffed/burnished, and occasional marks are spot-cleaned with solution before the pieces move to sewing/packing.

Small decorative or craft items (jewelry findings, ceramic and art-glass pieces, turned wood, custom one-off ornamental parts): pieces are buffed and polished on wheels with compounds, detail-brushed into crevices, and cleaned in solution before final inspection. High mix, small lots, frequently novel shapes.

tasks.label: Route items to provide cutouts for parts, using portable routers, grinders, and hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Composite/FRP or molded plastic parts plant (aerospace, automotive, marine supplier): worker clamps a cured molded part (fender, panel, hatch, cowling) to a bench or trim jig and uses a portable router with a template plus a die grinder to cut access holes, slots and perimeter cutouts to print, then dresses edges.

Stone/quartz/solid-surface countertop fabrication shop: worker lays out a slab on a work table, cuts the sink, faucet and cooktop cutouts with a hand router/angle grinder and diamond bits, then grinds and polishes the cutout edges to a finished, chip-free result.

Millwork, sign, display or fixture shop working panel goods (plywood, MDF, laminate countertop, acrylic, HDPE): worker routes openings for sinks, outlets, hardware, glass or inlay pockets in flat panels using a portable router with jigs/templates and trims the edges.

Metal or hard-part fabrication shop: worker uses a die grinder, burr or portable router to open up notches and cutouts, relieve openings so mating parts fit, and dress burrs and slag from cut edges on fabricated or cast parts.

Soft/flexible goods plant (gasket, rubber, foam, felt, carpet, leather, insulation): worker cuts interior cutouts and holes for parts to pass through, using knives, hole cutters, routers on backed stock, and hand tools against patterns.

In-place fit-up work at a jobsite or on an already-assembled unit (installed countertop, laid carpet, finished RV/boat interior): worker cuts an opening in the item where it sits, scribing to the actual as-built condition with a portable router or grinder, working around finished surroundings.

tasks.label: Transport items to work or storage areas, using carts.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Apparel/textile cutting room: after cutting, the worker stacks bundles of cut parts, bins or boxes onto a rolling cart and wheels them from the cutting table to sewing lines, bundling stations, or WIP storage racks across a flat plant floor shared with people and forklifts.

Roll retrieval and delivery: worker fetches heavy rolls (fabric, vinyl, carpet, rubber sheeting) from storage racks onto a roll cart or A-frame, moves them to the cutting table/machine, and returns partial rolls and remnants to storage; loads 50-500+ lb, indoor plant aisles.

General manufacturing plant: moving totes, bins, or pallets of trimmed parts (gaskets, foam, plastic, rubber, small fabricated goods) on carts from the trim bench to inspection, finished-goods storage, or the shipping dock, in a plant with marked aisles and standard containers.

Glass fabrication / window plant: moving cut sheets and lites on A-frame or harp racks/carts between the cutting line, storage, and downstream stations; fragile heavy loads, fixed plant layout, aisle traffic.

Stone/countertop fabrication shop: moving slabs and cut tops on A-frame slab carts and dollies between the slab rack, the saw/CNC, polishing, and the staging area; wet gritty floors, very heavy fragile loads.

Small custom job shop (upholstery, awning, sign, framing, gasket shop): pushing a utility cart of assorted cut pieces, offcuts, and scrap through narrow cluttered aisles, past doorways and thresholds, sometimes out to a loading dock or truck; loads are irregular and hand-stacked.

instances.label: Food plant slicing/portioning line (deli meat, cheese, bacon, bread, potato products): operator watches output, pulls off-weight/torn/misshapen portions off the line and out of the slicer discharge, and readjusts slice thickness, gripper/feed and blade settings until portions hit target weight and appearance.

Paper/film/foil converting: slitter-rewinder or sheeter run where streaks, ragged slit edges or defective sheets appear; operator removes bad sheets/scrap from the machine and repositions slitting knives, blade penetration/side force, tension or register so output is in spec.

Plastics, rubber, foam or insulating-material cutting (rotary/flatbed die cutting, gasket cutting, cut-off saws): operator pulls miscut or out-of-register blanks from the machine and adjusts cut depth, register, length or feed until parts meet dimensional spec.

Flat glass cutting line: sheets with bubbles, inclusions, bad scores or chipped edges are taken off the line/cutting table to cullet, and cutting head pressure/speed, wheel and cutting layout are readjusted so subsequent plates cut clean.

Stone/tile/quartz slab sawing shop (bridge saw, sawjet): a slab section is cracked, chipped or the cut runs out of tolerance; operator lifts the bad piece off the saw table and readjusts blade height/feed rate/water or re-indexes the slab layout before recutting.

Jam, wrap or blockage: torn web wrapped around rollers, product stuck in the cutting head, broken glass or a lodged offcut inside the machine; operator stops and locks out the machine, reaches in to extract the material, then realigns/resets guides, knives or anvils and restarts.

instances.label: Food processing plant: after a product or pack-format changeover on a high-speed meat/cheese slicer or portioner, the operator starts the machine, runs the first portions, checks slice thickness, portion weight and stack presentation, and adjusts cutting gap, slice thickness, product throat/grippers and portion program until output is on spec.

Commercial print/packaging converting plant: after loading a job on a digital flatbed cutting table, roll sheeter, or web slitter-rewinder, the operator starts the machine, runs first sheets/first wraps, checks cut-through, cut length, slit widths and registration to printed marks, and adjusts tool depth, knife positions and cut length.

Glass fabrication plant or stone countertop shop: on a CNC glass cutting table, bridge saw or robotic sawjet, the operator starts the program, watches the first score/cut, checks piece dimensions and edge quality (chipping, score depth, blade drift), and adjusts cutting/grinding pressure, feed speed, blade offsets or table calibration.

Rubber, plastics, foam, cork or insulation plant: on a die-cutting press, clicker press or band-knife splitter, the operator starts the machine, checks first-piece die penetration, thickness and dimensions, and makes mechanical adjustments — shims/makeready under the die, stroke depth, clamp pressure, guide and roller settings.

Small job shop or short-run department with older manual/semi-automatic cutting machines (hand-fed slicers, small saws, cork/rubber cutters), frequent changeovers, mixed and variable stock; verification is by eye, feel and hand measurement, and adjustments are made with wrenches, handwheels and shims.

instances.label: Food processing plant (meat, cheese, bakery, produce): operator running a slicer/portioner pulls packs and portions from the line, weighs them on a bench or in-line scale against declared/target weight, checks slice thickness and count, and logs results; wet, cold, high-throughput line.

Stone, tile or solid-surface fabrication shop: operator at a bridge saw or waterjet checks cut slab pieces against a shop drawing or template with a tape measure, square and straightedge, and examines the natural material for chips, cracks, and acceptable surface/veining; pieces are moved by cart, A-frame rack or forklift in a dusty, variable shop.

Rubber, foam, cork, plastic sheet or insulation cutting: operator at a die cutter, waterjet, band-knife or panel saw removes cut blanks, gaskets, panels or blocks, separates them from scrap/skeleton, sorts by part number and stacks them on pallets, skids or in totes for further processing.

Small high-mix job shop / custom department: operator removes odd-sized cut pieces from the machine one-off or in small batches, hand-stacks them on carts or shelving with interleaving/protection, and wheels or carries them across the shop floor to a staging or storage area for the next operation. automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Type instructions on computer keyboards, push buttons to activate computer programs, or manually set cutting guides, clamps, and knives.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Bindery/print shop: operator at a programmable guillotine keys in or recalls the cutting program on the touchscreen/keyboard, sets backgauge dimensions and clamp pressure, and pushes buttons to run the cut sequence for a job of sheets. Indoor plant floor, standard machine, several job changes per shift.

Stone/glass/composite fabrication shop: operator loads or enters the nested cut program at the machine PC, sets clamps, vacuum cups or bridge guides for the slab, then pushes cycle start on the CNC saw/waterjet/cutting bridge. Slab sizes vary; shop floor with crane traffic.

Food processing plant slicing line: operator enters product recipe, slice thickness and portion count on the slicer HMI, sets product guides, hold-downs and blade gap at changeover, then starts the program. Wet, sanitary, cold environment; several changeovers per shift.

Converting/slitting operation (paper, film, rubber, foam, insulation): operator positions slitter knife holders, spacers and edge guides on the shafts to the order's widths, keys the job recipe into the line control, and starts the run. Plant floor; repeat and new width patterns.

Routine tending of a semi-automatic cutting machine (die cutter, cork/rubber/foam cutter, tobacco or board cutter) during a production run: pressing start/stop/cycle buttons on the machine's own panel, entering counts, acknowledging alarms and restarting the program. Fixed station on a plant floor.

tasks.label: Select and install machine components, such as cutting blades, rollers, and templates, according to specifications, using hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Roll-goods slitting line changeover (paper, film, foil, rubber, insulation, nonwovens) in a converting plant: operator locks out the slitter-rewinder, pulls dull circular top knives and bottom bands/anvil rings from the knife shafts with hex keys and spanners, mounts fresh blades, sets each holder to the order's width layout and overlap/penetration per the job spec, and re-guards the machine.

Food plant slicer/dicer/portioner blade change: on a high-speed loaf slicer, cheese slicer or dicing machine in a washdown production room, the operator removes guards and the blade head or knife spindle, installs the correct circular/involute blade, knife cross-cut spindle or impeller/knife set per the product spec with hand tools, sets gap/shim and clearance, and re-sanitizes before start-up.

Die/press cutting changeover for gaskets, foam, rubber, or paperboard: operator selects the steel-rule or rotary cutting die/template for the job, moves it into the press or die-cutting station, locates and clamps it to the bolster or die cylinder, and installs/changes associated rollers (anvil covers, feed and impression rolls) per the job specification.

CNC/digital cutting equipment setup (flatbed digital cutter, CNC router, foam/composite/leather/gasket cutting table): operator selects the specified blade module, drag/oscillating knife blade, or router bit for the material and thickness, installs and clamps it in the tool head, and initializes depth/offset before running the job.

Flat glass cutting line setup in a glass fabrication plant: operator selects and installs the cutting wheel of the correct angle/diameter for the glass thickness and coating in the cutting head, sets pressure and oil feed, and replaces worn wheels between jobs.

Stone/tile fabrication shop bridge-saw setup: operator selects the diamond blade of correct diameter, bond and segment type for the material, removes the guard and flange nut, mounts the heavy blade on the arbor with the correct rotation, torques the flange, and re-fits the guard before cutting slabs.

tasks.label: Position stock along cutting lines, or against stops on beds of scoring or cutting machines.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Commercial print/converting plant: operator takes lifts of printed sheets or board from a skid at the guillotine, joggs/squares the pile, and positions it against the back gauge and side stops on the cutter bed for a programmed cut sequence; frequent job changes, varied sheet sizes and stock weights.

Food processing plant (meat, cheese, poultry, produce): loading calibrated or uncalibrated logs of ham/sausage/cheese into the slicer feed bed, or aligning irregular fillets/blocks on the infeed of a portion cutter so cuts fall on the intended lines; cold, wet, hygienic-washdown conditions, high line speed.

Flat-glass fabrication shop: taking a float or laminated sheet off an A-frame/harp rack, laying it on the scoring table, and squaring it against the table's limit stops/reference edges before scoring and breakout; large fragile sheets, coated stock.

Stone/quartz countertop shop: placing a granite, marble or engineered-stone slab on the bridge saw or sawjet table, squaring it to the rails/stops and aligning the programmed cut lines to veining, cracks and defects for best yield; heavy, valuable, one-off material.

Foam, rubber and insulating-material converting plant: setting foam buns, rubber sheets or rigid insulation/composite boards on the bed of a contour cutter, splitter or digital knife table, positioning against stops or into the feed conveyor for the programmed cut; bulky, low-rigidity stock.

tasks.label: Monitor operation of cutting or slicing machines to detect malfunctions or to determine whether supplies need replenishment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Food plant high-speed slicing line (meat, cheese, bread): operator stands at the slicer/HMI watching for misfeeds, jams, smeared or out-of-spec slices, listens for blade chatter or drive noise, and watches how many product logs/loaves remain in the infeed magazine so a refill can be called for before the line starves. Output is a determination reported to the line lead or acted on later under other tasks.

Paper converting plant sheeter or roll slitter/rewinder: operator observes the running web and finished stacks for streaks, dust, ragged edges or wrinkles that signal dull knives or misalignment, watches the control panel alarms and drive load, and judges from the diminishing parent roll and tape/core stock when replenishment will be needed.

Glass or stone fabrication shop CNC saw/waterjet: operator watches the cutting head and workpiece for chipping, wander or stalling, monitors water pressure, coolant and abrasive garnet hopper levels, and notes when abrasive, coolant or blade segments are running low.

Rubber, plastic, foam or insulating-material die-cutting or cut-off station: operator monitors for material build-up on blades, gumming, dulling shown by rough edges, and tracks remaining stock rolls, interleaf paper or adhesive supply.

Tobacco, cork, or similar batch/continuous cutter in a processing plant: operator watches feed uniformity and cut length, listens and looks for jams or foreign material, and checks hopper/bin level to judge when the upstream supply must be replenished.

tasks.label: Feed stock into cutting machines, onto conveyors, or under cutting blades, by threading, guiding, pushing, or turning handwheels.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Plant floor: operator hand-feeds manageable-size rigid blanks/workpieces (board blanks, small panels, plate or plastic parts under ~20 kg) from a nearby rack, bin or pallet into a cutting machine — positioning each piece against the gauge/fence or into the feed nip and cycling the machine, in an aisle shared with other workers.

Plant/shop floor: operator loads full-size sheet stock (4x8 plywood/MDF, gypsum or insulation board, paperboard piles, glass lites, 25-70 kg) off a stack or A-frame onto a panel saw, cutting table or guillotine, squares it against the fence/side lay and pushes it under the blade; sheets sag, scratch easily and often need two hands.

Food processing plant (cold, wet, hygienic): operator loads meat/cheese logs, hams, bread loaves or produce onto the infeed conveyor or lift tray of a high-speed slicer/dicer, orienting deformable, slippery product and keeping the machine fed continuously through the shift.

Converting plant or metal service center: operator mounts a roll or coil (paper, film, rubber sheeting, textile, metal strip) on the unwind and threads the web/strip through rollers, guides, tension stand and slitter knives to the rewind, splicing and tensioning before running; repeated at every roll change.

Stone/glass shop: operator moves a heavy slab (granite/quartz slab or large glass lite) from an A-frame rack to the bridge-saw or cutting table using vacuum lifter, jib or overhead crane, lands and aligns it on the table, and positions it under the blade before cutting.

Smaller cutting/slicing machine in a plant or job shop: operator feeds continuous or irregular stock — extruded rubber profile, hose, tubing, cork, foam block, gasket sheet, insulation — into the feed rollers or under the blade, guiding by hand and turning handwheels/cranks to advance the stock to the cut mark.

tasks.label: Move stock or scrap to and from machines manually, or by using carts, handtrucks, or lift trucks.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Plant floor of a converting/fabrication shop: operator uses a powered pallet jack, walkie stacker, or sit-down lift truck to bring pallets or skids of raw stock (paper board, rubber sheet, foam bun, cork, insulation, packaged food) from the storage rack or staging lane to the cutting/slicing machine, and to haul away pallets of cut output, moving through aisles shared with people and other trucks.

Roll/reel work in paper converting, film, textile, or rubber slitting: a parent reel or coil is brought from the roll storage area to the machine's unwind stand using a clamp truck, shaft cart, or hoist, mounted, and after the run the partially used reel, spent core, or butt roll is taken back out and returned to storage or the core scrap area.

Repetitive hand loading at a fixed station: operator lifts individual uniform pieces of stock (sheet stacks, boards, blanks, cartons, blocks) off a nearby cart, pallet, or rack and sets them on the cutting machine's infeed table or gauge, then takes the cut pieces off the outfeed and stacks them on a pallet or cart beside the machine.

Ad hoc manual handling of awkward or irregular stock: mixed sizes and part-used remnants, limp or oversized sheets, odd-shaped stone or glass pieces, drums and bundles moved with a two-wheel hand truck through tight aisles and around other equipment; the operator judges grip points, orientation, and route each time.

Scrap handling at the machine: the operator swaps the full trim/offcut gaylord, wire basket, or scrap cart sitting at the machine's drop chute for an empty one and hauls the full container across the plant to the baler, chip hopper, or scrap staging area, then returns the empty.

tasks.label: Change or replace saw blades, cables, cutter heads, and grinding wheels, using hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Replacing a worn spindle-mounted circular saw blade on a production cutting machine on the plant floor — a stone bridge/tile saw, board or insulation panel saw, tissue log saw, or food circular saw. Worker locks out the machine, opens the guard, breaks the arbor nut with a wrench, lifts off flange and old blade, seats the new blade, torques the nut, re-checks runout and restarts.

Replacing an endless band blade or band knife — meat/bone band saw in a food plant, band knife on a foam or insulation splitter, metal or stone band saw. Worker releases tension, unthreads the old loop from the wheels, threads and seats the new band through guides, sets tracking and tension, closes guards, test-runs.

Changing spindle-mounted cutter heads / tool heads on a CNC router, profiler, edge or contour machine used for stone, glass, foam or insulation — pulling the worn head or tooling from the spindle, mounting the replacement, setting projection/offsets and verifying the first cut.

Replacing bolted knife sets or a rotor cutter head assembly on a granulator, dicer, shredder, tobacco cutter, or rotary die — unbolting several heavy, sharp knives with hand tools, cleaning seats, fitting new knives, shimming and gapping to the bed knife, torquing to spec.

Replacing a grinding or polishing wheel — machine-mounted sharpening wheels on a slicer or log saw, diamond cup wheels on a stone/glass edge machine, or a bench/pedestal wheel. Worker inspects and ring-tests the wheel, removes flange nut with hand tools, mounts and centers the new wheel, torques, dresses and test-spins it.

Replacing the cutting cable on a wire saw — diamond wire on a stone quarry bench saw or slab shop wire saw, or wire on a foam/insulation wire cutter. Worker cuts out the failed loop, joins/crimps or splices a new length, routes it over the flywheels and pulleys, and tensions it, often outdoors in a quarry or yard.

tasks.label: Clean and lubricate cutting machines, conveyors, blades, saws, or knives, using steam hoses, scrapers, brushes, or oil cans.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Food processing plant (meat/poultry/cheese/bakery): end-of-run deep clean of a slicer, dicer or portioner and its infeed/outfeed belts — lock out, disassemble blade heads, guards and belt sections, scrape fat/dough/product residue with plastic scrapers, hot-water/steam hose and foam, detail-brush, rinse and sanitize, reassemble, then apply food-grade lubricant to blade shafts, chains and bearings.

Food/beverage plant sanitation shift: open-plant hose work over the slicing line — pre-rinse, apply foam chemical, rinse and sanitize machine exteriors, frames, guards, conveyor belts and the surrounding floor and drains; no disassembly, no lubrication.

Paper, plastics, textile or converting plant: cleaning a slitter, sheeter, guillotine or die-cutter — vacuum/blow out paper dust and trim scrap, wipe blade edges and knife bed with solvent rags, scrape adhesive and gum residue, then oil the knife bar and grease roller/conveyor bearings and drive chains with oil can and grease gun.

Stone, glass or tile fabrication shop: flushing slurry, sludge and cuttings out of the saw bed, splash guards, coolant tank and conveyor with a hose, scraping hardened slurry, clearing coolant nozzles and the blade, then greasing rails, bearings and lead screws.

Sawmill, wood, rubber, cork or insulation plant: blowing/vacuuming sawdust and fibre off saws, guides and conveyors, scraping pitch, resin or rubber buildup from blades, rollers and belts with scrapers and brushes, and oiling chains, guides and bearings with an oil can or grease gun in a hot, dusty, wide-area machine environment.

tasks.label: Set up, operate, or tend machines that cut or slice materials, such as glass, stone, cork, rubber, tobacco, food, paper, or insulating material.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Food processing plant: setting up and tending a high-speed slicing/portioning line (ham, sausage, cheese logs, poultry fillets, bread). Worker loads logs/product onto infeed, selects product recipe and thickness/portion weight, watches weight checks and shingling, clears jams, changes blades, runs changeovers, and hands off to packaging. Indoor, sanitary, institution-controlled plant with fixed line layout.

Paper/board converting or printing plant: operating a sheeter, slitter-rewinder, or programmable guillotine. Worker mounts jumbo reels on the unwind, threads the web, sets slitter knife positions and sheet length, runs the job, monitors edge quality and splices, and unloads finished stacks/rolls onto pallets. Fixed layout, standard equipment.

Flat glass fabrication shop: operating a cutting table/line. Worker loads float or laminated lites from racks or an automatic loader, runs the optimized cut pattern, breaks out sub-plates, snaps and separates pieces, handles remnants back to storage, and racks finished lites. Institution-controlled shop floor.

Stone/countertop fabrication shop: operating a bridge saw or sawjet. Worker loads a granite/quartz slab with a vacuum lifter or crane, aligns and digitizes the layout around veining/defects, programs and runs cuts, then unloads cut parts to carts. Wet, dusty, but fixed-layout shop.

Rubber, foam, cork, or insulating-material plant: die cutting, splitting, or CNC flatbed cutting of gaskets, foam blocks, insulation board, or cork sheet. Worker loads sheet/roll stock, sets tooling and depth, runs the nest, and removes cut parts and waste skeleton. Indoor plant with standard equipment.

Small job shop or specialty cutting operation with frequent changeovers across mixed materials and short runs (plastics, composites, textiles, leather, tobacco leaf, miscellaneous board). Worker sets up tooling and program for each job, makes trial cuts, checks dimensions against the spec, and adjusts. Institution-controlled shop, but jobs vary constantly.

instances.label: Abrasive waterjet cutting stone, glass, tile or metal in a fabrication/job shop: operator monitors garnet level, lifts 50-lb bags (or bulk sacks) and tops off the cutting-head hopper, and checks abrasive flow rate so cutting speed and edge quality hold during the job.

Loose-abrasive machines in a stone/glass/semiconductor plant — granite gang saw (steel shot + lime slurry), slurry wire saw, lapping/honing plate, glass edger: operator mixes and replenishes abrasive slurry, checks grit concentration and flow to the cut zone, and adds fresh abrasive when the cut rate falls off.

Abrasive-media cutting machines (abrasive cut-off saws, abrasive belt/disc cutters) in rubber, insulation, composite or metal shops: when cutting slows the operator replaces or replenishes the worn abrasive wheel, belt or disc and restores feed/speed.

Drive-belt tension on a slicing/cutting machine in a food, paper, tobacco or cork plant: lock out the machine, open the guard, loosen motor-mount bolts, shift the motor, gauge V-belt tension, retighten to torque, refit the guard and verify blade speed.

A loose or slipping sheave/pulley on a saw, slitter or grinder in a glass, stone or paper plant: operator tightens set screws or a taper-lock bushing, realigns the sheaves, and re-checks blade/belt speed, often in a dusty or wet area with limited access.

instances.label: Paper/paperboard/tissue converting plant or mill winder room: operator sets up a slitter-rewinder for the next order — sliding shear knife holders along the knife beam to the ordered slit widths using gauge/setting blocks or a rule, setting blade overlap and side load so blades run true, and locking each holder in place before the run.

Plastic film, foil, tape, nonwoven or thin rubber converting line: operator changes blade spacing on a shear/score slitting station or on a shaft of circular knives and spacer rings, checks that blades run level in the counter-roll grooves, and clamps/locks the knives before restarting the web.

Food or tobacco plant: operator rebuilds a multi-blade cutting head or blade frame — threading band blades into a bread-slicer frame with spacers and tensioning wedges, mounting cheese/loaf blades or wires in a frame, or setting knives in a dicer/tobacco cutter head — then levels and secures each blade before sanitation and start-up.

Other specialty multi-blade setups: cork slab and gasket splitters, foam/insulation board multi-saw trim lines, glass or fiber board gang cutters — operator fits blades and spacer collars or gauge blocks on shafts or in a blade frame, aligns and levels them, and drives wedges or tightens clamps to secure them.

instances.label: Food plant (meat, cheese, bakery): operator pulls the dull circular/sickle slicer blade or hand knife out of service and sharpens/hones it at the sharpening bench or grinding machine in the plant's blade room, then reinstalls it. Sawmill, pallet plant or woodworking shop filing room: operator sharpens carbide-tipped circular saw blades and band saw blades on a bench grinder/saw sharpener, tooth by tooth, restoring face and top angles; blades vary in diameter, pitch and tooth count.

Paper converting, printing or plastics plant: operator regrinds or hones straight machine knives (guillotine/trim knives, slitter knives, granulator blades) on a knife grinder with a magnetic bed, or touches up the bevel with a hone before reinstalling and setting the knife.

Mid-shift touch-up on the production floor: operator notices dull or nicked edges (streaky cuts, tearing), stops the machine and dresses the blade edge in place with a file or honing stone or a small hand grinder, then restarts and checks cut quality.

Miscellaneous standard blades in rubber, cork, foam, insulation, textile or stone/glass shops: circular knives, band-knife blades and counter-knives sharpened on a bench grinder or honing stone at a maintenance bench between runs.

One-off or irregular cutting tools: an odd-shaped, worn or shop-modified blade, punch, scraper or steel-rule die with no standard profile, freehand-ground on a pedestal grinder and finished on a honing stone by eye and feel.

tasks.label: Turn cranks or press buttons to activate winches that move cars under sawing cables or saw frames.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Large modern stone plant, multiwire diamond-wire block saw: the block, already craned onto the block-carrier trolley, must be run into the cutting zone under the wire array; operator presses console buttons to drive the motorized trolley in, stops it on position, and runs it back out after the drop. Indoor, machine foundation and dedicated rails.

Traditional gang saw / frame saw in a dimension-stone mill (marble, Indiana limestone, granite): operator turns a crank or presses buttons on a winch control to draw the loaded block car along floor rails into the saw pit or onto the lifting platform, jogging it to a painted stop mark by eye, then withdraws it after the cut. Older mill floor with overhead cranes, slurry, and people walking by.

Small monument/memorial or curb shop: a hand-crank winch, come-along, or pendant-controlled hoist pulls a cart carrying a stone under a slab saw or wire; the cart is chocked, the stone is eyeballed against the blade line, rigging is adjusted by hand. Non-standard block sizes and improvised setups.

Non-stone block cutting (foam, insulation, cork, rubber, board stock): a cart or table carrying the block is moved under a saw frame, band knife, or wire by button control; repeat passes for each slice, with the table reversing between cuts. Indoor machine line.

Exception handling during positioning: the car jams or derails on a worn rail, the block shifts or rocks on the car, or the cable/wire binds; the operator jogs the winch back and forth, re-wedges and re-chocks the block, re-rigs slings, checks clearance to the frame, then resumes.

Open-air or open-sided saw shed at a quarry-side mill or block yard: the car runs on track laid on a slab exposed to weather, mud, and stone chips; the operator winches the loaded car under a wire saw or frame with the winch crank/control at the trackside.

roles.description: Set up, operate, or tend machines, such as glass-forming machines, plodder machines, and tuber machines, to shape and form products such as glassware, food, rubber, soap, brick, tile, clay, wax, tobacco, or cosmetics.

tasks.label: Adjust machine components to regulate speeds, pressures, and temperatures, and amounts, dimensions, and flow of materials or ingredients.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Plastics/rubber extrusion line (pipe, tubing, profile, film, sheet) running production: operator watches gauge/dimension readings and trims screw rpm, barrel and die zone temperatures, melt pressure, haul-off/line speed and feed rates to hold wall thickness, diameter and output on spec. Plant floor, machine accessible from walkways.

Hands-on mechanical adjustment of machine components with hand tools during start-up, a run, or a size change: turning die-lip/profile bolts, centering the die, setting air-ring or calibrator gaps, repositioning cutters/knives, guide rails, roller clearances and hopper slide gates, judged by feel and sample measurement, often hot and cramped.

Glass container hot end (IS forming machine): adjusting gob weight and length (tube height, plunger/needle), shear and machine timing, blank/plunger cooling air, and blowing pressures to keep container weight, thickness distribution and defect rate on target; hot, noisy, but institution-controlled plant.

Tablet/powder compaction press (pharma, confectionery, catalyst, detergent tabs): setting and trimming fill depth/dosing cam, pre- and main-compression force, turret speed and feeder speed to hold tablet weight, thickness and hardness within limits during a batch, in a controlled production suite.

Food extrusion/forming (pet food, snacks, cereal, soap plodder-type continuous formers): adjusting screw speed, water and steam addition, preconditioner ratios, back-pressure/die restriction, knife speed and barrel temperatures to hold density, moisture, piece size and rate, with periodic sampling and weighing.

tasks.label: Clear jams, and remove defective or substandard materials or products.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Culling defective finished units off the machine's output line: operator watches formed products moving past on a conveyor or accumulation table in a brick, tile, glass, soap, wax or plastics plant and pulls out chipped, misshapen, cracked, discolored or off-dimension pieces into a scrap or rework bin, at line speed.

Removing defective or substandard input material at the machine's feed: pulling contaminated lumps, foreign objects, cured scrap or off-spec batch material out of hoppers, feed belts and melt streams, and purging off-spec extrudate at start-up or after a grade change, before it reaches the forming die.

Clearing a jam inside the forming machine itself: stopping and locking out the extruder, press or plodder, opening guards, prying out a workpiece wedged in the die, mold or tooling, scraping hardened material off surfaces, checking for tool damage, then restarting and verifying first pieces.

Clearing a hot or hazardous jam on a glass-forming or hot-press line: stuck or down ware on the dead plate/take-out, a gob hung in the delivery, or a jammed section, cleared with tongs and heat protection while the machine runs or a section is off.

Clearing a bulk-material blockage at a feed point: bridged clay, powder, pellets or aggregate in a hopper or chute, or an oversize lump plugging a feed opening, broken up and freed with bar, hammer or poker so material flow resumes.

Clearing a pile-up jam of formed product at a conveyor transfer, accumulation table or downstream station: toppled bottles, stacked-up bricks or tangled parts pulled apart and re-oriented or scrapped by hand so the line can restart.

GMP suite or controlled press room.

Non-instrumented setup and troubleshooting tweaks on any of these machines: operator walks the machine, cracks a hand needle valve feeding one cooling nozzle, tweaks a manual filter-regulator knob, re-aims a coolant line, or bleeds a vacuum line, judging the amount by sight, sound and feel of the product; controls scattered on, behind and under the machine with no sensor on that variable.

tasks.label: Clean dies, arbors, compression chambers, and molds, using swabs, sponges, or air hoses.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Rubber goods plant: at a product/compound changeover the tuber or extruder head is opened and the die plate, mandrel/arbor and breaker plate — still hot and caked with scorched or cured elastomer — are scraped, brass-brushed, solvent-swabbed and blown out with an air hose until the land and pin holes are clear.

Glass container plant: operator swabs the blank molds, neck rings and plungers of a running IS machine section on a fixed interval — applying/wiping graphite-bearing swab oil into hot mold cavities and blowing off excess — with the machine at temperature and the section either on the fly or briefly stopped.

Rubber molded-goods / tire plant: a curing or compression mold is taken out of the press and its cavity, sipes, engravings and vent holes are cleaned of vulcanization residue and release agent with air hoses, picks, brushes or blasting before the mold goes back into service.

Food, pet-food, soap or cosmetics plant: plodder/extruder dies, nozzle inserts, spacer plates and the compression chamber/barrel end are dismantled at a changeover or end of run and washed free of dough, paste, soap or fat with sponges, brushes, hot water and air, to sanitation-standard cleanliness including fine die holes.

Pharmaceutical/nutraceutical or powder-compaction plant: between batches the tablet press compression chamber (turret bore, feed frame, cams) plus punches and dies are vacuumed, swabbed with solvent-dampened wipes, washed and dried to a validated cleaning standard, with residue/cross-contamination limits and cleaning documentation.

Brick, tile, refractory or heavy-clay plant: the extruder die, lubrication box and auger nose, or a dry-press mold, are cleaned of stiff clay/body slip and dust build-up with scrapers, water hose, sponges and air hoses in a dusty, wet, hot area of the plant.

tasks.label: Synchronize speeds of sections of machines when producing products involving several steps or processes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Modern plastics/rubber extrusion line in a pipe, tube, profile, or wire-and-cable plant: operator matches extruder screw speed with the calibration/cooling section, cleated puller/haul-off, cutter, and take-up reel so wall thickness, diameter and cut length hold; ratios re-trimmed on grade changes, spool changes and speed ramps.

Food, soap, or tobacco forming line: operator matches the extruder/plodder output to the die-face or guillotine cutter, transfer conveyor, and downstream stamper/former so pieces are correct length and weight and do not back up or stretch between sections.

Sheet, film, or web line (cast sheet with roll stack and cooling rolls, calender, laminator/coater): operator sets and trims relative speeds of nip rolls, pull rolls and winder, and the draw/tension between them, to avoid stretching, sagging or wrinkling the web.

Clay/brick/tile extrusion or glass forming: operator synchronizes the de-airing auger extruder column speed to the wire cutter and setting conveyor, or the glass feeder/gob delivery to the forming machine sections, takeout and cross conveyor timing.

Older, mechanically coupled line where sections are not electronically linked: operator changes sheaves/change gears, adjusts variable-speed variator handwheels or potentiometers, and trims sections by eye and feel (watching sag, loop, or tension) while walking the line during start-up and running.

tasks.label: Move materials, supplies, components, and finished products between storage and work areas, using work aids such as racks, hoists, and handtrucks.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Plant floor / attached warehouse: operator moves pallet-loads of raw input (resin or compound sacks, clay body, soap base, powder, rubber slabs, batch containers) from racked or floor storage to the machine's feed area with a powered pallet jack or forklift, then returns the empty pallet. Marked aisles, standard pallets, other workers and lift trucks present.

Machine output to staging/storage: operator moves finished or in-process product away from the extruder/press (A-frame racks of glass, racks of green brick or tile, totes and gaylords of extruded parts, cartons of soap or cosmetics) to a QA area, staging lane, or storage rack using pallet jack, cart, or rack, repeatedly while the machine runs.

Supply replenishment in standard containers: operator fetches boxes, totes, cases, spools, or bagged additives from a stores area or supermarket rack and delivers them on a handtruck or cart to the machine work area, setting them down at the workstation.

Ad-hoc odd-item fetching: partially used bags, drums of lubricant, loose tooling, scrap bins, sample trays, cleaning supplies carried by hand or handtruck through congested aisles between mixed storage shelves and the machine, with no standard container or fixed location.

Heavy tooling moves: dies, molds, extrusion heads, calender rolls, screens, or mixer parts moved between the tool crib/die storage and the machine using an overhead bridge crane, jib hoist, or die cart - rigging, lifting hundreds to thousands of pounds, and setting the tool onto the machine mount.

Dock and yard moves: unloading incoming pallets/cases from trailers at the plant dock, moving material between buildings or to an outdoor storage yard (brick/tile packs, drums, cullet), and loading finished product back onto trucks, in dock and yard traffic.

tasks.label: Activate machines to shape or form products, such as candy bars, light bulbs, balloons, or insulation panels.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Plastics/rubber plant: operator at an injection-molding, extrusion or blow-molding machine engages the start/cycle controls on the machine's HMI or pushbutton panel to begin forming parts, restarting the cycle after each load/unload or after a short stoppage, and watching the first shots to confirm good product.

Food/confectionery plant: operator activates a depositing, moulding or dough-forming line (candy bars, bars/pieces, extruded snack) from a washdown-rated control panel after sanitation/setup checks, ramps the line up and keeps it running through the shift.

Heavy press/compacting work: operator positions material or a die-loaded tray at a brick/tile press, insulation-panel press, powder-compacting or rubber-molding press and actuates the press each cycle with two-hand controls, a foot pedal or a start button on a guarded machine.

Glass forming plant: operator starts and runs a hot-end forming machine (IS machine for containers, bulb/ribbon or press machine for glassware) from the machine's control station, engaging sections and restarting after jams or job changes in hot, dirty conditions.

Small shop or batch operation (soap plodder, wax/candle molding, cosmetics presser, balloon dipping, small clay/tobacco machine): operator engages older equipment with mechanical levers, clutch pedals or simple switches, with frequent product changeovers and hand-fed material.

tasks.label: Select and install machine components, such as dies, molds, and cutters, according to specifications, using hand tools and measuring devices.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Food/soap/wax extruder or plodder changeover: operator selects the specified die plate and cutter knife for the next product, unbolts and removes the old die head assembly, cleans product residue, installs and centers the new die plate, sets the knife clearance with feeler gauges, and torques fasteners; sanitary plant, warm sticky product, tooling weighs tens of kg.

Heavy die/mold set change on a hydraulic forming or compacting press for brick, tile, refractory or clay products: die set of hundreds to thousands of kg moved with hoist/cart, located on the bolster, shimmed and clamped, height and parallelism checked with gauges before trial pressing.

Glass-forming (IS) machine job change: swapping blank molds, blow molds, neck rings, baffles, funnels, plungers and take-out tooling per the job spec on a hot multi-section machine, with alignment and clearance checks; dozens of hot cast-iron parts, done under production pressure.

Rubber/tuber extruder die head and die plate change (tread tuber, hose, profile): hot heavy die head unbolted, purged of cured rubber, new die/preformer selected and installed, heating/coolant lines reconnected, die gap and concentricity measured.

Tooling change on a compacting/tablet/briquette press: selecting punches and dies per the specification sheet, installing them in the turret or tool holder, cleaning the tooling and powder-feed assembly, setting fill depth and checking punch length/die dimensions with micrometers.

Small cutter, blade or insert change and adjustment on a forming line (pelletizer knives, wire cutters, tobacco/soap/wax cutters, small stamping inserts): select correct cutter, mount in holder with hand tools, set gap and alignment with gauges, test run.

instances.label: Routine in-process product sample at the machine: at a scheduled interval the operator pulls a few finished units off the running line (soap bars from a plodder, tablets from a press, extruded profile cut, tile or brick, cosmetic sticks), marks them with machine/lot/time and walks them to the plant QC lab window or sample drop station a short distance away.

Hot or hazardous sample: the operator uses tongs, a knife or a cutter to take a sample of hot or semi-molten product at the forming machine (glass ware off the forming machine or lehr, hot extrudate, heated rubber compound), lets it cool or quenches it, then carries it to the on-site laboratory.

Bulk, granular or paste material sample: the operator draws a scoop of mix, powder, slip, dough or compound from a hopper, chute or extruder purge into a labeled container or bag and dispatches it to the plant laboratory by hand-carry or via a sample station/pneumatic tube.

Shift batch: the operator accumulates samples from several machines and lots through the shift in a rack or tote, labels and records each with lot data, loads them on a cart and delivers them to the on-site lab, signing them in on the lab log or LIMS terminal.

External laboratory shipment: a sample is bagged and sealed, packed in a box with a completed test-request or chain-of-custody form, addressed, and left at shipping/receiving for courier pickup to an off-site contract lab.

Non-routine investigation sample: after a defect run, customer complaint or process upset the operator selects specific atypical pieces from the line, a reject bin or a finished pallet, notes the problem and its origin, and sends them to the lab with that description.

tasks.label: Couple air and gas lines to machines to maintain plasticity of material and to regulate solidification of final products.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Plant floor of a plastics/rubber/soap extrusion or pressing shop at start-up or changeover: operator takes a standard compressed-air hose from a reel or wall drop, mates a push/pull quick-disconnect coupler to the nipple on the machine frame at accessible height, opens the ball valve and confirms line pressure on the gauge.

Glass-forming (IS/press-and-blow) machine: operator couples several cooling/blowing and settle-blow air hoses to a mold section or blank-side manifold, routing hoses in a hot, cramped, oily section, clamping them clear of moving mechanisms, then verifying air flow so the parison cools and solidifies correctly.

Burner/heater gas supply on a kiln, annealing lehr, curing oven or torch head serving a brick, tile, clay or glass forming line: operator connects a fuel-gas (natural gas/propane) line with threaded or flanged fittings, wrench-tightens with sealant, opens the manual shutoff, leak-checks with soap solution or a sniffer, and sets the regulator.

Die/head changeover on a rubber tuber, clay auger extruder or soap plodder: after the die, mandrel or barrel jacket is swapped, operator reconnects air (and sometimes steam/gas) lines to the head and jacket ports located behind or beneath the machine, working in awkward reach around hot surfaces, then pressurizes and checks for leaks before restarting.

Mid-run trouble: line pressure drops or a hiss is heard; operator traces the air/gas hose, finds a chafed hose, cracked fitting or failed gasket/O-ring, isolates the supply, replaces the part or swaps the hose, re-couples it and re-tests before resuming production.

tasks.label: Pour, scoop, or dump specified ingredients, metal assemblies, or mixtures into sections of machine prior to starting machines.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Charging a forming/extruding machine's feed hopper with bulk dry raw material at the start of a ...: slitting and dumping 25-50 kg sacks, or tipping totes/drums, of clay body, soap noodles, rubber or plastic compound, ceramic or metal powder from a pallet parked beside the machine. Dusty plant floor, forklift traffic, repeated through the shift.

Weighing and scooping measured secondary ingredients per a batch/recipe sheet (pigment, additive, flavoring, wax, cosmetic base, binder) from drums or bins and pouring them into the machine's charging or mixing section before start-up; several ingredients per batch, weights checked on a scale.

Placing metal assemblies or inserts (stamped terminals, lead frames, sheet-metal blanks, screens, bushings) into the cavities/fixture sections of a press or mold before the machine is cycled; parts arrive in racks, bins or trays; placement tolerance of a few millimetres, misplacement risks tool damage.

Depositing a measured charge of sticky, deformable mixture (rubber preform or slug, dough or clay charge, soft wax, soap billet) into each cavity of a multi-cavity mold or press section before closing and starting the press.

Small-batch, high-mix operation (specialty ceramics, candles, soap, cosmetics, artisanal food): short runs with frequent recipe and tooling changeovers, materials in assorted buckets, drums and bags staged around the machine, operator hand-scoops and pours varying quantities into the machine before each run.

tasks.label: Measure, mix, cut, shape, soften, and join materials and ingredients, such as powder, cornmeal, or rubber to prepare them for machine processing.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Food/feed extrusion plant (snacks, breakfast cereal, pasta, pet food): operator pulls 50-lb bags of cornmeal, flour, starch and minor powders from pallets, slits and dumps them into a mixer or hopper, weighs minor ingredients on a bench scale, adds water/oil, blends the batch to recipe and charges the extruder feed hopper. Indoor plant batching room, dusty, recipe changes between runs.

Rubber goods / tire plant mixing room and extruder (tuber) feed: cut raw rubber bales and slabs into charge-sized pieces, weigh polymers, carbon black, oils and small chemicals to the batch recipe, charge the internal mixer, then warm/soften stock on a mill and cut and splice strip stock to feed the extruder. Heavy, sticky, hot material; institution-controlled plant floor.

Structural clay / brick / tile / refractory plant: proportion clay, shale, sand, grog and water/additives, feed box feeders, mix and de-air the body in a double-shaft mixer/pug mill to the right consistency, and deliver plastic clay to the extruder, cutting the extruded column to length. Abrasive, wet material; moisture judged by feel/sensor.

Soap, wax, or cosmetics plant: weigh out a batch of soap noodles or wax base, dose perfume, colour and additives, mix in the amalgamator to a homogeneous mass, and feed the plodder/press. Enclosed indoor line, batch-wise recipe changes, sanitation constraints.

Glass container/tableware plant batch house: weigh sand, soda ash, limestone and other raw materials plus cullet to the glass recipe, mix the batch, moisten it, and convey it to the furnace serving the forming machines. Large indoor batch tower/plant, bulk silos, continuous operation.

Small-shop, short-run, trial or changeover work in any of the above industries: operator hand-weighs small quantities on a bench scale, softens or kneads material by hand or on a mill, cuts pieces to size with knife or shears, patches/joins scrap and remnant stock, and adjusts consistency by feel and appearance until the material runs right in the machine. Non-standard containers, frequent recipe changes, improvised handling.

sources.transferJustification: Same task: measuring/weighing powder ingredients (of the type listed, e.g., cornmeal-like powders) to recipe to prepare a premix for downstream machine processing.

tasks.label: Remove materials or products from molds or from extruding, forming, pressing, or compacting machines, and stack or store them for additional processing.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Plastics/rubber molding plant: operator takes molded parts (and sprues) out of an injection or compression press as the mold opens, trims/inspects, and stacks them in totes, boxes with interleaves, or racks beside the machine on the molding floor.

Brick/tile/clay plant: operator takes green ware off the extruder cut-off table or off the press and stacks it on pallets, dryer cars, or kiln cars in the required setting pattern; heavy, dusty, high throughput.

Glass plant: hot formed glassware taken off the forming machine (press or blow mold) and transferred to the dead plate/conveyor or racked for the annealing lehr; hot, fast-cycling work at the hot end.

Food/soap/wax/cosmetics plant: operator takes stamped soap bars, formed patties, molded candles or pressed cosmetic cakes off the press/plodder/former dies and places them on trays, racks, or infeed conveyors for wrapping or further processing; hygiene-controlled, delicate product.

Heavy, bulky, or awkward output in low-volume or job-shop conditions: large rubber goods (e.g., green tires, molded mats), large composite or thermoset moldings, refractory shapes or powder-metal compacts removed with hoists/two-hand lifts and stacked on carts, racks or pallets; frequent product changeovers.

tasks.label: Feed products into machines by hand or conveyor.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: On a plant floor, the operator hand-places discrete rigid or semi-rigid workpieces (rubber preforms, soap billets, green tile/brick blanks, molded plastic parts, gaskets) into a press die or the infeed nest of a forming machine, cycling with the machine every few seconds to a minute; parts arrive jumbled in totes, bins or on racks beside the machine.

The operator keeps a machine hopper/feed throat supplied with bulk raw material: cutting and dumping 25-50 lb sacks of powder, pellets or compound from a pallet, or tipping totes/gaylords, watching hopper level and clearing bridging. Occurs in the plant's material staging area next to the extruder or press.

The operator feeds soft, deformable bulk stock continuously into an extruder feed throat, plodder, or forming machine — dough from a trough, rubber slab/strip from a stack, clay pug, warm wax or soap mass — by hand, hook or shovel, keeping the feed even and unbroken so the machine does not starve. Plant floor, often hot and sticky material.

The operator transfers product from bins, pallets, carts or an upstream buffer onto the infeed conveyor that feeds the machine — placing cases, containers, trays, molds or semi-finished pieces at line rate and keeping the conveyor evenly loaded. Factory or packaging-hall floor with people and lift trucks moving nearby.

The operator feeds sheets, blanks or strip stock (plastic sheet, metal blanks, veneer, rubber pads) into a press or forming machine, aligning each piece to registration pins or marks before the cycle, at millimetre-level placement tolerance.

tasks.label: Measure arbors and dies to verify sizes specified on work tickets.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pre-run setup check at the machine's tool bench: operator pulls the extruder/tuber die and its mating arbor (pin/mandrel) called out on the work ticket from the tooling rack, measures the die orifice bore and the arbor tip OD with micrometer, plug/pin gauges and calipers to a few thousandths of an inch, confirms stamped tool numbers match the ticket, and signs off. Plant floor, standard tooling, institution-controlled premises.

Job-change batch verification in the tool crib or QC bench: several dies and arbors for the upcoming run are measured in sequence (bore diameters, ODs, land lengths, thickness), values recorded against the work ticket/setup sheet, worn or out-of-tolerance tooling pulled from service. Clean bench, standard hand gauges and a bench comparator.

Precision profile/cavity verification in the plant QC lab: a complex die or mold (pasta/food extrusion die plate, glass mold cavity, wax or cosmetic mold, rubber profile die) is checked on an optical comparator or lab CMM against the drawing dimensions listed on the work ticket, including multiple profile features and pass/fail tolerance calls.

Large, heavy tooling verification: brick/clay extrusion die plate, soap plodder nozzle/cone, or tire tread die is moved by hoist or cart, then overall opening dimensions, plate thickness, taper and bolt-hole spacing are measured with tape, large calipers and a height gauge and compared to the ticket. Coarser tolerances, awkward handling, plant floor.

In-place check of the die and arbor as installed in the extruder head/press: operator verifies pin protrusion, die-to-pin gap/concentricity and land clearance with feeler gauges, calipers and a depth gauge on the assembled, often warm head at the running machine, and records conformity to the ticket before or between runs.

A die or arbor is a machined steel part whose bores, ODs and lengths are checked to thousandths of an inch; the accepted output (pass/fail plus recorded dimensions versus the ticket) is identical in kind, object class and precision.

tasks.label: Complete work tickets, and place them with products.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: End-of-run finished-goods lot in a plastics/rubber extrusion plant: operator fills in the work ticket/lot traveler (part number, lot, quantity, machine, shift, date) from the machine counter or terminal, prints or writes it, and tapes it to the pallet or slides it into the pallet placard holder before the pallet leaves the line for the warehouse.

In-process container or cart: operator completes a routing/traveler card for a tote, box, rack, or kiln car of semi-finished product (green tile, brick cube, extruded parts, glass ware) and drops the card into the tote or clips it to the cart, which then moves to the next department.

Bundle, coil, or roll of extruded/formed product (profile bundles, rolls of extruded film or rubber, wire rod): operator completes an identification tag with the run data and hangs, straps, or adheres it to the strapped bundle or roll end on the packing line.

Food, soap, or cosmetics batch from a plodder/extruder: operator completes the batch identification ticket (lot code, batch weight, time, line) as part of the batch record and places the ticket in or on the tote/case of product heading to packaging, under food/GMP documentation rules.

Nonstandard lot: partial run, rework, or hold. Operator hand-writes a tag describing the observed problem (dimension drift, surface defects, machine stoppage notes, initials) and attaches it to a partial pallet, a scrap gaylord, or an odd-shaped part parked wherever there is floor space.

tasks.label: Disassemble equipment to repair it or to replace parts, such as nozzles, punches, and filters.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Product changeover or worn-tooling replacement on a forming/molding machine (glass IS machine blank mold and plunger set, brick/tile press die, extruder die plate or nozzle): lock out the hot machine, unbolt or unclamp the tooling, pull the old set, fit and align the replacement, re-torque and restart.

Rotary compacting/tablet press retool: strip upper and lower punches and dies (or segments) from the turret, inspect each for wear, chipping and dimensional drift, clean the bores, install the replacement tooling set and reassemble the press.

Filter and consumable-element replacement: change an extruder screen pack and breaker plate on a hot head, or open hydraulic/lube/compressed-air filter housings, pull the clogged element, seat new O-rings and elements, reseal and bleed the circuit.

Sanitation or product-change teardown of a food, soap, wax or cosmetics extruder/plodder: remove nozzles, die plates, cutting knives, augers, screens, hoses and gaskets, wash them down, replace worn seals and gaskets, reassemble and verify fit in a washdown bay.

Breakdown repair: diagnose the fault, disassemble the affected subassembly (heater band, thermocouple, drive belt, bearing, pneumatic valve, packing/seal) with hand tools in cramped machine framing, replace the failed component, reassemble and test-run.

tasks.label: Remove molds, mold components, and feeder tubes from machinery after production is complete.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Plastics/rubber plant: at the end of a production run the operator shuts down an extruder or forming press and removes the die head, die plate/breaker plate or mold from the machine — unbolting or unclamping it, disconnecting heater and water lines, and lifting the tooling out with a hoist or cart onto a tool trolley for cleaning and storage. Tooling is hot, residue-coated and heavy (tens of kg to several tonnes); the work is done on an open plant floor with other machines running nearby.

Glass container/glassware plant, IS-machine job change: operator removes blank and blow mould halves, neck rings, baffles, funnels and plungers from the machine sections, and pulls the feeder tube and orifice ring from the forehearth spout. Parts are at 400-600 C, mounted in cramped mechanism space, some work overhead; heat-resistant gloves, tongs and small mould carts are used.

Clay, brick, tile, refractory or technical-ceramic/powder-compaction press: after a size or product change the operator removes the die box, punches, liners and mould assembly from the press, using changeover carriages, hoists or die carts, and stages the tooling for cleaning and storage. Heavy steel tooling, abrasive powder residue, fixed machine location in the pressing hall.

Food or soap forming line, discrete tooling change: operator removes a single bolted/clamped die or forming plate assembly from a pasta press, snack/pet-food extruder or soap plodder head (die plate, knife assembly, nozzle plate) at the end of the ... and places it on a cart or into a die washer. One well-defined heavy tooling assembly, standard fasteners or clamp ring.

Batch-end hygiene teardown in food, pharmaceutical, nutraceutical or cosmetics production: operator strips the machine of moulds, mould inserts, punches and dies, feed frames, nozzles, hoppers and product feeder tubes and hoses, and carries all parts to the wash area for cleaning and documented changeover. Many small, varied, wet or powder-coated parts; tri-clamps, thumbscrews and hand tools; work in a cleanroom or washdown production room.

Small-batch or specialty operation (candle/wax moulding, tobacco, cosmetics pressing, custom rubber shop, R&D or prototype run): operator removes small moulds and mould inserts by hand from a bench-scale or older forming machine after a short run; tooling differs job to job and is set aside on a bench or rack.

tasks.label: Swab molds with solutions to prevent products from sticking.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Glass container/tableware plant hot end: operator swabs blank moulds and neck rings on a running IS or press machine with graphite-oil lubricant on a swab stick, between gobs or on section stops, in radiant heat, while production continues.

Rubber or plastic press shop: operator sprays/wipes mould release agent into open compression, transfer or injection mould cavities on a press between cycles during a production run, mould fixed in the press, same part repeated for hours.

Food plant: operator applies release oil/grease to bread and cake pans, trays, confectionery or cheese moulds moving on the production line before depositing product, at line speed, food-grade lubricant.

Brick, tile, clay or concrete products plant: operator applies release oil (or sand/dusting slurry) to press moulds, mould boxes or pallets between pressings so green units release cleanly; dusty, wet conditions.

Small-batch / short-run work (soap, wax and candle moulds, cosmetics sticks, specialty rubber goods, sample runs): worker cleans residue and brushes or hand-sprays release solution into many differently shaped moulds at a bench or small press, with frequent changeovers.

tasks.label: Install, align, and adjust neck rings, press plungers, and feeder tubes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Job change on a container-glass IS (individual section) machine: the operator/mold setter mounts new neck ring halves (with matching blank molds and plungers) on each of 8-12 sections, seats them in the neck ring holder arms, tightens screws/clamps, and checks parting-line seam and invert alignment. Hot end of a glass plant, radiant heat, multi-kilogram tooling, hand and impact tools, work reached into the section frame; the whole set must run correctly within minutes of restart.

Single-section change during production: a worn or chipped neck ring or a scored press plunger on one running section is swapped with the section shut off but the machine hot and cycling around it; the operator pulls hot tooling with tongs and gloves, fits and secures the replacement, re-checks plunger-to-neck-ring centering, and puts the section back on line.

Running adjustment of the feeder tube and feeder plungers (needles) at the forehearth spout to hold gob weight, length and shape on target - raising/lowering tube height, changing tube rotation, trimming individual needle heights - after weight checks or defect feedback. Done repeatedly per shift over molten glass at the feeder.

Installing or replacing the refractory feeder tube (and related spout/orifice ring parts) at a job change or after wear: lifting the tube into the tube holder above the feeder bowl, clamping it, and centering it over the orifice with correct immersion depth and concentricity, in an overhead, very hot position.

Defect-driven fine alignment: after finish defects (out-of-round finish, seams, plunger marks, loading faults) are reported by inspection, the operator re-aligns neck ring to blank mold and plunger - shims, guide-ring/invert adjustment, plunger height and stroke settings - then verifies with sample ware.

Analogous forming-tooling work outside container glass: fitting and adjusting dies/nozzles on a soap plodder, punches and dies on a ceramic/clay or tablet-type press, or die and mandrel on a rubber/clay tuber-extruder, including centering and clearance adjustment on a factory floor.

The operator only rolls the mould magazine into the robot's reach beforehand.

Same class of work as installing/aligning neck rings and plungers - multi-kilogram precision mould tooling picked from a presented magazine, inserted into the machine's holder and locked, with correctness verified by RFID and alignment set by holder geometry. It transfers only where machine and tooling are purpose-built for robotic exchange (guards, indexed stations, quick-lock holders), i.e. an E1 setting.

tasks.label: Press and adjust controls to activate, set, and regulate equipment according to specifications.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Sawmill/wood-products dry kiln: operator selects the species/thickness drying schedule, starts fans and steam, sets dry-bulb/wet-bulb setpoints and vent positions, then adjusts through the charge (ramp, equalize, condition) until target moisture content is reached and the kiln is shut down. Indoor/outdoor kiln yard at a mill controlled by the company.

Heat-treat, annealing or firing furnace/kiln in a plant (glass annealing lehr, ceramic/brick kiln, aerospace heat-treat furnace): operator loads the specified recipe/ramp-soak program, presses start, sets zone temperatures, atmosphere and belt/car speed, monitors thermocouple readings against spec (e.g., AMS2750) and trims setpoints during the cycle.

Industrial drier/curing oven/autoclave (spray or rotary drier, aggregate drier, rubber/composite cure autoclave, paint or coating oven): operator activates burners/fans, enters temperature, pressure, airflow, belt speed and dwell setpoints per the product specification, and regulates them as feed rate or product moisture varies.

Heated batch kettle/reactor (soap boiling, chemical cook, wax/pitch melting): operator opens steam or sets jacket temperature, starts agitation, follows the cook procedure through heating, hold and cooling stages, adjusting valves/setpoints against temperature, viscosity or endpoint checks.

Older, minimally instrumented equipment inside a plant (hand-wheel steam and gas valves, manual dampers, dial gauges, pilot lighting): operator physically opens/closes valves and dampers and judges settings from gauges and visual cues, with no closed-loop instrumentation on the machine.

Field/farm-site drying or heating equipment away from a plant (trailer or farm-installed grain/biomass drier, portable kiln or kettle at a job site): operator starts the burner, sets plenum temperature and moisture/discharge targets, and adjusts through the run under outdoor conditions at a site taken as found.
