tasks.label: Sort rough diamonds into categories based on shape, size, color, and quality.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: High-volume small rough (melee/near-melee, roughly under 0.25 ct) at a producer sort house, aggregation centre or dealer's sorting room: parcels of thousands of stones are screened into sieve size fractions, then separated by crystal shape (sawable/makeable/flat/cleavage), colour tint and quality into assortment categories, weighed, and packed into marked parcel papers. Per-stone value is low; accuracy is judged statistically over the parcel.

Medium rough (roughly 0.25-2 ct) sorted at a sorting bench under north-light lamps with tweezers, loupe and sieve set: each stone is judged for shape/crystal form, size, body colour and clarity/quality and dropped into the matching category tray or briefke; categories are reconciled by weight and count before hand-off to the cutting planner.

Large and high-value rough (about 2 ct and up, including specials): individual stones are examined for tint, inclusions, crystal form and likely polished yield and assigned to fine value/assortment categories that drive price; the sorter's judgement of cutting potential is the output the employer accepts.

Industrial and near-gem material at a processing plant: gem-quality stones are separated from boart/industrial grades, and the industrial fraction is classified by size fraction and by shape/blockiness for saw, drill and abrasive use. Very high volume, low per-unit value, statistical quality tolerances.

Rough lab-grown crystals and CVD plates at a US lab-grown producer or its US cutting operation: as-grown material is cleaned, then sorted by size, shape/geometry, colour grade and internal quality into batches for planning and cutting, in a company-controlled production room.

sources.system: Sarine Galaxy 1000 / Meteorite Plus rough inclusion mapping systems

tasks.label: Place stones in clamps on polishing machines and polish facets of stones, using felt-covered or canvas-covered polishing wheels and polishing compounds such as tripoli and rouge.
Hold stones, gems, dies, or styluses against rotating plates, wheels, saws, or slitters to cut, shape, slit, grind, or polish them.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Diamond cutting facility: rough diamonds (0.1–5 ct) are sawn with a rotating phosphor-bronze blade, bruted/girdled against a second diamond, then blocked and brillianteered by holding the tang-mounted stone against a rotating cast-iron scaife charged with diamond powder, working with the grain to certificate-grade cut/polish/symmetry.

Commercial colored-stone lapidary: production faceting of calibrated goods (CZ, amethyst, garnet, synthetic sapphire, 2–12 mm) — dopped preforms are held against rotating cutting and polishing laps at set index/angle settings to standard shapes and sizes, in batches, to trade-acceptable meets and polish.

Custom / one-off work in a small shop: a unique or high-value rough (tourmaline, spinel, fine sapphire, precious opal) is oriented for color and inclusions and cut to a bespoke or native design with in-process judgment; also recutting/repolishing chipped, abraded, or badly cut stones brought in by customers.

Cabochon work: trimmed slabs of agate, jasper, turquoise, opal are dopped and held against rotating diamond grinding wheels and sanding/polishing wheels to shape, dome, sand and polish cabs — mostly calibrated oval/round sizes for standard settings, some freeform shapes following the material's pattern.

Industrial diamond shop: grinding and polishing industrial diamond and PCD components — wire-drawing die blanks and die holes, tool blanks, dresser points, styluses — held against rotating laps, wheels, slitters or polishing wires to specified geometry and surface finish.

sources.system: Dialit GS7000-E automatic full-cut polishing machine
sources.title: Dialit - GS7000 E4 – Automatic Full-Cut Polishing Machine
sources.claim: Dialit's GS7000-E is a commercially sold automatic full-cut diamond polishing machine that polishes the facets of dopped stones (0.10–20 ct) on the scaife to certificate/special-cut quality, with one operator supervising up to 16 machines — i.e. autonomous cycles with occasional loading/intervention.

sources.system: Dialit Super Sawyer
sources.title: Dialit - Super Sawyer

sources.system: Dialit Super Blocker

sources.system: RK DieGrind PCD/ND die grinding and wire polishing machines
sources.title: PCD/ND • RK DieGrind
sources.claim: RK DieGrind supplies CNC-controlled machines for working natural-diamond and PCD wire-drawing dies, including fully CNC ultrasonic die-working machines with an integrated magazine and feeder, and wire polishing machines that finish the die bore.
sources.transferJustification: Same workpieces named in the task (diamond dies) and same shaping/polishing precision; the abrasive is presented by machine-controlled tooling and a rotating polishing wire instead of a hand-held die pressed to a rotating lap.

sources.system: Ajex+Turner automatic die reconditioning machine
sources.title: Automatic machine for the repairing of dies | WIRE
sources.claim: Ajex+Turner's automatic die repair machine reconditions diamond and PCD dies from 0.10–4.00 mm under program control, with automatic needle grinding, sensor-driven cycle completion and immediate progression to the next die, achieving accurate re-cut angles and mirror polish.
sources.transferJustification: Same workpiece class (diamond/PCD dies) and same finishing objective (shaping and polishing the die to spec); machine-controlled abrasive tooling substitutes for the worker holding the die against a rotating lap or polishing wire.

sources.system: automatic diamond polishing machines (industry-wide)
sources.title: Automatic For The People (IDEX Online)
sources.claim: Trade press describes automatic diamond-polishing machines and robots as commonly used in the industry for the bulk of production diamonds, with hand polishing persisting mainly for large stones and low-tech, low-labour-cost settings.

tasks.label: Replace, true, and sharpen blades, drills, and plates.
Secure stones in metal mountings, using solder.
Immerse stones in prescribed chemical solutions to determine specific gravities and key properties of gemstones or substitutes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Gemological laboratory bench: a single loose unmounted colored stone of uncertain identity (e.g., topaz vs. quartz, jadeite vs. serpentine) is cleaned, weighed in air, then suspended in a basket and weighed immersed in distilled water (hydrostatic method) or dropped into a bottle of heavy liquid such as di-iodomethane; float/sink or computed SG is recorded on the ID worksheet and the stone is rinsed, dried and returned to its stone paper.

Batch/parcel work in a lab or dealer's grading room: a parcel of small stones or rough (melee, faceted lots, mixed rough) is poured into heavy liquid of a prescribed density to separate sinkers from floaters, screening out simulants and substitutes; the two fractions are retrieved with a strainer, rinsed in solvent, dried, counted and packaged.

Jewelry store, pawnshop or independent appraiser's back room: a quick specific-gravity check on a customer's loose stone using a small heavy-liquid set or an electronic SG balance kit, done while the customer waits; extreme care not to lose, stain or damage the stone, and a verbal/written result the same day.

Immersion-cell work in a gem lab: the stone is placed in a cell of index-matching/heavy liquid (e.g., di-iodomethane, benzyl benzoate) under a microscope so that surface reflections are suppressed, and internal features — growth structures, color zoning, inclusions — are observed to determine natural vs. synthetic or treated, then the stone is cleaned of liquid residue.

Off-site testing: at a gem show booth, a mine-site buying office, or a client's home/office, a portable SG kit or vials of heavy liquid are used on a table of opportunity with variable lighting, temperature and no fume hood; stones must be tested and returned to the owner immediately.

sources.system: AMS Micro (Automated Melee Screening)
sources.title: De Beers Group Ignite launches latest diamond verification instrument, AMS Micro
sources.claim: De Beers Group Ignite's AMS Micro is a commercial benchtop instrument that autonomously loads a parcel of melee diamonds from a hopper, uses camera-guided robotic pick-and-place to seat each stone on a measurement disc, measures and categorises each stone as natural, lab-grown, non-diamond or refer, and dispenses it into the correct container without expert operators or supervision.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated screening of loose gemstones to determine whether they are natural diamond, lab-grown or a substitute — the same determination the immersion/SG test serves ('key properties of gemstones or substitutes'), on the same objects (loose stones down to 0.001 ct), including autonomous per-stone handling, measurement and sorting inside a purpose-built machine.

sources.system: AMS2 (Automated Melee Screener)
sources.developer: De Beers Group (International Institute of Diamond Grading & Research)
sources.title: De Beers Cuts Price on Melee Screening Device
sources.claim: The earlier AMS2 screener, sold commercially since 2016, accepts up to 500 carats of ... poured into it and automatically feeds each stone table-down into a testing station for screening.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: bulk screening of a parcel of small loose stones to separate natural stones from synthetics and simulants — the same purpose as pouring a parcel into heavy liquid to separate sinkers from floaters, with the same objects and the same accept/refer output; establishes automated bulk feeding and per-stone handling of gem parcels.

sources.system: GIA Melee Analysis Service
sources.title: GIA Pilots Melee Analysis Service for Diamonds
sources.claim: GIA operates a fully automated melee analysis system in its laboratories that analyzes and sorts round melee-size diamonds, separating natural untreated stones from simulants and potentially synthetic or treated stones and sorting them by color range.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated identification of natural stones versus simulants/synthetics in bulk parcels, the identification outcome the SG immersion test is performed to obtain; same objects (loose melee), performed in a purpose-built instrument line inside a gem laboratory.

sources.system: Dimensionics Density density-determination system
sources.title: Dimensionics Density introduces automated density testing for Additive Manufacturing
sources.claim: Dimensionics Density sells a commercial machine that determines the density of solid samples by the Archimedes method — weighing the object in air and then immersed in a liquid of known density — with the measuring cycle running fully automatically once samples are placed in universal component carriers that an axis robot lowers into the liquid; repeatability is quoted at 0.001 g/cm3.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated hydrostatic (immersion) density determination of small solid parts. It is the same physical procedure gem workers use — weigh in air, weigh immersed in a liquid of known density, compute specific gravity — with automated immersion, environmental compensation and result logging, at precision (0.001 g/cm3) exceeding what gem identification requires.

sources.system: Galaxy 1000
sources.title: Galaxy 1000 Inclusion Mapping_Sarine
sources.claim: Sarine's Galaxy 1000 is a commercially deployed system that fully automatically detects and maps internal features (inclusions) of rough diamonds up to 20 ct, the determination gemologists otherwise make by viewing stones in an immersion cell under a microscope.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated determination of a stone's internal characteristics. Immersion microscopy is performed to see inclusions and growth structure through the stone; Galaxy obtains the same internal map automatically on the same objects inside a purpose-built scanning machine, producing an accepted per-stone record.

sources.system: Dense Media Separation (DMS/HMS) plant
sources.developer: JXSC / DMS Powders (plant suppliers to diamond mines)
sources.title: Dense Media Separation (DMS) Plants - JXSC Machine
sources.claim: Diamond recovery plants routinely perform float/sink separation at a set specific gravity by suspending powdered ferrosilicon in water to make a medium near the density of diamond, so that stones above the cut density sink and lighter material floats, as a continuous machine-controlled process.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: immersing stones in a liquid of prescribed density to sort them by specific gravity. It is the same physics and the same accept/reject output as heavy-liquid gem testing, executed continuously by machine in a purpose-built plant, supporting that float/sink determination is machine-executable when the material is fed to ... machine.

tasks.label: Regrind drill points, and advance drill cutting points according to specifications for channel depths and shapes.
Split gems along pre-marked lines to remove imperfections, using blades and jewelers' hammers.
Lap girdles on rough diamonds, using diamond girdling lathes.
Dismantle lapping, boring, cutting, polishing, and shaping equipment and machinery to clean and lubricate it.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Small commercial lapidary/gem-cutting shop: at end of a run the worker takes down a bench faceting or cabbing unit — unscrews the master-lap retaining nut, lifts off the lap/grinding wheel, removes the splash pan and drip guards, washes off abrasive slurry and stone swarf, wipes and oils the spindle/quill bearings and index gear, then reassembles and checks the lap runs true.

Diamond polishing bench in a cutting shop: worker removes the tang/dop holder, dismounts the scaife (polishing wheel) from its spindle, cleans out diamond-powder-and-oil paste residue from wheel, housing and bearings, re-greases/oils the bearing and spindle, remounts the scaife and trues/levels it before restarting.

Slabbing/trim saw or bruting machine in a gem or industrial-diamond shop: worker takes off the blade guard and hood, pulls the arbor and diamond blade, drains and scrapes sludge from the coolant/oil tank, cleans or swaps the filter and coolant lines, wipes and lubricates the carriage slides, vise screw and bearings, reassembles and re-tensions/aligns the blade.

Scheduled preventive maintenance on a production lapping/polishing machine in an industrial diamond-tool or high-volume gem plant: covers and guards removed, lap plate and conditioning rings lifted off, slurry lines and pump cleaned of abrasive, ways and lead screws cleaned and greased at multiple lube points, machine reassembled, plate re-leveled and test-run.

Boring/drilling equipment at the bench (drill press, ultrasonic/mechanical gem driller, dop-and-chuck spindle): worker removes the chuck or collet and drill, dismantles the quill/spindle assembly, cleans stone dust, cutting oil and paste from the parts, applies fresh lubricant and reassembles for the next job.

sources.system: DHR REGO-FIX robotic tool-assembly cell (KUKA robot + PGA 9500 + wash/dry stations)
sources.title: Why Tool Assembly Automation Is the Missing Link in Lights-Out CNC Manufacturing
sources.claim: A commercially built robotic cell (KUKA arm, washing and drying stations, REGO-FIX PGA 9500 clamping unit) autonomously runs the complete cycle of taking used precision tool assemblies apart, washing them before and after disassembly, drying, and rebuilding them ready to run, unattended around the clock.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: teardown, cleaning and rebuild of precision toolholder/collet assemblies fouled with cutting fluid and swarf. Objects (threaded metal precision spindle/collet/wheel-mount hardware), the required precision of reseating, and the purpose-built cell setting match dismantling a lapidary spindle, lap or dop assembly to clean it.

sources.system: REGO-FIX PGA 9500 automatic clamping/unclamping unit
sources.title: Automation-Ready Toolholding System
sources.claim: The clamping/unclamping unit used in such cells is an automation-ready commercial product designed for robot-connected, unmanned round-the-clock tool assembly and disassembly.
sources.transferJustification: Corroborates that the mounting/dismounting hardware in the cited teardown-and-rebuild cell is a real, robot-integrated commercial product operating unattended.

sources.system: Nordson EFD automated fluid dispensing systems (RV/GV series dispensing robots)
sources.title: Nordson EFD Releases New 3-Axis Automated Fluid Dispensing Systems
sources.claim: Automated dispensing robots and systems meter and apply grease, oil and other assembly fluids onto fixtured parts on benchtop and automated assembly lines, with vision to compensate for part position shifts.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: metered lubricant application to fixtured mechanical parts in a cell. This is the 'lubricate' half of the gem-shop task, applied to comparable small metal components at comparable precision.

sources.system: Berger Gruppe robot grinding wheel changing system (circular knife processing cell)
sources.title: Robot grinding wheel changing system | Berger Gruppe
sources.claim: In an enclosed circular-knife grinding cell, an industrial robot performs the grinding wheel change on the CNC grinding machines as well as workpiece loading and unloading, using an integrated gripper-changing system.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic removal and refitting of abrasive wheels on grinding machinery inside a fenced cell — the same dismount/remount operation a gem worker performs on laps, scaifes and grinding wheels, at comparable precision.

sources.system: Daisy disassembly robot
sources.title: Apple expands global recycling programs
sources.claim: Apple's purpose-built disassembly line takes apart used, variable-condition consumer devices autonomously at production rate across many models, at deployed scale.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous disassembly of used, dirt- and wear-variable assemblies in a purpose-built line, showing that fastener/part removal from previously-used equipment is achievable at production quality when the work is presented to the machine.

sources.system: state of robotic disassembly/remanufacturing automation (survey)
sources.title: Automation in remanufacturing: how robots are extending product lifecycles
sources.claim: Trade-press review of remanufacturing automation reports that robotic disassembly systems are only beginning to emerge and are blocked by variability such as seized bolts and deformed parts, while component cleaning is a comparatively mature area of automation and reassembly is easier to automate than disassembly.
sources.transferJustification: Context for negative judgments: whole-machine teardown with unknown-condition fasteners and in-situ servicing of coolant tanks, lines and guards is not substantiated by any deployed robotic system.

roles.description: Construct and repair full or partial dentures or dental appliances.

tasks.label: Read prescriptions or specifications and examine models or impressions to determine the design of dental products to be constructed.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Fixed-restoration case arriving digitally: technician opens the lab portal, reads the dentist's electronic Rx (tooth number, shade, material, contact/occlusion preferences) and inspects the intraoral scan file of the prep and opposing arch on screen to decide crown/bridge design, margin placement, connector size and material. Output is a design decision recorded in the case notes/CAD file.

Fixed-restoration case arriving analog: technician reads a paper or emailed Rx accompanying a shipped PVS impression or poured stone model, visually examines the prep, margins, adjacent teeth and bite registration for a crown, inlay or veneer, and determines the restoration design and material before fabrication begins.

Removable prosthetics: technician reads the dentist's Rx for a full or partial denture, examines the master casts (surveying for undercuts, ridge form, path of insertion, existing dentition) and determines framework design, clasp type, major connector and tooth arrangement, often marking the design on the cast or a lab slip.

Ambiguous, incomplete or problematic prescription: technician reads the Rx, examines the model/scan, identifies a conflict (insufficient occlusal clearance, unreadable margin, missing shade, unrealistic pontic space) and determines the design that can be delivered, documenting the issue and querying the dentist before proceeding.

Appliances and repairs: technician reads the Rx or repair slip for a night guard, retainer, splint or fractured denture, examines the model or the broken appliance, and determines the appliance design, thickness/coverage or repair approach.

tasks.label: Test appliances for conformance to specifications and accuracy of occlusion, using articulators and micrometers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Final check of a single-unit crown or small fixed bridge in a mid-size commercial lab: technician seats the restoration on the die, mounts working and opposing casts in a semi-adjustable articulator, marks occlusal contacts with articulating paper, verifies proximal contacts and margins, and gauges occlusal/wall thickness with calipers or a micrometer, adjusting and re-checking until it meets the prescription.

Quality gate in a high-volume digital production center: milled/sintered zirconia or lithium-disilicate units come off the mill in trays and must be verified for dimensional conformance to the CAD design (fit, thickness, occlusal anatomy designed against the antagonist scan) and passed or rejected before shipping.

Processed complete or immediate denture: technician remounts the denture on the articulator, checks centric and eccentric occlusal contacts after processing/deflasking, verifies vertical dimension and tooth positions against the prescription and try-in record, and identifies deviations for selective grinding.

Cast or printed removable partial denture framework: technician seats the framework on the master cast, checks that rests seat fully with no rock, that clasp arms engage planned undercuts, measures clasp/connector dimensions with a gauge or micrometer, and checks occlusal clearance against the opposing cast on the articulator.

Orthodontic appliance, clear retainer, or occlusal night guard: technician checks fit on the working model, verifies wire diameters and acrylic/thermoplastic thickness with a micrometer, checks trim lines, and verifies occlusal contact distribution on articulated models before shipping.

sources.system: Glidewell Intelligent Manufacturing (robotic milling towers + optical inspection)
sources.title: How Glidewell Intelligent Manufacturing Elevates Simplicity, Quality, Speed and Predictability for Dentists
sources.claim: Glidewell's automated crown-and-bridge production line performs the conformance test itself: optical inspection compares each milled unit to its design file and only accepts units inside a ""50 µm tolerance, inside a robotic milling/inspection facility.
sources.transferJustification: Same task: verifying a finished dental appliance against its specification. The design file encodes occlusal surfaces generated against the antagonist scan, so the machine check substitutes for the technician's articulator/micrometer check of the same units.

sources.system: Glidewell Intelligent Manufacturing article scanners (closed-loop QC)
sources.title: Dental Technology: Driving Faster, Better Results
sources.claim: Glidewell explicitly replaced the human end-of-line inspection of a restoration on a stone model with article scanners that build a 3D model of the finished restoration ... issue an automated pass/fail determination.

sources.system: Glidewell BruxZir Factory (robotic arms, automated dimensional QC station)
sources.title: Robotics and Automation (Chairside Magazine, Vol. 21 Issue 2)
sources.claim: In Glidewell's BruxZir factory robotic arms select and move blanks through milling, and a finishing/quality-control station performs dimensional surface measurements on the sintered restorations to confirm accurate fit; operators deliver the parts to the station.

sources.system: Bionic Jaw Motion (BJM) robotic articulator
sources.title: Individual mandibular movement registration and reproduction using an optoeletronic jaw movement analyzer and a dedicated robot: a dental technique (BMC Oral Health)
sources.claim: The Bionic Jaw Motion robotic articulator holds upper and lower casts in robot cast holders and, under computer motor control, reproduces the patient's recorded mandibular movements so occlusal contacts can be read in static and dynamic positions during laboratory phases.
sources.transferJustification: The robot performs by machine the articulator excursions a technician performs by hand to test occlusion of a prosthesis, on casts fixtured in the machine's own cast holders.

sources.system: CNC coordinate measuring machine (CMM) metrology of dental frameworks
sources.developer: metrology industry (as used in prosthodontic accuracy studies)
sources.title: The effect of framework fabrication technique on the fit accuracy of full arch screw retained implant supported prostheses
sources.claim: Coordinate measuring machines are the standard machine method for measuring marginal fit and dimensional discrepancy of full-arch dental frameworks in three axes, at the micron precision a technician seeks with a micrometer and fit check.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: dimensional verification of dental prostheses. A programmed CMM measures, on a fixtured part, the same fit and thickness quantities the technician gauges with a micrometer, at comparable or better precision.

sources.system: Dandy AOI (automated optical inspection)
sources.title: AI, Robotics, and 3D Printing for Mass Customization: Dandy's Dental Revolution
sources.claim: Dandy runs an automated optical inspection system in its in-house digital dental labs that uses cameras and an AI model to catch crown defects that previously depended on a technician's subjective visual check.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: end-of-line acceptance inspection of finished restorations in a dental lab; it shows machine inspection replacing the technician's acceptance check on the same objects, though for surface/shade defects rather than occlusion.

sources.system: Universal Robots UR5 machine-tending cells at Glidewell Laboratories

tasks.label: Fabricate, alter, or repair dental devices, such as dentures, crowns, bridges, inlays, or appliances for straightening teeth.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Commercial dental lab: fabricate a monolithic posterior crown or small bridge (zirconia/lithium disilicate) from a case that arrives as an intraoral scan file or a physical impression — design/verify margins and occlusion, mill or print, cut from the blank, sinter, stain/glaze and polish to a prescribed stock shade, check fit on a printed model, and ship.

Esthetic anterior case: crown/veneer requiring custom shade matching, ceramic layering or cut-back-and-layer, internal characterization, incisal effects and hand contouring/texturing to blend with adjacent natural teeth; often photo-guided and remade if shade is rejected.

Removable full denture (or printed/milled acrylic partial base): from impressions/bite records or scans, set teeth to the occlusal scheme, produce the base and teeth (traditional flask-and-pack, or CAD design plus milling/printing), finish, polish and deliver a wearable prosthesis.

Orthodontic and thermoformed appliances: clear aligner sets, vacuum-formed retainers, night guards and splints — print or fabricate the arch models, thermoform or direct-print, trim and mark, polish edges, package the staged series.

Repairs and alterations on devices that arrive used and damaged: mending a fractured denture base, adding a tooth or clasp, chairside-type relines/rebases, soldering or adjusting an orthodontic wire appliance, adjusting contacts on a returned crown — each piece unique, unfixtured, often with adherent debris and no digital record.

Metal substructures: cast or laser-melted cobalt-chrome RPD frameworks and milled titanium implant bars/frames — devest or remove supports, fit and adjust clasps/rests on the master cast, finish and high-polish, verify passive fit.

tasks.label: Place tooth models on an apparatus that mimics bite and movement of patient's jaw to evaluate functionality of model.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Crown-and-bridge case in a commercial dental lab: technician mixes mounting stone, secures a gypsum working cast and its opposing cast to an average-value or semi-adjustable articulator using the dentist's interocclusal bite record, waits for set, then closes the articulator and checks that the casts seat in the record, that occlusal contacts and the incisal pin are correct, and that excursions clear.

Large restorative case (full-mouth rehab, multiple units, occlusal splint): maxillary cast mounted via facebow/transfer jig, mandibular cast mounted to a centric-relation record, condylar and Bennett settings dialed in from the prescription, split-cast accuracy verification and protrusive/lateral excursion checks performed on a fully adjustable articulator.

Removable prosthetics: edentulous or partially edentulous casts with wax occlusion rims mounted to the articulator using the CR record, vertical dimension and midline verified, articulator used through tooth setup and again for post-processing remount to correct processing-induced occlusal errors.

Plasterless/digital workflow: 3D-printed or milled models produced with keyed, magnetic or snap-fit articulator bases are seated onto a plasterless or printed articulator (or a magnetic mounting-plate system), then closed to confirm seating and occlusal relationship for a single unit, night guard, or ortho appliance.

Repair, reline and remount work in a small in-house or denture lab: an existing denture or appliance with its cast is fixed onto the articulator (often re-mounted to an existing index or remount cast), occlusion checked before and after the repair, with worn, contaminated or damaged parts and no fresh clinical records.

It does not transfer to plaster mounting or occlusal evaluation.

tasks.label: Remove excess metal or porcelain and polish surfaces of prostheses or frameworks, using polishing machines.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Monolithic CAD/CAM zirconia or lithium-disilicate crowns and small bridges: after milling and sintering the technician breaks off the sprue nub, smooths the attachment site and occlusal/interproximal surfaces, and polishes or glazes the restoration to a tissue-friendly finish before shipping.

Cast or milled metal restorations (gold, non-precious and noble full-cast crowns, copings, implant bars): cut the sprue from the casting tree, grind down the sprue button and casting nodules with stones and burs, then rubber-wheel, brush and high-shine the metal on a lathe.

Digital dentures (milled PMMA or 3D-printed) and flexible/acrylic partials: remove sprue or support nubs and support marks, smooth the flanges and polished surfaces, and bring to high shine while preserving the intaglio and tooth anatomy.

Conventionally processed (flasked, heat-cured) acrylic complete dentures: after deflasking, remove acrylic flash and stone residue with burs, refine the borders and palatal areas, then pumice on a rag-wheel lathe and finish with high-shine compound.

Cobalt-chrome removable partial denture frameworks (cast, milled or laser-sintered): remove sprues/supports, grind attachment points, smooth rests, clasps and major connectors with stones and rubber wheels, then electropolish and buff to a mirror finish without altering fit.

Layered porcelain restorations after firing (PFM, veneered zirconia) plus repairs and one-off appliances: adjust excess porcelain at contacts, margins and occlusion against the model/articulator, blend contours, and polish the ceramic or the repaired acrylic back to a smooth surface.

tasks.label: Train or supervise other dental technicians or dental laboratory bench workers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Senior technician demonstrates a fabrication technique (e.g., waxing a crown coping, setting denture teeth to an occlusal plane) at the bench for a junior bench worker, then watches the trainee attempt it and talks them through corrections.

Lead technician inspects work-in-progress or finished units produced by bench workers against the dentist's prescription and lab standards (margin fit, shade, contour, occlusion), then tells the worker what to redo and why.

Lab supervisor assigns cases across the bench each morning, tracks case status and turnaround deadlines, reprioritizes rush cases, and coordinates handoffs between departments (model, wax-up, ceramics, finishing).

Onboarding a new hire: instructing on lab safety rules, material handling, equipment operation (furnace, mill, 3D printer), and CAD design software workflows, largely through explanation, screen-sharing and written protocols.

Ongoing personnel supervision: coaching conversations, documenting performance and productivity, conducting evaluations, and enforcing quality/attendance policies for the technicians reporting to the worker.

tasks.label: Melt metals or mix plaster, porcelain, or acrylic pastes and pour materials into molds or over frameworks to form dental prostheses or apparatuses.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Model room of a commercial dental lab: technician mixes dental stone/plaster (hand or vacuum mixer), pours it into a patient impression on a vibrator, pours a base, and lets it set to produce working casts and dies; impressions vary in material and quality, casts must be bubble-free and dimensionally accurate.

Casting bench: technician mixes investment, invests sprued wax patterns in a ring, burns out, then melts alloy (Co-Cr, Ni-Cr or precious) and casts it into the mold to form crown copings, bridge substructures or removable partial denture frameworks.

Denture department: technician mixes PMMA acrylic (heat-cure dough, pour-type or injection resin) and packs/pours/injects it into the flask or mold over the tooth set-up and processes it to form complete or partial denture bases.

Ceramics bench: technician mixes porcelain powder with liquid and hand-applies, condenses and shapes successive opaque/dentin/incisal layers over a metal or zirconia framework for esthetic crowns and bridges, with shade characterization and multiple firings.

Press ceramics: technician invests the wax pattern, then loads the ring with a ceramic ingot into a press furnace so molten ceramic is pressed into the mold (e.max Press, ZirPress over zirconia, press-on-metal onto a cast framework) to form the restoration.

Appliance bench: technician mixes and pours/sprinkles self-cure or pour acrylic into molds or over frameworks to make custom impression trays, night guards/occlusal splints, orthodontic retainers and appliances, plus denture repairs and relines.

tasks.label: Prepare metal surfaces for bonding with porcelain to create artificial teeth, using small hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Single-unit porcelain-fused-to-metal coping in base-metal alloy (Ni-Cr/Co-Cr), cast or milled, at a commercial dental lab bench: cut/grind the sprue stub, contour and smooth the veneering surface with carbide burs and stones in a rotary handpiece under magnification, round sharp line angles while preserving the 0.3-0.5 mm wall, then alumina-blast (50-125 um), steam/ultrasonic clean and degas in the porcelain furnace.

Multi-unit PFM bridge framework (3-6 units) with connectors and embrasures: the same hand-tool prep over a larger, complexly shaped framework, achieving a uniform unidirectional surface texture including hard-to-reach interproximal areas, then blasting, cleaning and oxidation firing before opaque application.

High-noble/noble (gold-based) coping: contamination-sensitive prep with stones and burs reserved for noble alloys, gentler blasting pressure and media on the softer metal, oxidation firing and re-treatment of the surface before opaque; performed at the bench in a lab that also runs base metals.

Batch of laser-sintered / 3D-printed Co-Cr copings arriving attached to a build plate: cut and grind off support structures, remove partially sintered particles, even out the as-built surface, uniform alumina blasting, ultrasonic cleaning and degassing.

Repair or rework: a returned PFM unit with chipped porcelain, or a framework contaminated/over-oxidized after a failed firing - grind back porcelain to expose sound metal, judge where and how much to remove on a one-off worn part with no CAD file, re-prep, re-blast and re-oxidize the exposed metal for the repair bake.

tasks.label: Rebuild or replace linings, wire sections, or missing teeth to repair dentures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Commercial dental lab bench: repair a fractured acrylic denture base (midline crack or broken flange) on a patient's full or partial denture. Technician reassembles fragments with sticky wax, keys them in a plaster index, grinds a bevel/V-groove with a bur, applies self- or heat-cure repair acrylic, cures in a pressure pot, then trims and polishes to an invisible, non-irritating finish. Same-day/next-day turnaround.

Dental lab (or in-office lab): replace a debonded, chipped, or missing denture tooth. Grind out residual tooth and acrylic to make a retentive pocket, match mould/shade to the adjacent teeth, seat the replacement tooth in correct occlusion and esthetic position (checked against the opposing arch), secure with repair resin, then finish and polish around the gingival contour.

Dental lab: reline or rebase a denture from a dentist's wash impression taken in the patient's own denture. Box and pour the impression, mount, block out undercuts, grind out the old intaglio acrylic to uniform depth, pack or inject new resin, process, deflask, recover borders and post-dam, trim and polish without altering occlusion.

Dental lab: repair or replace a broken wrought-wire clasp or fractured cast metal component on a removable partial denture. Bend a new clasp to the abutment tooth contour on the working cast (or laser-weld/solder the framework), position and retain it, then embed in acrylic and finish; verify the RPD still seats without rocking.

Dental lab: add a tooth (and often a clasp) to an existing partial denture after an extraction, working from a dentist's impression with the partial in place. Pour and trim the cast, prepare the saddle area of the existing base, set the tooth to occlusion, process new acrylic to the old base, finish and polish.

tasks.label: Load newly constructed teeth into porcelain furnaces to bake the porcelain onto the metal framework.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Mid-size commercial dental lab: ceramist finishes an opaque or dentin/body build-up on a PFM coping or layered ceramic unit, seats the units on firing pins in a honeycomb firing tray, places the tray centered on the benchtop porcelain furnace's firing platform, selects the material-specific program (temperature, vacuum, hold), starts the cycle, then removes the tray to a draft-free cooling rack. Unfired porcelain is fragile and must not be knocked or touched.

Glaze/stain firing in a production crown-and-bridge lab: several short cycles per shift, finished crowns with applied stain/glaze slurry placed on firing pegs or a honeycomb tray and loaded into the furnace, program selected by material and shade recipe, unloaded hot and staged for cooling and inspection; surfaces must not be contaminated by contact.

Zirconia sintering / lithium-disilicate crystallization in a digital lab: milled and pre-colored units placed on sintering bead trays or crystallization pins, loaded into one of several high-temperature furnaces for long or overnight batch runs, correct program chosen per material and batch tracked to the job ticket.

Pressed-ceramic workflow: heated investment ring with ingot and plunger transferred from the burnout oven into the press furnace muffle, positioned centrally, press program started, ring removed hot after the cycle and set to bench-cool. Heavier, hotter handling than tray work.

High-volume milling center / large production lab: dozens of units per batch staged on trays and fed sequentially into a bank of furnaces on a production line, with barcode/ticket-driven program selection and continuous load/unload throughput.

One-person lab or in-office (chairside) lab: a single crown or small bridge fired in a small benchtop furnace on a cluttered shared bench, non-standard trays and pegs, technician interleaving the firing with other work and judging cycle choice ad hoc.

tasks.label: Mold wax over denture setups to form the full contours of artificial gums.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine complete denture: at a commercial lab bench the technician molds wax over an upper and/or lower tooth setup on the stone cast, building labial/buccal gum contours, palatal and lingual surfaces and periphery, producing a wax try-in denture for the dentist's try-in appointment. Repair, add-a-tooth, reline or rebase at the bench: re-waxing local gum contours on an existing patient denture or record base, blending new wax into cured acrylic, matching existing contour and thickness before reprocessing.

tasks.label: Create a model of patient's mouth by pouring plaster into a dental impression and allowing plaster to set.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Study/opposing/orthodontic model: an alginate impression in a stock tray arrives at the lab bench; the technician mixes Type III stone (often in a vacuum mixer), pours it into the impression on a bench vibrator working from one distal end so no air is trapped, forms a base with a rubber former, lets it set ~45-60 minutes, then separates the cast from the tray.

Crown-and-bridge working model: a PVS or polyether impression is poured in Type IV die stone; margins and prep detail must be reproduced bubble-free, water/powder ratio is critical, and the set model must be separated from a stiff elastomeric impression without chipping dies or thin teeth.

Complete or partial denture master cast: an edentulous custom-tray impression is beaded and boxed with wax rope/boxing strip to preserve the peripheral roll, poured in stone, allowed to set, then de-boxed and separated.

High-volume batch pouring in a production lab (ortho/retainer/nightguard/aligner shop): dozens of standardized impressions per shift, standard trays and model-base formers, a set routine with vacuum mixer and dosing unit, models poured, set and separated in batches.

Non-standard jobs: quadrant/triple-tray impressions, bite registrations, duplicating an existing denture or appliance, and impressions arriving with voids, drags or partial detachment where the technician must judge whether to pour, patch, or reject the case.

sources.claim: Two KUKA KR 1000 titan industrial robots autonomously pour molten iron into sand molds in a production foundry cell, filling molds at freely programmed points rather than a single fixed pouring station.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine-controlled pouring of a liquid that later solidifies into a fixtured mold cavity in a purpose-built cell. It shows that metered, position-controlled filling of molds is a routine deployed robotic capability, which is the core physical act of pouring stone into a fixtured impression at E1; it does not by itself show fine-detail, bubble-free filling.

sources.system: Loynds one-shot chocolate moulding line
sources.title: Advanced chocolate depositing and moulding lines
sources.claim: A commercial one-shot chocolate moulding line deposits viscous mass into detailed moulds and then vibrates each mould to drive out air bubbles and fill the cavity completely, under PLC and sensor control.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: depositing a viscous, setting material into a fine-detail mould and vibrating it bubble-free, which is mechanically the same operation and relies on the same physics (slow introduction plus vibration) that a technician uses when pouring stone into a dental impression on a bench vibrator.

sources.system: Loynds one-shot chocolate moulding line (demoulding module)
sources.title: Advanced chocolate depositing and moulding lines
sources.claim: The same moulding lines set the deposited material by cooling and then remove the solidified parts from the moulds automatically, using a twist-and-tap or vacuum demoulder.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: separating a set casting from its mould without damage, the closing step of pouring a model (separating the set stone cast from the impression tray) once the material has hardened.

sources.system: Whip Mix AquaSpense liquid dispenser
sources.title: Aquaspense Liquid Dispenser - WHIP MIX | US Dental Depot
sources.claim: Dental laboratories already use machine-controlled gypsum slurry preparation: the AquaSpense unit weighs the gypsum powder and automatically dispenses the matching measured water, removing the operator from the water/powder ratio step feeding a vacuum mixer.
sources.transferJustification: Same task, upstream sub-step: it substantiates that the mixing/dosing half of model pouring is already performed by machine in dental labs, so at E1 the correctly proportioned, vacuum-mixed stone can be presented to the pouring station.

sources.system: Perceptive batter stirring and pouring robot (RoboTouch Lab)
sources.developer: Carnegie Mellon RoboTouch Lab / Toyota Research Institute
sources.title: An Intelligent Robotic System for Perceptive Pancake Batter Stirring and Precise Pouring (arXiv:2407.01755)
sources.claim: A research robot autonomously mixes a flour-and-water suspension to a target uniformity, estimates its powder/water ratio and level from haptic sensing, and pours the viscous liquid accurately into specified shapes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: sensing-driven mixing of a powder-water slurry to a target consistency and controlled pouring of that viscous slurry to a target outline - the same control problem as mixing dental stone to the right consistency and laying it into an impression, though demonstrated on a griddle rather than a dental mould.

tasks.label: Prepare wax bite blocks and impression trays for use.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Conventional custom (special) impression tray built by hand in a full-service lab: technician receives a poured stone cast, outlines the tray border, adapts baseplate/spacer wax relief, adapts and cures a sheet of light-cure or self-cure acrylic over the cast, adds a handle and stops, trims and polishes the borders, checks it seats on the cast, and returns it with the case.

Conventional wax bite block (occlusion rim) for a complete or partial denture case: technician adapts a shellac, light-cure or acrylic record base to the cast, softens and forms a wax rim, sets it to prescribed height, width and occlusal plane with a Fox plane/rim former, seals it to the base, smooths it, and mounts the case for shipment to the dentist.

Digital-lab custom impression tray: an intraoral or model scan arrives as an STL, the tray (with spacer offset, stops and handle) is designed in dental CAD, nested and 3D printed in a biocompatible tray resin, then washed, post-cured, de-supported and inspected before shipping.

Digital-lab record base with occlusion rim / printed try-in carrying a bite block for a digital-denture case: base and rim designed from the edentulous scan, 3D printed (or milled), post-processed and shipped for the jaw-registration appointment.

Ad hoc preparation and modification of trays and rims: selecting and modifying a stock tray (adding wax stops, beading/boxing, extending borders with compound), converting a patient's existing denture into a reline tray, adding or re-shaping wax on a returned rim after a re-take, or repairing a broken bite block.

sources.title: Custom Tray Resin | Formlabs Dental

sources.title: A Digital Spin on Traditional Dentures | Glidewell Chairside Magazine

sources.claim: A dental laboratory manufacturing centre runs automation lines in which robotic arms select the correct patient-specific blank and pass it to milling machines, with little manual handling, and AI software auto-generates the design.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated lab fabrication of other patient-specific dental appliances (crowns/bridges). It shows that purpose-built cells inside dental laboratories already handle lot-size-one patient geometry, auto-generate the design and move workpieces between machines without technicians, which is the same material-handling and precision regime needed for trays and record bases.

tasks.label: Shape and solder wire and metal frames or bands for dental products, using soldering irons and hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Dental lab bench: bending stainless wire clasps and bows for removable appliances — Hawley retainer labial bows, Adams clasps, ball clasps, finger springs — adapted to a stone or printed working model before acrylic processing.

Orthodontic lab/clinic lab bench: shaping archwires and fixed lingual retainer wires (first/second/third-order bends, canine-to-canine retainer wires) to a prescribed arch form for a specific patient.

Dental lab bench: fabricating fixed band-and-wire appliances (lingual holding arch, transpalatal arch, Nance button, band-and-loop space maintainer) — contouring the wire to the model, positioning molar bands, waxing up, investing and free-hand torch soldering with silver solder, then finishing the joints.

Dental lab bench: repairing or modifying an existing patient appliance — soldering or laser-welding a replacement wrought-wire clasp onto a broken partial denture framework, adding a rest or loop for a tooth addition, repairing a fractured lingual bar on a repair cast.

Dental lab / crown-and-bridge bench: joining cast metal frameworks for fixed and implant prostheses — soldering sectioned bridge segments, assembling and joining implant bar components, correcting fit of a framework by section-and-solder.

sources.system: Coherent ExactWeld 410 / 430

sources.title: Implant-supported bars & bridges | CADstar
sources.claim: Implant bars and bridges are routinely produced as one piece by CAD/CAM milling in a milling centre, removing the soldered or laser-welded connections that the technician would otherwise have to make.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: producing the joined metal framework for a fixed/implant prosthesis. The accepted output (a passively fitting one-piece framework) is the same deliverable the technician produces by sectioning and soldering, made instead by a purpose-built machining cell.

sources.system: Metal laser-sintered (3D-printed) band-and-loop space maintainers
sources.title: Effectiveness of traditional band and loop space maintainer vs 3D-printed space maintainer following the loss of primary teeth: a randomized clinical trial (PMC)
sources.claim: Randomised clinical trial comparing machine-produced (metal 3D-printed) band-and-loop space maintainers with conventional band-and-loop maintainers made by adjusting bands and soldering wires found higher survival for the printed appliances at nine months.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: producing the band-and-wire fixed appliance whose conventional route is contouring wire and torch-soldering it to bands. The machine route yields the same clinically accepted appliance, so the instance's output is achievable inside a purpose-built production machine.

tasks.label: Fill chipped or low spots in surfaces of devices, using acrylic resins.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Commercial dental lab bench: after deflasking/processing a conventional heat-cured complete denture, the technician inspects the pink acrylic base under magnification, finds porosity voids and low spots at the flange border and palatal surface, roughens them with a bur, applies monomer then sprinkles/brushes PMMA powder-liquid acrylic bead by bead to slightly overfill, cures in a pressure pot, then trims, contours to the surrounding anatomy (rugae, festooning) and polishes to high gloss without altering the intaglio fit surface.

Repair work on a patient's returned denture in a lab or in-office lab: a chipped acrylic flange, a divot near a denture tooth neck, or a chipped/missing acrylic segment; the technician cleans and disinfects the appliance, grinds a bevel/undercut, mixes self-cure repair acrylic, packs it into the defect matching the shade of the existing pink or tooth-colored resin, cures, then trims and polishes to blend with the surrounding surface, often on a same-day turnaround.

Orthodontic and occlusal appliance work (Hawley retainer, bite splint, night guard, space maintainer): filling voids, bubbles, or low spots in the acrylic body or around embedded wires with self-cure acrylic using the salt-and-pepper technique, then curing, trimming around the wires, and polishing the thin, contoured acrylic without distorting the appliance or occlusal surface.

Removable partial denture: adding acrylic to low spots or deficient areas of the acrylic saddle, at the metal framework/acrylic junction, or over a reline where the resin fell short; requires the added resin to bond to both metal and old acrylic, to be contoured around clasps and finish lines, and to be polished without abrading the framework.

Digitally fabricated device (3D-printed or milled denture base, printed splint, or bonded-tooth digital denture): filling support-mark divots, small print voids, or gaps at bonded tooth sockets with flowable light-cured or self-cure resin, light-curing, then trimming and polishing the local area to match the machine-produced surface.

sources.system: Universal Robots UR5 cells at Glidewell Laboratories
sources.title: The Crowning Conclusion: Universal Robots Saves 9 Hours of Production Time at Glidewell Laboratories
sources.claim: Robotic automation actually deployed in a large US dental laboratory is limited to material handling and machine tending (loading crown blanks into CNC mills), not to freehand acrylic repair or contour finishing of removable appliances.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: dental-lab machine tending. Cited to show the state of robotics inside dental labs: pick-and-place of standardized blanks in a fixtured cell. It does not substantiate defect assessment, acrylic resin application, curing, or blend-polishing of a chipped denture, so it cannot support a positive judgment for this task.

sources.system: 3M Finesse-it Robotic Paint Repair System
sources.date: 2022 (RBR50 award; system commercially deployed at automotive plants)
sources.title: 3M Finesse-It Robotic Paint Repair System Fixes Paint Defects on Assembly Lines - The Robot Report
sources.claim: An autonomous vision-guided robotic system detects surface defects and repairs them by sanding and polishing on an automotive assembly line, but it removes material rather than filling defects with resin, and works on large sheet-metal panels.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated defect finding and finishing of a surface defect. Transfer fails: the system only abrades and buffs a painted panel in a fenced line; it does not roughen an undercut, mix and place acrylic monomer-polymer into a chip, cure it, or re-contour millimetre-scale denture anatomy, so it cannot complete this instance.

sources.system: Acme Manufacturing RFP (robotic finishing and polishing) series
sources.title: Adaptive Robotic Finishing Raises the Bar for Medical Manufacturing | IMTS
sources.claim: Adaptive robotic finishing systems can scan a small freeform medical part, generate polishing paths and polish it to specification inside a purpose-built cell, but they perform material removal only and do not add or cure resin into defects.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic polishing of patient-specific freeform medical parts. It substantiates only the finishing sub-step in an E1 cell on rigid metal implants; it does not substantiate assessing a chip, dispensing and curing acrylic repair resin, or blending the addition into surrounding pink/tooth-shaded acrylic, so it cannot complete the whole instance.

sources.system: Robotic automated composite repair multi-tool (KUKA-mounted) / Automated Epoxy Extruder
sources.developer: University/industry research consortium (reported in composite repair literature)
sources.title: (PDF) Automated Repair of Carbon Fiber Composites on AAM Vehicles
sources.claim: Automated composite repair research tools mounted on industrial robots can sand out a cavity ... damage and apply adhesive/patch material, but these are large-scale aerospace research demonstrations, not fine acrylic prosthesis repair.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic filling of a surface defect with resin. Transfer fails: it is an unclear-autonomy research demonstration on large flat/gently curved aerospace panels with prefabricated patches, not sub-millimetre free-form acrylic build-up, curing and gloss polishing on a hand-sized denture; it cannot support a positive judgment.

roles.description: Construct, maintain, or repair medical supportive devices such as braces, orthotics and prosthetic devices, joints, arch supports, and other surgical and medical appliances.

tasks.label: Repair, modify, or maintain medical supportive devices, such as artificial limbs, braces, or surgical supports, according to specifications.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Lower-limb prosthesis brought back to the O&P lab for component service: technician inspects the used limb, diagnoses a broken/worn part (foot, pylon, adapter, knee unit, suspension sleeve or liner), disassembles it, swaps the component, torques fasteners to the manufacturer's spec, restores bench alignment and cosmesis, and bench-tests before return to the patient.

Socket/interface modification in the lab after a fitting: grinding trim lines, spot-heating and reshaping thermoplastic to relieve a pressure point, adding pads/build-ups, re-lining or re-gluing a socket liner, and re-finishing edges to a spec noted by the practitioner.

Orthosis repair in the lab: AFO/KAFO/spinal brace with worn straps, Velcro, padding, rivets, joints or corroded uprights; technician cuts and rivets new straps, re-glues padding, replaces or re-aligns a joint, reshapes plastic with a heat gun, and finishes edges.

Foot orthotic / arch support / orthopedic shoe modification done by hand: replacing worn top covers with adhesive, adding metatarsal pads or wedges, splitting and re-cementing a shoe sole for a heel lift or rocker, and hand-grinding the result to blend.

Machining-type modification of a device shell to a specified geometry: an existing plastic or laminated composite shell/socket is fixtured and its trim lines lowered, strap slots or hardware holes drilled, or posting ground to a digitally specified shape in the lab's carving/milling equipment.

Chairside adjustment in a clinic fitting room or at a hospital bedside with the patient present: flaring a brim with a heat gun, trimming a strap, tightening or replacing a bolt, adjusting a joint stop, and re-checking fit on the patient within the appointment.

Repair/adjustment away from the lab: mobile service call, school visit, nursing home or field/mobile clinic, where the technician works out of a tool kit on whatever surface is available and improvises with the parts on hand.

sources.system: Ortis (Essential/Pro/Enterprise)
sources.title: Ortis™ Roboticom: high precision robot for orthopedic applications
sources.claim: Ortis is a commercial 7-axis robotic machining cell sold to orthotics and prosthetics labs; besides carving positive/negative models it performs trimming and drilling of plastic and composite patient-specific components under CAD-generated programs in an enclosed cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic carving/trimming/drilling of O&P workpieces in a fixtured cell. It transfers to the machining-type modification instance because the objects (plastic/composite orthosis shells and sockets), the required precision, and the fixtured lab-cell environment are the same; it does not transfer to hand repairs involving straps, adhesives, heat-gun reshaping, or diagnosis of used devices.

sources.system: Ortis Pro robotic milling system
sources.title: Ortis Pro Robotic Milling System
sources.claim: The Ortis Pro robotic milling system is marketed as producing the models used to create custom orthoses, prostheses, leg-foot braces, corsets, sockets and cranial helmets — i.e. automation in O&P labs targets model carving and fabrication, not repair of returned devices.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated fabrication of new O&P devices/models. Cited to show the scope of deployed O&P automation; it does not substantiate repair, component replacement or hand modification of an existing patient device.

sources.system: Orion orthotics manufacturing platform
sources.title: Traditional vs. 3D Printed Orthotics: The Complete Guide to Custom 3D Printed Insoles
sources.claim: Automation offered to orthotics labs today is an additive-manufacturing production platform for making new insoles, not a system that services or repairs existing devices.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated production of custom foot orthoses. Cited as the state of lab automation; it makes new devices from digital files and does not modify, re-cover or repair a patient's existing orthotic.

sources.system: Disassembly CPS (six-axis robot disassembly workcells)
sources.title: Appliance Manufacturer Uses Robots and AI to Disassemble Products
sources.claim: The closest analogue to repair-style work on used, variable products under machine control is robotic disassembly of end-of-life appliances in a workcell, which is still a development program rather than a deployed capability.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic teardown of used consumer products. Even this nearest analogue is limited to disassembly of rigid, mass-produced housings in a cell, with autonomy not established; it does not substantiate diagnosing and rebuilding a one-off custom orthosis or prosthesis to worker quality.

sources.system: manual oscillating-saw / grinder trimming (no robotic system)
sources.title: A New Approach to Trimming CAD/CAM Prosthetic Sockets
sources.claim: Finishing and trimming operations on prosthetic sockets in O&P labs are performed by hand with powered saws and grinders, indicating that even the machining-adjacent parts of device repair remain manual practice.
sources.transferJustification: Not a robotic system; cited only as context for the negative judgments that lab repair and finishing of O&P devices is hand work.

tasks.label: Polish artificial limbs, braces, or supports, using grinding and buffing wheels.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Central fabrication / O&P lab: after lamination or thermoforming, the technician buffs the exterior of a one-off prosthetic socket or cosmetic cover (acrylic/epoxy laminate, carbon composite, or thermoplastic) on bench grinding and buffing wheels to a smooth, glossy finish, blending seams and avoiding burn-through or heat distortion.

O&P lab: a custom thermoformed orthosis (AFO, KAFO shell, wrist splint, spinal orthosis) is trimmed, then its trimlines and edges are ground, rounded, chamfered and buffed smooth on a wheel so no sharp edge contacts the patient; each shell is a unique patient-specific shape.

O&P lab: metal components of braces and limbs — stainless/aluminum/titanium uprights, bars, joints, brackets, welded assemblies — are deburred, ground and buffed to a clean, bright finish on belt grinders and buffing wheels.

Foot-orthotics lab: custom foot orthoses / arch supports (polypropylene or graphite shells, EVA posts, bonded top covers) are edge-ground to the outline and sanded/buffed smooth on grinders, in semi-repetitive batches of patient-specific pairs.

Clinic back-room lab: after a fitting, the practitioner marks a relief or a modified strap slot/edge; the technician grinds out that local area on the finished device and re-smooths and buffs only the modified region, judging blend and finish by hand and eye against the patient's device.

O&P lab: buffing/finishing of soft or deformable components — leather-covered brace parts, foam liners, padded straps, cork/EVA build-ups — where the workpiece flexes under the wheel and finish is judged by feel.

sources.system: Acme RFP Series Robotic Finishing & Polishing System (FANUC robots, ATI tool changers)
sources.title: Adaptive Robotic Finishing Raises the Bar for Medical Manufacturing | IMTS
sources.claim: Acme Manufacturing's RFP robotic finishing/polishing cell scans each patient-specific knee implant and auto-generates a polishing path for its unique geometry, running a four-step abrasive-belt sequence with programmable compliance; deployed at Hammill Medical, with 250+ systems in the medical space.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic polishing of patient-specific orthopedic implants. It is the same operation class as this task — a robot manipulating a one-off custom medical device against abrasive belts and buffing heads to a specified finish — at tighter tolerances and on harder materials than prosthetic/orthotic shells, so surface-finish capability carries over.

sources.system: Acme robotic finishing cell for medical implants
sources.title: Medical Implant Robotic Metal Finishing — Acme Manufacturing
sources.claim: Acme's robotic finishing cells replace manual surface finishing of medical implants, performing belt grinding, flash removal, and cut/color/high-color buffing with programmable compliance on hips, knees, tibia trays, bone ... and nails in cobalt chrome, titanium and zirconium.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic metal grinding and buffing of implant hardware. Comparable metals, comparable buffing wheels and belts, and a comparable required finish to brace uprights, bars and joints.

sources.system: Scan&Sand / Scan&Polish (GMR-AI) with FANUC CRX cobot
sources.title: CRX Cobot & AI Solve Sanding Challenges for Performance Composites — FANUC America
sources.claim: GrayMatter Robotics' Scan&Sand / Scan&Polish combine 3D vision with active compliant tooling so a robot or cobot autonomously sands, buffs, polishes and trims high-mix parts; deployed at Performance Composites on fiberglass/composite products, programming itself and deploying on existing shop floors.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous high-mix surface finishing of one-off composite/plastic parts. Same freeform curved geometries, same abrasive/buffing media and force-controlled contact as buffing a laminated socket or orthosis shell; each part is scanned rather than pre-programmed.

sources.system: GrayMatter physical-AI robotic finishing cells
sources.title: GrayMatter Robotics Unveils 100,000-Square-Foot AI Robotics Innovation Center in Carson
sources.claim: GrayMatter's Carson innovation center houses more than 20 working robotic cells in which AI-powered robots autonomously sand, grind, ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic buffing/polishing across materials. Establishes that the same cells extend beyond sanding to buffing and polishing operations equivalent to those used on limbs, braces and supports.

sources.system: Ortis (ABB/KUKA 6-axis robot plus rotary 7th axis)
sources.title: Ortis™ Roboticom: high precision robot for orthopedic applications
sources.claim: Roboticom's Ortis is a 7-axis robotic cell sold specifically to orthotics and prosthetics facilities; it carves positive and negative models in plaster, polyurethane and soft foam and trims and drills plastic and composite AFO/KAFO, corset and seating components, with installations in orthopedic facilities worldwide.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic material removal (carving, trimming, drilling) on patient-specific O&P devices and models inside O&P fabrication labs. Same workpieces, materials (thermoplastic, carbon composite, foam) and lab setting as the polishing step, showing the fixturing and part presentation for these devices is solved.

sources.system: SandRob
sources.title: SandRob™ Roboticom: high Precision and Versatility in Surface Finishing
sources.claim: Roboticom's SandRob is a force-controlled 7-axis robotic surface-finishing cell performing sanding, polishing, grinding/deburring and trimming on plastics, composites, metals and high-gloss painted surfaces, with installed systems at industrial customers who automated grinding and polishing of parts.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic grinding and polishing of plastic and composite parts to a gloss finish, by the same vendor whose robots already work O&P materials, so the abrasive process and force control transfer to buffing sockets and orthosis shells.

tasks.label: Construct or receive casts or impressions of patients' torsos or limbs for use as cutting and fabrication patterns.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Central-fabrication / device-manufacturing lab intake: shipped cartons arrive containing plaster negative wraps, foam impression boxes or slipper casts; technician unpacks, matches the cast to the enclosed order form, prescription and measurement chart, checks the negative for cracks or missing anatomy, assigns/writes a job number and stages it for pouring or digitizing. Lab receiving area of a manufacturing facility.

In-house receipt at a patient-care O&P facility: the practitioner brings a freshly wrapped negative cast, foam box or torso wrap back from the fitting room; the technician takes custody, confirms patient/job details and casting notes, marks the cast, and racks it in the lab for fabrication. Standard clinic-attached lab.

Technician takes a plaster-wrap negative cast of a patient's residual limb (transtibial/transfemoral) in a clinic casting room: dons sock or liner, palpates and pen-marks bony prominences and tendon reliefs, wraps plaster bandage, hand-molds reliefs and holds the limb in alignment while it cures, then cuts and removes the cast intact.

Cast of a patient's torso/trunk for a spinal orthosis or body jacket (e.g., scoliosis TLSO, often a child or a patient with limited trunk control): stockinette applied, plaster bandage wrapped around the trunk while corrective pressure is held over pads, patient standing or in a traction frame, cast then cut off with shears without injuring skin.

Foot impression for custom foot orthotics in a clinic or pedorthic retail setting: patient's foot held in subtalar neutral while pressed into a foam impression box, wrapped in a plaster slipper cast, or pressed onto a pin-array contact digitizer under operator-controlled pressure; impression checked for a usable arch and heel capture.

Digital capture replacing a physical cast: technician marks landmarks on the patient, positions the limb, torso or infant cranium, sweeps a handheld 3D scanner, checks the mesh for holes/motion artifacts and adds tape/caliper measurements so the file can serve as the fabrication pattern. Clinic room.

tasks.label: Test medical supportive devices for proper alignment, movement, or biomechanical stability, using meters and alignment fixtures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In the O&P fabrication lab, a technician mounts a newly assembled transtibial/transfemoral prosthesis in an alignment jig or transfer fixture and verifies bench alignment against the prescription: socket flexion/adduction angles, A-P and M-L offset of the foot relative to the reference/plumb (or laser) line, and overall length, then documents the result before the device goes to dynamic fitting.

Post-fabrication functional check of an orthosis (AFO, KAFO, knee brace, spinal orthosis) at the bench: free motion and range of the joints/hinges, lock and stop engagement, hinge axis alignment to the marked anatomical axis, and shell/strut rigidity, checked with goniometers, gauges and manual flexing against acceptance criteria.

Strength and stability load testing of a finished prosthesis, pylon/adapter assembly or reinforced brace in a central-fabrication or manufacturer QC test area: static proof loading and/or cyclic loading in a test fixture with load/deflection meters, to confirm the assembly is structurally stable before release.

Dynamic/biomechanical check with the patient wearing the device in the clinic fitting room: patient stands on a force-line meter (e.g., laser posture unit) or pressure platform and walks a short course while the technician reads the meters, judges load line, movement and stability, adjusts and re-tests.

Verification of custom foot orthoses/arch supports and diabetic insoles in the lab: posting angles, heel cup and arch height, that the device sits flat without rock or twist on a flat plate, and appropriate rigidity/flex, checked against the prescription and positive model with gauges and a flat reference surface.

Post-repair verification of a worn device brought in by a patient (broken KAFO joint, replaced prosthetic knee unit, re-riveted brace, refurbished suspension): after repair the technician checks joint movement, alignment relative to the original setup, and load stability by hand and with simple meters before returning it, with criteria set case by case.

tasks.label: Drill and tap holes for rivets, and glue, weld, bolt, or rivet parts together to form prosthetic or orthotic devices.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Bench assembly of a modular lower-limb prosthesis in an O&P fabrication lab: bolting the socket adapter, pylon/tube clamp, knee and foot together with cap screws and set screws, applying threadlocker and torquing each fastener to the manufacturer's spec; sometimes drilling and tapping the lamination attachment plate first.

Finishing a custom vacuum-formed or 3D-printed AFO/KAFO/TLSO shell: marking and drilling holes through the plastic, positioning webbing straps, D-rings and buckles, and setting rivets with a hand press or pop-rivet tool, then gluing padding over the rivet heads.

Joining metal parts of a custom orthosis or prosthesis: drilling and tapping holes in aluminum or steel sidebars and stirrups, bolting or riveting knee/ankle joints to uprights, and welding or brazing metal bars, shoe stirrups or frame members.

Adhesive bonding work: cementing EVA/foam posts, wedges and top covers onto foot orthoses, gluing leather covers to metal uprights, bonding liners, cosmetic covers and shoe modifications, with contact cement applied to contoured custom surfaces and clamped or pressed until cured.

Repair of a worn patient-owned device brought back to the lab or clinic, often while the patient waits: drilling out a broken rivet, re-riveting a torn strap, re-gluing a delaminated pad or liner, replacing a stripped bolt on a device of unknown prior construction and unpredictable damage.

sources.system: Messer inkjet marker / Multi-Jet marking head on CNC cutting machines
sources.title: Inkjet Marking Machine | Messer Cutting Systems

sources.system: Hypertherm CNC plasma marking (mechanized cutting table)

sources.claim: Mechanized CNC plasma marking is used to indicate layouts, bending and scoring ... on metal plate with precisely controlled depth, replacing soapstone/ink hand layout.

sources.system: TRUMPF marking lasers with VisionLine Detect / VisionLine Model

sources.system: Robotic trimming / 5-axis CNC router trim cells for thermoformed parts
sources.title: Robotic Trimming and CNC Router Trimming | Productive Plastics

sources.transferJustification: Related task: laying out and executing the trim line on a vacuum-formed shell, the same workpiece type as an AFO or check socket; it demonstrates E1-level (fixtured) capability and simultaneously shows why the capability does not extend to unfixtured bench work.
