sources.transferJustification: Related task: transferring patient-specific dimensions onto orthotic stock. The mill executes the same dimensional layout the technician would mark on a blank with template and calipers, on the same materials, inside an enclosed machine.

tasks.label: Cover or pad metal or plastic structures or devices, using coverings such as rubber, leather, felt, plastic, or fiberglass.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: O&P fabrication lab: lining/padding the inside of a custom thermoplastic orthosis (AFO, spinal jacket, cranial helmet) with closed-cell foam, felt or plush — cutting the material to a pattern, brushing/spraying contact cement, conforming it over compound curves without wrinkles, pressing and trimming edges flush.

Central-fabrication or lab bench: bonding top covers (leather, vinyl, EVA, Poron) onto custom foot-orthotic shells and arch supports — cement, vacuum/press bond, then grind and skive the covered edge flush to the shell.

Clinic fitting room / adjacent adjustment bench: adding small relief pads (felt, moleskin, PPT) at pressure points identified and hand-marked during a patient fitting, with the patient waiting for the device to go back on.

Bench work on metal-component orthoses: covering metal uprights, knee/ankle joints and calf/thigh bands of a KAFO or HKAFO with leather or plastic — wrapping and cementing the covering around curved bars and bands, then riveting or stitching the seam.

Lamination area of an O&P lab: covering a device or positive model with fiberglass/carbon reinforcement — pulling and wetting out fiberglass over a socket mold or reinforcing a brace with composite, then curing and trimming.

sources.system: RoboTape (Innovative Automation)
sources.title: Automated Tape Dispense System Increases Throughput
sources.claim: RoboTape is a commercial robotic system that feeds and dispenses adhesive-backed foam and felt material onto contoured parts inside production cells, applying controlled press force after placement.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic application of adhesive-backed foam/felt padding to contoured automotive parts held in fixtures. The materials (foam, felt, adhesive backing), the curved plastic substrate and the required press-down adhesion match padding an orthosis shell; only part geometry differs.

sources.system: Grabit Stackit
sources.title: Grabit Robots Use Static Electricity to Make Nikes Faster than Human
sources.claim: Grabit's Stackit electroadhesion robots pick and precisely stack the dozens of limp leather/textile pieces that form Nike shoe uppers, installed in Nike factories in Mexico and China.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: precise machine placement and bonding of limp leather/fabric coverings in a purpose-built cell. Covering a medical appliance needs the same handling of compliant sheet coverings onto a rigid substrate at comparable placement precision.

sources.system: Real-time 3D vision-based robotic adhesive spraying cell
sources.title: Real-Time 3D Vision-Based Robotic Path Planning for Automated Adhesive Spraying on Lasted Uppers in Footwear Manufacturing
sources.claim: A vision-guided robotic cell reconstructs each individual lasted upper with 3D scanning and generates a customized adhesive-spraying path executed by a six-axis arm, handling part-to-part geometry variation without reprogramming.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: applying contact cement to individually varying curved leather/plastic surfaces. Cementing a one-off orthotic shell or top cover requires the same per-part path generation from a scan, comparable coverage precision, and the same adhesives.

sources.system: Robot-based shoe upper/sole manufacturing testbed
sources.title: Robot-Based Automation for Upper and Sole Manufacturing in Shoe Production
sources.claim: An industrial robot cell with 3D scanning and a cementing tool performed roughing and cementing of shoe uppers and soles on a demonstrative production line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic surface preparation and adhesive application on leather/rubber footwear parts — the same roughen-cement-bond sequence used to attach leather or EVA covers to orthotic shells.

sources.system: Cevotec SAMBA fiber patch placement (Patch2Patient)

sources.transferJustification: Directly related: robotic placement of fiber-reinforcement patches over patient-specific prosthetic/orthotic geometry is the machine equivalent of covering a device or positive model with fiberglass/carbon reinforcement.

sources.system: Steptics automated filament winding line
sources.title: Filament winding increases access to high-performance composite prostheses
sources.claim: Steptics industrialized production of carbon-fiber prostheses by winding resin-impregnated fiber onto mandrels carrying the inner geometry of the prosthesis, enabling hundreds of parts per day.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine-applied composite covering of a mandrel/positive model with resin-wetted fiber — the automated analogue of hand-laminating fiberglass over a prosthetic model.

sources.system: Ortis (Roboticom)
sources.title: Ortis™ Roboticom: high precision robot for orthopedic applications
sources.claim: Roboticom's Ortis robot cell is sold to orthopedic workshops to carve patient-specific positive and negative models for ... in plaster, foam and polyurethane.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot cells already work on patient-specific O&P geometry inside fabrication facilities, showing one-off device geometries can be presented to and handled by a fixtured robotic cell (the E1 counterfactual).

tasks.label: Order parts or supplies for orthotic or prosthetic devices.
Mix pigments to match patients' skin coloring, according to formulas, and apply mixtures to orthotic or prosthetic devices.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Definitive lower-limb prosthesis in an O&P fabrication lab: technician tints lamination resin or a topcoat with pigments per a written formula to the patient's skin tone/selected shade and applies it as an even coat over the rigid socket/frame in the lab spray booth, then cures it.

Foam or laminated cosmetic cover for a limb prosthesis: technician mixes skin-tone paint or pigmented coating per formula and sprays it over the shaped cover to a single blended tone with light shading at the edges; done at the bench/booth in the lab.

High-definition silicone restoration (partial finger/hand, ear, nose, orbital, or silicone limb skin): intrinsic pigment mixing into silicone plus hand-layered extrinsic coloration - mottling, veining, freckles, nail beds - built up in thin translucent layers to match living tissue.

Chairside color work at a fitting/delivery appointment: technician mixes a small batch of pigment, applies it to the device, holds it against the patient's sound limb or face under room and natural light, and iterates until the patient and clinician accept the match.

Orthoses (cranial remolding helmet, AFO, spinal brace, hand orthosis): pigmenting or painting the shell to a selected skin tone or decorative color, uniform coat over a cleaned/masked shell in the lab booth, then cured.

sources.system: ABB PixelPaint on IRB 5500 paint robot
sources.title: ABB deploys PixelPaint at Mercedes-Benz plant in Germany - The Robot Report
sources.claim: ABB's PixelPaint robotic paint head (1,000+ individually controlled nozzles on an IRB 5500 paint robot with 3D vision) applies precise color areas and intricate multi-color designs to curved vehicle bodies in a fully automated paint-shop process; deployed in series production at Mercedes-Benz Sindelfingen since early 2025.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic application of pigmented coatings, including graded and patterned two-tone color, to a fixtured curved workpiece in a booth. Transfers to applying a tinted finish to a prosthetic socket or cosmetic cover: same act (controlled deposition of a mixed color coating on a contoured shell), with far finer positional precision than a cosmesis topcoat requires; the workpiece is larger but the coating operation is the same.

sources.system: Robotic Helmet Painting Machine (6-axis spray painting robot cell)
sources.title: Automatic Helmet Spray Painting Machine - Robotic Paint Group Ltd
sources.claim: A commercially sold robotic spray-painting cell paints helmet shells: the helmet is carried on a chain conveyor through a spray booth and the painting machine traces the conveyor and coats the part automatically, with workers only loading and unloading.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic spray coating of small curved shells. A safety helmet shell is close in size, geometry and material (thermoplastic/composite) to a prosthetic socket, a shaped cosmetic cover, or a cranial remolding helmet, and the required output - an even, cosmetically acceptable colored coat - is the same.

sources.system: Axalta Irus Mix (with Irus Scan)
sources.title: Axalta Irus Mix
sources.claim: Axalta Irus Mix is a commercially sold, fully automated paint mixing machine used in collision repair shops: it dispenses and mixes the colorants of a selected formula hands-free, with automated dosing for accurate, repeatable color; paired with Irus Scan spectrophotometric color reading to select the formula.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mixing a coating to a stated formula. The task's mixing step - dosing pigments per a formula to hit a specified color - is exactly what this machine does physically and hands-free, with a spectrophotometer-derived formula standing in for the skin-tone formula the technician works from.

sources.system: COROB automatic dispensers (e.g., D410x, EVOPWR)

sources.claim: COROB automatic paint dispensers are widely sold machines that dose colorants to a stored formula for retailers and manufacturers, marketed on custom color accuracy and repeatability of tinting.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: formula-driven colorant dispensing and mixing. Corroborates that machine mixing of pigments to a numeric formula, at accuracies buyers accept for color-critical work, is routine commercial equipment.

sources.system: Graco ProMix PD / 2KS / 3KS proportioners with robotic automatic spray guns
sources.title: Paint Automation - Robotic Paint Systems | Graco
sources.claim: Graco supplies proportioning and meter-mix systems (ProMix PD, 2KS/3KS) that mix multi-component coatings close to the spray gun and integrate directly with painting robots and reciprocators in automated paint lines.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated mixing of multi-component pigmented material feeding a robotic applicator. Shows the mix step and the apply step exist as one integrated machine line, which is what an E1 cell for tinting and coating a prosthetic shell would use.

tasks.label: Service or repair machinery used in the fabrication of appliances.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Post-use cleaning of fabrication machinery in the O&P lab: blowing/vacuuming plaster and thermoplastic dust off the bench router/grinder table and hood, clearing the carver bed and dust pickups, wiping down the oven racks and vacuum-forming table so the next job runs clean.

Scheduled preventive-maintenance round on shop equipment: emptying or replacing dust-collector bags and cleaning cartridge filters, cleaning the plaster trap, greasing/oiling bearings and slides, checking and tensioning/tracking drive belts, draining the air compressor, checking guards and dust hoods.

Replacing worn consumables and tooling on shaping machines: swapping sanding cones/drums and hook-and-loop discs on the bench router head, changing abrasive belts on the belt sander, changing carbide burrs and carver/router bits, band-saw blades and buffing wheels, then re-tightening and test-running.

Diagnosing and repairing a breakdown mid-production: grinder motor won't start or overheats, vacuum pump loses suction, thermoforming oven element or thermostat fails, foot switch/wiring or contactor faults, worn bearings or a broken drive belt — troubleshoot, disassemble, source and fit the replacement part, reassemble and test.

Servicing and calibrating the CNC carver / thermoforming or vacuum system: cleaning and lubricating rails and lead screws, changing spindle collets, checking runout and axis alignment/squareness, recalibrating probes or limit sensors, replacing worn rollers, gaskets or vacuum seals, applying firmware/controller updates and running verification cuts.

Servicing small bench equipment used for soft goods and finishing: industrial sewing machine (needles, timing, thread tension, bobbin race cleaning and oiling), heat gun, rotary handpiece motor brushes, drill press chuck and small hand-tool repair.

sources.system: FerRobotics abrasive (sandpaper) changing station with ACF sanding units
sources.title: Sandpaper changing station - FerRobotics
sources.claim: FerRobotics sells a patented abrasive/media changing station and magazine that automatically strips the worn abrasive disc off a robotic sanding unit and fits a fresh one, marketed for unmanned operation in fully automated grinding/sanding cells; deployed in automotive paint-repair cells (SEAT Cupra case study).
sources.transferJustification: Related task: replacing worn abrasive media on a powered sanding/grinding machine. This is the same service action and the same class of consumable (hook-and-loop abrasive discs/pads) that a medical appliance technician performs on lab sanders and router heads, done unattended inside a robot cell.

sources.system: ANCA TXcell / Dual Robot grinding cell
sources.title: Dual Robot Grinding Cell | ANCA's Advanced CNC Automation Solution
sources.claim: ANCA's TXcell automated CNC grinding cell uses a robot that automatically loads grinding wheel packs as well as workpieces, so tooling changeovers on the grinding machine happen unmanned inside the enclosed cell; a second robot adds secondary operations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: changing the abrasive wheel/tooling on a grinding machine. Comparable objects (mounted abrasive wheel packs vs. sanding cones/drums on an O&P router head) and comparable precision (spindle mounting, clamped and run-out checked), performed by the robot without an operator.

sources.system: Kawasaki machine-tending robot cells with air blow-off end effector
sources.title: Machine Tending | Robotic Applications | Complete Guide
sources.claim: In standard robotic machine-tending cells the robot itself performs the routine cleaning step an operator would otherwise do, using an air blow-off end effector to clear chips, dust and coolant from the machine fixture every cycle.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: cleaning dust and swarf off a shaping machine's work area after use. Same action (blow-down of a machine table/fixture), same debris class (dry dust and chips), run autonomously as part of the cell cycle.

sources.system: Tianxun (2nd generation) data-centre O&M robot
sources.title: Alibaba Cloud Enables Five Super Data Centers to Support Double 11
sources.claim: Alibaba's second-generation Tianxun data-centre operations robot works without human intervention to inspect racks, locate faulty hard disks and physically replace them; Alibaba reported it in operation across five of its data centres.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fault-triggered component replacement on machinery inside a structured facility. It is the closest deployed case, but it covers only standardized tool-free hot-swap modules in uniform racks, not diagnosis, fastener removal, wiring or bearing/element replacement on varied shop machines, so it does not transfer to repairing fabrication equipment.

sources.system: UR10e vision-guided robotic unscrewing system for e-waste disassembly
sources.developer: academic research group (published in Robotics and Computer-Integrated Manufacturing)
sources.title: Robotic system for automated disassembly of electronic waste: Unscrewing
sources.claim: A research system combining a UR10e arm, a RealSense ... mechatronic screwdriver autonomously located and removed screws from a real recycled hoverboard on a laboratory bench, demonstrating automated unscrewing as a disassembly sub-step.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: removing fasteners to open a machine for repair. It substantiates only the unscrewing sub-step on a single known product in a lab rig, not fault diagnosis, part sourcing, refitting and functional test of shop machinery.

tasks.label: Take patients' body or limb measurements for use in device construction.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Clinic or medical-supply/DME store: technician measures a cooperative, standing or seated adult for a custom-fitted or custom-fabricated limb orthosis, support or compression garment - tape/caliper circumferences and lengths at defined anatomical points on thigh, calf, ankle, forearm or wrist, recorded on the manufacturer's measurement form.

Prosthetics fitting room: technician measures a residual limb for a socket - circumferences at 2-inch intervals, AP/ML dimensions, limb length, palpating and marking bony landmarks (fibular head, tibial crest, distal end), often alongside a plaster wrap cast; limb may be recent post-op, sensitive or volume-changing.

Orthotics clinic/lab: shape capture and measurement of the foot for custom arch supports/foot orthoses - holding the foot in subtalar neutral for a foam-box or plaster slipper impression, plus foot length/width, shoe size and arch measurements, patient prone or seated.

Clinic: torso measurement for a spinal orthosis, TLSO or body jacket - chest, waist, hip circumferences, trunk heights and landmark levels on a standing or seated patient, sometimes with a torso cast or scan.

Pediatric/cranial clinic: measuring an infant's head for a cranial remolding helmet, or measuring a young child for a brace - the patient cannot hold still or follow instructions and must be held and soothed while circumference, diagonals and shape data are captured.

Hospital ward, rehab unit or nursing home bedside: measuring a non-ambulatory patient (post-op, edematous, contracted or wound-dressed limb) who cannot stand; technician supports and positions the limb by hand, works around dressings and adjusts for swelling.

sources.system: Bauerfeind Bodytronic 600
sources.title: Special use for customized orthotics - Bauerfeind life
sources.claim: Bauerfeind's Bodytronic 600 is a commercially deployed measurement system in medical supply stores: the patient stands on a motorized platform that rotates while the system projects light patterns and automatically records body measurements.

sources.system: Bauerfeind Bodytronic 600
sources.title: Special use for customized orthotics - Bauerfeind life
sources.claim: The same deployment produced enough 3D data from the automated upper-body scan of an elderly patient to manufacture a corset (spinal orthosis) of acceptable quality, replacing manual torso measurement/casting.

sources.system: Bauerfeind Bodytronic 600

sources.claim: Bodytronic 600 automatically extracts the product-specific measuring points and dimensions needed to size and make knee/ankle orthoses, supports and compression stockings, i.e. it performs the landmark-based measurement step itself.

sources.system: Bauerfeind Bodytronic 600
sources.title: Measuring the body in its entirety - Bauerfeind life
sources.claim: Measurement accuracy of the Bodytronic 600 was clinically validated against CT reference values at the University of Rostock orthopedic clinic, with average standard deviation under one percent for circumference and length values - worker-comparable measurement quality.

sources.system: Aescape robotic massage table
sources.title: Product focus - AI and robot massage | spabusiness.com
sources.claim: Aescape's robotic massage table is an entirely autonomous, self-service system deployed in Equinox spas and Massage Envy franchise locations - a robot that operates on human bodies in staffed commercial facilities without a therapist.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (robotic massage): shows an autonomous machine registering a clothed human body in 3D and making force-controlled contact with it in an institution-run facility - the same body-registration and safe human-contact capability limb measurement requires.

sources.system: Aescape robotic massage table
sources.title: Equinox | The World's Most Advanced Massage
sources.claim: Aescape builds a 3D model of the client's body from over 1.1 million scanned data points before its robotic arms work on the body, at Equinox spa locations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (robotic massage): dense autonomous 3D capture of a human body surface in a commercial facility is the same sensing step used to derive body/limb dimensions for device construction.

sources.developer: Federal University of Pernambuco (de Oliveira, de Araujo, da Silva)
sources.title: Automated 3D Scanning Device for the Production of Forearm Prostheses and Orthoses (IFMBE Proceedings)
sources.claim: A purpose-built automated scanning device consisting of a rotational axis and 3D-scanner support captures body parts (forearms) accurately enough to produce prostheses and orthoses, replacing manual shape capture.

sources.system: STARscanner Laser Data Acquisition System
sources.title: Orthoses manufacturing 3D scanner - STARscanner - Orthomerica
sources.claim: The STARscanner laser data acquisition ..., FDA-cleared and used in cranial clinics and children's hospitals since 2001, captures an infant's head shape in under two seconds and eliminates plaster casting; the data is transmitted for fabrication of the custom cranial orthosis.

sources.system: Aletta Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device (ARPD)
sources.title: Vitestro raises $70m to fuel blood-drawing robot's global commercial readiness
sources.claim: Vitestro's Aletta autonomous robotic phlebotomy device uses AI-guided Doppler ultrasound to locate a vein in a patient's arm and robotically insert the needle; it is CE-marked and launched in European healthcare settings, with about 95% first-stick success.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (robotic venipuncture): an autonomous robot registers the anatomy of a seated patient's arm from imaging and acts on it to clinical tolerance in an outpatient clinic - the anatomy-localization and safe limb-contact capability needed to measure a limb.

tasks.label: Instruct patients in use of prosthetic or orthotic devices.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Retail/clinic front-of-house delivery of off-the-shelf or custom orthoses (knee/wrist/ankle braces, custom foot orthotics, diabetic shoes and inserts): technician explains the break-in wear schedule, how to tighten straps and lace shoes, skin/pressure-point warning signs, cleaning, and when to return for adjustment; patient is ambulatory and cooperative.

Fitting room at an O&P facility, delivery of a new lower-limb prosthesis: technician instructs the amputee on donning the liner and socket, sock-ply management for volume change, suspension/valve or pin-lock use, daily wear-time progression, residual-limb skin checks, and socket hygiene, answering questions as the patient tries the sequence.

Pediatric case in the clinic: technician instructs a parent (and child) on an AFO, cranial helmet, or scoliosis TLSO — donning over a seamless sock, strap order and tension, hours-per-day schedule, redness rules, growth checks, and cleaning; instruction is repeated and reassurance is given.

Hospital bedside or inpatient rehab unit: technician instructs a post-operative or spinal-cord patient and the attending nursing/therapy staff in use of a TLSO, halo, or post-op knee brace — log-roll donning while supine, in-bed vs. upright wear rules, precautions, and pin/skin care.

Multi-visit training on a complex device: upper-limb myoelectric or body-powered prosthesis, microprocessor knee, or powered orthosis — teaching muscle-site signal control, grip-pattern switching, app/mode settings, charging and battery care, and troubleshooting, over one or more sessions.

Follow-up instruction at the repair counter or by phone/telehealth: re-teaching care and wear rules after a repair or adjustment, walking a patient through a squeaking joint, a loose strap, liner replacement, or a charger problem, and confirming the patient can perform the routine.

tasks.label: Fit appliances onto patients, and make any necessary adjustments.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Delivery/fitting of a custom lower-limb prosthesis in an O&P clinic fitting room: technician helps the amputee don liner and socket, checks suspension and static/dynamic alignment, palpates and marks pressure/redness areas over bony prominences, removes the device, heat-adjusts or grinds the socket and trim lines, adjusts pylon alignment and foot position with hand tools, then refits and watches the patient stand and walk until fit is accepted.

Fitting custom foot orthotics or arch supports: technician places the devices in the patient's own shoes, has the patient stand and walk, observes rearfoot/forefoot posting and comfort, then grinds or heat-molds the shell, posts and top cover, adds accommodative padding, and refits repeatedly until the patient reports comfort and gait looks correct.

Fitting a custom or prefabricated body-worn orthosis (TLSO/spinal jacket, KAFO, AFO, knee or wrist brace) in the clinic: positioning the device on the patient's trunk or limb, adjusting strap lengths and closures, spot-heating and flaring thermoplastic edges, trimming and padding areas of impingement, setting joint stops, and instructing the patient in donning while verifying fit seated, standing and walking.

Follow-up adjustment appointment: patient returns reporting rubbing, red marks, pain or loosening; technician has the patient don the appliance, locates the offending area by inspection and palpation and patient report, then relieves/pads/grinds the shell, re-tensions or replaces straps, re-checks the fit on the body, and repeats until resolved.

Pediatric fitting: sizing and fitting a cranial remolding helmet on an infant or a scoliosis brace on a child, working with a squirming, sometimes crying patient held or assisted by a parent, adding/removing foam pads, trimming shell edges around ears, neck and axilla, and re-checking skin after a wear trial.

Bedside or wheelchair-side fitting in a hospital ward, rehab unit or skilled nursing facility: fitting a post-op brace, immediate post-operative prosthesis, or spinal orthosis on a patient with limited mobility, working around dressings, drains and lines, log-rolling or being assisted to position the patient, and making on-the-spot strap, pad and trim adjustments.

sources.system: Ortis (Roboticom)
sources.date: 2026-01 (page last modified); product line marketed since ~2019
sources.title: Ortis™ Roboticom: high precision robot for orthopedic applications
sources.claim: Commercial robotics in orthotics and prosthetics is confined to the fabrication bench: Roboticom's Ortis is a 7-axis robotic carving cell installed in orthopedic workshops that mills positive/negative models and trims and drills devices. It never contacts the patient and does no fitting or on-body adjustment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic carving/trimming of O&P models and shells in a fabrication cell. It is cited to show the frontier of deployed O&P robotics, but it does not transfer to this task: the workpiece is a plaster/foam model held in a fixture, not a living patient, and the system performs no donning, palpation, fit assessment or on-body adjustment.

sources.system: Self-Wearing Adaptive Garments (soft robotic unfurling)
sources.developer: KAIST (N. Kim) with Stanford University (A. Okamura group)
sources.title: KAIST team wins IEEE RA-L Best Paper Award for second year in a row
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic dressing of a human body remains a laboratory research problem. The 2025 IEEE RA-L best-paper work from KAIST/Stanford achieves assisted donning only by building pneumatic eversion actuators into the garment itself, evaluated as prototype sleeves, jackets and pants.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-assisted dressing, the closest published analogue to placing an appliance on a patient's body. It does not substantiate this task: it is a lab prototype of compliant garments, not a robot that dons a rigid custom socket or brace, assesses fit, and then grinds, heats and re-pads the device to acceptance.

sources.system: Aescape AI massage table
sources.title: Introducing Aescape Fully Automated Customizable Massage For Personalized Wellness And Recovery
sources.claim: Aescape's AI massage table is a deployed, fully automated robot that makes sustained physical contact with a human body inside structured commercial facilities (Equinox clubs, hotel spas), showing that autonomous robot-human body contact is commercially viable - but only for delivering massage strokes to a client lying in a fixed prone position, with no object handling.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous robotic manipulation applied directly to a human body in a human-work facility. Transfer fails for this task: the robot applies pressure to a passively positioned back through a table interface and manipulates no device; it cannot don a socket or brace, evaluate fit against skin tolerance, or modify the appliance and refit it.

roles.title: Ophthalmic Laboratory Technicians
roles.description: Cut, grind, and polish eyeglasses, contact lenses, or other precision optical elements. Assemble and mount lenses into frames or process other optical elements. Includes precision lens polishers or grinders, centerer-edgers, and lens mounters.

tasks.label: Mount and secure lens blanks or optical lenses in holding tools or chucks of cutting, polishing, grinding, or coating machines.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: High-volume wholesale Rx surfacing lab: technician takes a semi-finished lens blank from a job tray, applies tape/alloy or an adhesive block piece, aligns it to the prescribed axis/prism on a blocker, and loads the blocked lens into the chuck of a CNC generator and then a polisher. Standard round blanks, plastic/poly, high throughput.

Retail in-store or small finishing lab: technician marks and centers a finished uncut lens, mounts it on a leap-pad/finish block, and chucks the blocked lens between the clamps of an edger; mixed one-off jobs, varied frame shapes, slippery AR-coated lenses, bench work beside the dispensary.

Coating department: technician loads cleaned lenses into holding rings/domes or carriers of an AR vacuum coater or hard-coat machine, orienting each lens and avoiding surface contamination, then transfers the loaded dome/rack into the chamber.

Precision/specialty optics shop (non-ophthalmic elements, glass blanks): technician mounts single or blocked lens blanks in chucks, collets or vacuum fixtures of CNC grinders, centering machines and polishers; small lots, frequent size changeovers, tight concentricity requirements.
Contact lens / IOL lathe cell: technician mounts lens buttons or blocked parts into the collet/spindle nose of a precision lathe or mill-lathe, ensures seating and runout, and removes finished parts.

Non-routine bench work: oversized, glass, heavily decentered, drilled-rimless or prototype/repair pieces for which the technician improvises or hand-fits a holding tool, pads or wax mounting so the part can be held safely in an existing machine.

sources.system: CCU Modulo blocker

tasks.label: Inspect lens blanks to detect flaws, verify smoothness of surface, and ensure thickness of coating on lenses.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Wholesale/central Rx lab, post-surfacing inspection: uncut lens arrives at the QC bench in a job tray on the lab conveyor after generating, fining and polishing. Technician holds it under an arc lamp / dark-field inspection box, checks the freshly cut back surface for scratches, grey/haze, chatter, spiral, cutting marks, pits and center dots, and calls go / rework / breakage against the lab's written quality standard, in seconds per lens.

Wholesale/central Rx lab, post-coating inspection: after hard coat and vacuum AR coating, technician inspects each lens for coating uniformity and completeness — reflex colour consistency (a proxy for stack thickness), comets, waves, wrinkles/crazing, spotting, dust inclusions, uncoated edges — under a coating inspection lamp, and passes, sends for strip-and-recoat, or scraps.

Wholesale/central Rx lab, final QC before shipping or before edging: full inspection of the finished lens combining cosmetic surface inspection with verification of power, thickness, prism, add, engravings/markings and shape against the job ticket.

Rx lab, incoming/at-blocking inspection of semi-finished lens blanks: blanks pulled for the job are checked in the tray at the blocking or layout bench for chips, bubbles, striae, moulding marks and scratches or flaws in the factory-applied front-surface coating before the job is started.

Small independent or in-store finishing lab (retail optical, one to a few benches): technician inspects a handful of uncut lenses received loose in job envelopes from the supplier, and the finished edged lenses, under a lamp for surface flaws, coating defects and scratches before and after mounting; low volume, wide mix of lens types and materials, no tray-conveyor or lab-automation infrastructure.

tasks.label: Shape lenses appropriately so that they can be inserted into frames.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Wholesale/central Rx lab, finishing department: high-volume standard plastic or polycarbonate single-vision and progressive lenses for full-rim plastic or metal frames. Job travels in a barcoded job tray; shape comes from a digital frame-shape database or traced frame; lens is centered/blocked (or edged blockless), edged to shape with a bevel, safety-beveled and polished, then verified against the job.

Retail chain or independent optical shop's in-store finishing lab: technician traces the frame, lays out and blocks the uncut lens on the axis/OC, edges it on a patternless edger, then test-fits the lens in the frame, one or two jobs at a time, across a wide mix of frame styles and lens materials.

Rimless (drill-mount) and semi-rimless (nylon supra/groove) jobs in either a lab or a store: shape must be edged plus holes/notches drilled at correct angles or a groove cut, with edges polished, to a tighter tolerance because the lens carries the mounting hardware.

High-curve wrap/sport frames and specialty work: base 6-16 curves needing tilted or step bevels and compensation, thick high-minus lenses needing edge polish/roll, safety eyewear to certified frame specs, or glass lenses.

Problem/rework jobs at the bench: lens comes out too tight or too loose in the frame, chipped, mis-axised or mismatched to a warped/odd frame; technician judges the misfit by hand-inserting the lens, then hand-stones or re-edges by feel, or re-cuts a replacement, iterating until it seats correctly.

tasks.label: Clean finished lenses and eyeglasses, using cloths and solvents.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Wholesale Rx surfacing lab: after generating/polishing and deblocking, the technician cleans each finished lens of polish slurry, blocking alloy/adhesive, surface-saver tape residue and layout ink, wiping with solvent and a lint-free cloth before it goes to inspection; lenses travel in job trays.

Coating room of an Rx lab: critical pre-coat cleaning of finished lenses immediately before hard-coat or AR vacuum coating - solvent/detergent and ultrasonic cleaning plus spot-free drying, handled in racks or trays under low-contamination conditions; any fingerprint or film causes coating rejects.

Finishing lab: after edging, the technician removes the edging block pad and leap tape from the cut lens, wipes off coolant, swarf, water spots and ink with cloth and alcohol, and inspects the cleaned edged lens before mounting it into the frame.

Wholesale lab final inspection/packing bench: the assembled pair (lenses mounted in a plastic, metal, semi-rimless or drilled rimless frame) is cleaned with lens spray/alcohol and a microfiber cloth - fingerprints, marking ink and handling smudges removed from both lens surfaces, bevels and frame - then inspected and packed.

Retail optical store's on-site lab/dispensary: the technician cleans the finished job before dispensing, and cleans customers' existing eyewear at pickup or after adjustment, using an ultrasonic bath and/or spray and cloth, drying and polishing the lenses and frame by hand on a varied mix of customer frames.

tasks.label: Mount, secure, and align finished lenses in frames or optical assemblies, using precision hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Full-rim plastic (zyl/acetate) frame in a retail or wholesale finishing lab: technician warms the frame front in a frame warmer, snaps the edged Rx lens into the eyewire with the correct cylinder axis / progressive fitting-cross orientation, works the bevel fully into the groove without chipping or stress-cracking the coated lens, then checks seating and axis. Frames vary job to job in material, wrap, and bevel depth.

Full-rim metal frame: technician backs out the tiny eyewire screw with a jeweler's screwdriver, opens the rim, seats the beveled lens in the groove, closes the eyewire and threads/tightens the 1.2-1.4 mm screw without cross-threading, checks for rim gaps and lens rotation, and re-tightens after a settling check.

Semi-rimless (nylon supra / groove) and rimless drill-mount jobs: threading and tensioning the nylon cord in the lens groove, or aligning drilled lenses to the chassis and mounting posts, inserting bushings, washers and screws, tightening/peening with precision hand tools, and mutually aligning right and left lenses for tilt, height and rotation.

Final truing and verification of the mounted pair before it leaves the lab: verifying axis, optical centers/PD, add height and unwanted prism on a lensmeter against the Rx, rotating or reseating a lens that reads off-axis, and hand-aligning the finished eyewear (temple alignment, four-point touch, pantoscopic tilt) with pliers.

Remount/repair work in a retail dispensary lab: fitting new lenses into a customer's own used frame (possibly warped, brittle, or with stripped screws), or reinserting a lens that popped out, salvaging screws and pads, and re-aligning the whole frame afterward.

Non-eyewear precision optical assembly at an optics/photonics manufacturer: mounting finished lenses or windows into cells, barrels or instrument housings, seating them against a shoulder, securing with retaining rings, spacers or adhesive, and aligning the optical axis/spacing to spec before cure and inspection.

tasks.label: Adjust lenses and frames to correct alignment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Optical lab / retail lab bench: final alignment of a completed Rx job in a plastic (acetate/zyl) frame. Tech warms the frame in a hot-air or salt-pan warmer, checks standard alignment (four-point touch, coplanar lens planes, equal temple spread and pantoscopic tilt, no x-ing), corrects by hand and with alignment pliers, seats the lens fully in the groove, and re-verifies. Frame styles differ job to job.

Metal / titanium frame job: straighten and level temples, correct front twist and x-ing with end-piece and angling pliers (cold), set nose-pad arms symmetrically, tighten eyewire and hinge screws to the right torque without stripping, confirm lens is fully seated and cylinder axis is correct on the lensmeter.

Correcting lens alignment specifically: a lens sits off-axis, is proud of the bevel, or pops after edging. Tech releases/heats the eyewire, removes and reseats the lens, rotates it to the prescribed cylinder axis, re-checks on the lensmeter and against layout marks, and re-tightens; sometimes decides the lens must be re-edged.

Rimless / semi-rimless (drill-mount or nylon-groove) eyewear: align the two lenses so they are level and coplanar, stop lens rotation on the mounting bushings/compression posts, adjust bridge and end-piece geometry and temple alignment without cracking or chipping the drilled lens.

Frame manufacturing / mass-production setting: on a run of identical frames, set or correct temple bend angles, inward deflection and downward arc to the model's specification (and even up left/right temples) before final inspection and packaging.

tasks.label: Select lens blanks, molds, tools, and polishing or grinding wheels, according to production specifications.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Wholesale Rx lab lens-pick station: technician reads the LMS work ticket (OPC codes for right and left lens, material, base curve, chirality), walks racks of semi-finished/finished blanks in boxes and paper sleeves, scans the barcode, removes the blanks and places the correct pair in the numbered job tray on the conveyor; handles out-of-stock substitutions.

Retail/in-store or small finishing lab: technician selects the correct finished uncut lens blanks from stock drawers for the Rx and frame, and selects the matching edger wheel/cycle, blocking pad and mounting tooling for the lens material (poly, hi-index, glass) and frame type (rimless, groove, bevel).

Conventional surfacing department: technician retrieves the lap tool whose base/cross curve matches the job from the lap library racks, mounts the correct fining and polishing pad on it, and installs it in the fining/polishing machine; also selects blocking rings and pads for the job.

Digital freeform surfacing line: technician selects and mounts polishing tools/pads, generator cutting tools, and block pieces called for by the job or material spec, keeping the automated line supplied with the tooling each job requires.

Cast-to-Rx or molded lens production: operator selects the front and back mold pair (and gasket/spacer) whose curves match the prescribed power per the production order, cleans and loads them into the casting/curing line, and returns molds to the library after use.

Precision/specialty optics shop (non-eyeglass elements): technician selects the glass or crystal blank per the print, and selects, mounts and dresses the correct diamond grinding wheel, pitch lap or polishing tool for the low-volume or one-off part on a CNC generator or bench spindle.

tasks.label: Position and adjust cutting tools to specified curvature, dimensions, and depth of cut.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Wholesale/central Rx surfacing lab: for each job the technician sets up the digital lens generator (e.g. Satisloh VFT/Schneider HSC) — selects the turning/milling tool, sets tool offsets and depth of cut for the prescribed back-surface curvature, center thickness and blank diameter, runs calibration and verifies the cut surface. Blocked lenses arrive on barcoded job trays; volumes of hundreds to thousands of lenses per shift.

Finishing lab or in-store optical lab: setting the patternless edger's cutting/grinding wheel path for a traced frame — bevel curve and bevel placement (front/rear/ratio), lens size, groove or step-bevel depth, adapting to lens material and high base-curve wrap frames, then verifying fit in the frame.

Rimless / drill-mount and notched jobs: positioning the drill or notching tool to the specified hole locations, drill angle relative to the lens front curve, hole diameter and depth (through-holes, slots, counterbores) so the mounting hardware seats without cracking the lens.

Custom contact lens shop (RGP, scleral, ortho-K) or IOL/mold work: mounting and aligning the diamond tool on an ultra-precision lathe, setting tool height/offset and depth of cut for the specified base curve radius, diameter and center thickness, checking with a calibration cut before running the job.

Precision optics shop working non-ophthalmic elements (spheres, aspheres, prisms, windows): setting up a CNC curve generator/grinder — selecting and dressing the diamond wheel, registering tool offsets, and setting infeed/depth of cut for the specified radius and thickness on a fixtured blank.

tasks.label: Assemble eyeglass frames and attach shields, nose pads, and temple pieces, using pliers, screwdrivers, and drills.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Wholesale/central prescription lab finishing bench: technician takes an edged lens pair and an acetate (plastic) full-rim frame, warms the frame in a hot-air warmer or salt pan, snaps each lens into the rim temporal-edge first, checks the cylinder axis and that the lens is fully seated and untwisted, re-heats and re-seats if it is out, then cleans and inspects the finished pair against the job ticket.

Metal full-rim frame glazing: technician backs out the tiny eyewire (rim) screw with a jeweler's screwdriver, opens the rim, seats the beveled lens in the groove, closes the eyewire and retightens the screw with a screwdriver and pliers, checks for gaps, lens rotation and axis, and adjusts frame alignment.

Rimless / drill-mount assembly: technician drills and countersinks holes in the edged lenses to the mount pattern (often on a drill or CNC drill unit), then attaches the bridge and endpieces through the holes with bushings, washers, screws or nuts, tightens and trims with pliers/screwdriver, and checks that lenses sit level, unstressed and without rotation.

Semi-rimless (nylon supra / groove) mounting: technician grooves the lens edge, threads and tensions the nylon cord, seats the lens into the metal upper rim and cord, trims and knots or clips the cord, and verifies seating and alignment.

Retail-store lab bench repair and parts work on customer-owned or stock frames of unknown make and condition: replacing missing or stripped screws, swapping screw-in or push-in nose pads with pliers/screwdriver, fitting a replacement temple to a front, attaching snap-on side shields to safety frames, and re-tightening/aligning after the swap.

Production-run frame component assembly in an eyewear/safety-eyewear manufacturing operation: identical new frame fronts and temples in batches, hinges heat-set or screwed into the fronts and temples, nose pad arms and endpieces attached, side shields fitted, at a dedicated station with parts in bins.

tasks.label: Set dials and start machines to polish lenses or hold lenses against rotating wheels to polish them manually.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Central/wholesale Rx surfacing lab: technician takes blocked semi-finished plastic lens blanks that have just been generated, loads them into a soft-tool CNC polisher, calls up the polishing cycle for that material/curve from the job ticket, starts the machine, then unloads, washes and inspects the polished surface. High volume, hundreds to thousands of lenses per shift.

Small independent surfacing lab or in-store/retail back-shop surfacing: technician runs a single standalone or all-in-one surfacing/polishing unit, keys in or selects the polish program on the control panel, loads one blocked lens at a time, starts the cycle, unloads and checks for haze, waviness or missed spots on mixed low-volume jobs.

Finishing (edging) lab, retail or central: after cutting a lens to frame shape, technician runs the edger's polishing cycle on flat-edge, rimless and grooved lenses to bring the edge to a clear luster, selecting polish mode and material settings, then removing and checking the lens for edge clarity and chips.

Routine hand polishing at a bench buffing/polishing wheel: technician holds a finished lens edge, drilled-hole edge or safety bevel against a rotating felt/cloth wheel charged with polishing compound to bring it to an even luster on jobs the edger's polish cycle does not fully cover.

Salvage/rework hand polishing: technician judges where a nib, chip, tool mark, scratch or a modification (re-cut bevel, reshaped rimless edge) needs work and freehand-buffs that specific spot against a rotating wheel, repeatedly inspecting under light and varying pressure and angle until the defect blends out without distorting the lens.

Precision/specialty optics work: polishing glass optical elements, prisms, aspheres, or lathe-cut RGP contact lenses on CNC polishing machines or multi-spindle polishing spindles — setting spindle speed, stroke and cycle time, running the cycle, and checking against metrology/inspection.

tasks.label: Repair broken parts, using precision hand tools and soldering irons.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Retail/wholesale optical lab bench: a customer's frame arrives with a temple loose or off because the hinge screw is missing, backed out, or snapped. Tech selects the right diameter/length screw from a stock assortment, mates the hinge barrels, drives and torques it with a jeweler's screwdriver, sets hinge friction, trims or thread-locks the excess, checks temple swing.

Optical bench small-hardware swaps: pry off and press in new push-in silicone nose pads (or screw-in pads), heat and slip replacement plastic temple tips over metal cores, replace rim-lock screws, bushings, sleeves and spring-hinge parts across assorted frame brands, then clean and check symmetry.

Broken metal frame (bridge, endpiece, rim, temple, pad arm) fractured or snapped: clean and prep the break, align and hold the pieces in correct three-dimensional relation, join with silver solder/torch or a laser welder, file and polish the joint, touch up or re-plate the finish, straighten and realign the frame, reinsert lenses and verify fit.

Acetate/plastic frame repair: hinge pulled out of an acetate temple or front, cracked rim or bridge, snapped temple. Tech removes and reseats the hinge with a hinge heater or hot tool, fills or glues the damaged hole/crack, refits screws, then re-sands, buffs and reshapes the area on a finished, lens-mounted frame.

Rimless / semi-rimless (drill-mount, nylon groove) repair: replace broken mounting screws, bushings and compression posts through lens drill holes, re-drill or re-notch a lens, restring nylon cord, retorque without cracking the lens, then realign the mount.

Repair of lab equipment, tooling and fixtures with precision hand tools and a soldering iron: replacing broken chuck pads, blocks, belts and small mechanical parts on edgers/blockers, resoldering a broken wire or connector on a machine harness or foot switch, refurbishing jigs and patterns.

tasks.label: Immerse eyeglass frames in solutions to harden, soften, or dye frames.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Retail/finishing optical lab: tech immerses a plastic (zyl/acetate/nylon) frame front in a hot-water or hot-salt bath (or bead/salt pan) to soften it so lenses can be inserted or removed; mixed frame materials and thicknesses, one job at a time, pliability judged by feel, work moves straight to lens insertion.

Wholesale Rx lab tint department: technician immerses plastic lenses and small frame parts in heated dye baths to a specified color and density (solid and gradient dips), times the dip, checks against a color standard/transmission target, rinses and neutralizes; steady batch flow through the shift.

Production lab hardening/coating area: racked batches of lenses or frame components immersed in hardening solutions — molten-salt chemical tempering of glass lenses, or dip hardcoat/primer tanks — with controlled temperature and dwell time, then rinse, drain and cure.

Eyewear manufacturer or specialty frame-finishing shop: batch immersion dyeing of acetate or 3D-printed nylon frame fronts and temples in dye tanks to match a color standard, followed by rinse, dry and color inspection.

Independent dispensary bench, one-off custom job: soften an unusual or vintage customer frame in hot water for repair/lens change, or hand-dye a single frame to match a customer request, with no batch recipe and color/pliability judged by eye and feel.

tasks.label: Lay out lenses and trace lens outlines on glass, using templates.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: High-volume wholesale/central Rx finishing lab: for each job tray of finished or semi-finished lens blanks, the technician establishes the layout — optical center, cylinder axis, decentration/segment height — and registers the frame or pattern outline on the blank so the shape can be cut; standard blanks, standard job flow, hundreds of jobs per shift.

Retail-store or small independent finishing lab: technician marks the lens with a lensmeter, sets the hard plastic pattern/template (or demo lens) over the marked blank on a layout/blocking stand, checks that the traced outline fits inside the blank with adequate edge thickness, and marks/blocks it; mixed one-off jobs, frequent frame changes.

Glass lens work / legacy manual layout: optical center and axis dotted on a glass blank, the metal or plastic template laid over the marked blank on a light box, and the lens outline scribed or ink-traced onto the glass before cutting and edging.

Difficult jobs: rimless drill mounts, high-wrap sports frames, prism/slab-off, strong prescriptions needing large decentration, or a custom pattern cut in-house; layout must be reasoned out and the blank is often marginal in size.

Precision/industrial optics shop: laying out non-ophthalmic elements — filters, windows, mirror or prism blanks — by positioning a template on flat glass and scribing the outline before cutting and grinding to the finished shape.

tasks.label: Control equipment that coats lenses to alter their reflective qualities.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: High-volume wholesale/central Rx lab, AR coating department: technician takes cleaned uncut round lenses from job trays, seats them in the sector/full dome fixtures of a vacuum box coater (Satisloh 1200-TLX/1200-DLX, Schneider EBC), rolls the dome into the chamber, selects the recipe for lens material and coating stack, runs pump-down and the multilayer evaporation cycle, then unloads and gives each lens a reflex-color and cosmetic check. Standard clear AR, hundreds of lenses per shift.

Medium/small lab or in-store finishing lab with a compact box coater (MC-380/MC-280/SP-200 class): small mixed batches, frequent switching between clear AR, back-side-only AR, top coats and different lens materials including glass; operator sets up the correct holder or flip-over dome, runs the cycle, unloads and checks.

Mirror / flash reflective coatings on plano and Rx sun lenses: color-critical runs where the technician loads front-side-only holders, runs the mirror stack, then compares residual reflex color and mirror shade against a master or spectrophotometer reading and accepts, reworks, or adjusts the process for the next batch.

Pre-coat preparation and post-coat handling around the coater: loading/unloading the ultrasonic or plasma cleaning line and degassing oven, checking lens cleanliness under an inspection lamp, taping/masking surfaces that must stay uncoated, staging clean lenses under the flow box, and returning coated lenses to job trays.

Coater setup, changeover and upkeep: recharging crucibles/evaporation material and ion-source parts, cleaning chamber shields, dome and glass shields between campaigns, running witness/test batches, reading the layer-thickness or spectral result and adjusting recipe parameters when residual reflection color drifts out of spec.

tasks.label: Remove lenses from molds and separate lenses in containers for further processing or storage.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Soft contact lens cast-molding plant (cleanroom): after cure, front-curve/base-curve plastic mold pairs are opened, the cured lens released from the mold, and lenses transferred into hydration carriers/trays for extraction and packaging; thousands per hour, technician tends the demold/delens station, clears jams and handles rejects.

High-volume cast spectacle lens plant (CR-39/high-index): after oven polymerization, tape/gaskets are stripped and the glass mold pairs pried apart to release the cast lens blank; lens checked for chips/adhesion and racked into baskets or trays by base curve/SKU for annealing, tinting or hard coating, mold halves returned for washing.

Small or specialty casting operation (photochromic, polarized/laminated, custom Rx, in-lab casting systems): small mixed batches, varied mold diameters and curves, manual pry/air-knife release, visual inspection for stuck or chipped lenses, then sorting lenses into per-job envelopes, trays or vials with the job ticket for the next step or storage.

Prescription (Rx) surfacing lab: lenses removed from block pieces/holders (deblocking) after generating, polishing or coating, adhesive/alloy separated, lens cleaned and placed back into the numbered job tray or coating basket with its ticket for the next process or storage.

tasks.label: Attach identification labels to finished packaged items, or cut stencils and stencil information on containers, such as lot numbers or shipping destinations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In-line labeling of primary containers on a running packaging line (bottles, cans, jars, tubs, pouches): the operator keeps identification/product labels applied to each container as it moves through the labeler at line speed, loading label stock and correcting misapplied labels. Setting is the packaging line itself, built around the machines.

End-of-line case/carton identification: applying printed shipping/ID labels and marking lot numbers, date codes and destination information onto corrugated cases moving on the case conveyor before palletizing, in a food or CPG plant.

Unit-load (pallet) identification in the plant's shipping/staging area: printing and attaching SSCC/shipping placards and destination labels to one or two faces of finished, stretch-wrapped pallets before they go to the dock. Human-scale warehouse floor with forklifts and people moving through.

Off-line, short-run or rework labeling at a bench or table on the plant floor: over-labeling mispackaged or relabeled goods, applying promotional/country-of-origin/customer-specific stickers, and hand-labeling odd-shaped or low-volume items in small batches with frequent changeover.

Marking and stenciling directly on rigid shipping containers in the packing/shipping department: cutting or setting a stencil and spraying/inking lot numbers, weights and shipping destinations onto drums, pails, sacks, kegs or wooden crates.

tasks.label: Sort, grade, weigh, and inspect products, verifying and adjusting product weight or measurement to meet specifications.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: High-speed filling/bagging line for food or CPG powders, snacks or granules: operator monitors net pack weights, pulls or rejects under/overweight packs, and tweaks filler/weigher settings to hold target weight and legal minimum fill. Product presented continuously on the line conveyor.

Finished-package inspection on a food, beverage or pharma packaging line: checking fill level, seal integrity, label/date code, package damage and foreign material, and removing defective packs from the moving line.

Sorting and grading incoming or in-process product on a belt or sorting table in a cannery/produce packhouse: separating by size, color, ripeness or grade, and pulling off-grade, damaged or foreign items by hand at line speed.

Catch-weight hand-weighing/portioning at a scale station (meat, seafood, cheese, bulk hand-pack): placing pieces on a scale and adding/removing product to hit a fixed target weight before the pack is sealed and labeled. Station is a human workbench beside the line.

tasks.label: Stop or reset machines when malfunctions occur, clear machine jams, and report malfunctions to a supervisor.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Jam inside the primary packaging machine's forming/filling/sealing zone on a food or consumer-goods line: a crumpled carton wedged in the cartoner bucket chain, a pouch caught in the VFFS sealing jaws, or a misfed case in the case packer. Operator e-stops, opens the guard door, reaches into the confined machine frame, pulls out deformed board/film and spilled product, wipes residue off the jaws, closes the guard, resets the fault at the HMI, restarts and logs/reports the stoppage.

Container jam or pile-up in the conveying/infeed section of a bottling, canning or jar line: bottles tipped over at a transfer plate, cans backed up on an accumulation table, a misfed container at the infeed worm or star wheel. Operator stops the conveyor, removes or uprights the offending containers, sweeps away spillage, restarts and reports if repeated.

Web/roll-stock fault: label web break or bunched labels in the labeler, film jammed or wrapped around rollers/sealing bars on a wrapper or bagger, torn foil in a lidding machine. Operator stops the machine, cuts and pulls out the wrapped film, re-threads the web through the roller path, re-registers the eye mark, resets and restarts.

Closure or small-component feeder jam: caps bridged in the cap sorter or chute, lids stuck in the denester, pumps/spouts jammed at the escapement of a vibratory feeder supplying the capper. Operator stops the feeder, frees or removes the jammed pieces, restarts the feed and reports chronic jamming.

Non-jam malfunction on the line: a machine alarm, drive fault, low air pressure, leaking fill nozzle, out-of-tolerance seal or unusual noise. Operator stops or e-stops the machine, locks it out if needed, notifies the supervisor/maintenance, records the fault and downtime reason, and resets/restarts once cleared.

Jam in end-of-line/secondary equipment: a case stuck in the case sealer with tape wrapped in the applicator, a jammed carton at a merge or divert on the takeaway conveyor, a mis-picked layer in the palletizer cell. Operator stops the equipment, extracts the crushed case and loose tape/film, clears the guard-interlocked cell, resets and restarts.

tasks.label: Observe machine operations to ensure quality and conformity of filled or packaged products to standards.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: High-speed beverage filling line (bottles/cans) in a brewery or beverage plant: the tender watches containers coming off filler, capper and labeler for correct fill level, closure seating/seal, label position, and date/lot code legibility; pulls periodic samples, culls out-of-spec containers, and calls a stop when a fault repeats.

Food plant packaging line for flexible/tray packs (snacks, bakery, fresh-cut produce, meat): the tender monitors bagger/thermoformer output for seal integrity and wrinkles in the seal, correct pack weight, missing pieces, foreign material and date coding; product is naturally variable and film changeovers create defect bursts; bad packs are pulled off the belt.

Cannery / retort line: the worker checks filled cans and jars at the end of the packaging line for fill level, double-seam or lid seal, label application and foreign material before cases go to distribution, with two to three product changeovers per shift.

Pharmaceutical or medical-device blister and cartoning line under GMP: the operator verifies tablet presence and correctness in each blister pocket, lidding-foil print (batch/expiry), leaflet and carton codes, and seal quality, and records documented in-process checks and line-clearance results.

End-of-line secondary packaging area on the plant floor: the operator roams between case packer, shrink wrapper and palletizer, checking case count and case labels, wrap tightness, crushed or open cases, and pallet build/stability before the load is released to shipping.

Small-batch contract/co-packing operation with frequent changeovers and mixed SKUs, including hand-assembled kits, club-store displays and short runs: the tender compares packed units against a golden sample for correct components, label/artwork and appearance, and logs QC checks by hand.

tasks.label: Remove finished packaged items from machine and separate rejected items.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: High-speed beverage/canned-goods line: finished bottles, cans, multipacks and cases discharge from the filler/wrapper onto a conveyor; the tender takes cases off the discharge, builds or feeds pallets, and pulls units flagged by fill-level/seal/weight inspection plus visibly damaged packs into a reject bin. Guarded, conveyor-fed line running one or two SKUs per shift.

Food plant form/fill/seal or thermoform line with a manual pack-off station: retail vac-packs, trays or pouches exit the machine in uneven groups onto a belt; the operator standing at the discharge checks each for leaks, bad seals, missing/illegible label, date and barcode, sets failures aside, and hand-packs good packs into shipping cases at line rate. Frequent SKU and case-size changes.

Bagging/sacking line (flour, pet food, feed, chemicals, produce sacks): operator removes filled and sealed 20-50 lb bags from the bagger/sealer discharge, stacks them on pallets in pattern, and culls torn, leaking, or over/underweight bags flagged by the checkweigher. Plant floor shared with forklifts and other operators.

Pharma / medical device / cosmetics GMP packaging suite: operator collects cartons, blisters, bottles or vials at the cartoner/labeler discharge, verifies coding, labels and serialization, segregates rejects into a controlled, reconciled reject bin, and places accepted units into shippers. Cleanroom-standard room, documented procedures, line clearance rules.

Fresh produce packhouse: filled and sealed clamshells/punnets come off the filler-sealer line; workers lift them off, cull over/underweight, damaged, leaking or poorly presented packs, and place accepted packs into master cases or trays. Seasonal crews, high volume, washdown/chilled conditions.

Small producer or high-mix contract packer with semi-automatic equipment (craft brewery seamer, tabletop filler/capper, small bakery flow wrapper): operator removes finished units from the machine by hand onto a table, eyeballs each for fill, cap, seal and label defects, boxes the good ones and sets rejects aside; several changeovers per day, short runs, no line integration.

tasks.label: Monitor the production line, watching for problems such as pile-ups, jams, or glue that isn't sticking properly.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: High-speed beverage bottling/canning line (brewery, soft-drink bottler, cannery): operator stands at/walks the filler-capper-labeler section for a full shift, watching for fallen or jammed containers, pile-ups on the accumulation table, misfeeds into the master machines, fill/closure faults; hundreds of containers per minute, wet and noisy.

Cartoner / case-packer / case-sealer section with hot-melt adhesive at the end of a food or beverage line: operator watches for cartons jamming at the cartoner, cases backing up on the discharge conveyor, and glue beads that are missing, cold, or misplaced so flaps pop open; includes occasional hand pull-checks of glued flaps.

Vertical form-fill-seal or flow-wrap bagging line (snacks, frozen food, produce, pet food): operator monitors film tracking and splices, seal quality (product caught in the seal, wrinkles), bag jams at the discharge, and product build-up/bridging at the infeed hopper and scale.

End-of-line area: case conveyors, fenced palletizer cell, stretch wrapper and shipping label applicator; operator monitors case flow for tipped cases and pile-ups at accumulators, film breaks, mis-built or leaning pallets, and label misapplication.

Small or mid-size plant / contract packager (cannery hand-pack, cosmetics, seasonal produce shed): mixed semi-automatic and hand-fed machines with people feeding and hand-packing, frequent product and format changeovers, older equipment; operator watches several stations and the product flow between them for jams, spills, mis-fed packaging and weak seals/glue.

tasks.label: Inspect and remove defective products and packaging material.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: High-speed filling/sealing line (beverage, food, personal care, pharma): operator watches containers/pouches flowing on the conveyor and pulls out underfilled, unsealed, mislabeled, dented or contaminated units into a reject bin while the line runs.

Cannery / frozen-food / produce plant: operator works a moving belt or picking table ahead of the filler, removing rotten, off-color, undersized or broken pieces and foreign material before product is filled into cans, bags or trays.

Culling defective packaging components from the machine's feed stream at the hopper/feeder — malformed closures, damaged preforms or empty cans/jars, mis-die-cut labels — so only sound components reach the filler/capper/labeler.

Removing defective bulk packaging material from the machine itself: a damaged or misprinted roll of film/label stock, a warped or crushed stack of carton blanks in the magazine, torn web threaded through the former — the operator pulls the bad material out and re-threads/reloads good stock.

End of line: inspecting sealed cases, shrink bundles, cartons and pallet loads for crushed corners, open flaps, bad tape, missing or unreadable case labels, and pulling defective cases off the conveyor or pallet.

Low-volume hand-pack operation in a small plant or co-packer (bakery, meal kit, gift/kitting, specialty foods): worker at a pack table visually inspects each item and its wrapper as it is packed and discards defective ones into a scrap tote.

tasks.label: Start machine by engaging controls.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine shift/batch start-up of an automated packaging line (filler, capper, cartoner, case packer) in a food or beverage plant: after verifying guards are closed and film/product is loaded, the operator engages power/start pushbuttons or an HMI 'start' softkey at the machine's control panel and watches the line ramp up to speed.

Re-engaging controls after a stoppage (jam cleared, film splice, minor changeover) on a plant-floor packaging machine: operator acknowledges/resets the fault on the panel or HMI, presses reset then start (sometimes jog/index first), and confirms the machine is running.

Semi-automatic or tabletop equipment in a smaller co-packing plant, cannery or produce packhouse (bag sealer, shrink tunnel, vacuum sealer, labeler, small filler): operator flips a power switch, sets a dial/timer, and presses a start button or foot pedal to begin each cycle.

Walking a large integrated line or cannery and starting several machines in sequence at their local control stations (conveyors, washer, filler, seamer, wrapper), verifying each starts via stack lights/indicators before moving to the next.

Start-up of a regulated pharmaceutical/cosmetic or aseptic filling line in a gowned cleanroom: operator logs in on the HMI with credentials, selects the batch recipe, and engages the start sequence following SOP, confirming interlocks and status screens.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine tending of an injection press. The engaged control is the same class of object as a packaging machine's start pushbutton (a human-designed panel button on a production machine), pressed with the same precision, on an ordinary plant floor rather than in a fenced cell.

tasks.label: Tend or operate machine that packages product.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: High-speed primary packaging line in a food or beverage plant (bottling, canning, filling): operator tends filler/capper/seamer/labeler, keeps caps, cans, labels and film supplied, watches fill levels and seals, clears jams and container falls, runs quality checks and logs counts across a shift.

End-of-line secondary packaging at a CPG/food plant: operator tends cartoner, case packer, shrink wrapper and palletizer, loads carton/case blanks into magazines, changes stretch film and tape, performs format changeovers between SKUs, and inspects finished cases.

Pharmaceutical, nutraceutical or cosmetic filling and packaging line in a cGMP facility: tend vial/bottle filler, capper, labeler and blister/cartoner; supply pre-sterilized containers, closures and labels; perform in-process checks, line clearance and batch documentation.

Semi-automatic filling/bagging/sealing station at a small food plant or contract packager on a general plant floor: operator positions bags/pails under a filler or on a bagger spout, actuates fill, checkweighs, heat-seals or closes, stacks output, and re-rigs the station for frequent short-run job changes.

Seasonal cannery or produce packing line: tend filler/seamer/tray sealer/flow wrapper on natural, variable product; keep the infeed supplied, pull defective containers, unjam the machine, and keep pace with the line amid many co-workers.

Fulfillment center or 3PL packaging machine tending: operate an auto-bagger or box-on-demand/box-forming machine, keep paper/film rolls and label stock loaded, induct items, clear misfeeds, and release sealed parcels to the takeaway conveyor.

tasks.label: Clean, oil, and make minor adjustments or repairs to machinery and equipment, such as opening valves or setting guides.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: End-of-run wet sanitation of a filling/packaging machine in a food or beverage plant: foaming, scrubbing and high-pressure rinsing of the machine frame, guards, conveyors and immediate floor area, then sanitizer application and visual verification. Wet, slippery, chemical-laden conditions on the plant floor during the sanitation shift.

Product-contact cleaning of a liquid filler and its product lines between runs or at shift end: opening/closing product, water and chemical valves, flushing, running caustic/acid/rinse cycles, sanitizing before startup on CIP/COP-capable equipment in a dairy, juice or beverage plant.

Teardown cleaning of product-contact change parts: removing filling nozzles, starwheels, augers, formers, hoppers and belts, hand-washing or tank-washing and sanitizing them, then reassembling on the machine and verifying alignment before pre-op inspection.

Scheduled lubrication round on packaging equipment: oiling chains and slides, greasing bearings from a checklist, checking and topping off gearbox and air-line lubricator oil levels, wiping excess grease, all on a fixed PM schedule in the plant.

Minor adjustments at setup or during a run: setting conveyor side guides and rails for a new pack size, adjusting starwheels, timing, fill volume and sealing pressure, opening or throttling air and product valves, repositioning photo-eyes and date-coders until output meets spec.

Minor repairs and troubleshooting during production: clearing a jam or crushed carton/bottle, re-threading film, replacing a worn belt, O-ring, seal, blade or nozzle, tightening loose fasteners, then restarting the line and confirming good product.

tasks.label: Regulate machine flow, speed, or temperature.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: High-speed beverage bottling/canning line: operator regulates filler speed and fill level/flow, adjusts capper and conveyor speeds to keep the line balanced, and sets/trims pasteurizer or hot-fill temperatures when product or line stoppages shift conditions. Work is done at the line's HMIs and at valves/drives on the machines.

Vertical/horizontal form-fill-seal or flow-wrap bagging line (snacks, frozen food, confection): operator regulates film feed speed and machine cycle rate, sealing jaw temperatures, and product flow from the multihead weigher/feeder, trimming settings when seals scorch or weights drift on new film or product lots.

Liquid/viscous or pharmaceutical-cosmetic filling line: operator regulates pump/valve flow and dosing volume, fill speed, and product or tunnel temperature (hot fill, melted wax/lotion, depyrogenation), holding fill weights within tight legal/GMP tolerances.

Cannery or produce packing house with seasonal raw product: worker regulates incoming product flow at hopper gates and shaker feeders, steam/water valves for blanchers and retort cook temperature, and line speed to match hand packers, moving between stations on a wet, crowded plant floor with variable raw material.

Small contract packager or plant with older semi-automatic machines: operator hand-adjusts dial thermostats on band sealers/shrink tunnels, air-pressure regulators, hand valves and speed potentiometers on several standalone machines, with frequent changeovers and little instrumentation or feedback.
