tasks.label: Adjust machine components and machine tension and pressure according to size or processing angle of product.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Size/format changeover on a vertical or horizontal form-fill-seal bagger or flow wrapper in a food plant: set bag length, film web tension/dancer setting, sealing jaw temperature, pressure and dwell for a new pack size, swap or reposition forming set and guides, then run and verify first packs.

Mid-run corrective adjustment on a running line: film wrinkling, web wandering, print registration drift or weak seals appear, and the tender trims web tension/brake torque, jaw pressure and guide position until packs are back in spec, without stopping the line.

Case erector / case sealer / case packer set for a different carton size in a plant or distribution center: reposition side rails, head height, flap folders and squaring arms, set drive-belt pressure, run a test case.

Stretch wrapper, bundler or shrink tunnel in a warehouse shipping area: set film tension/containment force, carriage speed and wrap height for a new pallet size or an unstable load profile, adjusting as loads vary.

Filler / capper / labeler changeover on a container line: swap or reposition star wheels, guide rails and centering bells for a new bottle size, set capping torque (pressure) and label applicator position/angle, verify torque and label placement.

tasks.label: Supply materials to spindles, conveyors, hoppers, or other feeding devices and unload packaged product.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: End of line in a food/beverage or consumer-goods packaging plant: the operator takes finished packaged product (cases, cartons, bundles, bagged product) off the machine's discharge conveyor, stacks it on pallets in the required pattern with slip sheets, and stages the full pallet for the forklift. Steady line rate, open plant floor shared with forklifts and coworkers.

Keeping the machine supplied with stacked/cased packaging materials: lifting stacks of corrugated blanks, cartons, trays, pads or sleeves off pallets staged beside the line and loading them into the case packer's or cartoner's magazine/feeder; also placing cases of pouches or components onto the infeed conveyor.

Filling machine hoppers with bulk product or ingredients: cutting open 25-50 lb bags or emptying totes/cartons of powder, granules, snack pieces or hardware into the feed hopper of a filler/bagger, keeping the level up during the run, handling dust and disposing of empty bags.

Feeding empty containers and loose components: pushing layers of empty bottles, jars, cans, tubs or trays from pallets onto the infeed conveyor, dumping boxes of caps/closures/pumps into a sorter hopper, loading small parts onto spindles or into vibratory feeders, keeping the feed from starving or jamming.

Roll changes on form-fill-seal, wrapping or labeling equipment: hoisting a 20-50 kg roll of film, foil or labels onto the unwind spindle/mandrel, aligning and locking it, and threading or splicing the web through the machine before restarting.

Small co-packer, cannery or seasonal plant with frequent SKU changeovers: hand-feeding assorted product onto conveyors or into filler hoppers, moving totes between stations, and unloading finished packs into cases or totes in a cramped, variable line layout.

instances.label: End-of-line case packing in a food/beverage/CPG plant: finished, uniform primary packages (pouches, bags, bottles, cartons, jars) come down a conveyor and the worker collates them and places them into corrugated shipping cases in a set count/pattern, then closes the case. tasks.label: Stock and sort product for packaging or filling machine operation, and replenish packaging supplies, such as wrapping paper, plastic sheet, boxes, cartons, glue, ink, or labels.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Beverage/food/consumer-goods plant: keeping the filler or packer supplied with product and containers — bringing pallets or totes of empty cans, bottles, jars, pouches or bulk product from the staging area to the line and loading them onto the machine infeed/hopper, repeatedly through the shift, on an open plant floor with forklift traffic.

Cannery/bakery/produce or meat plant: sorting and staging incoming product before it reaches the packaging machine — culling damaged or off-spec pieces, orienting and grouping items, arranging them on the infeed belt or into trays so the machine runs without jams.

Replenishing web packaging supplies on a form-fill-seal machine, flow wrapper, stretch/shrink wrapper or labeler: fetching a heavy roll of film, laminate, wrapping paper or label stock from the supply rack, stripping its wrap, mounting it on the spindle/mandrel and threading or splicing the web.

Replenishing stacked packaging supplies: moving pallets or bundles of corrugated cases, carton blanks and trays to the cartoner/case erector/tray former, cutting straps, removing slipsheets, and loading blank stacks into the machine magazine while the line runs.
Refilling adhesive on the line: keeping the hot-melt melter/gluer topped up with adhesive pellets from bins or boxes at the case sealer or cartoner.

Replenishing small consumables on coders and printers: ink and make-up fluid cartridges for CIJ coders, thermal-transfer ribbons, small pre-printed label rolls and similar supplies, each in a different awkward machine-specific holder.

instances.label: End-of-line closure of shipping cases in a food/CPG plant: worker folds flaps and secures filled corrugated cases with tape or hot-melt glue (occasionally staples) as they come off the packing line; mostly uniform case sizes, steady cadence, seals must hold for palletizing.

High-rate consumer-bag closure in a bakery, produce house or snack plant: worker gathers the bag neck and applies a twist tie, plastic bread clip, wire tie or metal clip to individual retail packages moving past on a conveyor.

Bundling and unitizing finished packages for shipment: strapping or banding cartons and bundles, cross-tying bundles with twine or polytape, securing bundles of trays or multipacks; sizes vary within a run.

Attaching fasteners, tags and seals to finished consumer packs: applying tamper-evident seal labels, glued closure stickers, printed closure tags or hang tags, and plastic security fasteners to cartons and bagged goods.

Manual pack-out bench for variable or non-standard orders (e-commerce fulfillment, kitting, mixed multi-item cartons, soft goods): worker sizes and closes each parcel by taping, gluing or stapling, with the parcel differing order to order.

tasks.label: Clean and remove damaged or otherwise inferior materials to prepare raw products for processing.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Cannery/packhouse inspection belt: worker stands at a moving grading conveyor of incoming raw produce (peas, corn, beans, potatoes, fruit) and pulls out rotten, bruised, off-color pieces, stems, husks, insects and other extraneous vegetative matter before the product goes to blanching/filling. Wet, cold, high-throughput shift work.

Bulk raw-material pre-clean: removing foreign material (stones, soil clods, wood, metal, plastic, glass) and off-spec pieces from bulk streams of grain, nuts, dried fruit, diced or IQF product feeding the filling line; operator monitors and hand-picks at a picking table or dumps and screens material.

Container prep on a filling line: inspecting incoming empty bottles, jars, cans or tubs for chips, cracks, dirt or residue, pulling defective ones out of the line, and rinsing/blowing out containers before they reach the filler.

Washing raw product and cleaning handling containers: running/attending wash, destone, polish and dry stages for soiled root crops or produce, hosing off dirt and debris, and washing out bins, lugs and totes before product is loaded for processing.

Prep-station hand trimming: cutting away bruised, discolored or damaged portions, bone fragments and defects from raw meat, poultry, fish fillets or vegetables at a table/belt station so only sound product enters the filling or packing machine.

Non-food packaging line: checking incoming packaging components and raw stock (carton blanks, preforms, closures, film, trays, small parts) as it is fed to the machine, and pulling crushed, dirty or off-spec items out of the feed so the machine runs clean.

tasks.label: Apply coatings, such as paint, ink, or lacquer, to protect or decorate workpiece surfaces, using spray guns, pens, or brushes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Furniture/cabinet/millwork plant finishing room: worker hand-sprays stain, sealer and lacquer topcoat onto batches of wood parts (doors, drawer fronts, frames) racked, hung, or laid on carts in a downdraft booth; must get uniform film build, no runs/sags, and color consistency across the batch.

Job shop or product plant coating small manufactured articles — plastic housings, toys, metal hardware, jewelry findings, sign panels — racked or hand-held and sprayed/dipped with primer, color, and clear coat in a booth; short batch runs with frequent part and color changes.

Ceramics/glass plant: spraying glaze or enamel onto ware and applying decorative ink, gold banding, or painted patterns to pottery, tile, plateware, or glassware; fragile ware, even coverage, decoration registered to the piece.

Hand touch-up and finish repair: worker inspects assembled or handled goods (cabinets, furniture, molded/painted parts) for scratches, sand-throughs, and color mismatch, then applies stain, toner, glaze, or paint with a pen, brush, or small spray gun at each defect and blends it into the surrounding finish; defect location, size, and color differ on every piece.

Custom/one-off decoration in a small studio or shop: airbrushing or hand-painting a specified design, logo, lettering, or pinstripe onto individual articles (helmets, guitars, glassware, giftware, props) to a customer proof.

On-site sign and mural work: painting lettering, a logo, or a large image on a building wall, storefront, or hoarding, working outdoors from a ladder or lift in ambient conditions with no controlled layout.

tasks.label: Examine finished surfaces of workpieces to verify conformance to specifications and retouch any defective areas.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Finishing/decorating department of a manufacturing plant: sprayed or lacquered articles (metal giftware, high-gloss plastic or wood components, painted panels) arrive on racks or a conveyor; worker examines each piece under inspection lights against a finish standard for dirt nibs, dust inclusions, orange peel and gloss defects, and repairs them locally by sanding out the blemish and buffing/polishing the spot back to the specified gloss.

Furniture, cabinet or millwork finishing shop: worker examines assembled stained-and-topcoated pieces for color mismatch, sand-throughs, blotching, nicks and dust nibs, then retouches with color markers, padding stain, glaze, burn-in sticks and blend spray, feathering and rubbing out so the repair is invisible on an assembled three-dimensional item.

Ceramic, porcelain or glass decorating plant: worker inspects hand-painted, banded or decal-decorated tableware, ornaments and giftware for gaps in gold bands, smeared or misplaced decoration, skips and blisters, and retouches with a fine brush and matching enamel/lustre before the decorating fire, holding the piece by hand under a lamp.

Toy, figurine, model and collectible decorating line: worker checks small mask-sprayed, pad-printed and hand-detailed parts for missing paint, bleed under the mask, and misregistered details, then retouches tiny features with a fine brush or scrapes/wipes away excess paint on parts a few centimeters across.

Small custom or artisan studio (personalized glassware, hand-painted signs and furniture art, decorated leather, enameled jewelry): one-off or short-run items are checked against a customer proof or sample for color, line quality and coverage, and retouched freehand; every job differs in substrate, artwork and acceptance criteria.

Field/on-site touch-up after delivery or installation: worker inspects installed cabinetry, store fixtures, decorated architectural glass or delivered furniture at the customer's home or premises and retouches scratches, chips and rub marks with markers, fill sticks and small airbrush work amid furniture, people and uncontrolled lighting.

tasks.label: Clean and maintain tools and equipment, using solvents, brushes, and rags.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: End-of-shift/between-color cleaning of hand brushes, liners, sponges, palettes and small hand tools at a wash station in a decorating shop (pottery/glass/furniture/toy decorating): soak or flush in water or solvent, work the ferrule clean, wipe on rags, reshape and stow.

Cleaning a hand-held spray gun or airbrush after a color run: relieve pressure, dump and wipe the cup, disassemble air cap/needle/nozzle, flush fluid passages with solvent, brush the cap holes, wipe the body with a solvent rag, reassemble and test-spray.

Flushing and cleaning paint delivery hardware after a color change: pressure pots, siphon cups, mixing containers, hoses and fluid lines flushed with solvent, containers scrubbed and drained, solvent waste handled per shop rules.

Cleaning paint-fouled ancillary equipment: racks, hangers, jigs, holding fixtures, masks, stencils and decorating screens with built-up cured coating, stripped/soaked/scrubbed or run through a stripping process until reusable.

Preventive maintenance on tools and equipment: inspecting for wear, replacing worn spray tips, needles, nozzles, seals, filters and brush sets, lubricating packings, checking hoses/regulators, and logging the work.

Housekeeping of the work station and booth as part of equipment care: wiping down benches, turntables, booth walls/windows and equipment housings with solvent rags, sweeping/mopping overspray, changing booth filters.

sources.transferJustification: Directly the 'clean paint-fouled fixtures and equipment' portion of the task, done by machine cycle instead of hand solvent-and-brush work.

sources.system: M&R Eco-Tex / Eco-Tex Lite automatic screen cleaning and reclaiming system
sources.title: ECO-TEX Automatic Screen Cleaning and Reclaiming System :: M&R
sources.claim: M&R's Eco-Tex is a commercial automatic screen cleaning and reclaiming system that removes ink and emulsion from decorating screens inside an enclosed machine with recirculated chemistry and no direct employee contact with the cleaning process.
sources.transferJustification: Decorating workers who screen-print glass and plateware clean screens and stencils with solvent and brushes; the machine performs that cleaning with the screen presented to it.

sources.system: ABICOR BINZEL TCS Compact / BRS torch cleaning station
sources.title: TCS Compact Nozzle Cleaning Station | ABICOR BINZEL

sources.transferJustification: Related task: cleaning process residue from a hand-tool-scale applicator with small orifices at a purpose-built station, closely comparable to cleaning a spray gun nozzle and air cap.

sources.system: Nasarc TES (REVOLUTION360 torch, AUTOTIP tip changer, AUTOCLEAN maintenance center)

sources.transferJustification: Related task: replacing worn consumable tips and nozzles and cleaning them on a process tool is the same maintenance act as changing worn spray tips, needles and air caps on paint equipment — small threaded parts, similar precision, in a purpose-built cell.

tasks.label: Read job orders and inspect workpieces to determine work procedures and materials required.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Wood furniture/cabinet finishing shop: worker takes a job ticket (stain color, sheen, quantity, customer spec), inspects the raw or repaired wood parts on a cart or bench - grain, mill marks, glue squeeze-out, dents, patches, prior sealer - and determines the prep and coating schedule (grit sequence, filler, sealer, stain, topcoat) and the materials to pull.

Production plant hand-decorating articles (pottery/plateware, glassware, toys, leather goods): worker reads the decorating order specifying pattern, color and quantity, inspects each blank or bisque piece for chips, warpage, glaze faults and correct shape, and determines whether it is fit to decorate and by which method (decal, banding, hand-brush, spray) and which paints/glazes are needed.

Job-shop coating/painting operation (metal fabrication, powder coat, plastics): worker reads the traveler/print, checks the part against the order, inspects incoming parts for oil, rust, weld spatter, prior finish and threads/holes to mask, and determines pretreatment, masking, coating type/color, film build and cure schedule.

Custom or one-off decorative work (sign lettering, personalized hand-painted items, art glass, jewelry enameling, antique or furniture restoration): worker reads a customer order or sketch, inspects the specific item's existing finish, substrate and damage, and works out the sequence of steps and the specific materials/colors to use.

Rework/touch-up gate: worker inspects already-coated pieces against the job order and finish standard at the end of a line or in a touch-up booth, and determines for each piece whether it passes, needs touch-up, sand-and-recoat, buffing, or full strip, and what materials that will take.

sources.system: Omnirobotic AutonomyOS / OmniBrain (Shape-to-Motion)
sources.title: A Software Platform for Self-Programming, Autonomous Robotics | Products Finishing
sources.claim: Omnirobotic's AutonomyOS lets a finishing robot perceive each part arriving on a coating line in 3D and autonomously generate the coating process for it, including automatically programming itself for one-off rework parts in powder coating job shops.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous spray-coating path generation. It carries over because the system's first step is exactly this task - sensing the incoming workpiece and deciding the work procedure (coverage, passes, tooling) for it, on the same class of coated articles and in the same finishing-line setting.

sources.system: Omnirobotic PSA-80 PRO
sources.title: PSA-80 PRO: Autonomous Cabinet Door Sanding - Omnirobotic
sources.claim: The PSA-80 PRO is a commercial autonomous sanding cell for cabinet doors and panels: a mixed batch of parts is dropped on the table, the finish is selected, and 3D vision identifies each part and determines the sanding process with no jigs or programming.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous sanding of wood parts. Transfer holds because the machine must first inspect each unfixtured wood workpiece it is handed and derive the prep procedure for it - the same determination a finishing-shop worker makes on cabinet parts.

sources.system: 3M Finesse-it Robotic Paint Repair System with Inovision SMARTInspect and FANUC M-710iC robots
sources.title: General Motors and 3M Partner on New Robotic Paint System | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: At GM's Spring Hill plant a vision system inspects every vehicle body on the moving line, finds and categorizes paint defects, and robots then execute the corresponding sand-and-polish repair.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated paint-defect inspection and repair. It substantiates the inspect-and-determine step: the system judges each coated workpiece against the finish standard and decides per-defect what rework procedure and abrasive/polish materials are applied.

sources.system: Finesse Paint Repair inspection cameras
sources.title: Here's How GM Leverages AI In Its Assembly Plants
sources.claim: GM has multiple plants running the Finesse paint-repair cameras that identify surface imperfections on bodies moving through the line and feed the results into paint decision-making.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated inspection of coated workpieces. Same determination step as the task - grading a finished piece against spec to decide whether and how it must be reworked.

sources.claim: Robot-mounted reflectCONTROL deflectometry sensors at inspection stations in premium carmakers' paint shops detect and localize paint defects on finished bodies and feed downstream automatic error processing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic surface inspection of painted parts. The robot positions the sensor over the workpiece and classifies its surface condition - the perception-and-judgment core of inspecting a workpiece to decide what work it needs.

sources.system: ISRA VISION paint shop surface inspection (Car Paint Vision / PAINTSCAN)
sources.title: Intelligent machine vision solutions for paint shop applications
sources.claim: ISRA Vision supplies inline, robot-guided sensor inspection of painted add-on parts in paint shops that evaluates defects objectively against OEM specifications and relevance classes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: inspection of coated articles (add-on parts, not whole bodies) against a written specification, which is the same act as inspecting a workpiece against a job order to determine what finishing work it requires.

tasks.label: Select and mix ingredients to prepare coating substances according to specifications, using paddles or mechanical mixers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Wood furniture/cabinet finishing shop: worker reads a formula card or work order, selects stain concentrates, sealer, lacquer/conversion coating, catalyst and reducer from shelved cans, measures by volume or weight into a pot, blends with a hand paddle or drill-mounted mixer, checks viscosity with a Zahn cup, strains into the spray cup.

Production decorating/coating plant mix room ('paint kitchen'): batches of several gallons to a drum of paint, ink or coating made from bulk base, pigment dispersions, resin and solvent; components weighed or metered into pails/tanks, homogenized with a mechanical agitator or high-shear mixer, adjusted to spec for viscosity/color and released to the line.

Ceramic, glass or plateware decorating: glazes, engobes, underglaze colors and enamels prepared from dry frits, oxides and stains weighed on a scale, wetted with water or oil/medium, mixed with a propeller/paddle mixer, sieved, and adjusted to target specific gravity or working consistency.

Bench-scale custom color match in a shop with a standard tint or dye system: worker mixes a few ounces to a pint of paint, stain, enamel or leather dye to match a supplied sample or previously produced lot, drawing down/testing and adding tint increments with a small mixer until accepted.

Idiosyncratic artisan media mixed by feel with no written formula: china paints or lusters mulled with oil on a glass slab with a palette knife, gilding size, shellac/dye washes, gold-leaf mediums; the decorator judges body, tack and working consistency by hand and eye and adjusts on the fly.

Field/mobile work: furniture touch-up and restoration technician or on-site decorator mixes small quantities of stain, glaze, lacquer or enamel at a customer's home, retail showroom or in a van, matching the existing finish under whatever light and space are available.

sources.system: Axalta Irus Mix
sources.title: Axalta demonstrates Irus fully automated mixing machine | FenderBender and ABRN
sources.claim: Axalta Irus Mix is a commercially deployed automated body-shop mixing machine whose carriage retrieves each toner bottle from its cabinet, agitates it and doses it by weight into a cup on the machine's scale to build a paint formula.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automotive refinish paint mixing. Same act as the rated task - selecting specified ingredients and dosing/blending them to a formula - with the same class of pigmented solvent/waterborne coatings, gram-level precision, and pint-to-quart containers used by decorating workers.

sources.system: Axalta Irus Mix
sources.title: Axalta Announces 100th Installation of Fully Automated Axalta Irus Mix Machine for Automotive Refinish Industry
sources.claim: Irus Mix is a fully automated, hands-free mixing machine sold and installed in production body shops (100th installation announced July 2024); the operator selects a formula and the machine mixes it.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as above: formula-driven selection and blending of coating ingredients, delivered to a color-accuracy standard an employer accepts in place of a hand mix.

sources.system: PPG MOONWALK
sources.title: GOOD TO THE LAST DROP - BodyShop Business
sources.claim: PPG MOONWALK automatically verifies the correct toners by barcode and dispenses each component to the specified weight, replacing hand pouring in the shop's mixing room.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: refinish color mixing. Ingredient identification (barcode) plus gravimetric dosing to a specification is the machine analogue of selecting and measuring coating ingredients per a formula card.

sources.system: PPG MOONWALK

sources.transferJustification: Establishes deployment scale for the refinish mixing machine cited above; the underlying operation (select and dose coating ingredients to a formula) is the rated task.

sources.system: Chemspeed FORMAX (paints and coatings configuration)
sources.title: Automated high quality formulations for paints and coatings
sources.claim: Chemspeed FORMAX is a commercial robotic formulation platform built specifically for paints and coatings: it gravimetrically dispenses liquids, pastes and solids into vessels/blenders and mixes/disperses them under program control.

sources.claim: Chemspeed's coatings platforms dispense materials spanning water-thin to extremely viscous and combine gravimetric dispensing with dual asymmetric centrifuge mixing - machine preparation of pigment pastes and high-viscosity coatings to a recipe.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated coating formulation in R&D/QC. It covers the same physical operations - dosing selected ingredients including powders and viscous pastes and homogenizing them - on the same materials as shop-floor coating preparation.

sources.system: COROB Automatic In-Can Production Line
sources.title: Automatic In-Can Production Line for Paint
sources.claim: COROB supplies fully automatic in-can paint production lines in which cans are fed and barcode-scanned, colorant and base are dispensed to the recipe, lids are placed and closed, and heavy-duty gyroscopic mixers homogenize the finished coating.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-plant tinting/batch make-up of paint. It is the same task - dosing selected ingredients to a formula and mechanically mixing them - at production volumes, with the machine also handling the containers.

sources.system: COROB TATOCOLOR / D600 automatic dispensers and gyroscopic mixers
sources.title: TATOCOLOR Automatic Paint Dispenser: Compact and Reliable
sources.claim: COROB automatic dispensers used in paint stores and labs meter colorants into a base can to fractions of a fluid ounce, with the shelf self-positioning for can size; matching gyroscopic mixers then blend the closed can.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: retail/lab paint tinting. Identical operation to the rated task at small batch size - selecting colorants per a formula, metering them accurately, and mechanically mixing the container.

sources.system: Palamatic Process DosingRobot
sources.title: Automatic powder dosing unit - DosingRobot | Palamatic Process
sources.claim: Palamatic's DosingRobot is a commercial enclosed dosing cell using a 6-axis robot and 12-36 powder feeders to weigh multiple dry ingredients per recipe and prepare premixes automatically.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: multi-ingredient powder batching. Glaze/enamel preparation begins with weighing several dry frits, oxides and stains to a recipe; this system performs that selection and gravimetric batching at comparable or finer tolerance inside a fenced cell.

sources.system: Graco ProMix 2KS
sources.title: Operation ProMix 2KS Plural Component Proportioner 312776L EN
sources.claim: Graco ProMix 2KS is a widely deployed electronic proportioner that meters and blends two-component catalyzed coatings at the specified ratio through a static mixer, replacing hand mixing of paint and catalyst.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: on-demand catalyzed coating mixing in finishing shops. Furniture/wood finishing mixes routinely require adding catalyst and reducer at a specified ratio; this machine performs that ratio mixing to production quality.

tasks.label: Place coated workpieces in ovens or dryers for specified times to dry or harden finishes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Custom/job finishing shop: worker hand-sprays or brushes coating on assorted metal, wood or plastic articles, sets them on racks or hangs them, then loads a batch cure oven or IR dryer, sets time/temperature, and unloads and inspects after cure. Mixed part types, varying batch sizes, shop floor shared with people.

Production coating line (powder or liquid): freshly coated parts hang on hooks/carriers or sit on trays that travel into a curing oven for a fixed dwell; worker loads/unloads carriers, verifies line speed and cure time, and pulls cured parts at the exit.

Ceramic/pottery decorating: glazed or decal-decorated ware placed on kiln shelves or kiln cars in a set pattern (no touching, spacing for airflow), fired on a specified schedule, then removed after cooling.

Small delicate items - decorated glassware, enameled jewelry, painted figurines - set on trivets, mesh trays or fixtures and placed in a small bench oven/kiln for a short specified cycle; wet or tacky finish must not be smudged; several short batches per shift.

Large or awkward coated pieces (furniture panels, doors, signage, fabricated frames) loaded on carts/racks and rolled into a walk-in drying room or large batch oven; door opened and closed, long cure timed, cart pulled out after cure.

sources.system: KUKA KR QUANTEC robots / Gaiotto glazing line at GSI Ceramica
sources.title: Automated Production Line in Ceramic Manufacturing | KUKA Global
sources.claim: At GSI Ceramica's ceramic plant, KUKA industrial robots handle in-house transport of glazed sanitaryware parts between processing stages and up to firing in the 1,250 ..., on an automated production line.
sources.transferJustification: Same task class: moving freshly glazed (coated) ware into a kiln for a specified firing cycle; comparable objects (glazed ceramic bodies) and comparable no-mar handling precision, in a purpose-built production line.

sources.system: MWES robotic heat-treat load/unload cell (Fanuc M-900iA/260L)

sources.transferJustification: Related task: loading workpieces into baskets for a timed oven thermal cycle and unloading them afterwards - the same load/dwell/unload cycle as placing coated workpieces in curing ovens, with rigid parts of similar size in a fixtured cell.

sources.claim: MWES installed six FANUC robot cells on an existing paint line: three load unpainted steel beams (4-12 ft, up to 80 lb) onto paint-line carriers and three remove painted beams and stack ..., at 15 seconds per beam.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robots put workpieces onto the carriers that carry them through the paint line's oven and take the coated pieces off after cure - handling of large coated parts into and out of ... drying stage of a finishing line.

sources.system: Harrop Robotic Sagger Handling System (Fanuc multi-axis robots)

sources.claim: Harrop commissioned a Fanuc robotic system that fills ceramic saggers, sets them (with lids) onto kiln cars for firing, and removes each fired sagger from the kiln car afterwards, using vision to locate saggers.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: a robot placing tray-borne items into an oven, holding them for a specified time and removing them at the right moment - the same insert/time/retrieve cycle as tray-loading small coated pieces into a bench oven, with purpose-built tray presentation.

sources.system: Moldow automated powder coating line (Toyota Material Handling Europe)
sources.title: Automated Powder Coating Line in two levels | Moldow
sources.claim: Moldow's automated powder coating line for Toyota Material Handling conveys freshly powder-coated parts by integrated conveyor lifts into the curing oven and cooling zone before returning them for unloading; the plant is PC-controlled and monitored from the production ....
sources.transferJustification: Direct: the mechanized conveyor system performs the 'place coated workpieces in the oven for the specified time' function, with dwell time set by line speed, in a purpose-built coating line.

sources.claim: Figure 02 humanoids ran a multi-month deployment on an active BMW Spartanburg line, autonomously picking sheet metal parts and inserting them into fixtures over ten-hour shifts supporting production of more than 30,000 vehicles.
sources.transferJustification: Frontier reference for humanoid pick-and-place inside a human-built plant; transfer is limited because the robot worked one fixed station with parts presented in known racks and inserted into dedicated fixtures - no oven tending and no freshly coated surfaces.

tasks.label: Clean surfaces of workpieces in preparation for coating, using cleaning fluids, solvents, brushes, scrapers, steam, sandpaper, or cloth.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Wood furniture/cabinet finishing shop: after machine or hand sanding, worker removes sanding dust from doors, panels, frames and assembled casework with compressed air, brush and a tack cloth or solvent-dampened rag before stain or lacquer; parts of many sizes arrive on carts to a finishing bench.

Scuff-sanding / de-nibbing a primed or first-coated article (furniture part, composite or sheet-metal body panel, decorated ware) with fine sandpaper or a scuff pad, then wiping/blowing the dust off before the next coat, to a uniform matte with no burn-through.

Glass, ceramic, plateware and toy decorating plant: batches of ware are washed, dried, de-dusted and de-staticked (brush, air, alcohol wipe) at a bench or on a conveyor immediately before hand decorating, screen printing or glazing; contamination causes print/coating defects.

Metal, plated or plastic parts and hardware in a coating shop: racks or trays of parts degreased in solvent/detergent, brushed or scrubbed to remove oils, buffing compound, scale or release agent, rinsed and dried before coating.

Delicate one-off artisanal articles at a bench — leather goods, jewelry, hand-thrown pottery, book covers — cleaned by hand with cloth, soft brush, solvent, and light scraping of residue; each piece a different shape, surfaces easily marred, worker judges by feel and eye how much to clean.

On-site/customer-location work: cleaning an installed or fixed item (architectural woodwork, a mural wall, a large sign, a restoration piece) with solvents, scrapers and cloths before applying a decorative coating; layout and conditions taken as found.

sources.system: Scan&Sand
sources.title: Scan&Sand helps automate labor-intensive ambulance manufacturing - The Robot Report
sources.claim: GrayMatter Robotics' Scan&Sand autonomous robotic sanding cell was deployed at Life Line Emergency Vehicles to sand raw and primed vehicle bodies (surface preparation before coating); the robot scans the part and generates its own program for high-mix geometries.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic abrasive sanding of raw and primer-coated bodies. It is the same surface-preparation-before-coating step this task names (sandpaper), on comparable fabricated panels, and the deployment shows the part is brought into a robotic cell and scanned rather than handled as found.

sources.system: EcoClean / EcoRS Clean Brush / EcoBlow-Off

sources.claim: Dürr supplies fully automated feather-duster machines and robot-mounted sword-brush systems (EcoClean, EcoRS Clean Brush, EcoBlow-Off) that remove loose dust and dirt from vehicle bodies immediately before painting; in use worldwide since the late 1980s.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: pre-paint cleaning of a workpiece with brushes and blow-off. It is the same dust-removal-before-coating step, done by robots, but only inside a paint-shop line where the workpiece is conveyed to the machine.

sources.system: Stäubli HE washing robots
sources.title: Robotic solutions for washing-cleaning parts | Stäubli United States
sources.claim: Stäubli sells sealed HE industrial washing robots used in production cells for low- and high-pressure cleaning, degreasing, rinsing and drying of workpieces before downstream operations such as coating.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic washing/degreasing of workpieces. This is the task's 'cleaning fluids, solvents' step applied to metal and plated parts, executed by an industrial robot inside a sealed washing cell.

sources.system: Rapid Series Sanding cell

sources.claim: Vention sells a turnkey robotic sanding cell (Rapid Series Sanding) for cabinet manufacturers and woodworkers; operators place panels on the cell's table and run recipes from a pendant.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: abrasive surface preparation of wood cabinet panels prior to finishing. Same workpiece class (furniture components) and same prep-for-coating purpose; the cell requires panels to be placed on its own table, i.e. work brought to the machine.

sources.system: Combi Sword Brush Una U 121
sources.title: Cleaning of furniture boards and panels with Sword Brushes
sources.claim: Wandres Combi Sword Brush machines clean furniture boards and panels in industrial production, removing chips and dust generated by machining before subsequent processes such as coating.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: dedusting furniture panels in production. Same workpieces (furniture components) and the same dust-removal step this task performs with brush and cloth, but on a machine the panels are fed through.

sources.claim: GrayMatter Robotics operates 25+ robotic cells running real customer production work in which robots autonomously sand, grind, polish, ... of diverse materials and geometries, self-programming from a scan of a previously unseen part.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: abrasive and blast surface treatment of high-mix parts. Blasting and sanding are the cleaning-before-coating operations of this task; the demonstrated setting is a floor of enclosed robotic cells fed with customer parts.

sources.system: Wilder Systems automated sanding cell
sources.title: Press Release | Sanding Robot — Wilder Systems
sources.claim: Wilder Systems designed, built and integrated a custom automated robotic sanding ... at Hughes Bros. Aircrafters, using compliant sanding end-effectors, custom suction-grip fixtures and pre-programmed paths to replace manual sanding.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated sanding of aerospace parts for finish preparation. Confirms that current deployed surface-prep robots rely on custom fixtures holding the workpiece, i.e. an E1 presentation.

sources.claim: GrayMatter Robotics was cited in the 2026 RBR50 awards for an autonomous mobile robotic sanding deployment ..., an aircraft painting company, for aerospace MRO surface preparation.

Suggests movement toward robots that go to the workpiece, but the source is a secondary aggregator of a company post and the workpiece (aircraft skin) differs from the bench-scale articles in this occupation.

tasks.label: Conceal blemishes in workpieces, such as nicks and dents, using fillers such as putty.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Wood products/flooring/cabinet plant: flat components (panels, boards, veneered stock, door fronts) travel through the finishing line; worker locates knots, checks, small voids and nail holes and presses in colored wood putty, scraping it flush so the part can be sanded and stained. Repetitive, high volume, parts presented one at a time.

Furniture/cabinet finishing room bench work on shaped or already-assembled parts: nail holes in face frames and mouldings, dents on turned legs, chipped edges and corners of a case. Worker picks the matching putty color, works it into the void by hand or knife on a curved or inside-corner surface, wipes excess, passes the piece on for sanding and stain.

Final touch-up/repair station (end of finishing line, warehouse or store repair bench) on already-finished goods: worker fills a dent, gouge or scratch in a lacquered surface with wax fill stick, burn-in stick or glazing putty, levels it, and blends color and sheen so the repair is invisible on a customer-ready piece.

Ceramic/glass/plateware/concrete-product plant (nonmetallic mineral manufacturing): worker patches chips, pinholes, mold-seam marks and small voids in greenware, bisque ware or cast product with slip, filler or patching compound before it is glazed, decorated or coated. Small three-dimensional ware, hand-held, varying shapes.

Coating/engraving shop or metal fabrication finishing: worker fills weld pits, porosity, casting flaws, dents and parting-line marks in metal or resin articles (fabricated parts, castings, jewelry, toys, giftware) with body filler or epoxy putty, then sands flush before painting or plating.

Repair/refinish shop prep (automotive repair and maintenance and similar large-article refinishing): worker mixes and applies plastic body filler or spot/glazing putty over nicks, dings and dents on a panel in place on the vehicle or article, then block-sands and feathers it level before primer and paint.

sources.system: WINTERSTEIGER Timber Repair & Cosmetics range (TRC 1000, TRC Panel, TRC Woodpatch, TRC Preclean)
sources.title: TRC timber cosmetics by Wintersteiger
sources.claim: The TRC product line is currently marketed as systems that detect, clean and fill defects in the top layer ... for flooring, furniture and boards, using thermoplastic or organic filling material or real wood inserts, including multi-color repairs on one component and repair of defects at component edges.

sources.system: WINTERSTEIGER TRC 3000 at Scheucher Holzindustrie
sources.title: "Fully-automatic timber cosmetics" at Scheucher Holzindustrie
sources.claim: Scheucher Holzindustrie runs a fully automatic TRC 3000 system in production: a scanner finds the cracks or knots to ... in the top layer and fixes their exact position, and software computes the filler quantity within seconds.

sources.title: Veneer Patching Line R7 - Raute
sources.claim: Raute's Veneer Patching Line R7 is a fully automated line that uses machine-vision analyzers to find veneer defects and patch them out; it is installed in production mills (e.g., Paged's Morag mill, 2013).

sources.system: Woodot

tasks.label: Rinse, drain, or wipe coated workpieces to remove excess coating material or to facilitate setting of finish coats on workpieces.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Wood furniture/cabinet finishing department: after stain, glaze or filler is applied to doors, panels, frames and mouldings, the worker wipes back the excess with a rag, pad or brush to even the color and clear the surface before sealer/topcoat; parts move on carts and conveyors at line pace, other people work nearby.

Metal/plastic parts coating shop: racks, baskets or barrels of dip-coated, lacquered or plated parts are rinsed in water/solvent tanks, held to drain over the tank, spun or blown off, and drips wiped from fixtures and part edges before cure or the next coat.

Glass, plateware and jewelry decorating: small delicate items that have been dipped, enameled, lustred or lacquered are rinsed, set to drain on trays, and excess coating is wiped from rims, edges, threads and unwanted areas with cloth or solvent swab before firing/curing.

Small custom/artisan finishing shop: one-off or short-run pieces (antiquing glaze wiped back on carved furniture, hand-decorated art ware, refinished antiques) where how much coating to wipe off and leave in crevices is judged by eye for appearance, on shapes the shop has not run before.

On-site/field touch-up: wiping excess stain, glaze or finish on installed cabinetry, millwork or furniture in a customer's home, showroom or job trailer, working around furnishings and uncontrolled conditions.

tasks.label: Dispose of hazardous waste in an appropriate manner.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Auto-body/refinish shop: at end of shift the painter drains spent gun-wash solvent and paint thinner from the gun washer and mixing bench into a labeled satellite-accumulation drum, closes the bung/lid, wipes spills, and returns the drum to the flammables area. Mixed small volumes, varied containers, open shop floor with people and vehicles around.

Industrial coating line (metal, wood, plastic parts): operator pulls saturated overspray arrestor filters / paint-clogged pads from the booth plenum or floor grates during a changeover, bags them, and drops them in the labeled hazardous-waste container. Heavy, floppy, paint-loaded media; awkward reach inside booth structure.

Routine shop housekeeping of paint waste: solvent-soaked rags and tack cloths, used mixing cups and strainers, empty and partially full paint/hardener cans, and used masking collected from benches, booth, and mix room and segregated into the correct oily-waste can and hazardous-waste bin. Small, deformable, scattered, mixed items.

Transport and staging: sealed and labeled drums/pallets of accumulated hazardous waste (spent solvent, filter waste, paint sludge) are moved by drum dolly or pallet jack from the paint area to the central 90-day accumulation area and staged for the licensed hauler's scheduled pickup. Fixed indoor route, standard drums and pallets.

Water-wash / downdraft booth cleanout: coagulated paint sludge is skimmed, shoveled, or vacuumed out of the booth sump and dewatered, then loaded into drums and sealed for disposal; cured overspray scraped off grates. Wet, sticky, heavy, confined booth space, done on a periodic cleanout schedule.

Plating / e-coat / powder line: spent chemical bath, rinse concentrate, or reclaimed waste powder is pumped or transferred into drums or totes at a dedicated transfer station, containers closed and sealed for hazardous-waste pickup. Bulk liquid or dry powder, piped or pumped source.

tasks.label: Monitor painting operations to identify flaws, such as blisters or streaks, and correct their causes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Collision-repair/auto body shop: painter hand-sprays sealer, basecoat and clearcoat on a repaired vehicle in a downdraft booth, watching the wet film for runs, sags, fisheyes, dry spray/streaking and solvent pop or blisters; diagnoses the cause (gun pressure/fluid setting, contamination, wrong reducer for booth temperature, moisture in air line), corrects it mid-job or between coats, and after bake de-nibs and polishes remaining defects before delivery.

General industrial finishing line in a metal-fabrication, machinery or plastics plant: operator tends a conveyorized reciprocator/robot spray booth coating parts, checks parts coming off the line under inspection lights for runs, streaks, orange peel, thin coverage and blisters, gauges film thickness, and corrects causes by adjusting fluid/atomizing pressure, gun position and line speed, cleaning or replacing tips and filters, and correcting material viscosity.

Powder coating line: operator monitors parts leaving the booth and after cure for thin build, orange peel, faraday-area voids and contamination, measures film thickness, and corrects causes by adjusting gun voltage/powder output, reciprocator stroke, gun-to-part distance, and cleaning guns/hoses and the recovery system.

Wood, furniture or cabinet finishing shop: operator sprays or flat-line coats stain, sealer and lacquer, inspects for streaks, blush, runs, orange peel, dust nibs and bubbling, and corrects causes (adjust viscosity/retarder for humidity, change fluid tip, adjust air pressure or conveyor speed, clean booth filters), then scuff-sands and recoats affected pieces.

High-volume automotive OEM or tier-1 paint shop: operator/monitor oversees robotic body or bumper painting, inspects bodies at the light tunnel/inspection deck for dirt inclusions, craters, sags and blisters, feeds defect data back, and corrects causes (purge/clean the atomizer, change a filter or paint batch, adjust applicator parameters, address booth cleanliness).

Specialty and small-batch coating work: glassware and ceramic glazing, medical device or aerospace component coating, one-off or short-run job-shop spraying, where the operator monitors each piece for streaks, crawling, pinholes or blisters and adjusts spray technique, material and equipment for that specific part and material.

Industrial liquid-finishing plant (wood, metal, plastics): shift-end/color-change teardown of manual and automatic spray guns, pressure pots and cups, fluid hoses, filters and tips — solvent flush, disassemble the front end, wire-brush dried coating from caps and tips, wipe, reassemble and verify spray.

Automated liquid coating line (robot or reciprocator booth): routine color-change and shift-end cleaning of the automatic applicators/bell atomizers — purge and flush the paint channels, clean the air cap/bell exterior and shaping-air holes of overspray so the applicator sprays to spec on the next run.

Automated liquid coating line: scheduled deep maintenance of an automatic applicator — remove it or its bell cup/air cap/fluid nozzle/needle, soak parts in solvent, clear hardened paint from small orifices with brushes and picks, wipe, reassemble to torque and re-qualify the pattern.

Powder coating booth: color-change cleanup of the application equipment — purge and blow out the hopper, injectors, powder hoses and gun interiors, wipe down gun bodies, so the system runs clean powder on the next color.

Support/power equipment maintenance in the shop: disassembling airless or paint-circulation pumps, regulators, filters and agitators (also sanders and other power tools), cleaning caked coating off parts with solvent and wire brushes, replacing seals/packings, reassembling and running a test.

instances.label: Auto-body/refinish or small-shop finisher, end of a paint job: take the HVLP/gravity spray gun and cup to the mix room, dump leftover material, disassemble the gun (cap, nozzle, needle), flush and scrub passages with solvent or water, blow dry, reassemble and check the spray pattern; also clean mixing cups, sticks, strainers and wipe the mixing bench. Routine between-job cleanup of the spray booth interior: blow down and wipe overspray dust from walls, ceiling and lights, sweep or vacuum the booth floor and grates, remove tape/paper scraps and masking debris so the next job is contamination-free.

Periodic booth maintenance cleaning: peel and re-apply peel-coat or masking film on booth walls and window glass, lay new floor paper, pull and replace intake ceiling filters and exhaust/paint-arrestor filters, scrape hardened paint from grates and door seals, clean light lenses. General housekeeping of the shop or finishing department: scrub/sweep large concrete floor areas around booths, ovens and conveyors, pick up dust, chips and dropped parts, hose or squeegee spills, empty trash and rag bins at shift end.

Deep cleaning of ancillary finishing equipment: strip cured paint/powder buildup from parts hangers, hooks, racks, jigs and masking fixtures; clean dip-tank rims, paint kitchen strainers and filter housings; scrape and rinse conveyor components so parts hang and ground properly.

Metal fabrication / structural steel or machinery shop: apply rust-inhibitive shop primer or undercoat to blasted steel plate, profiles and weldments and caulk/seal lap joints and seams on assemblies before topcoat, with parts moved by crane, cart or conveyor.

Field / on-site industrial coating: prime and seal in-service steel - storage tanks, bridge members, building metal panels, equipment - taken as found outdoors, working from lifts or scaffolds, caulking seams and spot-priming rusted areas in variable weather.

tasks.label: Determine paint flow, viscosity, and coating quality by performing visual inspections, or by using viscometers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Collision-repair/vehicle refinish shop mixing room: painter mixes and reduces the refinish paint to formula, checks its viscosity by filling a Ford/Zahn flow cup and timing the drain (or with a shop viscometer), shoots a test card to check atomization and fluid delivery from the gun, and adjusts reducer/pressure until the material sprays right.

Collision-repair shop booth/inspection bay: after spraying, painter inspects the wet and cured finish on the vehicle under booth and handheld inspection lights for runs, sags, dirt nibs, orange peel, dry spray, solvent pop, mottling and color/blend match to adjacent panels, and decides accept, de-nib/polish, or respray. Vehicle make, color and repair area differ every job.

Industrial finishing plant, liquid coating line (metal, wood, or plastic parts): operator periodically draws paint from the circulating system, tank, or pressure pot and checks viscosity with a Zahn/Ford cup and stopwatch or a viscometer, checks fluid delivery rate at the gun/bell by timed shoot-out into a graduated cup, and adds solvent or adjusts pump/pressure to hold the spec.

Industrial finishing plant, line-side inspection: operator watches parts leaving the booth/oven on the conveyor or racks and judges coating quality - coverage, thin spots, runs, sags, orange peel, gloss, dirt inclusion - plus spot film-thickness checks with a gauge, and pulls/tags rejects for rework while the line runs.

Field or job-shop coating away from a fixed line: spraying structural steel on site, bridges/tanks, marine or heavy/agricultural equipment, or custom items in a small shop. Shop reach access: worker carries, opens and positions a step ladder or extension ladder, or rolls a mobile work platform up to a large workpiece (truck body, tank, machine frame) to reach upper surfaces; levels it on the shop floor, locks spreaders or casters, and moves it several times during the coating job.

Scaffold erection and dismantling inside a plant, fabrication shop or shipyard around a large item to be coated: carrying frames/tubes, couplers and planks, leveling base plates, connecting and bracing sections, laying planks and guardrails, tagging it off, then striking it after the coating job.

Confined-space or enclosure ventilation: positioning a portable blower/ventilator outside a tank, vessel or temporary enclosure, feeding and securing flexible duct through the manway or opening to the interior, connecting power, verifying air movement and adjusting during blasting/coating.

Field/outdoor coating job (bridge, water tower, tank farm, building exterior, customer site): setting extension ladders on uneven ground, erecting scaffolding and containment sheeting, positioning portable blowers/exhaust units and a generator, and running hoses and cords across the site.

tasks.label: Adjust controls on infrared ovens, heat lamps, portable ventilators, or exhaust units to speed the drying of surfaces between coats.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Conveyorized industrial finishing line (metal, plastic, wood parts) in a plant: between primer/base/topcoat stations the operator adjusts flash-off tunnel and IR/convection oven zone setpoints, lamp intensity, conveyor speed and booth exhaust/air-makeup at the line HMI so each coat is dry before the next station.

Batch finishing in a manufacturing plant or job shop: racks/carts of sprayed parts are moved into a walk-in batch or IR panel oven, or dried in the booth; operator sets temperature, lamp banks and timers, switches booth exhaust or a portable ventilator on, checks flash-off by touch and re-adjusts before recoating.

Collision-repair / vehicle refinish booth or prep bay: between filler, primer, basecoat and clear the painter runs the booth flash/bake cycle and positions and sets a portable or rail-mounted infrared arch (distance, program, time) over the repaired panels, then checks cure before the next coat.

Small custom shop (cabinet/furniture finisher, sign shop, small fabricator): clamp-on heat lamps on stands, box fans and portable exhaust units are aimed at odd-shaped workpieces on benches or carts in an ad hoc layout; operator moves and dials them in by feel and by ambient humidity between coats.

On-site/field coating work (tank interior, structural steel, large equipment at a customer site): operator sets up and adjusts portable heaters, dehumidifiers, blowers and exhaust ventilation, changing settings with weather and confined-space conditions to force-dry each coat.

tasks.label: Apply primer over any repairs made to surfaces.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Collision repair shop: after body filler is applied and sanded on a car or light-truck panel, the painter mixes 2K primer surfacer, masks adjacent panels, and sprays two to three coats over the repaired area in a prep station or downdraft booth; vehicle models, damage size and repair location differ job to job.

Heavy/large-vehicle and equipment refinish bay (trucks, trailers, buses, RVs, rail cars, off-highway machines): the operator spot-primes welded, filled or sanded repair areas on large units parked in a shop bay or large booth before topcoating, working from ladders/lifts around the unit.

Manufacturing coating line rework/touch-up station inside a plant: parts or bodies that came back from weld grinding, porosity filling or sand-through repair are re-primed on the repaired area with a hand or automated spray gun before returning to the coating line.

Wood furniture, cabinet or millwork finishing room: after defects are patched (filled knots, repaired dents, sanded-through edges), the sprayer primes/seals the repaired areas of the piece in a spray booth before the topcoat, with pieces on carts, racks or a conveyor.

Field/on-site maintenance coating: priming spot-blasted or repaired areas on installed assets (storage tanks, bridge steel, structural steel, building exteriors, ship hulls in dock), reached from lifts, scaffolding or rope access, outdoors and weather-dependent.

tasks.label: Fill small dents or scratches with body fillers and smooth surfaces to prepare for painting.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Collision-repair shop stall: prep tech scuffs a small dent/ding on an attached vehicle panel (door, fender, quarter), mixes two-part polyester body filler with hardener, spreads it in thin conforming layers over the curved panel, lets it cure, then rough-sands and block-sands to the panel contour with feather-edged paint transition, ready for primer.

Auto body shop prep bay: glazing/spot putty applied over pinholes, sand scratches and low spots on a primed panel or a detached part (bumper cover, hood) on a stand or paint rack; putty squeegeed thin, dried, then hand/DA-sanded and feather-edged to a paint-ready surface with no mapping.

Transportation-equipment plant or heavy-vehicle refinish shop (truck body, trailer, bus, RV): filling weld seams, small dents and handling scratches on large steel, aluminum or fiberglass panels with body filler, then sanding flat over long spans before primer, often on ladders/lifts alongside other trades.

Metal fabrication / industrial coating shop: fabricated steel or aluminum parts arrive on carts or hooks; operator fills weld pinholes, grind marks, casting flaws and scratches with polyester filler or glaze, sands smooth by hand or with a DA sander before primer, paint or powder coat.

Wood panel, flooring or cabinet finishing plant: filling knots, checks, nail holes and small surface defects in flat wood boards and panels with wood putty/filler as they move through the finishing line, then sanding smooth before stain, sealer or paint.

Field or yard work: touching up dents, gouges and scratches with filler on installed equipment, aircraft in a hangar, machinery or a hull in a boatyard; variable access, awkward positions, weather and lighting, work performed where the item sits.

tasks.label: Mix paints to match color specifications or original colors, stirring or thinning paints, using spatulas or power mixing equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Collision/auto-body refinish mix room: painter retrieves the formula from a paint code or spectrophotometer reading, sets a can on the scale, weighs in each toner from the shelved/stirred toner rack, shakes or stirs the mix, adds activator and reducer at the mix ratio, strains into the gun cup and labels the leftover.

Industrial coating plant / paint kitchen: operator batches 5-gallon pails, drums or supply tanks of primer, enamel or 2K catalyzed coating, runs a pneumatic/lightning power mixer or tank agitator, adds thinner and catalyst to the datasheet ratio, checks Zahn-cup viscosity and adjusts, then charges the circulation pot feeding the spray line.

Custom match with no usable formula: matching a faded original finish or a customer sample by measuring/eyeballing the target, tinting a starting formula in small increments, spraying let-down or spray-out cards and re-tinting until the match is accepted.

Wood/furniture or cabinet finishing shop: tinting stains, sealers, glazes and lacquers from concentrated bases to a sample chip, thinning topcoats to spray viscosity, catalyzing conversion varnish, stirring by hand paddle or drill mixer for the day's run.

Booth-side small-batch pot mixing: mixing a few hundred milliliters to a quart in a graduated mixing cup at the ratio printed on the can (paint:hardener:reducer), stirring with a stir stick, straining into the gun cup for a spot repair or touch-up, then cleaning cups and sticks.

tasks.label: Remove grease, dirt, paint, or rust from surfaces in preparation for paint application, using abrasives, solvents, brushes, blowtorches, washing tanks, or sandblasters.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Production coating line in a plant: operator hangs metal parts on conveyor hooks and tends a multi-stage wash/pretreatment tunnel (alkaline degrease, rinse, phosphate/iron treatment, dry-off), checking parts for residual oil, dirt or flash rust before they enter the powder/e-coat booth, and hand-wiping or re-running rejects.

Job-shop / OEM finishing department: worker preps a mixed run of medium parts (fiberglass, plastic, wood or fabricated metal) at a bench or on racks - solvent/wax-and-grease wipe, scuff sanding of primer or gel-coat, feathering of small defects, air blow-off and tack rag - before they are sprayed.

Auto body / vehicle refinish shop: painter preps a repaired vehicle - washes the panel, degreases with wax-and-grease remover, block-sands and feather-edges body filler and primer over the repair area, scuffs adjacent panels and blend zones, blows off dust and tacks the surface before priming/basecoat.

Blast booth or blast room in a fabrication/heavy-equipment shop: operator abrasive-blasts rust, mill scale and old coatings off steel weldments, castings, structural sections or wheels to a specified surface profile, then blows off spent media and dust before the parts go to the paint booth.

Field / on-site prep: crew cleans and de-rusts large fixed items where they stand - storage tanks, in-place machinery, ship or barge hulls in a yard, structural steel - using solvents, power tools, hand tools and portable blasting or hydroblasting under variable weather and access conditions before recoating.

tasks.label: Sand and apply sealer to properly dried finish.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Collision-repair / vehicle refinish shop: after body filler and primer-surfacer have cured, the refinish tech block- and DA-sands the repair area flat and feathers the edges, blows off and tacks the panel, masks, then sprays a primer-sealer coat over the repair before basecoat. Vehicle sits in a prep bay or downdraft booth; every job's damage location and panel shape differ.

Cabinet/millwork or panel-furniture plant finishing department: batches of flat doors, drawer fronts and panels that received a sealer coat and were dried/UV-cured are sealer-sanded (denibbed) and then given the next sealer or build coat, either by hand on a table plus booth spraying or fed through the plant's finishing equipment. High volume, standard part sizes.

Furniture/millwork plant working shaped stock: profiled doors, curved panels, moldings, turned or shaped legs and small assemblies whose dried sealer coat must be scuff-sanded on contours and edges without cutting through, then re-sealed by spray. Parts come in mixed batches and are hung, racked or laid on a bench.

Metal fabrication / machinery / specialty-vehicle paint shop: large weldments, truck and equipment bodies whose cured primer coat is scuff-sanded (pole sanders, DA sanders, ladders/lifts for the top surfaces) and then a sealer/second primer coat is sprayed in the shop's booth before topcoat. Parts are large, one-off or low-volume.

Aerospace or marine component finishing bay: cured primer or gelcoat on fuselage panels, composite structures, boat parts or interior components is sanded to spec (thickness/roughness controlled, no burn-through) and a sealer/primer coat is then sprayed in a controlled coating facility with documented process specs.

Mobile / on-site work: technician goes to a dealership lot, fleet yard or customer site to spot-repair a coated surface — sands the cured primer or finish on a small area and sprays sealer from a portable rig, working outdoors or in a borrowed bay with no fixed layout or controlled conditions.

tasks.label: Inspect materials, components, or products for surface defects and measure circuitry, using electronic test equipment, precision measuring instruments, microscope, and standard procedures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In-line defect inspection of patterned production wafers in a fab cleanroom: technician stages a FOUP (or it arrives by OHT) at an optical/e-beam inspection tool load port, runs the layer recipe, and the wafer is scanned for particles, scratches, residues and pattern defects; defect maps are compared to spec and the lot is passed, held or sent to review.

In-line metrology on production wafers: measuring film thickness, critical dimensions, overlay, sheet resistance or step height with CD-SEM, ellipsometer/reflectometer, overlay tool or four-point probe; results are checked against SPC control limits and out-of-spec lots flagged for engineering.

Microscope-level review and visual inspection at a review station: high-magnification optical or SEM review of flagged defect sites and post-develop/post-etch visual checks for resist issues, scratches, edge chips and contamination, with each defect classified into a defect code and logged.

Electrical measurement of circuitry: wafer sort / parametric (e-test) probing of test structures and die on a prober tied to test equipment, or final test/inspection of packaged devices, measuring device parameters and binning good vs. failing units.

Incoming/outgoing quality inspection of bare and monitor wafers, substrates and packaged components: haze/particle counts and surface quality on unpatterned wafers, and dimensional/cosmetic inspection of packages, leads, bumps and substrates at an assembly-and-test facility.

Ad hoc inspection of non-standard items with hand-held instruments and a bench microscope: cracked or contaminated wafers pulled from a jammed tool, ingots/boules and sawn segments, quartzware, chamber parts and incoming consumables, inspected on a bench or at the tool with calipers, loupe and portable meters.

tasks.label: Clean semiconductor wafers using cleaning equipment, such as chemical baths, automatic wafer cleaners, or blow-off wands.

instances.label: Advanced 300mm logic/memory/foundry fab: lots of patterned wafers needing post-CMP, post-etch or pre-furnace cleans arrive in FOUPs. The technician dispositions the lot and gets it cleaned on a single-wafer or batch cleaning tool (SPM/SC1/dilute HF, rinse, dry) in a Class 1 cleanroom; wafers are never touched by hand and output is verified by particle/defect metrology.

150/200mm legacy or specialty fab (analog, power, MEMS, discretes, compound semi): technician retrieves a 25-wafer cassette or SMIF pod from a stocker, walks it to an automatic wafer cleaner (spin scrubber / batch spray / spin-rinse-dryer), docks it on the load station, selects the recipe, then unloads and visually inspects wafers in the cleanroom bay.

Manual wet bench batch clean on a small-volume or pilot line: technician in full gown moves a cassette with a quartz handle through a sequence of timed chemical baths (SC1, SC2, dilute HF), overflow DI rinse tanks and a spin-rinse dryer, monitoring bath temperature/concentration and drag-out at a fume-exhausted cleanroom bench.

University / R&D / prototype nanofab: mixed substrate sizes and cleaved coupons handled one at a time with tweezers, solvent beaker cleans (acetone/IPA) on a hot plate or in a fume hood, piranha or BOE dips, then rinse and nitrogen blow-off wand drying; containers, holders and recipes vary by user and project.

Ad hoc blow-off / spot cleaning at a workstation: technician uses an N2 blow-off wand or ionized air gun to remove visible particles or fibers from a wafer, carrier, cassette, chuck or fixture at an inspection microscope or tool load station before the item goes on.

Solar PV / LED / prime-wafer production line: cassettes or carriers of wafers run through an inline or batch wet-chemical cleaning system (saw-damage removal, RCA/ozone clean, rinse, dry) at very high throughput; technician loads/unloads carriers and monitors bath chemistry and breakage.

tasks.label: Inspect equipment for leaks, diagnose malfunctions, and request repairs.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Reactive first-response troubleshooting at a process tool (furnace, etch/CVD chamber, implanter, CMP) that has alarmed or thrown a process excursion mid-lot: technician reads the tool HMI error codes and trend/SPC data, opens access panels or the maintenance bay, checks fittings, hoses, O-rings, sensors, gas/vacuum pressures, may sniff or pressure-check a line, isolates a probable cause, puts the tool down and writes a maintenance work request with findings.

Routine per-shift walkthrough of a cleanroom process bay: for each tool on the checklist, check status/indicator lights and HMI screens, look at drip trays, slurry and DI lines, chemical fittings and load-port areas for drips or residue, read panel gauges (N2/CDA pressure, exhaust magnehelic, vacuum), listen for abnormal pump/blower noise, log readings and file work requests for anything out of spec.

Round through the subfab / facilities chase and chemical-gas delivery areas (football-field-scale space with thousands of dry pumps, abatement units, pipelines, valves, and exhaust ducts): check pumps and abatement for overheating, vibration, oil or coolant leaks and water/gas leaks at fittings, read local gauges, note anomalies, and raise repair requests.

Response to a gas leak or ambient-gas alarm in the subfab, gas farm or bulk-gas yard: technician goes to the flagged area, confirms whether a leak is real, localizes the source along piping/valves/pump exhaust with a detector, quantifies severity, and escalates with an urgent repair request while the area is restricted.

Suspected liquid chemical leak inside a tool enclosure or wet bench (acid/solvent/slurry drip detected by a leak sensor or seen as residue): technician dons PPE, opens the enclosure or crawls under the deck, finds the leaking fitting, valve or drain, verifies the chemical, contains the drip, and files an urgent repair request.

Post-maintenance or preventive-maintenance integrity verification: after a seal, valve or chamber part is changed, the technician verifies vacuum/gas-line integrity (pump-down rate, pressure-decay or helium leak check on the chamber or line), records the result, and either releases the tool to production or requests further repair.

instances.label: Production wafer lots in a 200/300 mm fab or wafer plant: technician runs the laser scribe/wafer-ID tool — brings the cassette/FOUP to the load port, selects the lot's mark data (SEMI T7 2D matrix / SEMI-OCR characters) per the traveler spec, marks each wafer in the designated edge band, and verifies the mark reads back before the lot moves on.

Engineering, R&D, or small-lot pieces at a bench in a cleanroom or lab: scribing or ink-marking IDs on partial wafers, coupons, odd-shaped or fragile pieces, or running a benchtop laser marker one piece at a time, with the ID and location taken from an engineer's work order.

Marking identification on carriers, quartz boats, cassettes, fixtures, jigs, or finished module/subassembly housings — dot-peen stamping, engraving, laser marking, or applying and verifying an etched/printed identifier on a hard, non-wafer object.

Marking IDs on grown crystal ingots, cropped blocks, or sawn segments in the crystal-growing/shaping area: applying the boule/segment number, orientation and grade information to a large, heavy workpiece after grinding or sawing.

tasks.label: Clean and maintain equipment, including replacing etching and rinsing solutions and cleaning bath containers and work area.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Wet-process bay of a wafer fab or R&D cleanroom: technician takes a chemical bath (BOE/HF etchant, SC-1, piranha, or a DI rinse tank) out of service, drains the spent chemistry to the waste system, rinses/wipes the tank, refills it from carboys, a chemical cart, or the plumbed chemical delivery line, verifies concentration/temperature, and logs the bath change. Full PPE, acid hood.

Parts-cleaning sink/station in the fab: technician cleans bath containers and quartzware — quartz tanks, diffusion-furnace tubes and boats, Teflon carriers/cassettes — by chemical soak, scrub, DI rinse, dry, and inspect before returning them to service.

Removable tool components: technician pulls spin-coater bowls and cups, chucks, developer nozzles/cups, wafer cassettes, saw hold-down fixtures, etc., cleans them (solvent/DI soak, wipe, rinse, dry), and reinstalls them at the tool.

In-place wipe-down and housekeeping at the tool: wiping bench tops, hood interiors, tool exteriors, load ports and windows with IPA-soaked cleanroom wipes; wiping up drips; emptying drain bottles and waste containers; restocking wipes and gloves; tidying wafer boxes and consumables in the work area.
Periodic particle-control cleaning of the work area's floor and aisles in the cleanroom bay: vacuuming/mopping perforated or vinyl cleanroom flooring around the tools, often on off-shift hours.

Scheduled preventive maintenance on a process chamber (etcher, PECVD, sputter tool): vent and open the chamber, remove and replace consumable kit parts (edge rings, liners, shields), clean polymer/deposit build-up from chamber surfaces, reassemble with torqued bolts, pump down and leak-check/qualify.

tasks.label: Load semiconductor material into furnace.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Advanced 300 mm cleanroom fab (logic/memory/foundry): technician stages a wafer lot for a vertical diffusion/oxidation/LPCVD/ALD batch furnace. FOUPs move from stocker to the furnace load port, 25-wafer lots are transferred into a quartz boat with dummy/monitor wafers, and the boat elevator raises the load into the tube. Cleanroom protocol, particle and lot-tracking requirements.

Legacy/specialty 150 mm or 200 mm fab (analog, power, MEMS, RF, discretes): operator moves cassettes or SMIF pods to a horizontal cantilever or vertical furnace load station, transfers wafers from cassettes into a long quartz boat, and pushes/loads the boat into the tube; frequent lot mixing, split lots, and monitor wafers.

Crystal-growing plant: technician hand-packs high-purity polysilicon chunks (irregular, several kg each) plus dopant into a fragile fused-silica crucible, then the crucible/charge is set into the CZ puller's hot zone before melt-down. Packing density, crucible integrity, and contamination control matter; recharging between pulls also occurs.

Photovoltaic/solar cell line: high-volume loading of large batches of thin silicon wafers into quartz boats for POCl3 diffusion/oxidation tube furnaces on a continuous cell line, with breakage-sensitive thin wafers and takt-time constraints.

R&D, pilot line, university cleanroom, or compound-semiconductor shop: loading small or non-standard substrates (2-6 inch GaAs/SiC/GaN wafers, coupons, cleaved pieces) into tube furnaces, RTP tools, or susceptors using tweezers and custom quartz carriers; recipes and carrier configurations change run to run.
