tasks.label: Drain, clean, and refill machines or tanks at designated intervals, using cleaning solutions or water.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Food/dairy/beverage processing plant, scheduled (end-of-run or nightly) cleaning of a process or wash tank: drain the used water/solution, clean the interior surfaces, refill with fresh water and cleaning solution to set concentration and temperature; stainless vessels plumbed to plant utilities, result verified by rinse checks or ATP swabs.

Brewery/beverage plant bottle washer or keg washer: at the designated interval drain the spent caustic bath, clear label pulp, glass fragments and settled sludge out of the tank, rinse it, then refill with fresh water and caustic to the specified concentration.

Industrial aqueous parts washer in a machine shop, engine remanufacturer or truck shop: shut the machine down, pump/drain the contaminated detergent solution, shovel or vacuum metal chips, sand and oily sludge out of the reservoir, wipe the walls and screens, refill with water plus detergent concentrate.

Metal pickling or plating line: drain a spent acid or rinse tank to treatment, flush out iron sludge and scale, check the tank lining, and refill with fresh acid or water; hazardous chemicals, acid-resistant PPE, occasionally confined-space work.

Institutional/industrial warewashing machine (flight-type dishmachine, bakery pan washer, laboratory glassware washer): drain the wash and rinse tanks, pull and clean scrap trays and filters, delime/scrub the chamber, and refill with fresh water and detergent.

Heavy wash plant (coal preparation, aggregate washing, pulp washer): drain a sump or settling tank at the scheduled interval, dig, hose or vacuum out tons of settled solids, then refill with process water.

Steel, tube or wire plant: tending a pickling/surface-cleaning line where coil or product runs continuously through acid tanks and rinses; operator monitors acid concentration, temperature and line speed from a pulpit, handles entry/exit coil changes, and inspects surface quality.

Reusable container cleaning: crate, tote, pallet, drum, keg or barrel washing at a food plant receiving bay or a drum/IBC reconditioning facility. Worker feeds soiled containers into a washer, inspects for residue and damage, re-runs failures, and stacks or palletizes clean containers.

tasks.label: Examine and inspect machines to detect malfunctions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Food/beverage plant, production running: operator walks the bottle/can washer, keg washer, CIP skid and adjoining conveyors on a routine round — reads pressure, temperature and level gauges, looks for leaks and drips, listens/feels for hot or noisy motors, pumps, gearboxes and drives, and reports anomalies for maintenance.

Heavy process plant (steel pickling line, coal preparation plant washer, pulp mill washing stage, chemical wash/clean line): routine condition round of pumps, tanks, valves, drives and piping in a hot, wet, dusty or corrosive area — checking for leaks, overheating, abnormal noise/vibration and out-of-range gauges.

While the machine runs, detecting an emerging malfunction from the process itself: containers jamming or tipping, product coming out dirty because spray jets are plugged, foaming or carryover, belt/chain mistracking, wash quality off — then narrowing the fault to a subsystem of the machine.

Machine stopped for shift start, changeover or post-CIP: open guards and access doors and inspect the interior — spray nozzles and headers for plugging or misdirection, screens/strainers, brushes, chains, belts and seals for wear and correct tension, lubricant and detergent levels, hand-checking for play and looseness.

After an alarm, trip, breakdown or a batch of rejects: examine the machine to locate what failed — check the suspect valve, solenoid, sensor, hose, motor and panel indications, try the function, and decide whether the operator can correct it or maintenance must be called.

Steel/galvanizing pickling line: sampling the acid bath with a suction tube or dipper, determining free acid and iron, then metering fresh hydrochloric or sulfuric acid and inhibitor from bulk storage through a measuring tank into the pickle tank to bring it back to concentration.

Weighing dry chemical (powdered detergent, soda ash, reagent or flocculant) on a scale and dissolving it into a measuring/make-up tank with metered water at a coal preparation plant, pulp mill or food plant, then transferring the batch to the wash circuit.

Small-scale batch mixing in a general-purpose area: filling a portable tank, small washer reservoir or bucket with a graduated jug of sanitizer/detergent concentrate and water (small bottling shop, glassware washroom, small keg line), stirring and verifying with a test strip or hydrometer.

tasks.label: Adjust, clean, and lubricate mechanical parts of machines, using hand tools and grease guns.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Scheduled lubrication round on a washing line (bottle/keg washer, produce or parts washer) during downtime: operator locates dozens of grease fittings on bearings, chain drives, cam followers and gearboxes, wipes each zerk, seats a grease-gun coupler, pumps the specified number of shots until purge is seen, and oils drive chains; wet, cramped, partly overhead access inside the machine frame.

Cleaning mechanical parts of the machine: removing guards, covers and access panels with hand tools, then brushing, scraping, blowing or hosing product residue, label pulp, scale, sludge and old grease off sprockets, chains, spray nozzles, screens, rollers and drive components, then refitting the guards.

Adjusting by fastener: re-torquing loose bolts and clamps found during inspection, securing spray-bar and bracket positions to spec, and setting fasteners on chain take-ups and covers with wrenches, sockets and screwdrivers on a stopped machine.

Dynamic adjustment with the machine running or jogged: tracking a conveyor belt, tensioning belts and chains by feel, aiming spray nozzles by watching the spray pattern, and setting clearances/gaps with feeler gauges while judging noise, wobble and wash quality.

Replacing worn wear items encountered during the round: swapping brushes, seals, gaskets, plugged or eroded nozzles, chain links or worn bushings, requiring partial disassembly of fouled, corroded or seized hardware and correct reassembly.

Lubrication and cleanup on large, heavy or harsh installations (pickling-line rolls and tanks, coal-preparation washer, bulk barrel/keg washer): climbing ladders and catwalks, hosing down build-up, and greasing many points on large drives amid acid mist, dust, heat and confined access.

tasks.label: Monitor pressure gauges, ammeters, flowmeters, thermometers, or products, and adjust controls to maintain specified conditions, such as feed rate, product consistency, temperature, air pressure, and machine speed.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Frozen-food plant, continuous spiral/IQF or cryogenic tunnel freezer line: operator watches HMI and gauges (evaporator/suction pressure, belt speed, infeed load, exit product temperature), spot-probes product temperature and looks at product on the belt, and adjusts belt speed, fan/refrigerant or cryogen injection setpoints to hold the frozen-core spec as load and product mix change through the shift.

Ice cream / frozen dessert plant, continuous (or batch) freezer: operator monitors draw temperature, overrun/air flow meter, mix feed pump rate, dasher motor ammeter and product consistency at the outlet, and adjusts refrigerant supply, air injection and pump speed to hold viscosity, overrun and draw temperature within spec.

Central ammonia/CO2 refrigeration engine room serving freezers, blast cells and cold rooms: operator makes rounds reading compressor ammeters, suction/discharge and oil pressures, vessel liquid levels and room temperatures, logs them, and adjusts compressor loading/sequencing, condenser fans/pumps, liquid feed and defrost schedules to hold suction pressure and room temperature setpoints.

Blast-freezer cells, cold-storage rooms, or pharmaceutical/blood-plasma freezing units in a GMP or chemical facility: operator starts the specified freezing profile, monitors chamber/room temperature and pressure charts and product core temperature, and adjusts controls (fan speed, setpoint, defrost, hold mode) to keep the batch inside its validated temperature band, documenting readings.

Older or small plant (seafood/meat plate freezers, brine chillers, small dairy) with mostly manual instrumentation: dial gauges and thermometers not wired to any control system, hand expansion/king valves and mechanical speed adjustments; operator walks the line, reads local gauges, hand-checks and probes product, and cracks or throttles hand valves and belt drives to correct off-spec conditions.

tasks.label: Read dials and gauges on panel control boards to ascertain temperatures, alkalinities, and densities of mixtures, and turn valves to obtain specified mixtures.

instances.label: Ice cream / frozen dessert plant: operator watches the continuous or batch freezer's panel (draw temperature, cylinder pressure, overrun/air-to-mix ratio, viscosity) during a run and start-up, and adjusts air and mix valves and pump settings to hold the specified overrun and draw temperature. Indoor sanitary production floor, plant-controlled access.

Dairy/beverage mix preparation and blending: operator reads panel indications of mix temperature and concentration (density/Brix/fat or solids) from inline transmitters and turns/throttles valves on the blending or standardization line to bring the mixture to recipe specification, including during ingredient changeovers. Indoor processing hall.

Sanitation / CIP cycle between runs: operator reads the CIP panel for solution temperature and detergent alkalinity (caustic concentration via conductivity) and operates valves to route the circuit and to add caustic, acid or water until the wash solution is at specified strength. Indoor plant, standard skid and piping.

Refrigeration machine room / freezing tunnel or blast freezer: operator reads compressor and refrigerant panel gauges (suction and condenser pressure, evaporator and product-side brine/glycol temperature, oil pressure) and adjusts expansion, liquid-feed, hot-gas defrost and brine mixing valves to hold specified conditions. Indoor equipment room within a plant or cold-storage facility.

Legacy or partially manual line: local analog dial gauges and thermometers plus hand-wheel valves, with periodic grab-sample checks (hydrometer for brine/mix density, titration strip for alkalinity); operator walks the line, reads the local dials, and cranks manual valves to correct the mixture. tasks.label: Start machinery, such as pumps, feeders, or conveyors, and turn valves to heat, admit, or transfer products, refrigerants, or mixes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Ice cream / frozen dessert plant, start of run: operator starts mix feed pumps and the continuous freezer, opens sanitary butterfly and plug valves on lines from ageing tanks to the freezer barrel, admits refrigerant to the barrel, then starts the extrusion/filling conveyor into the hardening tunnel. Wet, cold floor; other workers, hoses and portable equipment present; valves and local start/stop stations are human-facing hardware spread along the line.

Frozen-food plant IQF / spiral freezer line: operator starts the infeed conveyor, freezer belt and evaporator fans, opens liquid ammonia or CO2 supply hand valves at the freezer's refrigeration skid, starts the recirculation pumps, and throttles/admits refrigerant as product load builds. Standard plant layout, sub-zero enclosure, PPE required.

Refrigeration engine room and cold-storage warehouse: operator starts compressors, ammonia/CO2 pumps and condenser fans from local motor-control panels, and opens/closes king, suction, liquid-line and hot-gas defrost hand valves (handwheels, gear operators) on vessel manifolds to transfer refrigerant, pump down a vessel, or bring a room online. Hazardous refrigerant, lockout/tagout discipline.

Cryogenic and blast freezing for food or biologicals (including blood plasma / pharma shock freezers): operator opens the LN2 or CO2 supply valve from the bulk tank, purges the line, starts the tunnel conveyor and circulation fans, or loads a blast/plasma freezer, admits refrigerant and starts the programmed freeze cycle. Clean, institution-controlled room; documented cycle records required.

Chemical or industrial process cooling: operator starts chillers, brine/cooling-water pumps and agitators, opens valves to admit product or coolant to a chilled reactor, crystallizer or heat exchanger, and lines up valves to transfer chilled product to storage or the next unit. Fixed piping and skids, local panels plus a control-room HMI.

tasks.label: Correct machinery malfunctions by performing actions such as removing jams, and inform supervisors of malfunctions as necessary.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Frozen-food plant, spiral or tunnel (IQF) freezer: product backs up or fuses to the belt at the infeed/discharge or the belt tracks off; the tender stops the line, opens an access door, enters the cold enclosure, breaks out and removes stuck product with a scraper/mallet, checks belt tension and tracking, restarts, and logs the stoppage.

Jam on the equipment immediately downstream of the freezer (bagger/flow-wrapper, case packer, metal detector reject chute, checkweigher): torn film, crushed carton, or a toppled package blocks the path; the tender clears the debris and any product in the machine, resets the fault on the HMI, restarts, and scraps affected product.

Ice cream / frozen-novelty line: batch or continuous freezer, filler, extruder or moulding line malfunctions — product freezes up in the barrel, a nozzle or fruit feeder clogs, sticks jam in the inserter; the tender purges or partially disassembles parts, clears the blockage, re-sanitizes contact surfaces, and restarts.

Refrigeration or ancillary fault the operator is expected to correct: heavy frost/ice on evaporator coils, door seals or product entry curtains, a failed defrost cycle, a tripped sensor or drifting temperature; the tender chips/scrapes ice, adjusts setpoints, resets the controller, verifies temperature recovery, and tells the supervisor what happened.

Malfunction beyond the operator's scope, noticed while monitoring or on rounds of the freezing/refrigeration equipment (compressor or motor overheating, abnormal noise or vibration, refrigerant/air leak, gauge or temperature reading out of range): the tender recognizes the abnormal condition and escalates it to the supervisor or maintenance rather than fixing it.

tasks.label: Assemble equipment, and attach pipes, fittings, or valves, using hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Ice cream / frozen dessert plant: after CIP or wash-down, the operator reassembles a continuous or batch freezer — inserts the dasher and scraper blades, seats O-rings and shaft seals, bolts or clamps the front head onto the barrel, and torques fasteners with wrenches before restarting the run. Wet floor, cold room, parts of several kilos.

Food/beverage processing plant: setting up a product run by connecting flexible sanitary hoses and swing-bend piping between mix tanks, pumps, the freezer and the filler — seating gaskets, mating tri-clamp/bevel-seat fittings and tightening clamps or unions by hand and with a spanner, then checking for leaks.

Frozen-food plant with a cryogenic (LN2/CO2) or mechanical freezing tunnel: attaching the cryogen supply hose and vacuum-jacketed fittings to the tunnel manifold, fitting or swapping spray nozzles/injection headers, connecting exhaust ducting and glycol/brine lines, wrench-tightening threaded and flanged joints before start-up.

Plant machine/compressor room or behind installed equipment: replacing or attaching a valve, strainer, gauge or gasketed fitting on refrigerant, glycol or brine piping — isolating, unbolting the old part, dressing threads/flange faces, fitting the new valve and torquing it up with hand tools in cramped, cold, sometimes overhead positions.

Pharmaceutical / blood-plasma / specialty-chemical facility: assembling freezer or lyophilizer service connections in a controlled room — attaching tubing sets, sanitary or compression fittings, sample valves and manifolds to plasma freezers or cold chambers, using hand tools and documented torque, under cleanliness and integrity requirements.

Non-food cooling/freezing operations (chemical, pharma, plasma/biologics): operator weighs chemicals, additives, cryoprotectant or glycol/refrigerant charges to a documented recipe and loads them into a process vessel, tank or freezer unit, with batch-record documentation and containment requirements.

tasks.label: Adjust machine or freezer speed and air intake to obtain desired consistency and amount of product.

instances.label: Large frozen-dessert plant, continuous (scraped-surface) freezer on an ice cream line: operator trims mix pump rate, air injection to hit the overrun target (e.g. 100%), dasher speed and drawing temperature so product leaves at the specified stiffness and weight per gallon; re-trims during runs and at flavor/SKU changeovers, verifying by cup weights.

Small creamery, gelato/foodservice production room or product-development lab, batch freezer: operator selects and adjusts beater speed, freezing time and air incorporation, judges stiffness by feel/eye and checks fill weight, and re-adjusts between batches and recipes.

Blood center or pharmaceutical/biotech facility: operator runs plasma blast freezers or controlled-rate freezers, setting and adjusting cooling rate, cryogen/air handling and cycle timing for the load so product reaches the specified core temperature and quality within the validated time.

instances.label: Ice cream / frozen dessert plant: continuous freezer feeding a rotary cup/pint/quart filler. Open-plant sanitation shift in a frozen-food/meat/poultry/beverage plant: rinsing down the outside of freezing tunnels, spiral freezers, conveyors, chillers and floors with hose, applying foam detergent, rinsing, then spraying a sanitizing solution over all equipment surfaces in a wet, chemical-heavy environment during the cleanup window.

Clean-out-of-place work: fittings, valve seats, gaskets, hoses, dasher blades and small freezer parts that cannot be CIP'd are taken off, cleaned and sanitized in a COP tank or wash cabinet, then dried and staged for reassembly.

Hands-on inspection: after flushing, the operator opens sight glasses, unions and spray devices, looks and feels for milkstone/product residue, checks gaskets, seals and spray balls for wear, plugging or leaks, takes ATP/swab verification samples, and re-cleans or replaces parts before release to production.

Plasma/pharmaceutical or chemical facility: sanitizing or steam-flushing transfer lines, filling circuits and freezer/chiller loops to a validated sterilization or sanitization recipe, with pressure, temperature and hold-time documentation for the batch record.

Mid-run spot sanitizing while the line is running: wiping and spraying sanitizer on filler nozzles, hoppers, sample valves and contact surfaces between batches or after a jam, working around moving equipment and other people on the floor.

instances.label: Ice cream / frozen-dessert plant: operator draws liquid mix from a flavor tank, mix line, or batch-freezer feed valve into a cup, checks Brix/total solids with a handheld refractometer and pH with a meter at a bench beside the line, logs the result and flags off-spec mix. Juice, soft-drink or beverage chilling/freezing operation (concentrate, chilled fill, slush/frozen novelty): operator pulls a sample from a line sample cock or takes a filled container off the line, measures degrees Brix with a refractometer and pH, and adjusts blend or reports to QC. Plant floor / at-line QC bench.

Winery, brewery or cidery cold-side cellar with glycol-cooled tanks: cellar worker opens a tank sample valve, fills a cylinder, floats a hydrometer for specific gravity/Brix and reads pH (and titratable acidity) before or after cold stabilization. Tanks of varied design, valves at differing heights, wet floor.

Chemical / industrial process cooling or crystallization (brine, glycol, solution cooling, ammonia refrigeration side streams): operator collects a grab sample from a plant sample point, tests specific gravity with a hydrometer and pH with a meter in the plant lab, and adjusts concentration.

Frozen finished/solid product check: operator retrieves hardened product from a freezing tunnel exit, hardening room, or packing line, tempers, melts or homogenizes it, then measures Brix/soluble solids and pH on the prepared sample. Variable, non-pumpable sample; sub-zero areas.

tasks.label: Start agitators to blend contents, or start beater, scraper, and expeller blades to mix contents with air and prevent sticking.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Large ice cream / frozen dessert plant, continuous freezer: at the start of a production run the operator engages the dasher, beater and scraper blades in the freezing cylinder as mix and air are metered in, sets blade speed/overrun and viscosity for the product recipe, and keeps the blades turning (and restarts them after brief line stops) so the barrel does not freeze up.

Dairy, beverage or prepared-food plant, refrigerated storage silos, mix ageing tanks and flavor/blend tanks: operator starts tank agitators on schedule or before a transfer to blend contents, redisperse stabilizers and prevent fat separation or stratification in chilled product.

Small creamery, gelateria production lab or novelty producer, batch freezer: after mix is poured into the barrel the operator starts the beater/dasher, runs it while the product stiffens, watches consistency and overrun, and holds the blades turning until extraction.

Chemical / pharmaceutical / industrial process plant: operator starts agitator or scraped-surface blades in a jacketed chilling, crystallizing or blending vessel to keep the batch moving, avoid ice or solids building on the cooled wall, and hold uniform temperature during cooldown.

Frozen food plant, scraped-surface freezers and slush/brine chillers for purees, concentrates or slurries: operator starts scraper/expeller/mutator blades in coordination with product feed and refrigerant so product is continuously scraped off the chilled surface and discharged.

Non-routine restart: blades have jammed, seized or become caked with frozen product; the operator shuts down, opens/clears the barrel or vessel by hand, checks blades and seals, then bumps and restarts the blades at reduced speed while watching motor load and product behavior.

Small or specialty operation (small dairy, commissary, short run, R&D batch): tabletop or semi-manual mould press/cutter with frequent fixture swaps, non-standard tooling, hand feeding of frozen slabs, operator judgement on portion appearance.

tasks.label: Place or position containers into equipment, and remove containers after completion of cooling or freezing processes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Continuous in-line freezing in a food/beverage plant: the tender positions filled containers, packages or trays onto the infeed belt of a spiral, tunnel or hardening freezer, keeps spacing/orientation correct, and takes the frozen containers off at the discharge into cases or onto pallets. Batch blast freezer / blast cell in a food plant or cold-storage facility: the operator moves pallets, wheeled racks or carts of cartoned or trayed product into the freezer room or cell with a pallet jack or forklift, positions them for airflow, closes the door, then pulls them out after the cycle and checks/records product temperature.

Meat, poultry or seafood plant (including factory vessels): the operator loads pans, cartons or bulk product into horizontal/vertical plate or contact freezers, presses/closes the stations, and removes the frozen blocks or cartons after the freeze for packing.

Bakery, prepared-foods or commissary operation: the worker loads sheet pans, trays or containers onto rolling racks/trolleys, rolls them into a blast chiller/freezer or walk-in, and removes them after the chill/freeze cycle. Mixed product sizes, human-scale doors and aisles, kitchen or bakery floor.

Pharmaceutical, plasma or laboratory setting: the tender places vials, trays, bottles, plasma bags or sample racks into a lyophilizer, blast/plate freezer or ultra-low-temperature freezer in a cleanroom or lab, and removes them after the cycle, with lot documentation and sterility/cold-chain requirements.

tasks.label: Scrape, dislodge, or break excess frost, ice, or frozen product from equipment to prevent accumulation, using hands and hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: During a production run in a frozen-food plant, the operator opens access doors of a spiral or straight-belt IQF freezer and knocks/scrapes frost and stuck frozen product off belt edges, guide rails, transfer chutes, product infeed, fan guards and drip pans with a plastic scraper, mallet or gloved hands, in -30F air, cramped, without damaging belt links or sensors.

End-of-run / pre-sanitation defrost of a freezing tunnel or spiral: after the hot-gas or water defrost cycle, workers enter the enclosure to break up and shovel out residual ice slabs and slush from the floor, drain troughs, coil faces and belt returns before washdown; bulk ice of irregular shape, ladder and stoop work in a wet, cold enclosure.

Walk-in blast freezer / cold storage ice control: chipping and breaking frost sheets and ice stalactites off evaporator coils and coil guards, ceiling panels, structural trusses, refrigerant piping, door frames and floor ridges, using ice scrapers, chisels, mallets and shovels from a ladder or lift, then hauling the ice out.

Frozen product removal from process equipment during changeovers or jam clearing: dislodging frozen product from a batch/continuous freezer barrel and dasher, moulds and mould plates, plate-freezer plates, trays, extruder heads and fill nozzles - parts often unbolted and worked at a bench or cleared in place with scrapers and mallets.

Non-food freezing operations (blood plasma, pharmaceutical, chemical): scraping frost off plate/blast freezer shelves and gaskets, lyophilizer condenser and cold-trap surfaces, cryogenic tunnel components and chiller heat-exchanger faces in a controlled, validated facility, taking care not to scratch product-contact surfaces.

tasks.label: Activate mechanical rakes to regulate flow of ice from storage bins to vats.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Packaged/industrial ice plant: operator starts the mechanical rake in a bulk ice storage bin and regulates discharge rate so ice flows from the bin through screws/conveyors into receiving vats, hoppers or bagger bins; monitors bin level, ice quality and jams during a shift.

Seafood/fish processing plant or dockside ice house: operator activates the rake in a flake-ice bin to send measured ice to icing vats, fish tubs or slurry tanks as chilling demand arises; hygienic stainless equipment, cold wet floors, batches vary with landings.

Bakery, dairy, beverage or chemical plant: operator activates ice storage rake/screw to dose flake ice from a silo into dough mixers or process vats by weight or temperature demand, several times per batch.

Older or small plant with a legacy manual-control bin: ice bridges or packs, the rake stalls or the discharge chute plugs, and the operator jogs the rake, breaks up bridged ice, hoses the chute and judges flow visually while filling vats.

tasks.label: Stir material with spoons or paddles to mix ingredients or allow even cooling and prevent coagulation.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Food or chemical plant, large-vessel batch cooling: worker works a long-handled paddle through a 100–500 gal jacketed kettle, tank or vat of sauce, dairy mix, syrup, curd or chemical solution as it cools, sweeping the walls and folding the batch so it cools evenly and does not skin, lump, set up or crystallize. Heavy, sustained force; hot/cold vessel; sanitary rules.

Ice cream / frozen dessert production: stirring the mix in the batch-freezer barrel or blending tank during freezing, scraping the cylinder or tub walls, and folding candy, nuts or fruit inclusions through a stiff semi-frozen batch with a paddle so they distribute evenly and no large ice crystals form.

Small-batch / bench-scale food work (small creamery, chocolate and candy shop, commissary, test kitchen): hand-stirring with a spoon or small paddle a pot, bowl, bakery tub or pan of custard base, ganache, fudge, pudding or sauce set out to cool, mixing in additions and watching consistency by eye and feel.

Bench/lab-scale chemical, biotech or pharma cooling: stirring a flask, beaker, carboy or small reactor of solution while it is chilled, to keep solids in suspension, keep the temperature uniform, and prevent crystallization, gelling or clumping; done at a lab bench or pilot station under written procedure.

Blood plasma / biologics cold processing in a blood bank, plasma center or pharma cleanroom: gently swirling or agitating plasma bags/bottles, cryoprecipitate or cell products during freezing, thawing or cold hold so the product stays uniform and does not clump, aggregate or coagulate.

tasks.label: Inspect etched work for depth of etching, uniformity, and defects, using calibrated microscopes, gauges, fingers, or magnifying lenses.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Awards/personalization shop (trophy, gift, jewelry engraving): worker checks one-off rotary- or laser-engraved plaques, tumblers, medals, pet tags, rings and hollowware at the bench under a loupe or magnifier — cut depth consistent, no skipped strokes, burrs, chatter or double-strike, fill even, artwork centered — on mixed substrates (brass, coated aluminum, acrylic, wood, leather, precious metal), a different job every few minutes.

Industrial nameplate / tag / panel shop: batch runs of etched or laser-engraved metal and laminate plates, control panels, serial-number tags and data-matrix marks; worker inspects depth of engraving/etch, character legibility and stroke uniformity, paint-fill quality, and defects (missed characters, smearing, pitting) with a magnifier, depth gauge and go/no-go standards, sampling or 100% by lot.

Photochemical machining / chemical milling job shop: worker inspects lots of etched thin sheet-metal parts (shims, screens, lead frames, encoder discs, half-etched fold lines) for etch depth on half-etched features, undercut, line/edge uniformity and defects, using a stereo microscope, optical comparator/measuring stage, micrometer and depth gauge, against drawing tolerances and FAIR/PPAP paperwork.

Printing-industry engraving/plate-making: worker checks engraved or etched gravure cylinders, anilox rolls, flexo plates and screen-printing screens for cell/engraving depth, cell wall condition, screen-count uniformity and engraving defects, using a scanning microscope, magnifier and depth measurement before the form is released to press.

Etcher-circuit processor in PCB / flex-circuit / electronic component production: worker inspects freshly etched inner layers, flex circuits and etched metal parts for line width and spacing, undercut, opens/shorts, nicks, protrusions, pinholes and residual copper, using calibrated microscopes and measuring reticles on production panels.

Glass, stone and decorative etching: worker inspects sandblasted or acid-etched glassware, mirrors, awards and monument/stone lettering for frost depth and evenness, blowouts, resist lift, chipped edges and uneven coverage, judging by eye, raking light and fingertip feel on large, heavy or curved pieces.

instances.label: Retail/award & personalization shop: high-mix small batches of giftware (glass tumblers, wine glasses, acrylic and wood plaques, metal plates, pens, tumblers). Worker unwraps and inspects items, wipes with solvent/alcohol, peels protective film, applies masking tape or a cut photoresist/vinyl sandblast stencil and burnishes it, then loads the item into a laser or rotary jig. Items change every job; bench-scale hand work.

Industrial photochemical machining / PCB / nameplate plant: sheet or panel stock sheared or laser-cut to size, chemically cleaned, degreased and brush-scrubbed, then coated with light-sensitive enamel (roller-coated liquid photoresist or hot-roll dry-film laminate) under safelight, buffered and staged for exposure. Repetitive, high-volume, flat stock.

Engraving job shop / industrial marking: batches of like metal or plastic workpieces (nameplates, mold blocks, valve bodies, gun parts, machine tags) cut to size on shear/saw/laser, deburred and sanded/blasted, degreased in a washer, then fixtured for pantograph, rotary or laser engraving.

Jewelry / hollowware hand- or machine-engraving prep: individual rings, bangles, lockets, flatware and trophy cups are pre-polished and buffed, ultrasonically cleaned/degreased, set into an engraver's block or fixture, and given a wax or transfer layout for the cut. Small, delicate, high-value pieces; damage tolerance near zero.

Art / architectural glass studio: large flat mirrors, glass panels and door lites are washed and dried, then covered with sandblast resist film or wax/acid resist, with the pattern registered to the panel, before deep etching or acid etching.

On-site / field prep: adding an inscription to a headstone already set in a cemetery, or lettering installed architectural glass, a cornerstone or a memorial plaque in place. tasks.label: Prepare etching chemicals according to formulas, diluting acid with water to obtain solutions of specified concentration.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Small custom engraving / photoengraving / metal-marking shop: the etcher mixes a few gallons of etchant (e.g., nitric acid and water for zinc or magnesium plates, or ferric chloride) by pouring from 1-gallon jugs into water in a tray or bench tank, stirring, and checking strength with a hydrometer or test kit; done at a vented bench in PPE, containers handled by hand.

PCB or photochemical-machining production plant: technician makes up and replenishes etch, developer and stripper baths in machine reservoirs, adding acid concentrate and water to a posted formula, titrating or reading specific gravity, adjusting to spec and logging the result.

Industrial etch line tank charge-up: after dumping and rinsing a several-hundred-gallon etch tank, the worker charges it from drums/totes of concentrated acid plus DI water to a specified concentration, then samples and adjusts to spec before production restarts.

Glass / decorative etching studio: small batches of hydrofluoric or ammonium-bifluoride etch solution mixed or diluted from purchased concentrate per a recipe in jars or buckets at a ventilated bench, hand-stirred and labelled.

Screen-print / photo-etch prep area: mixing developer, stripper and etch solutions from concentrate at posted dilution ratios into buckets or machine reservoirs, checking with test strips or a conductivity meter and topping up during the shift.

Glass and mirror etching shop: masked or stencil-resisted glass awards, panels and mirrors are exposed to hydrofluoric-based acid cream or an acid dip to develop frosted designs and lettering, held for the specified dwell, then flushed, neutralized and demasked; work done under fume extraction with acid-handling PPE.

Fine-art printmaking studio: an artist's grounded or aquatinted copper/zinc intaglio plate is bitten in ferric chloride, with the plate repeatedly pulled from the bath and inspected, bubbles feathered off, and stop-out varnish brushed onto selected areas between successive bites to build the tonal range; bite judged by eye and by proofing rather than by a fixed recipe.

Artisan / one-off hand etching (printmaking studio, jewelry shop, firearms or trophy engraver): a copper, zinc or steel piece of irregular shape is lifted from the acid, neutralized in a baking-soda bath, and the wax hard ground or asphaltum resist is dissolved off with solvent, rags and brushes without marring the polished surface. Bench work, one piece at a time.

Glass, mirror or stone etching shop: after HF acid-cream or acid-bath etching, the panel is flushed and neutralized, the resist mask or stencil is stripped or peeled, and the glass is washed and dried before inspection. Flat panels handled on benches and washing lines in a shop.

tasks.label: Set reduction scales to attain specified sizes of reproduction on workpieces, and set pantograph controls for required heights, depths, and widths of cuts.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Awards/trophy/gift engraving shop: operator sets up a computerized rotary or laser engraver for a plaque, tumbler or award — scales the layout so the text fills the specified plate area, selects cutter/lens, sets the Z reference and cut depth (typically 0.003–0.010 in) or laser focus and power, runs a test cut on scrap, then adjusts. Retail/commercial shop premises, standard equipment, one-off or small batches.

Industrial identification/nameplate or part-marking production run in a manufacturing plant: setting character heights, cut depth and stroke width to a print spec (e.g., 0.005 in deep, 1/8 in characters), setting the reproduction scale so the mark fits the panel or part, verifying a first article, then running the batch on a CNC rotary engraver, laser marker or dot-peen unit.

Traditional manual pantograph (New Hermes / Gorton style): operator loosens and repositions the pantograph arm pivots to the marked reduction ratio (e.g., 2:1, 4:1), loads master copy type in the copyboard, sets the cutter depth stop with the micrometer collar, makes a trial cut on scrap and re-adjusts ratio and depth until size and depth match the order. Small shop bench.

Die, mold, stamp or seal engraving from a master pattern (3D pantograph or CNC engraving mill in a tool-and-die/machine shop): set the reduction ratio from pattern to workpiece, set roughing and finishing cutter heights and depth stops on hardened steel, verify depth by measurement before the finish pass.

Jewelry and small personal-item engraving (ring inner/outer band, bracelet, pendant, pen, medical ID) in a jewelry store or personalization counter workroom: fixture the piece in a jig, set a very small reproduction size, set a shallow depth on a curved or thin section so as not to cut through, test on scrap or a hidden area.

Portable / oversize-workpiece marking taken to the piece: a portable dot-peen or hand-held engraver used on a large casting, an installed plaque, a monument, machinery in a customer facility or yard — operator sets character height, force/depth and layout against an as-found, unfixtured surface with variable lighting and access.

tasks.label: Print proofs or examine designs to verify accuracy of engraving, and rework engraving as required.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Small commercial engraving/awards/signage shop: after laser or rotary engraving a plaque, trophy, sign, ID tag, pet tag, or customer-supplied gift item, the engraver prints or displays a proof for approval, then examines the finished piece on the bench under light (text accuracy, centering, depth, missed strokes, burn residue, paint-fill quality) and reworks it - re-runs a pass to deepen, re-cuts on a fresh blank, cleans, or touches up the fill. High-mix, mostly one-off jobs on items of every shape.

Industrial production marking/engraving line: nameplates, data plates, serial numbers, logos and 2D data-matrix codes engraved/marked on metal or plastic parts. Worker verifies each mark against the job file (legibility, position, code grade), and reworks failures by re-marking, deepening, or re-blanking before the parts move on. Repeat parts, fixtured presentation, standard equipment.

CNC/pantograph engraving of metal parts, mold cavities, dies, dial plates and instrument scales in a machine shop: the engraver checks engraved feature depth, width, position and character form with probe, gauge, comparator or eye against the drawing, and reworks by re-cutting with corrected offsets, a second deeper pass, or hand-stoning.

Etcher-circuit processor in a PCB / photochemical-etching plant: examines etched panels or precision etched parts against the artwork for shorts, opens, undercut, line-width and registration errors, and reworks defects (removing excess copper, repairing broken conductors, re-etching or touch-up) before the panel continues down the line.

Gravure/flexo cylinder and plate engraving in a prepress plant: engraver runs test cuts and measures engraved cells, pulls or prints a proof from the engraved cylinder/plate, compares tone, depth and register to the approved design, and reworks - re-engraving, correcting depth/parameters, hand-tooling or stripping and re-plating.

Hand/artisan engraving at the bench (jewelry, firearms, glassware, seals, hand-cut trophy inscriptions): examines the cut work under a loupe or stereo microscope for line quality, spacing, symmetry and design fidelity, then reworks with graver, burin or rotary handpiece to deepen, re-cut, or blend lines to match the surrounding artwork.

Custom etching shop, cylindrical sandcarved drinkware and bottles: after blasting, the worker peels the photoresist/vinyl mask off each piece by hand, lifting an edge with a fingernail or knife, then soaks and rinses the piece to clear leftover adhesive. Flat work - etched mirrors, architectural panels, glass awards and plaques: worker peels the large tape/vinyl mask sheet off the flat etched face on a bench or easel, scrapes stray bits of tape and adhesive with a knife, wipes and inspects the panel.

One-off ornate hollowware (vases, stemware, crystal bowls, lampshades) with hand-applied wax resist that comes off cleanly: worker immerses the fragile piece in hot water until the wax softens and floats free, rinses, dries and inspects. Piece geometry differs from job to job.

Detail finishing on deep-carved or ornate pieces: wax or tape remains lodged in fine engraved lines, undercuts and stems after the initial soak; the worker holds the fragile piece and picks the residue out selectively with a stylus or knife point under a light, touching up without scratching the etched surface, then inspects and passes it.

tasks.label: Insert cutting tools or bits into machines and secure them with wrenches.

instances.label: Small awards/trophy/retail engraving shop: operator swaps a diamond-drag stylus or carbide cutter in a benchtop rotary engraver's spindle/collet, tightens the collet nut or set screw with the supplied mini spanner/hex key, and sets cutter depth in the nosecone before a nameplate job. Tools kept loose in a bench drawer; shop floor shared with customers/staff.

Industrial marking / mold / nameplate shop: technician assembles an engraving cutter or end mill into an ER collet toolholder, torques the collet nut with two wrenches in a bench holder-fixture, then inserts the assembled holder into the CNC engraver/mill spindle or its tool magazine and confirms clamping.

Sign shop with large-format CNC engraving router: bit changes between operations (V-bit, profile cutter, drill) — loosen collet with spanner, insert new bit to correct stickout, retighten, re-zero. Several changes per job, dusty shop environment.

Mid-run change on a production engraving/marking machine because a cutter dulled or broke: machine paused, operator wrenches out the worn bit, installs an identical replacement, resets depth, resumes the run under throughput pressure.

Legacy/manual equipment: pantograph engraver or older rotary machine where the cutter is dropped into a cutter holder or spindle bore and locked with a set screw using a small hex wrench, then micro-adjusted for depth; holder designs vary machine to machine.

tasks.label: Fill etched characters with opaque paste to improve readability.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Industrial nameplate/tag/panel shop: batches of flat chemically etched or machine-engraved metal plates (legends, serial data, safety text) are filled with enamel or epoxy paste, excess is squeegeed/wiped off the surface, and the plates are cured/baked. Repetitive, dozens to hundreds per run, on a production bench or line.

Awards/trophy/personalization shop: one-off or small-batch engraved brass, aluminum or plastic plates and plaques are color-filled with a lacquer paint stick or bottled engraving paint, then the surface is wiped with solvent and a cloth. Sizes and layouts vary job to job; work done at a bench.

Small precision items at a jeweler's/engraver's bench: fine engraved script or logos on rings, pens, medals, dog tags, coins, cufflinks and firearm parts are filled with enamel or paint under magnification and the surrounding surface is cleaned without smearing or scratching the finish.

Sandblast- or acid-etched glass, crystal, acrylic and wood awards and signs in a shop: recessed/frosted characters are filled with opaque paint or enamel (often with the sandblast resist still in place), excess removed, and the piece cleaned for display quality.

Large or awkward in-shop pieces: cast or engraved bronze/aluminum plaques, control panels, dials and cylindrical or curved parts are paint-filled in the shop; the piece must be positioned or rotated, and paint must reach deep or vertical character faces without running.

On-site work at the customer's location: refreshing or filling lettering on installed monuments/headstones, building dedication plaques, or machinery nameplates already mounted in the field; weathered surfaces, outdoor conditions, no fixed layout.

tasks.label: Brush or wipe acid over engraving to darken or highlight inscriptions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Awards/trophy/promotional engraving shop bench: after rotary or laser engraving brass, aluminum or pewter plates, cups and gift items, the engraver brushes an acid/oxidizer darkening solution over the cut lettering, watches the reaction, rinses/neutralizes, then wipes and buffs the flat surface so only the engraved characters stay dark. Mixed shapes and sizes handled loose on the bench.

Industrial nameplate / photochemical-etch / metal-marking shop: production batches of etched or engraved stainless, aluminum and brass plates get an acid blackening or darkening chemical applied over the etched areas, then the surface is wiped or lapped clean of excess so the recessed characters read dark. Repeated identical parts, racks and fixed stations.

Jewelry / hand-engraving bench: engraved silver or gold ring, locket, flatware or knife bolster; artisan works acid/liver-of-sulfur into the fine engraved lines with a small brush on a curved 3D piece, judges the color by eye, rinses, then polishes the raised highlights back to bright metal.

Firearm, knife, tool or die/mold shop: acid etch or darkening solution wiped over a deep-engraved or stamped mark on a hardened steel part, sometimes masked and touched up on a large or assembled part that cannot be dipped; excess neutralized and wiped off.

Bronze memorial plaque / architectural sign shop: chemical patina or acid darkener brushed over the cast or engraved lettering and background of a large plaque, worked back with rag and brush to highlight raised letters, then rinsed and lacquered.

On-site refresh: darkening/patina solution brushed over the inscription of an already-installed bronze plaque, cornerstone or monument at a cemetery, building lobby or outdoor memorial; variable access, weather and surface condition, no fixturing possible.

tasks.label: Trim or remove excess material, using scrapers, knives, or band saws.

instances.label: Ceramic plant (sanitaryware, tableware, tile, pottery): after demolding slip-cast or pressed greenware, the worker fettles mold seams and flash, cleans up holes and rims, and scrapes/knifes off excess clay and glue before drying and glazing. Pieces are fragile, of many models, moved on ware boards and racks.

Precast concrete / cast stone plant or casting yard: after stripping forms, the worker chips, scrapes and grinds off fins, laitance and excess concrete on panels, steps, balconies, pipes and pavers, and saws off protruding excess. Heavy parts handled by crane/forklift; dusty, wet conditions.

Food plant molding/casting line (cheese, chocolate, confectionery, butter, molded novelties): the worker scrapes excess product from molds and trims overfill, tails and ragged edges from molded pieces with knives and scrapers, in a sanitary, chilled or tempered production room at line rate.

Small plaster/gypsum, cast-resin or composite shop (statuary, architectural moldings, ornament, dental/craft castings): the worker knife-trims flash along parting lines and scrapes excess plaster off freshly demolded pieces at a bench, with frequent model changes and short runs.

Stone or glass shop: the worker cuts away excess stock from a rough-shaped or cast blank with a band saw or diamond saw, trims excess material, and dresses edges of the shaped article on a fixed saw/grinder station.
Candle, wax and soap plant: the worker trims excess wax/flash from molded or extruded candles, cuts pieces to length, levels bases and trims wicks, at a bench or alongside a molding/extrusion line.

tasks.label: Clean, finish, and lubricate molds and mold parts.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Precast/concrete-products plant, stationary bed or own-mould production: after a wall panel, beam, stair, pipe or box culvert is stripped, the worker scrapes hardened concrete off the steel form bed, side rails, bulkheads and inserts, brushes and blows out debris, dresses damaged faces, then sprays or rolls form-release oil over the whole form. Forms differ job to job; work is done on the plant floor around cranes and other crews.

Automated pallet-circulation (carousel) precast plant: steel pallets/moulds and magnetic shutter profiles come round on the conveyor after deshuttering and must be scraped, brushed and sprayed with release agent before plotting and shuttering for the next cycle.

Glass container / pressed-glassware plant hot end: blank moulds, neck rings and blow moulds on an IS machine must be swabbed with graphite/oil lubricant every few minutes during running production, and moulds cleaned of carbon build-up and dressed at job changes, at 400-600 C next to operating sections.

Food-products plant: baking pans/tins, chocolate and confectionery moulds, cheese hoops and similar moulds are washed of baked-on residue, dried, inspected and greased/oiled with food-grade release before the next fill, on a high-speed line under hygiene rules.

Ceramic whiteware plant (sanitaryware, tableware, technical ceramics): plaster or porous resin moulds are blown out and sponged clean of slip residue, seams and parting lines scraped/trued, mould parts checked for wear, and parting/release compound applied before the mould is closed for the next cast.

Small custom shop or jobsite: candle, statuary, cultured-marble, GFRC or terrazzo moulds of latex, silicone, fibreglass or plaster cleaned by hand with solvents, brushes and picks, small chips/flash repaired, and wax or spray release applied; also cleaning and oiling site-cast or tilt-up forms outdoors on a construction site.

Small consumer molded-goods plant (candles, soap, wax figures, plaster/resin figurines, cast stone ornaments): moderate volume, many SKUs, molds loaded and stripped at benches or on a small line; worker inspects each piece for chips, bubbles, flash and shape.

tasks.label: Set the proper operating temperature for each casting.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Glass plant (container, tableware or specialty): for each job/article change the worker sets and trims furnace, forehearth/feeder zone and mold/plunger temperature setpoints on the control desk so gob and casting temperature suit the ware being pressed or blown; several job changes per week, hot indoor plant floor.

Ceramic/tile/sanitaryware or pottery production shop: for each load of cast ware the worker selects and enters the firing schedule (candle, ramp rates, peak temperature, soak, cool) on kiln controllers or the kiln SCADA, matching clay body and glaze; repeatable products, standard kilns.

Food-products molding (chocolate/confectionery, cheese, molded candy): worker sets melt, tempering and depositing temperatures on the tempering unit/depositor for each recipe or product changeover in a food plant, holding tight bands (e.g. 45°C melt, 27-31°C working).

Candle/wax casting plant: worker sets melt-tank and pouring temperatures for each wax blend, fragrance load and candle type (pillar, container, taper) on the melter's digital thermostat/PLC before each casting run.

Precast concrete, plaster or cast-stone plant: worker sets accelerated-curing chamber, heated-bed or steam curing temperature profile (preset, ramp rate, soak temperature, cool-down) for each casting batch or mold line.

Small artisan/craft studio (one- or two-person pottery, glass, candle or soap shop, often a converted garage or rented space): worker sets kiln or melter temperature for each individual piece or small batch, with mixed vintage equipment, one-off ware and schedules customized by feel and past results.

instances.label: Concrete products plant (block, paver, pipe, precast panel): freshly filled molds/production boards or casting pallets, still wet and heavy, are moved as palletized or crane-handled loads into a curing chamber rack, kiln, or yard storage position; fixed layout, standard racks, plant traffic rules.

Ceramics, pottery, tile or sanitaryware plant: filled plaster molds or freshly demolded greenware are set on drying racks, dryer cars, or kiln cars in set patterns; fragile ware that must not be marred; plant is dust- and climate-controlled with standard car/rack fixtures.

Food product molding (cheese molds, chocolate/confectionery shells, baked or frozen dessert trays): filled molds and trays are stacked on racks or wheeled carts and rolled into coolers, curing rooms, ovens, or cooling tunnels under sanitation rules and time pressure.

Candle, soap, wax, or cosmetics plant: worker places filled molds/trays of hot poured wax or soap onto cooling racks, carts, or into curing/cooling boxes; molds are light but the liquid content must remain level and undisturbed until set.

Artisan or custom job shop (art castings, plaster figurines, architectural ornament, small-batch specialty items): many one-off mold sizes and shapes poured on a general workbench, then carried to mismatched shelving, drying cabinets, or hand carts in a cluttered small workshop.

tasks.label: Align and assemble parts to produce completed products, using gauges and hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Precast/concrete products plant: worker assembles and aligns mold and form sections (side rails, shuttering profiles, bulkheads) on a casting bed or pallet, fits blockouts, embedded inserts, lifting anchors and reinforcement, clamps/magnetizes them, and checks dimensions against the shop drawing with tape and templates before the pour.

Ceramic tableware or sanitaryware plant: worker joins cast/jiggered components into a complete piece — sticking handles, spouts, feet, rims or the multiple parts of a WC bowl onto leather-hard greenware with slip — aligning against jigs/templates, sponging seams, on fragile parts with tight positional tolerance.

Molding and casting shop for consumer goods (candles, plaster/resin figurines, cast food items): worker fits wicks, clips, bases and hardware, and glues cast halves/components together on a production bench, repeated on large runs of identical items, checking with simple gauges and hand tools.

Glass plant or shop: worker assembles glass product components into a finished unit — mating pressed/molded parts, setting panes with a spacer frame and sealant into a completed insulating or laminated unit — with precise edge alignment checked by stops and gauges.

Stone shop (monuments, architectural cast stone): worker assembles multi-piece heavy products — sets a die on a base, bonds ornaments/panels with epoxy, shims and aligns using square, level and hoist — a few units per day, each dimensionally checked.

Custom/short-run studio or job shop (art castings, prototypes, one-off architectural pieces): worker aligns and fits non-repeating cast parts that seldom match exactly, trimming, shimming and reworking by judgment until the assembly is true.

tasks.label: Operate and adjust controls of heating equipment to melt material or to cure, dry, or bake filled molds.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Ceramics plant (tile, brick, sanitaryware, tableware): start up and run a tunnel/shuttle kiln or dryer for filled or formed ware - select the firing/drying curve, set zone temperatures, burner ratios, draft/pressure and cycle speed, watch for deviations (cracking, underfiring) over a multi-hour cycle and correct setpoints.

Precast/cast concrete or gypsum plant: operate steam-curing chambers, heated casting beds or tarped curing lines - set steam/temperature/humidity, follow a ramp-hold-cool cure, adjust for mix design, ambient temperature and strength gain before stripping molds.

Food manufacturing (molded chocolate/confectionery, processed cheese, molded bakery items): operate melting kettles, tempering units and the molding line's cooling or baking tunnel - set and adjust melt/temper temperatures and tunnel zone temperatures so product melts, deposits and sets correctly.

Candle, wax, soap or cosmetic products plant: operate jacketed wax melting tanks and holding kettles - set and hold melt/pour temperature for the wax blend, adjust for additives and pour viscosity, and control mold/container cooling.

Glass shop or plant (containers, art glass, optical, lab glass): operate a melting furnace or day tank to melt batch and run annealing lehr/kiln cycles - adjust burner or element power, temperature and cycle times for melt quality and stress-free annealing.

Small studio or custom shop (pottery/ceramic studio, statuary, plaster/investment or composite prototype shop): fire an electric or gas kiln or a drying/curing oven with a varying, non-standard load - set the program or valves, judge progress from cones, color or feel, and adjust manually.

tasks.label: Select sizes and types of molds according to instructions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Precast/concrete products plant (wall and slab lines, pipe, block, cast stone): reading the day's production schedule or element drawing, the worker selects the form/mold set of the specified size and product type — magnetic side forms and rails, steel jackets/cores, block-machine mold boxes — and gets it onto the casting pallet or machine; pieces range from tens of pounds to several tons and move with hoists, cranes or forklifts.

Ceramic whiteware, pottery, tile or sanitaryware plant: per the job ticket, the worker pulls plaster or resin molds of the specified model and size (typically 10-60 lb, fragile, many similar-looking molds on dense storage racks) and sets them on the slip-casting bench, jigger, or casting line.

Food-products plant (chocolate/confectionery, bakery, cheese): the worker chooses mold trays/pans of the specified cavity shape, size and count for the scheduled run from sanitized mold racks or the line's mold circuit and loads them onto the moulding line at changeover.

Small craft/decor shop (candles, soap, plaster figurines, small concrete ornaments): the worker picks mold sizes and types off mixed open shelving for each customer order — many small silicone, metal and plastic molds, often unlabeled and stored ad hoc in a cluttered shop — and carries them to the pouring bench.

Cultured marble / GFRC / large casting shop: per the work order the worker selects the large mold or pattern (tub, shower pan, countertop, architectural panel mold) from palletized rack storage or the yard, verifies size/type against the order, and brings it to the pour station with a forklift or pallet truck.

tasks.label: Patch broken edges or fractures, using clay or plaster.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Plaster/gypsum casting shop (statuary, figurines, architectural ornament, lamp bases): after demolding, worker inspects each casting, mixes a small batch of plaster, fills chipped edges, air pockets and seam breaks, rebuilds the missing contour by hand with spatula and fingers, then scrapes/sands so the repair disappears under paint.

Architectural precast/cast-stone plant: worker patches chipped arrises, bugholes and honeycombing on cast panels and trim with a color- and texture-matched patch mortar, feathers the edges and sponges/stipples the surface so the repair is invisible from a few feet; parts sit on casting beds, pallets or racks in varied orientations.

Utility precast plant (pipe, box culvert, vaults, barriers, septic tanks): worker fills shrinkage cracks, chipped tongue-and-groove edges and voids with grout or patch mortar and strikes it flush; acceptance is functional (crack filled, sound, dimensionally correct), appearance is secondary.

Pottery/ceramic ware production: worker mends cracks, chipped rims and broken-off attachments in fragile greenware or bisque using slip or plastic clay, works the patch in with sponge and tool to match wall thickness and surface, and blends it so no seam shows after firing.

Mold/model shop: worker repairs the working plaster molds and models themselves — patching broken mold edges, chipped keys and cracked case pieces with fresh plaster, then re-cutting and scraping the detail back to the original profile.

Field/off-premises repair: patching chips and fractures on cast items after shipping or installation (cast-stone cornice on a building, monument, fountain, custom cultured-marble top at a customer site) with plaster or patching compound, working around scaffolding, weather and finished surroundings.

sources.system: Vision-based adaptive crack repair system (UR10e + extruder end-effector), Univ. of Houston
sources.title: Vision-Based Adaptive Robotics for Autonomous Surface Crack Repair
sources.claim: A UR10e arm with an RGB-D camera, laser profiler and custom extruder/pump autonomously detects a surface crack, measures its cross-section and adaptively deposits a clay-type filler (Play-Doh/water) into 3D-printed crack specimens placed in its bench workspace; pre/post laser profiles verify fill.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: filling a measured crack with a soft clay-like paste on a workpiece presented in the robot's fixed workspace. It transfers to the functional end of 'patch fractures using clay or plaster' — same class of defect, same deposition-into-a-void action, millimetre-scale control — but it only deposits into simple machined grooves and does not trowel, feather or blend the patch.

sources.system: APCSbot
sources.developer: Chang'an University / Michigan Tech research group (Zhang, Yang et al.)
sources.title: Vision-guided robot for automated pixel-level pavement crack sealing
sources.claim: An autonomous mobile crack-sealing robot (APCSbot) performs pixel-level crack segmentation and sealant application on pavement, with reported sealing error of about 6 mm.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous detection and filling of cracks in a cementitious/asphalt surface. It shows the perception-plus-deposition loop works outside the lab, but the ~6 mm sealing error and bead-only finish are far coarser than the flush, blended patch a cast product requires.

sources.system: Tracer
sources.title: Fondo | Pave Robotics Launches: Robots That Repair Roads
sources.claim: A commercially launched autonomous road robot detects pavement cracks, cleans them and applies sealant without a crew.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous crack filling in the field. Transfer is limited — hot sealant on a flat road, no surface finishing or contour restoration — so it supports only functional crack filling, not appearance-grade patching of cast items.

sources.system: Okibo EG7 / EG7+
sources.title: Behind the Gloss: Construction's Dirty Work Is Going Robotic — Architect Magazine
sources.claim: A cordless mobile robot autonomously applies plaster, finishes drywall and paints interior walls on construction sites.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous application and smoothing of plaster/compound. It covers large planar wall areas to a uniform coat; it does not localize an individual fracture on a three-dimensional cast object, rebuild a missing edge profile, or blend a patch into surrounding detail, so it does not carry over to this task.

sources.system: Canvas 1200CX drywall finishing robot
sources.title: Drywall Finishing Robot That Perfectly Imitates Humans
sources.claim: A robotic drywall-finishing machine used on commercial jobsites applies and sands joint compound to Level 4/5 finishes, but is described as operating semi-autonomously with an operator setting it up.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine application and smoothing of a plaster-type compound to a fine finish. Even at its best it finishes flat wall planes under operator supervision; nothing indicates localized fracture repair on cast goods.

sources.system: Gaiotto/SACMI sanitaryware robotic cells (robot casting, glazing, automatic sorting)
sources.title: automatic sorting for sanitaryware | GAIOTTO AUTOMATION
sources.claim: State-of-the-art ceramic sanitaryware plants robotize casting handling, demolding, glazing and fired-piece inspection/classification in dedicated robotic cells; defect handling is inspection and sorting, not robotic patching of the ware.
sources.transferJustification: Same industry and workpieces (slip-cast ceramic ware in purpose-built robotic cells). The most automated ceramic plants robotize handling, glazing and defect inspection, but the repair of casting defects in green ware is not among the robotized steps offered, which bears on whether a cited system could patch greenware at all.

sources.system: Hierarchical text-to-3D robotic clay shaping (follow-on to SculptDiff)
sources.developer: Carnegie Mellon University (Bartsch, George et al.)
sources.title: Planning and Reasoning with 3D Deformable Objects for Hierarchical Text-to-3D Robotic Shaping
sources.claim: A research system autonomously sculpts clay into target 3D shapes with a robot arm, working coarse-to-fine on a clay body fixed in the workspace.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous manipulation of clay by a robot arm on a fixtured workpiece. It marks the frontier of robotic clay work — deforming a lump into coarse primitive shapes with parallel-jaw grasps — well short of adding clay to a fracture in a fragile cast piece and blending it to an invisible seam.

tasks.label: Withdraw cores or other loose mold members after castings solidify.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pallet-circulation precast concrete plant (walls, floors, double walls): after the concrete has hardened on the steel pallet, the worker releases and lifts off the magnetic side shutters, rails, chamfer strips and magnetic recess/block-out formers before the element is tilted and lifted, then sends the shutters for cleaning.

Dry-cast concrete products machine (pipe, manhole rings/cones, catch basins) in a pipe plant: each cycle the freshly formed product must be stripped from the inner core/mandrel and the jacket released, with the core withdrawn and the jacket lifted before the product goes to curing.

Wet-cast standard concrete products in reusable multi-part steel moulds (utility vaults, box culverts, barriers, septic tanks, steps): after cure the worker collapses/withdraws the inner core, unbolts and swings back side plates, pulls out blockout formers and inserts, with crane or hydraulic assist.

Ceramic slip-casting plant (sanitaryware/tableware): once the cast has firmed up, the multi-part plaster or resin mould is opened and the core pieces/spares are withdrawn from the fragile greenware without damaging it, and the piece is set on a board or belt.

Custom architectural precast / cast stone / GFRC shop: one-off or low-volume moulds; timber, foam and rubber loose pieces, tapered cores and undercut inserts are wedged, tapped and pried out of a fragile ornamental casting by hand, mould geometry differing piece to piece.

Small studio or craft shop (plaster statuary, figurines, ornamental plaster restoration, candles, art castings): multi-piece plaster/silicone moulds opened at a bench, loose cores and cope pieces lifted off delicate green castings by hand and set aside for re-use.

tasks.label: Repair mold defects, such as cracks or broken edges, using patterns, mold boxes, or hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Ceramic/pottery/sanitaryware plant mold shop: plaster working molds chip at parting edges, spall, or crack after casting cycles. Worker inspects the mold, cleans and undercuts the damage, mixes plaster, fills the void, then scrapes, files, and sands to restore the casting face, parting line, and key fit — sometimes recasting a section against the master pattern or in a mold box.

Sand/no-bake mold and core repair at a casting or refractory shop: after the pattern is drawn, edges break away, corners crumble, or a core cracks. Worker re-rams sand against the pattern, patches with core paste/slurry, mends and smooths the surface with trowel, slick, and lifter, blows loose sand out of the cavity, and re-seats the mold box before closing.

Precast concrete / cast-stone plant: fiberglass, wood, or steel forms damaged during stripping — gouges and dents filled with resin or putty and sanded flush, broken edges rebuilt or re-welded, warped rails straightened, joints and bolt-hole leaks sealed so the next pour releases a clean architectural face.

Small studio/craft shop (candles, figurines, statuary, tile, terrazzo): one-off silicone, latex, plaster, or fiberglass molds repaired at a cluttered bench with adhesive, filler, or a freshly cast section taken off a pattern; the worker judges per mold whether the defect is repairable or the mold must be remade.

Field/jobsite work: repairing damaged forms and molds on site for cast-in-place or on-site cast decorative concrete — patching torn form liners and plywood panels, rebuilding broken form edges, sealing seams — under variable weather, footing, and clutter.

sources.system: Vision-Based Adaptive Robotics for Autonomous Surface Crack Repair (UR10e crack-repair arm)
sources.title: Vision-Based Adaptive Robotics for Autonomous Surface Crack Repair
sources.claim: A UR10e-based system autonomously detects surface cracks with an RGB-D camera and laser scanner and deposits filler material with an extruder/pump, validated on 3D-printed crack specimens in a university lab — crack filling only, with no restoration of a molding surface contour or finishing pass.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: filling cracks in a hard surface. It is the closest robotic analog to patching a cracked mold, but it deposits sealant into cracks on flat concrete-like specimens in a lab and does not undercut/clean the defect, mix plaster, or scrape and sand the filled area back to a mold's casting contour and parting line, so performance does not carry over to mold repair.

sources.system: Canvas drywall finishing robot (1200CX)
sources.title: More Contractors See Benefits of Drywall Finishing Robot | Engineering News-Record
sources.claim: A commercial mobile robot autonomously spray-applies drywall joint compound and sands it on real construction projects, but workers still do taping and all complex geometries — i.e., the deployed capability is flat, large-area finishing, not defect-specific rebuilding of shaped tooling.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: applying a plaster-like compound and sanding it smooth. Objects and precision differ decisively — large flat wall planes versus small three-dimensional mold cavities whose repaired surface must match a pattern contour and release a cast part — and the vendor's own account excludes complex geometries, so it does not substantiate mold repair.

sources.system: Laser Material Deposition (LMD/EHLA) mold repair process

sources.claim: Laser material deposition is used to remanufacture cracked or spalled metal casting molds: damaged areas are welded up and then machined back to original geometry — a machine-tool/programmed process on metal dies, not applicable to plaster, sand, or fiberglass molds.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: restoring cracked mold geometry. Material and workflow differ fundamentally (metal deposition plus CNC machining with per-part programming versus hand patching of plaster/sand molds against patterns), and autonomy of defect assessment is not established.

Small artisan or custom shop (candle, figurine, art casting, architectural ornament studio): one-off or short-run plaster, silicone and fiberglass molds are hand-scraped and sanded — parting lines, flash, undercut detail — with judgment about which spots to touch so fine detail is not lost. instances.label: Precast/concrete-products plant (pipe, block, pavers, architectural precast): batch cement, sand/aggregate, water, pigments and admixtures to a written mix design, correct for aggregate moisture, charge the mixer, and check slump/consistency before the mix goes to the molds.

Ceramic tile/whiteware/sanitaryware or glass plant: weigh out body and glaze constituents (clays, feldspar, frits, silica, colorants, deflocculant, water) per recipe, blunge/ball-mill, and adjust to target specific gravity, viscosity and screen residue before casting or glazing.

Plaster/gypsum or investment mold shop (statuary, architectural ornament, ceramic mold making): measure water and plaster to the prescribed water:powder ratio in buckets or a mixing vessel, slake and mix for a timed interval, and pour before set.

Candle, wax or cast food-product operation (chocolate, confections): melt and hold wax/chocolate at a set temperature, dose colorant, fragrance or flavor by percentage of batch weight, and blend to a uniform pourable consistency.

Small custom/artisan studio or job-shop: mix varied small batches of two-part casting resin, urethane, or silicone mold rubber, weighing part A and part B to ratio, adding filler or pigment, hand-mixing and degassing within a short pot life.

Field/on-site work: mix cementitious grout, mortar, patching or castable refractory compound at the point of use, adding water to bagged/bulk dry mix and mixing to the prescribed consistency under changing outdoor conditions.

instances.label: Concrete products plant (block, paver, pipe, precast panel): worker spot-checks cured units against spec — height, wall thickness, length, diameter, squareness — with tape, caliper, square and go/no-go gauges, on the plant floor or in the curing yard; high volume, standard repeated shapes, dusty conditions.

Ceramic tile / brick / structural clay plant: worker measures greenware and fired pieces for size (caliber), thickness, squareness and warpage with calipers, gauges and templates to track shrinkage and set sorting classes; repeated standard formats, line-side.

Glass forming plant (containers, tableware, technical glass): worker checks diameter, height, wall thickness and finish dimensions of formed ware with calipers, ring/plug gauges and thickness gauges at the cold end or in a line-side QC bench.

Food product molding/forming plant (chocolate, confectionery, cheese, dough pieces): worker verifies molded piece length, width, thickness/profile with calipers or gauges against product spec at the line, several times per shift.

Cast stone / architectural precast / stone fabrication shop: worker verifies custom pieces made to shop drawings — overall dimensions, opening locations, bevel angles — with tape, protractor, bevel gauge and templates; pieces are large, heavy and vary from job to job but have drawings.

Small studio or artisan short-run production (pottery, plaster figurines, candles, hand-formed glass, custom carving): worker checks one-off or hand-formed pieces at the bench with calipers and templates against a master or sketch, with no CAD model and constantly changing geometry.

tasks.label: Bore holes or cut grates, risers, or pouring spouts in molds, using power tools.
