tasks.label: Observe operation of various machines to detect and correct machine malfunctions such as improper forming, glue flow, or pasteboard tension.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Corrugator wet end in a box plant: operator watches running board for warp, blister/delamination and poor bond, and corrects during the run by trimming steam, wrap arms, glue gap, bridge/web tension and line speed from the console.

Roll-fed converting machine (sheeter, bag/envelope machine, laminator, rewinder): operator watches web tension and tracking, catching loose/tight web, wander and wrinkling, and corrects with tension setpoints, brake/dancer settings and edge guides while the line runs.

Flexo folder-gluer / folding-carton gluer: glue flow drifts during the run (skipped or thin beads, glue volume off after a speed change); operator spots it in the delivery and corrects glue amount/pattern timing and pulls the bad product.

Flexo folder-gluer / folding-carton gluer: improper forming - out-of-square or fishtail cartons, crushed or mis-set scores, flaps not closing, feeder misfeeds; operator gauges samples and mechanically re-adjusts feeder skew, section gaps, folding rails, belts and plows by hand.

Jam, crash or web break on any converting machine: operator hears/sees the fault, stops the machine, opens guards, reaches in to pull crushed board or jammed cartons out of rollers and folding sections, re-threads or re-feeds the web/blanks, and restarts.

Mechanical/wear malfunction noticed by sight, sound, vibration or smell: worn belts or vacuum cups, dull slotter/creaser knives, glue build-up on applicator rolls and heads, misaligned plow or forming shoe, loose chain; operator cleans, adjusts, swaps the part or hands off to maintenance.

tasks.label: Start machines and move controls to regulate tension on pressure rolls, to synchronize speed of machine components, and to adjust temperatures of glue or paraffin.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Corrugator line in a corrugated box plant: operator starts wet end and dry end, sets/adjusts steam and starch-glue temperature and glue gap, brings roll-stand/splicer web tension to spec, and synchronizes wet-end/dry-end speeds and bridge level, adjusting continuously as board grades change during a shift.

Folder-gluer / carton-gluing line: operator loads the job, starts the machine, sets belt and transport-section speeds so folding, gluing and compression sections run in sync, adjusts squeeze/pressure-roll tension, and brings the hot-melt or cold-glue system to the correct temperature and pattern.

Slitter-rewinder, sheeter or paper bag machine: operator starts the line and regulates unwind brake and rewind tension on pressure rolls, matches draw/section speeds, and sets heat-seal or hot-melt temperature, correcting tension as roll diameter changes through the run.

Waxing/paraffin coating or laminating machine: operator brings the paraffin or adhesive bath up to running temperature, sets nip-roll pressure and line speed, then trims temperature and roll pressure as coat weight or bond quality drifts.

Older/small legacy converting machine (stitcher, tuber, envelope or small bag machine) in a small plant: manual handwheels, pneumatic pressure regulators and dial thermostats, with the operator starting the machine and adjusting tension, speed and glue-pot heat by feel while watching the product.

tasks.label: Disassemble machines to maintain, repair, or replace broken or worn parts, using hand or power tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine wear-part swap on the converting line: operator locks out a sheeter/slitter/scorer, removes guards, unbolts a worn bolted-on cutting knife, slitter blade or scoring wheel, fits the replacement, torques fasteners and sets blade clearance, then runs test sheets. Plant floor, standard machine, scheduled downtime.

In-situ replacement of drive and transport wear parts on a folder-gluer, bag machine or corrugator: worn belts, chains, timing pulleys, feed rollers, vacuum wheels or a failed bearing. Cramped access behind frames, fasteners fouled with glue/dust or corroded, pullers and tensioning gauges needed, reassembly with alignment and timing.

Disassembly of glue system and feeder components for maintenance: pulling glue heads, nozzles, hoses, suction cups, seals and O-rings; cleaning hardened adhesive off small parts; replacing worn seals and nozzles; reassembling and pressure-testing. Sticky residue, small fasteners and deformable parts.

Unplanned mid-shift breakdown: a jam or crash damages parts; operator diagnoses which component failed, tears down the affected section with hand and power tools, replaces bent or broken parts from the crib, reassembles and re-times the section under production time pressure.

Subassembly removed and taken to the maintenance bench/shop: knife shaft, gearbox, pump, air cylinder or clutch unit lifted out with hoist, torn down on the bench, worn bearings/seals/gears replaced (press-fits, heating, pullers), reassembled, shimmed and bench-tested before reinstallation.

tasks.label: Install attachments to machines for gluing, folding, printing, or cutting.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Corrugated box plant or folding-carton plant: for a new order, the operator mounts flexo printing plates/printing dies onto the print cylinders or sleeves of a flexo folder-gluer, printer-slotter or narrow/wide-web press, aligning register marks, taping and locking the plate in place, then loading the cylinder/sleeve into the print unit.

Die-cutting changeover: installing the cutting/creasing tooling — bolting a wooden rotary die onto the die drum of a rotary die cutter, or sliding and clamping a steel-rule chase plus stripping/blanking tools into a flatbed die-cutter — inside the converting plant, using hoists and hand tools.

Cutting attachments on slitters, sheeters, bag and envelope machines: mounting circular slitting knives and knife holders, scoring/creasing wheels, perforating blades, spacers and cutoff/trim knives on shafts and crossheads, then setting them to the order widths.

Gluing attachments: fitting glue wheels/discs, glue pots and trays, hot-melt extrusion heads, nozzles and hoses, or gum applicator arms onto folder-gluers, bag machines and envelope machines, plumbing/hooking them up and aligning them to the glue lap.

Folding/forming attachments: bolting on folding rails, hooks, plows, forming plates and shoulders, buckle plates, belts and guide attachments on folder-gluers, buckle folders and bag/envelope formers, sized and positioned for the current job.

tasks.label: Cut products to specified dimensions, using hand or power cutters.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Corrugated/paper converting plant floor: operator tends an in-line cutting unit (corrugator cut-off knife and slitter-scorer, sheeter, or web slitter), sets the ordered width/length, runs the order, pulls a first sheet, measures with tape/square, and trims knife positions until sheets meet spec.

Finishing/converting department: operator loads jogged stacks of printed sheets, labels, or carton blanks onto a programmable power guillotine, enters the cut program, cuts the pile down to specified panel dimensions, squares and checks against the job ticket, and stacks the finished cuts.

At machine-side with a hand cutter (utility knife, straightedge, hand shear): operator cuts flat stock to a specified size — liners, pads, spacers, filler sheets, QC coupons, or a short piece of web/board trimmed to marked dimensions — checking with a rule.

Short-run, custom, or sample work: cutting box blanks, display panels, or pads of paperboard/corrugated to customer-specified outside dimensions on a table/CNC knife cutter or by hand cutter, one or a few pieces per order, with frequent size changes.

Cutting cylindrical/heavy product to length with a power saw: tissue or towel logs cut into finished rolls, paper cores/tubes cut to ordered length, or roll/slab stock trimmed, with dimension set at the saw and lengths verified by gauge.

tasks.label: Place rolls of paper or cardboard on machine feed tracks, and thread paper through gluing, coating, and slitting rollers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Corrugator wet end in a corrugated box plant: liner/medium rolls of roughly 1,000–2,500 kg are brought from the roll store, set on the mill roll stand chucks, damaged outer wraps peeled off, the web end prepared and threaded into the splicer so the new roll splices into the running corrugator; several changes per shift across three to five stands.

Tissue/towel or napkin converting line: 3–5 tonne parent reels moved from the mill or warehouse and loaded onto the unwinder of a rewinder/embosser-laminator, the web joined to the running web and carried through embossing and glue rollers; a reel change every 20–60 minutes in a high-volume plant.

Web-fed coater, laminator, waxer or web converting press in a converted-paper plant: a 500–2,000 kg roll is set on a shaftless unwind or turret, splice tape applied, and the web fed through coating/gluing heads, dryers and slitting rollers; job changes several times per shift.

Small-format paper goods machines (bag, envelope, cup, stationery, tube winder, narrow-web slitter): rolls of 50–500 kg lifted by hoist or roll cart onto feed tracks or shafts, then paper hand-threaded from a dead stop through glue applicators, formers, perforators and slitting knives on a variety of legacy machines.

Recovery threading: after a web break, tear-out, jam or wrap-up, the operator clears the torn web, wipes glue-fouled rollers, re-feeds a ragged tail through the gluing/coating nips and slitters, and restarts the line under time pressure.

tasks.label: Monitor finished cartons as they drop from forming machines into rotating hoppers and into gravity feed chutes to prevent jamming.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Steady-state tending of a high-speed carton/cup forming machine in a converting plant: the operator stands at the delivery end watching formed cartons drop into a rotating hopper, checking that they nest and orient correctly, and occasionally reaching in to straighten a cocked carton or pull out a malformed one before it stops the flow.

Watching the gravity feed chute that carries formed cartons down to the packing/case-packing station: spotting cartons that bridge, tip, or back up at the chute exit, nudging or realigning them and modulating downstream take-away so the chute keeps flowing.

A jam actually forms despite monitoring: cartons crush and wedge in the hopper throat or chute; the operator e-stops the machine, opens a guard, extracts the crushed cartons and torn scrap by hand, checks fingers/guides for damage, then restarts and verifies flow.

One operator covering two to four forming machines at once: walking a route between machines, glancing at each hopper and chute, and intervening at whichever line starts to back up, while also doing counting, banding, or stock-feeding duties.

Degraded or changed conditions: warped/damp board, a worn hopper fence, or a new carton size just set up after changeover produces frequent misfeeds; the operator watches the drop closely, adjusts hopper guides/chute gates and machine speed, and culls bad cartons to keep the stream clean.

tasks.label: Adjust guide assemblies, forming bars, and folding mechanisms according to specifications, using hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Corrugated box plant, flexo folder gluer (or rotary die cutter/FFG line): between orders the operator sets folding guides/rails, gauging rollers, forming belts, side guides and squaring devices to the box spec for a standard RSC/HSC (often repeat) order, then checks first-off boxes for squareness and manufacturer's-joint gap. Open plant floor, standard machine, institution-controlled premises.

Same corrugated plant, non-standard or corrective setup: installing and repositioning folding hooks, hold-downs, special forming attachments, glue-unit brackets or a guide that has worn/drifted, using wrenches and gauges in tight machine spaces, with trial sheets and iterative tuning.

Paper mill/converting plant web line (corrugator dry end, sheeter, slitter-rewinder): repositioning slitting knives, scoring/creasing heads, edge and web guides to the new order's widths and score (forming) positions before/at order change.

Folding carton plant, straight-line gluer: setting the main transport carrier rails and side guides, blank-alignment section and delivery pressure for a straight-line tuck carton per the job spec, then running trial cartons.

Folding carton plant complex styles and tissue/napkin folding lines: hand positioning of folding hooks, helices, plough/forming bars, 4/6-corner tooling, tuckers and lapping fingers with hand tools, followed by trial folds and micro-adjustment.

Bag, envelope, or specialty forming machine size change: swapping and adjusting forming plates/collars, plows, folding rollers, tuckers and guides for a new bag/envelope size using hand tools and feeler gauges, then running and fine-tuning.

tasks.label: Measure, space, and set saw blades, cutters, and perforators, according to product specifications.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Corrugated box plant, corrugator dry end: for each order change the operator sets the slitting knives and scoring heads of the slitter-scorer to the ordered board widths and score/crease positions (often many changes per shift, some on the fly), then checks trim and score placement against the order spec.

Paper/board mill or roll-converting plant: winder or slitter-rewinder set change — measure and space the top and bottom slitter knives across the web to the trim and roll widths of the next set, set knife penetration/overlap, and verify slit widths on the finished rolls.

Box plant flexo folder-gluer or printer-slotter changeover: set slotting heads, trim/lap knives, creasing and perforating wheels laterally to the blank's panel dimensions per the job spec, run a first-off box and confirm panel and slot dimensions before running.

Tissue/roll-goods converting line: pull a dull or damaged blade (log saw circular blade, winder slitter blade) and install a sharp one, seat and torque it, reset the grinder/sharpening cycle and blade position so cuts meet spec.

Bench/machine tooling build in an envelope, forms, tag, bag or sheeter operation: slide cutter discs, perforating wheels and spacer rings onto an arbor/shaft in the sequence and widths given by the job ticket (measuring with rule/calipers), lock the stack and install the shaft in the machine.

In-machine perforator and cutter fine setting: mount or index perforating blades against the anvil, set blade-to-anvil clearance/penetration with feeler gauges and shims on older or specialty machines, run test sheets and adjust until perf tear strength and cut quality match the product spec.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Corrugator (single facer / double backer glue machine) in a corrugated sheet plant: keep the glue unit reservoirs supplied with starch adhesive from the starch kitchen, and set/verify the glue applicator roll gap and metering roll clearance for the flute size, board grade and running speed; adjust as speed and board change.

Flexo folder gluer / gluer-folder in a corrugated box plant: fill or maintain the hot-melt melter or cold-glue tank from pails, drums or a pellet bin; set the glue wheel or applicator head position and gap over the glue tab; run test sheets and re-adjust so the glue line lands on the tab.

Folding carton folder-gluer or specialty gluer in a paperboard carton plant: charge the glue pot / hot-melt tank with adhesive, position glue wheels or nozzle heads on the bar for the side seam and specialty patterns, and verify glue placement on sample cartons before the run.

Wax/paraffin line (wax cascader, curtain coater or wax applicator on corrugated or paper goods): keep the paraffin reservoir filled and at temperature from the bulk wax supply tank, and set the applicator/metering roll or weir for the coating weight.

Older or small converting machine in a job shop or small plant (bag machine, envelope machine, tube/core winder, partition assembler, small gluer): hand-pour cold glue from a pail into an open glue pan or pot as it runs down, loosen and slide glue rollers/wheels along the shaft by hand crank or wrench to the required lateral position, wipe spills and clear skinned glue.

tasks.label: Stamp products with information such as dates, using hand stamps or automatic stamping devices.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Tending an in-line coder on a converting/packaging line (corrugator, folding-carton, bag or envelope line): operator keys in the date/lot/order code, runs the automatic stamping device (roller coder, large-character inkjet head) as cartons or bundles pass on the conveyor, checks legibility on samples, refills ink and clears print faults during the run.

End-of-line marking station beside a plant conveyor: each finished case, bundle or shrink-wrapped pack that comes off the machine gets the manufacture/pack date, shift and lot code applied — by print-and-apply labeler that the operator loads and monitors, or by the operator hand-stamping each bundle as it arrives at the station.

Hand-stamping finished goods where they sit: worker walks to skids/pallets of boxes, bundles or cartons staged on the plant floor or in the shipping area, and stamps date, order number or customer code on wrappers and on cases at varied heights and orientations, sometimes on stretch-wrapped or irregularly stacked loads.

Marking large paper/board rolls or reels at the winder or roll-finishing area with grade, order, weight and date — stamping the roll end or wrapper, or applying a printed identification label to the wrapped roll before it goes to storage.
Bench/inspection-area stamping: applying date, inspector or approval stamps to first-piece and sample cartons, sheet stacks, tags or bundle tickets pulled for QC at a table or inspection stand.

tasks.label: Remove finished cores, and stack or place them on conveyors for transfer to other work areas.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: High-volume small/medium paper cores (tape, label, textile, tissue cores; a few ounces to ~15 kg) coming off a core cutter/recutter outfeed in a tube-and-core converting plant; the tender takes cut cores from the outfeed trough or table, stacks them in bins or on pallets, or lays them on the takeaway conveyor, keeping pace with 30-60 cuts/min while watching for out-of-length or crushed pieces.

Cores from a spiral tube winder with inline cut-off: the operator lifts finished tubes off the runout table and places them on a transfer conveyor or loads them onto a curing/drying cart or rack for movement to the drying room and finishing area; tubes are still soft/tacky and must not be dented.

Large, heavy industrial cores (150-300 mm ID, up to ~3 m long, tens of kilograms) from a mill-core line; removed from the machine, stacked in racks, bins or set carts, or laid on a conveyor for transfer to core prep/winder areas, often with hoist or two-person assist.

End-of-line unitizing: stacking finished cores in a defined pattern on pallets or into shipping bins, banding or wrapping the stack, and moving/placing it for transfer to the warehouse or the next work area.

Short mixed-size runs and quality sorting: cores of several diameters/lengths from the same job removed and segregated to different racks or pallets, with out-of-spec cores measured and set aside for rework or scrap.

Off-standard recovery: cores jammed or misfed at the cut-off, tubes that fell to the floor or spilled from a rack, damaged cores retrieved and re-handled around older equipment lacking a takeaway conveyor.

tasks.label: Lift tote boxes of finished cartons, and dump cartons into feed hoppers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Folding-carton/converting plant: at the packing end of a folder-gluer, die-cutter or patcher, the operator lifts plastic totes/tubs (roughly 20-50 lb) of finished folded cartons off a cart or pallet standing beside the machine and dumps them into the feed hopper of the next machine, topping the hopper up repeatedly while the line runs, on a plant floor with forklift and pallet-jack traffic.

Cartoning / case-erecting line: the operator keeps the carton magazine (feed hopper) of a cartoner or erector supplied, lifting totes and cases of blanks staged on a pallet at the machine, squaring and nesting the blanks as they go in, pulling out crushed or misfed blanks, and watching the low-level sensor so the machine never starves.

Short-run job with frequent changeovers: partially filled totes of several different carton sizes staged in different spots near the machine; operator judges how much to dump, re-squares the loose cartons in the hopper, and adjusts hopper rails between sizes.

Bulk container work: a large tote, tub or gaylord of finished cartons (several hundred pounds) is emptied into a large bulk feed hopper using a lift assist, hoist, box tipper or forklift-mounted rotator; low frequency, heavy, done at a fixed dumping point.

Reject/rework handling: totes of off-spec, crushed or reclaimed cartons are carried to a rework or scrap/baler feed hopper elsewhere on the floor and dumped; contents are mixed and irregular and the dump quality standard is loose.

tasks.label: Build semi-raw rubber treads onto buffed tire casings to prepare tires for vulcanization in recapping or retreading processes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: High-volume cold (precure) retreading of truck/bus casings in a franchised retread plant (Bandag/Michelin/Marangoni-type): worker mounts the buffed, inspected 22.5" casing on the builder's expandable rim hub, applies/extrudes cushion gum around the crown, centers and applies the precured tread strip or ring under correct tension, splices and stitches it, and sends the built tire to enveloping/curing.

Mold-cure (hot) retread building of truck/bus casings: semi-raw camelback strip or bead-to-bead extruded rubber is laid onto the buffed casing (crown, shoulders, sometimes sidewall), weight/profile controlled, tire made ready for the segmented mold press.

Small independent retread/recap shop with an older semi-automatic bench builder: mixed and sometimes marginal casings, irregular buff contours, skives and craters that must be gum-filled, hand rolling/stitching of the tread over repairs, manual splice, low volume and frequent size changes.

OTR/earthmover or large industrial tire retreading: heavy casing handled by hoist onto a large chuck or gantry machine, semi-raw rubber applied as a ribbon by strip-winder/extruder gun over crown and shoulders to a specified profile and weight, in an OTR retread plant bay.

Light-truck/passenger remold (mold-cure) production line: buffed casing spun while an Orbitread-type extruder winds raw rubber ribbon onto crown and shoulders, tread built up to gauge before the tire goes into a full mold.

tasks.label: Trim excess rubber and imperfections during retreading processes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Truck-tire retread plant, post-buff casing preparation: worker takes a buffed commercial truck casing on a skiving stand/spreader, finds the marked nail holes, cuts and rock-drilled areas, and uses a low-speed air grinder/skiving tool to remove loose and damaged rubber down to sound material, cleaning up the buffed surface before cement and tread application.

Precure (cold) truck retread, post-cure finishing: after the envelope is stripped, the worker trims the cushion-gum squeeze-out and flash along the tread edges and shoulders, cuts back the tread splice and any whiskers or loose rubber, and grinds off small surface imperfections before final inspection and paint.

Mold-cure retread (passenger/light-truck or truck): a cured retread comes out of the matrix/mold with vent spews and parting-line flash over the tread and shoulders; the worker trims the flash and vents flush with the finished surface.

Repair and building stations: worker trims excess rubber around section repairs and patches (cutting filler gum flush inside and out, trimming patch edges) and trims the excess cushion gum and tread-strip overlap at the splice on the green retread before curing.

OTR/mining (or aircraft) retread shop: worker skives large injuries out of a giant earthmover casing and trims excess or uneven rubber on the built-up tread, working on a large fixtured casing on a rotating stand.

tasks.label: Fill cuts and holes in tires, using hot rubber.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Truck/bus casing at a retread plant repair station: after buffing and nail-hole detection the worker skives out nail holes and small cuts in the crown and fills each skive flush with hot rubber from a heated extruder gun, readying the casing for cushion gum and precured tread.

Light- and medium-truck casings on a high-volume precure retread line: many small holes and shallow skives per casing, filled with hot extruded rubber on a short takt time between the buffing and gumming stations.

Section repair on a truck casing: a larger cut skived out into a crater reaching the belts; the worker builds the crater back up in layers with hot rubber from an extruder gun, flush with the buffed contour.

Injuries away from the crown - shoulder, sidewall and lower sidewall/bead-area cuts - skived into craters on the curved flank and filled with hot rubber while the worker reaches around and under the mounted casing at awkward angles.

OTR/earthmover (or aircraft) tire in the large-tire repair bay of a retread plant: deep, wide skived craters in a very large heavy casing filled with hot rubber or camelback build-up, often several kilograms of material per repair.

New-tire plant repair station: filling small cuts, voids and pick-outs in a green (uncured) tire, or a cured-tire blemish, with hot rubber/repair gum before curing or at final finish, the tire held on a stand or spreader.

tasks.label: Place tires into molds for new tread.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: High-volume new-tire plant, passenger/light-truck curing area: green tires arrive from building machines or the green-tire buffer on carts/pallets; the tire is set on the press's green-tire holder and loaded into the mold cavity, bead-centered, and the press closed; hundreds of cycles per shift with standard SKUs.

New-tire plant, truck/bus and specialty sizes or older presses: operator stages heavier green tires (30-60 kg) at the press, positions them for loading into the mold, handles frequent size/mold changeovers and checks bead seating and centering before cure.

Truck/bus tire retread plant, hot (mold) cure: a built casing (~60-90 kg) with cushion gum and uncured tread rubber is mounted on a rim/curing tube and positioned in a segmented matrix mold press with a loading arm or hoist, centered, and the mold closed for vulcanization.

Precure (cold-process) retread plant: enveloped casing on a rim is moved by monorail/J-hook or trolley rack and loaded into the curing chamber (batch of roughly 4-20 tires), spaced and hooked up for inflation before the chamber door is closed.

OTR/earthmover, aircraft or other outsize tire work: very heavy casings (200 kg to several tonnes) hoisted with overhead crane or manipulator into large molds/matrices, low volume, mixed and often one-off sizes, casings with irregular repairs.

tasks.label: Buff tires according to specifications for width and undertread depth.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Modern truck/bus retread plant: standard 22.5-inch steer or drive casing is rolled to the buffer, mounted on the expandable rim hub and inflated; the buff radius, buff width and undertread target are recalled from the plant's spec database (often via RFID); the CNC buffer strips the remaining tread and the operator gauges undertread depth (2/32-5/32 in.) and texture before releasing the casing.

Truck casing with irregular or uneven wear, shoulder step wear, out-of-round condition or an unfamiliar brand/design radius: the operator picks or adjusts buff radius and width, may run multiple radii or extra passes, watches for belt/cable exposure, and re-gauges until undertread depth is uniform across the crown and belt edges.

Bead-to-bead / sidewall and shoulder work: after the crown buff, the shoulders are trimmed to the specified buff width and the sidewalls are buffed and brushed clean for mould-cure or bead-to-bead precure retreads.

Freehand touch-up with a hand-held rasp or burr at a stand: cleaning up localized under-buff, buffing and texturing around skived injuries, removing loose rubber and exposed cable ends, and re-texturing spots the machine missed.
Passenger/light-truck or aircraft casings on a dedicated smaller CNC buffer: high throughput, tight profile and undertread tolerance, frequent size/spec changeovers.

OTR / earthmover casings (25 in. to 63 in.) on a large buffer-peeler: heavy casing handling and mounting, deep rubber removal to a specified profile and undertread, with inspection stops during the cycle.

tasks.label: Brush or spray solvents onto plies to ensure adhesion, and repeat process as specified, alternating direction of each ply to strengthen tires.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: High-volume US passenger/light-truck radial plant: green tire built on a modern two-stage tire building machine. Servicers present innerliner, body ply and belt stock to a rotating drum; tack/adhesion between layers is ensured by cement or solvent applied to component surfaces and splices, and belts/plies are laid in the specified alternating orientation. ~1-minute cycles, operator monitors and intervenes on faults.

Truck/bus radial (TBR) building on a semi-automatic uni-stage or two-stage machine: heavier steel-cord plies and wider stock, operator brushes or sprays cement/solvent on ply splices, turn-up areas and repaired spots between successive ply applications, then stitches. Slower cycles, more hands-on correction than PCR.

Specialty plant building large off-road, agricultural or industrial radial tires: oversized plies and belt packages on a drum-based building station, substantial manual cement/solvent application to ply surfaces and splices, hand stitching, low volume, many size changes.

Bias-ply and low-volume specialty work (aircraft, racing, industrial, prototype/development builds) largely hand-built in a build room inside the plant: worker brushes solvent onto each fabric ply, lays many plies at alternating bias angles on a drum, stitches, repeats per spec sheet that changes build to build.

Retread/repair plant: worker sprays or brushes bonding cement/solvent onto the buffed casing crown, skived injuries and repair patches/plies before applying cushion gum and tread. Casings arrive from customers in varying sizes and conditions on a shop floor with fixed stations.

Giant OTR / specialty tires (mining, agricultural, industrial, aircraft) on uni-stage or bias machines: operator engages winding/stitching rollers over thick, heavy plies and tread on a slowly revolving large drum, often with multiple passes and roll-pressure changes for each component and size changeover.

Start-up, size changeover and defect handling: after a splice defect, blister or lifted ply edge is spotted, the builder re-runs or hand-guides a stitcher roller over the affected area, adjusts roller pressure/traverse limits, and re-verifies the bond before releasing the green tire.

tasks.label: Inspect worn tires for faults, cracks, cuts, and nail holes, and to determine if tires are suitable for retreading.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Initial (pre-buff) casing inspection at a commercial truck-tire retread plant: worker mounts each returned casing on a spreader/NDT station, inspects the inner liner and outer sidewalls under light, probes and locates nail holes, cuts and cracks, judges bead and shoulder damage against repair limits, marks injuries in crayon and accepts or scraps the casing.

Non-destructive test station: casing is loaded into a shearography (or high-voltage) machine, tested for belt/ply separations, blisters and penetrations, and the results are read to decide reject vs. repairable, with defect locations recorded for downstream skiving.

Post-buff inspection: after the tread is buffed off, the casing on the buffer hub is examined for exposed or broken steel cables, injuries opened up by buffing, and residual separations; the worker marks injuries for skiving/repair or scraps the casing.

Intake grading/sorting of incoming used tires at the plant receiving area or casing yard: stacks or trailer-loads of worn tires are handled one by one for a quick suitability call (tread/undertread, age, brand, obvious sidewall or bead damage) to route them to the retread line, to a casing dealer, or to scrap.

Field inspection at a customer fleet yard, truck shop bay or scrap pile: worn tires on or just off the vehicle are inspected in place, in varying light and weather, to advise which casings are worth pulling for retread and which are scrap.

Large specialty casings (OTR/earthmover, industrial or aircraft tires) inspected in the plant: heavy, oversized carcasses handled with lifts, inspected visually and with probes/ultrasonic checks for cuts, cracks, penetrations and separations before retread acceptance.

tasks.label: Measure tires to determine mold size requirements.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: At the tire building machine in a tire plant: after a green (uncured) tire is built, the builder measures its outside diameter/circumference and width with a pi-tape, tape measure or gauge and compares the numbers to the build spec for the size being run, confirming the tire matches the mold/curing-press size before it moves to curing.

Size changeover / first-article check: when switching the machine to a new tire size, the builder measures the first green tires (component and tread widths, bead-to-bead dimension, circumference, splice) against the spec sheet for the mold to be used, to confirm the built tire conforms to the mold size requirement.

Periodic audit sample: once per shift or lot, the builder carries a green tire to a measuring stand/gauge fixture in the build area, measures diameter, width and weight, records the readings, and flags out-of-spec tires so they are not routed to a mold they do not fit.

Cured tire verification at or after the press: the operator measures a finished tire's outside diameter and section width against the mold specification to verify the correct mold size was used and the dimensions are within tolerance.
Retread plant: the builder measures a buffed truck-tire casing (outside diameter, buffed tread width, bead-to-bead dimension) to determine the correct mold/matrix or tread size for the retread build.

tasks.label: Cut plies at splice points, and press ends together to form continuous bands.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Passenger/light-truck radial first stage in a modern US tire plant: innerliner and body ply are wrapped on the building drum, cut at the splice point and the ends pressed/stitched together into a continuous band; 30-60 s cycles, splice overlap held to a few millimetres, splice positions balanced around the drum.

Truck/bus radial (TBR) building: heavy steel-cord body ply and steel belts drawn from servicers, cut to length and the ends butted or overlapped on the carcass/belt drum and stitched down; stock is wide, heavy and tacky, tolerances tight.

Ply/breaker preparation area: calendered cord fabric is cut at the specified angle and the successive cut lengths are joined end-to-end (overlap or butt splice) into a continuous ply band wound on a liner/reel for the building machines.

Retread plant: precure tread strip or camelback is cut to the length matching the buffed casing circumference and the two ends are spliced/pressed together to form a continuous band around the casing, then stitched down.

OTR, agricultural, industrial or other specialty/low-volume tires: wide, heavy plies and breakers, frequent size changes; the ply is cut at the splice point and the ends pressed together on a large drum or into a band before application.

Splice rework/repair: an open, overlapped or crooked splice spotted by the builder or by inspection is opened up, trimmed with a hand knife and re-pressed/stitched by hand on the drum or green tire before it moves on.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: High-volume US passenger/light-truck plant, first-stage carcass building: operator at a semi-automated tire building machine loads material cassettes, indexes the drum, has innerliner and body plies wound on from servicers, splices ply ends butt-to-butt, sets beads and stitches; station is guarded by light curtains and fed by servicers, cycle ~40-60 s.

Medium/heavy truck and bus radial plant: carcass building of heavier steel-cord body ply, innerliner and sidewall stock wound onto a large carcass drum, ply ends spliced and stitched, beads set; larger, heavier stock and slower cycles than passenger tires, in a fixed machine station on the building floor.

Second-stage / combined-stage passenger tire building in the same plant: belts, cap strip and tread wound over the shaped carcass on the belt-and-tread drum, components centered to laser lines, packages transferred and consolidated into a finished green tire, which is removed to a conveyor.

Low-volume specialty and bias-ply work (aircraft bias tires, industrial/solid, racing, small-batch farm tires) at a specialty plant: older semi-automatic or largely manual building machines, many plies pulled from racks and laid by hand on a rotating drum, frequent size changes, hand stitching and turn-up with rods.

Giant OTR/earthmover radial (49"-63") building: crew works on platforms around a huge drum, heavy ply and belt components positioned with hoists and manual guidance, long build cycles, very low volume, no two builds identical.

Retread/tread-building work in a commercial retread plant: buffed truck casing mounted on the builder hub, cushion gum and precured tread or camelback wound around the rotating casing, aligned and stitched down to remove air, then handed off for curing.

tasks.label: Clean and paint completed tires.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: High-volume passenger/light-truck line in a tire plant: the builder takes the completed green tire off the building machine, blows/wipes off dust and stray debris, and applies inside bladder lubricant and outside mold-release paint before the tire goes to curing. Standard size range, continuous flow, indoor plant floor.

Truck/bus radial (TBR) green tires in a plant: heavier carcasses (30-80 kg) moved by hoist or conveyor; the completed green tire is cleaned of loose debris and sprayed inside and outside with release paint before curing. Fewer sizes per line, larger and heavier workpieces.

Large/specialty green tires (OTR, agricultural, industrial, aircraft): low volume, wide size mix, very heavy and bulky; the completed tire is cleaned and coated with release paint, often by hand spraying or brushing in a booth or at a dedicated station in the plant.

Retread or small specialty tire shop: the completed built/retreaded tire is cleaned of buffing dust, cement smears and debris, then painted with black sidewall paint or protective coating and given identification markings before shipment. Mixed casings and sizes, small batches, general shop floor.

Off-line cleaning and touch-up of completed tires: wiping cement/solvent smears, picking off foreign material and excess talc, spot re-spraying areas missed or scuffed in handling, applying stencils/paint marks. Requires judging by eye which spots need work; done by hand at or near the building station.

tasks.label: Rub cement sticks on drum edges to provide adhesive surfaces for plies.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: High-volume passenger/light-truck plant, semi-automatic first-stage building machine: the builder wipes a cement stick along both edges of the building drum (standard drum size for the run) before laying the innerliner/body ply, every tire or at set intervals, at a fixed operator station on a plant floor shared with other operators and material handlers; ~30-60 s cycle.

Truck/bus or two-stage radial building in a plant: cement stick rubbed along the edges/shoulders of a larger carcass drum and again on the second-stage band drum before plies and breakers are wound; several size changeovers per shift, drum still fixed on its spindle at a standard station.

OTR / agricultural / industrial large-tire department: very large building drum, builder works from a platform, low volume and many sizes; cement applied by hand in specified bands on the drum edges per the build ticket before heavy plies are laid.

Prototype, racing, or aircraft tire build room / short-run specialty department: bespoke or frequently reconfigured drums, cement placement specified per build by an engineer, one-off constructions with hand operations interleaved between cement application and ply laying.

In-cycle touch-up and recovery: builder sees a ply edge lifting, a wrinkle, or a drum area that has lost tack (dust, old cement, humidity), stops the drum, judges where extra tack is needed, rubs cement on that specific spot of drum or ply edge, and re-seats the ply before continuing.

tasks.label: Depress pedals to collapse drums after processing is complete.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: High-volume passenger/light-truck radial plant: after the green tire build cycle finishes on a single- or two-stage tire building machine, the builder depresses the foot pedal to collapse the carcass drum / release the transfer-ring assembly so the finished green tire lets go of the drum, then strips it off to the inspection table. Repeats every 40-90 seconds, drum surfaces tacky with uncured rubber.

Truck & bus (all-steel radial) building station: after the belt & tread package is consolidated onto the shaped carcass, the builder pedals the shaping drum/transfer ring to collapse so the heavy (40-100 lb) green tire releases; tire is then lifted off with a removal arm or hoist. Longer cycles, larger drums.

Sub-assembly drum station (belt & tread drum, ply band / band-building drum, bead-apex drum): after the band or belt-tread package is spliced and stitched, the operator pedals the drum to collapse it, strips the band off, and puts it on the transfer ring, cart, or conveyor for the next stage.

Agricultural radial, industrial, and small/medium OTR tire building on lower-volume machines with frequent size changeovers: after building, pedal collapses the large-diameter drum to break the green tire free; operator assists removal with a lift or roll-off table.

Giant OTR / mining (49-63 inch) and aircraft or other very low-volume specialty tires built in a crane-served bay over long cycles with multiple operators: pedal/foot-switch collapses the massive building drum after hours of layup so the multi-thousand-pound green tire can be craned off.

Retread / rebuild plant building station: casing or band mounted on an expandable chuck or building drum; after cushion gum and tread ring are applied and rolled, the operator pedals to collapse/deflate the drum-chuck and release the built tire for curing. Casings vary in size and condition.

tasks.label: Wind chafers and breakers onto plies.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: High-volume passenger/light-truck plant: builder runs one or more modern uni-stage tire building machines. Chafer strips and steel breakers/belts are fed from servo let-off servicers onto the ply-covered drum; worker loads material rolls and beads, watches splice quality and centering, clears faults, releases the green tire.

Older semi-automatic two-stage passenger/light-truck machines: worker pulls chafer strips and breaker plies from servicers, hand-guides and aligns them onto the rotating ply band on the drum, butts/skives the splice and stitches it down, repeating each cycle at line takt.

Truck/bus radial building: heavy steel-cord breakers and chafer/chipper strips applied to carcass and belt drums on a two-drum or uni-stage truck machine; worker loads heavy let-off reels, checks belt tip position and splice width, corrects centering.

Agricultural, industrial and small-to-medium OTR radial tires: larger, heavier chafer and breaker components applied on semi-automated building machines with frequent size changeovers, more manual guiding, hoist-assisted material handling and hand stitching.

Specialty bias-ply work (aircraft, motorcycle, industrial, large bias OTR) at a semi-manual building station in a plant bay: worker takes precut chafer and breaker strips from carts/racks, winds them by hand onto the ply stack on the drum to marked reference lines, stitches with hand rollers.

Prototype, R&D and very short-run builds: engineer-specified novel constructions, non-standard chafer/breaker gauges, widths or angles, one-off dimensions, built with frequent manual adjustment and measurement in a pilot/development building area.

tasks.label: Pull plies from supply racks, and align plies with edges of drums.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: High-volume passenger/light-truck radial plant: builder works a first-stage/uni-stage tire building machine, drawing rubberized body ply stock from servicer let-off racks beside the drum, laying the leading edge square and centering it on the drum edges, splicing and stitching; 30-60 s cycles, standard sizes, thousands of green tires per shift.

Truck/bus radial (TBR) building: heavier steel- and textile-cord body plies and larger, wider drums; ply pulled from let-off racks/servicer pans and aligned to drum edges within a few millimeters, then stitched; institutional plant floor, frequent size changes across a few dozen SKUs.

Older semi-automatic or second-stage machines and short runs in legacy US plants: pre-cut plies stored in trays/racks or ply books, builder hand-pulls each ply, hangs and eyeballs/laser-aligns it against the drum edge, smooths wrinkles and splices by hand before machine stitching.

Mid-size off-road and agricultural radial tire building (roughly 20-30 in. rim): multi-component carcass, heavy plies pulled from servicer racks and aligned on a large building drum; lower volumes, longer cycles, more setup changes, inside an OTR/ag tire plant.

Giant mining OTR (49-63 in.), aircraft bias, racing and prototype/R&D tires: many plies per carcass, very heavy or awkward stock hand-pulled from racks, hand-aligned on the drum with laser/edge guides, extensive manual smoothing and splicing; low volume, frequent one-off constructions.

Mold-cure retread / repair building in a retread plant: builder pulls cushion gum and repair ply stock from racks and aligns it on the buffed casing mounted on a builder drum/chuck, centering to the casing shoulders before tread application.

tasks.label: Lift raw materials, finished products, and packed items, manually or using hoists.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: End-of-line handling of finished packed goods in a plant: taking 15-50 lb cases, cartons or bagged product off the packaging line conveyor or hand-pack table and stacking them in layers on pallets or carts for wrapping and staging; repetitive high-cycle work on a plant floor with other workers nearby.

Charging machines with bulk raw material: hoisting or manually lifting 50 lb sacks, boxes, pails or drums of ingredients, resin or chemicals off pallets, cutting and dumping them into hoppers, mixers or blenders and returning empties; dusty, variable pallet stacks, often on mezzanines or beside process equipment.

Loading discrete stock and parts into production machines and removing finished pieces: lifting blanks, castings, moldings, sheet stock or subassemblies from bins, racks or carts into presses, molding machines and welding fixtures, then placing finished pieces into racks, totes or dunnage on the plant floor.

Receiving and shipping dock work at the plant: unloading floor-stacked cartons and palletized raw material from trailers and containers, loading finished packed goods into trailers, and moving pallets between dock, staging and storage racks with pallet jacks or lift equipment.

Lineside material supply: bringing totes, bins, carts and pallets of components, packaging and supplies from stores to workstations, lifting them onto benches, racks and conveyors for production workers, and removing full containers of finished parts; done in aisles shared with people and traffic.

Heavy and awkward lifts with hoists, jib and overhead cranes: rigging and moving dies, molds, coils, castings, motors, large weldments or drums with slings, chains or dedicated lifters and guiding the load into a press, machine or storage stand; also ad hoc lifts of odd, unpackaged or fragile items in cluttered areas.

tasks.label: Mark or tag identification on parts.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: End-of-line identification labeling: a helper at a bench or line-side station in a manufacturing plant peels printed barcode/part-number labels (or prints them from a thermal printer) and applies them to finished parts, cartons, trays or totes as they come off the line, matching the right label to the right item per the work order.

Direct part marking of serial, lot or heat numbers on machined/fabricated metal parts using a dot-peen or laser marking station, electro-etch pencil, or hand steel stamps and hammer; parts arrive in totes or on trays in mixed batches at a marking bench in a machine shop, foundry or medical-device plant.

tasks.label: Observe equipment operations so that malfunctions can be detected, and notify operators of any malfunctions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Helper stationed at a packaging/filling/labeling line watches the machine run — looking for jams, misfeeds, crooked labels, product backups — and verbally alerts the line operator when something goes wrong.

Helper on a food or beverage processing line monitors conveyors, mixers, ovens and fillers while supplying materials, listening for unusual noise and watching for leaks or spills, and tells the operator when a malfunction appears.

Helper assisting at a printing press, textile machine or paper converting line watches for web/thread breaks, ink or tension problems and misfeeds, and signals the press or machine operator immediately.

Helper feeding a plastics extruder, molding machine or chemical mixing unit periodically checks gauges, indicator lights and alarm panels and reports off-spec pressures, temperatures or fault codes to the operator.

Helper in a woodworking or metal fabrication shop holds/positions stock at a saw, press or CNC machine and notices unusual vibration, smoke, overheating or dulling tools, notifying the machine operator.

tasks.label: Count finished products to determine if product orders are complete.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Finished-goods/shipping area of a plant: helper counts uniform labeled cases and cartons stacked on finished-goods pallets in racks or on the dock, reconciling the physical count against the order/pack list and flagging shortages.

End of a production or packaging line: helper counts individual finished units (bottles, molded parts, printed pieces, food packs) as they are packed into cartons/trays in set quantities and tallies running totals against the work order to see if the ordered quantity has been produced.

Loose small parts in totes, gaylords or bins (fasteners, clips, small moldings, stampings) counted by hand, by handful, or with a counting scale to verify batch/order quantity before the tote is released to shipping.

Large or irregular finished goods (bundles, fabricated metal parts, rolls, panels, furniture components) stacked loose on the floor or in racks with no uniform arrangement; helper walks around and moves/restacks pieces to count them against the order.

Staging area: helper walks a mixed customer order (several SKUs, pallets plus loose cases/carts) with a pick or order sheet, counting each item type and checking off whether the order is complete before it is loaded.

tasks.label: Examine products to verify conformance to quality standards.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Inline inspection of rigid discrete items moving on a packaging/processing line (bottles, cans, filled pouches, molded parts): helper watches product pass at line speed, spots cracks, short shots, fill-level, seal or label faults and foreign material, and pulls rejects off the belt into a scrap tote.

Inline/table inspection of natural, variable products in a food plant (produce, poultry or meat pieces, baked goods) flowing on a belt: grade by size, color and defect, remove off-spec, damaged or foreign pieces by hand while keeping up with the flow.

Bench inspection at a workstation on the plant floor: helper takes parts from totes, racks or a machine outfeed, examines all faces for burrs, flash, scratches, missing features, checks a dimension with a go/no-go gauge or caliper, sorts into good/rework/scrap bins and tallies counts on a sheet.

End-of-line package and labeling checks: verify correct label applied and date/lot code legible, seal/closure integrity, correct count and no carton damage on units and cases; divert or set aside non-conforming packages before palletizing.

Inspection of large or awkward assemblies on a shop floor (welded frames, painted panels, furniture, appliance subassemblies): walk around the item, look over multiple faces for finish defects, check fit and hardware presence, tag defects for rework.

Hand inspection of soft, limp or texture-judged goods at a table (sewn garments, upholstery and foam, dough/bread, fresh-cut items): pick up and turn the item, feel it, judge seam quality, hand-feel and texture against the standard, set aside seconds.

tasks.label: Operate machinery used in the production process, or assist machine operators.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Loading/unloading parts at a production machine on a plant floor: helper takes metal or plastic parts from racks, bins or carts and places them into a press, welder, molding machine or fixture, and removes finished pieces, repeating a single part family all shift alongside operators.

Tending a CNC lathe/mill or similar machine in a job shop: open the door, chuck or clamp a blank, press cycle start, unload, blow off chips, deburr, gauge the part, and swap part numbers between short runs; coolant, chips and mixed part sizes.

Feeding and off-loading a production/packaging line: placing product onto a conveyor infeed, loading cartons/film/labels into a packaging machine, taking finished cases off the line and hand-stacking them onto pallets at line rate.

Supplying an operator and the machines: fetching raw stock, totes, boxes and tooling from stores, moving carts/bins of work-in-process between machines and staging areas, swapping full bins for empties, returning empties.

Running a simple production machine start-to-finish for a shift: start/stop, feed material, watch for misfeeds, clear jams and hang-ups, make minor adjustments, do basic visual/dimensional checks and set the machine up for the next run.

Food, meat or bakery plant line work: feeding raw product into a machine, hanging/placing product on a moving line, taking product off and packing it, in a wet, cold, sanitized environment with variable natural product.

instances.label: Machine tending on the production floor: the helper loads blanks, billets, resin inserts or sub-assemblies into a press, injection molder, CNC, saw or packaging machine and pulls the finished part out each cycle. Parts come from bins, carts, racks or pallets standing beside the machine; sizes and part numbers change at every changeover; hot or sharp parts are common.

Conveyor work with cases, cartons and totes in the packaging/shipping area: taking sealed cases or totes off a moving line and stacking them on carts or pallets, and feeding boxes, totes and trays back onto conveyors and takeaway lines, keeping up with line speed.

Conveyor work with loose product at line speed: picking food pieces, small molded parts, printed sheets or garments off a moving belt and placing them into trays, cartons or fixtures (or feeding them onto the belt), at a pace set by the line and with hygiene/handling constraints.

End-of-line palletizing and depalletizing: stacking cases, bags or bundles onto pallets in a set pattern as they come off the line, and breaking down incoming pallets of raw material or empty containers to feed machines and conveyors.

Loading and unloading conveyances at the plant dock: hand-stacking or unstacking floor-loaded cartons, bags and bundles in trailers, containers or railcars, or moving palletized loads in and out with a pallet jack; freight is stacked irregularly and the trailer is hot, dim and uneven.

Charging process equipment with bulk material: dumping 25-50 lb ingredient or resin sacks into hoppers and mixers, tipping totes and drums, and loading racks, trays or baskets into ovens, dryers, washers or plating tanks, then unloading them when the cycle ends.

tasks.label: Remove products, machine attachments, or waste material from machines.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Metalworking/plastics shop floor: helper stands at a CNC lathe/mill, stamping press or injection molding machine and takes the finished part out at end of cycle, setting it on a rack, cart, tote or conveyor; same part family repeated for hours, hot/oily parts, machine holds the part in a known position (chuck, mold, die).

Food/consumer-goods processing or packaging line: helper removes product from the machine — pulling baked goods off pans and out of ovens, taking molded/formed items off the line end, transferring product into trays, lugs or cartons — at line rate in a plant or in-store bakery, alongside other workers.

Helper pulls waste material away from machines: scrap, trim, skeletons, runners/sprues, offcuts and reject pieces coming off the machine, tossing them into gaylords, hoppers or scrap bins beside the equipment and swapping full bins.

Between runs, helper cleans waste out of the machine itself: blowing/vacuuming chips and dust from the work zone, scraping buildup, emptying internal catch pans and trays inside varied machine enclosures.

Setup support: helper removes machine attachments — molds, dies, tooling, blades, fixtures, guards, end-of-arm tooling — unclamping/unbolting, lifting them out (often with a hoist or cart) and staging them for the next job.

Mid-run problem: helper clears a jam or hung-up material — a stuck workpiece in the die, product bridged in a chute, tangled film/paper, a part wedged in the guarding — reaching into a stopped machine and freeing it by hand or with tools.

tasks.label: Separate products according to weight, grade, size, or composition of materials used to produce them.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Food plant / packhouse: helper stands at a moving belt, roller table or grading station in a produce packing house, poultry, or seafood plant, culling off-grade, undersized or defective product and diverting product by size/weight into different bins, totes or lines; wet, cold, high line speed, product arriving in bulk and random orientation.

Recycling / scrap facility: helper on a picking line in a MRF, scrap yard or C&D facility separating a chaotic mixed stream by composition (PET vs HDPE vs film, ferrous vs non-ferrous, fiber, wood) into chutes and bunkers; dusty, noisy, heterogeneous and contaminated objects.

Metal / plastic / rubber parts plant: helper at a press, molding machine or inspection bench takes parts from a chute, gaylord or tote, checks size/gauge and visual grade (flash, short shot, burrs), and separates good parts by size or cavity into cartons while culling scrap; mixed part numbers, frequent changeovers.

Wood products / building materials plant: helper at a planer mill lug chain, panel line or block/brick line pulls and separates pieces by grade and dimension into sort bins or stacks; heavy, long pieces, dust, grade determined by visible defects.

Light manufacturing (apparel/textiles, printing, consumer goods): helper sorts finished goods by size, style, weight or material into cartons, totes or racks at a table or end-of-line station; small batches, many SKUs, deformable or fragile items.

tasks.label: Pack and store materials and products.

instances.label: End-of-line packing of uniform finished product at a production line in a plant (food, beverage, CPG, plastics): erecting cartons, loading a fixed count of packages/units into cases or trays, sealing and labeling, working to line rate beside conveyors and packaging equipment.

Packing assorted or mixed-SKU durable goods into shipping cartons at a pack bench (kits, spare parts, short runs, varied box sizes): selecting items, choosing and erecting the box, taping, weighing and labeling; frequent changeovers.

Packing fragile, heavy, or irregular items for storage or shipment: wrapping parts in paper, foam or VCI film, cutting and inserting dunnage, building custom cartons or wooden crates, blocking and bracing, in a job shop or fabrication plant with no two jobs alike.

tasks.label: Wash work areas, machines, equipment, vehicles, or products.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Scheduled washing/scrubbing of large open floor areas in a plant — production bays, main aisles, staging, shipping and warehouse floor — at shift end, using a mop or a walk-behind/ride-on scrubber; aisles are kept clear by the facility, people and forklifts move through.

Sanitation-window wet washdown in a food, beverage or protein plant: pre-rinse, foam, rinse and sanitize equipment exteriors, conveyors, tables, floors, walls and drains in defined production zones with a high-pressure hose and chemical applicator.

Detail cleaning in and around equipment that a floor machine cannot reach: hosing and scrubbing congested floor under and behind machines, catwalks, drain trenches, walls, benches, and mopping up oil, coolant or product spills wherever they occur.

In-place cleaning of machine surfaces between runs in non-washdown manufacturing (printing, plastics, metal, paper converting): wiping ink/resin/coolant off rollers, blankets, molds, guards, hoppers and conveyors with solvent rags, brushes and compressed air, plus detail cleaning of processing equipment that requires partial disassembly.

Batch washing of items taken to a wash area: removed tooling, molds, screens, trays, dies, parts, product containers, totes, bins and racks cleaned at a parts washer, pressure-wash booth or sink, then rinsed, sanitized and set out to dry.
Washing vehicles and mobile plant equipment — delivery trucks, trailers, tankers, forklifts, yard carts and dumpsters — at the plant's wash bay or in the yard with brushes, hose and detergent.

tasks.label: Place products in equipment or on work surfaces for further processing, inspecting, or wrapping.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Food/beverage plant: helper takes raw or semi-finished product (portions of meat or poultry, dough pieces, produce, baked goods) from bulk bins, racks or an infeed belt and places it into processing equipment or onto trays/tables for inspection and wrapping. Wet, cold, sanitary conditions; high repetition; product is deformable and variable; frequent product changeovers.

Plastics/rubber/metal fabrication: helper loads workpieces into a press, molding machine, CNC or laser, and sets finished pieces on a bench or conveyor for inspection. Parts arrive loose in gaylords, totes or on pallets in mixed orientations; moderate weight, oily or sharp; low-volume high-mix runs.

End-of-line packaging area: helper places finished goods from a cart, tote or accumulation belt onto the infeed of a wrapping, labeling or case-packing machine, or onto a work table for hand wrapping and boxing. Several SKUs, cartons/bottles/bagged goods, steady line rate.

Durable-goods assembly (automotive, appliance, furniture, electronics): helper picks components or subassemblies from a rack, kit cart or dunnage and seats them into fixtures, jigs or nests on the line for welding, gluing, pressing or further assembly. Millimetre-level seating required; work shared with people on a moving line.

Small or high-variety shop (cut-and-sew/textiles, upholstery, foam, printing/signage, woodworking): helper spreads or lays limp, floppy or oversized items (fabric plies, garments, panels, printed sheets) flat on a work surface or into equipment for inspection, pressing or wrapping. Items nest and cling; stacks are irregular; layout and job change often.

tasks.label: Transfer finished products, raw materials, tools, or equipment between storage and work areas of plants and warehouses, by hand or using hand trucks or powered lift trucks.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Plant/warehouse: helper moves palletized raw materials or components from rack or floor storage to a production line or staging lane using a powered pallet jack, counterbalance or reach truck; includes putaway into racking; aisles shared with people and other lift trucks.

Plant stockroom to workstation: helper carries or hand-trucks cartons, totes, and small-parts bins of components to line-side racks and benches, replenishing on operator request, several trips per shift.

End-of-line to warehouse: helper takes finished cases/pallets off the line, stages them, and transports them to the finished-goods area or shipping dock (including loading trailers) by pallet jack or lift truck.

Ad-hoc retrieval: a production worker asks for a specific tool, die, fixture, gauge or small piece of equipment; the helper locates it in a tool crib or storage shelving among many similar loose items and brings it to the machine.

Awkward or oversized loads: drums, coils/rolls, long stock, carts of work-in-progress, or machine parts moved through congested aisles between storage and work areas with a cart, drum handler, tugger or lift truck.

tasks.label: Help production workers by performing duties of lesser skill, such as supplying or holding materials or tools, or cleaning work areas and equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Line-side material supply in a manufacturing plant: the helper fetches totes, bins, cartons or rolls of stock from the stockroom/staging area and delivers them to assembly stations or machines on the production floor, taking empties back, on a repeating cycle through aisles shared with people and forklifts.

Feeding and off-bearing at a machine or line: the helper loads blanks/parts from a rack or cart into a press, welder or molding machine, takes finished pieces away, and stacks them into totes, on racks, or on pallets staged for the next station.

Routine cleaning of plant floors and aisles: sweeping, scrubbing and mopping the open production floor, aisles and around the line at shift change or end of shift, including spill wipe-up in a facility kept to a housekeeping standard.

Washdown/sanitation of production equipment in a food or beverage plant: hosing, foaming, rinsing and sanitizing machine exteriors, conveyors, tables and surrounding surfaces during the sanitation window between production runs.

Detail cleanup around machines and workbenches in general manufacturing: brushing chips, swarf, offcuts and packaging scrap into bins, emptying scrap and trash containers, wiping down tooling, benches and machine guards, and tidying tools back to their places among clutter and fixed obstacles.

Assisting a skilled worker at the point of work: steadying or positioning a panel, weldment or fixture while the worker cuts, welds, fastens or measures, and handing over the tools, fasteners and parts the worker calls for as the job proceeds.

tasks.label: Prepare raw materials for processing.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Food/beverage plant: preparing incoming raw produce, grain or meat for the processing line — washing, culling defective units and foreign material, trimming/peeling/cutting to size, and feeding the prepared material onto the line. Wet, cold, high-throughput plant floor.

Plastics, rubber, chemical or food plant: charging bulk raw material into hoppers, mixers and blenders — moving pallets of 25-50 lb sacks/boxes of resin, powder, flour or additives to the feed point, slitting bags, dumping contents, disposing of empty bags, and keeping the machine fed while it runs.

Batch preparation by recipe (bakery, paint, coatings, rubber compounding): weighing and measuring minor/micro ingredients and additives on scales into pails or totes, checking against the batch sheet, labeling and staging them beside the mixer for the operator.

Metal, wood or plastics fabrication shop: bringing stock to the machine and getting it ready — unbanding bundles, destacking sheets/bars/boards, cutting or shearing to length, deburring or wiping down, and loading the blank into the press, saw, CNC or extruder.

Receiving/staging in any plant: unloading incoming cases, totes and pallets of raw material from trailers, depalletizing them, transporting them across the plant floor to the line, and loading them onto infeed conveyors or feed tables while forklifts and people work around.

tasks.label: Start machines or equipment to begin production processes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Metal/plastics shop: helper loads a blank or part into a CNC mill, lathe, wire EDM, press or injection molding machine, closes the guard door, and presses the cycle-start (often a two-hand or panel button), then confirms via stack light/spindle noise that the cycle is running before moving to the next machine.

Food, beverage, paper or consumer-goods packaging line: at shift start the helper follows a startup sequence — energize disconnects, reset faults, select the product recipe on an HMI touchscreen, then start conveyor, filler, capper, labeler and case packer in order, watching for jams or misfeeds and stopping/restarting until product flows cleanly.

Batch/process equipment in a bakery, chemical, paint or compounding plant: after ingredients are charged, the helper secures the lid or clamps, sets speed/time dials or selects a program, and engages the start lever or button on a mixer, blender, grinder or extruder, staying to confirm the batch is turning properly.

Woodworking, foundry or fabrication shop start-of-shift power-on round: the helper walks the shop turning on air compressor, dust collector, exhaust fans, conveyors and individual saws/sanders/presses at their local switches or disconnects, checking guards, blades and air pressure as each is brought up.

Outdoor yard or field production area: helper starts portable or auxiliary equipment — generator, pump, portable mixer, concrete saw, conveyor stacker — with a key switch or pull cord in weather and on uneven ground, then verifies it runs before production begins.

tasks.label: Record information, such as the number of products tested, meter readings, or dates and times of product production.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Turn valves to regulate flow of liquids or air, to reverse machines, to start pumps, or to regulate equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Production plant floor: on the operator's instruction, the helper opens or closes manual hand valves (quarter-turn ball levers, handwheels) on fixed process piping feeding a machine — city water, steam, compressed air, or product line — at known locations along the line, then verifies flow started/stopped.

Machine-side controls at the helper's workstation: pressing start/stop/reverse pushbuttons, throwing levers to reverse a conveyor or mixer, jogging a machine, and adjusting an air-pressure regulator knob or coolant valve on the machine, dozens of times a shift interleaved with loading and unloading duties.

Throttling to a condition: the helper cracks or closes down a valve to hold a flow rate, pressure, or temperature — watching a gauge, sight glass, or the product itself (e.g., coating thickness, tank level) — and readjusts as the process drifts, per the lead operator's direction.

Liquid/air transfers: opening tank, tote, drum, or tanker valves, connecting or opening a hose, starting a transfer pump, watching the level, then shutting the valve and stopping the pump at the right point; also purging air lines and draining sumps.

Awkward or dirty access: stiff or partly seized valves needing a wrench or valve key, valves overhead, in floor pits, behind machine guarding or inside wet washdown areas during cleanup and changeover, where the helper must reach, brace, and apply body force.

tasks.label: Tie products in bundles for further processing or shipment, following prescribed procedures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: End-of-line bundling of long stock in a sawmill, extrusion plant or steel/pipe fabrication shop: the helper stacks cut lumber, bar, pipe or profiles to a prescribed count/pattern and secures the bundle with wire or strapping before it goes to shipping.

Bundling printed or converted paper products in a print plant, bindery or corrugated plant: counting or jogging stacks of newspapers, inserts, cartons or blanks and tying/strapping each bundle to a prescribed count, then labeling for the next operation.

Bench or line bundling of small/soft manufactured goods: stacks of plastic bags, garment cut parts, molded parts, tubes or small assemblies counted and tied with twine, band or strap and tagged for the next department.

Coiling and tying flexible goods at the end of an extrusion or winding line: hose, tubing, wire, cable or rope wound into a coil and tied at several points before shipment.

Ad hoc bundling around the plant floor: mixed offcuts, rework pieces, odd-shaped or oversized items, scrap and returns gathered from carts, racks and the floor and tied with twine or wire wherever they sit, with counts and tie patterns varying job to job.
