tasks.label: Check aircraft prior to flights to ensure that the engines, controls, instruments, and other systems are functioning properly.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Light piston single or twin (C172/C182/C206/Baron) at an FBO ramp or tiedown before a sightseeing, skydive, survey or small charter flight: full walkaround — check control surface freedom and hinges/fasteners, drain fuel sumps and inspect samples for water/contamination, check oil quantity on the dipstick and add oil, inspect tires/brakes/struts, remove pitot cover, chocks and tie-downs, inspect prop and cowling, then cockpit flow (fuel selector, flight controls free and correct, instruments, avionics), engine start and run-up with magneto, carb heat and gauge checks; accept or ground the aircraft.

Turbine business jet or cabin-class turboprop (Citation, King Air, PC-12) at an FBO ramp before an on-demand charter leg: exterior walkaround of gear pins, tires and brakes, static ports and probes, engine inlets and fan blades, pylon/nacelle fluid leaks, service-panel fluid quantities; then cockpit power-up, annunciator and warning-system tests, flight control and trim checks, FMS/avionics setup, engine start with ITT/N1/oil pressure monitoring and generator/bleed checks.

Helicopter preflight (air tour, HEMS, or utility ship such as an AS350, Bell 407, EC135) on an airport ramp, heliport, or hospital pad: main rotor head, pitch links, blade condition and tape, swashplate, tail rotor and drive shaft, transmission and hydraulic fluid sight glasses, engine deck and cowlings, plus cockpit checks, engine start, hydraulic and warning-system checks and system run-up.

Preflight at a remote or off-airport location taken as found — backcountry strip, ranch or field staging area, EMS scene/rural landing zone, or unattended gravel ramp — often at night, in wind, dust, rain or cold, with no lighting, ladder, GPU or shelter; includes frost/snow removal decisions, fuel quality checks from drums or truck, and full systems verification before departure.

Quick-turn between-leg checks during a high-tempo tour, skydive or shuttle day: abbreviated walkaround with engine hot, fuel and oil quantity verification, prop/rotor and control surface look-over, tire and leak check, cabin/door security, and cockpit instrument and warning checks, all with passengers waiting on the ramp.

Cockpit-side portion of the preflight in a two-crew turbine charter operation: while the other pilot walks the aircraft, this pilot powers up the aircraft, runs the cockpit preparation checklist, tests annunciators, stall/fire warning and stby instruments, verifies fuel quantity and hydraulic/pressurization indications, checks flight controls and trim, and confirms all systems are functioning before start.

It shares the object (a transport aircraft's exterior) but covers only camera-based damage detection — it does not sump fuel, check oil, move control surfaces, or run cockpit/engine checks — so it substantiates at most a sub-step of the pilot's preflight.

It bounds capability: for a purpose-built autonomous aircraft the automated portion is onboard built-in test (e.g., aileron travel, propeller condition), while the physical inspection of the airframe still requires a human team member.

instances.label: Single-pilot Part 135 on-demand charter or feeder-cargo leg in a piston/turboprop (Caravan, King Air, Navajo): preflight, taxi, IFR/VFR departure from a towered or non-towered public airport, ATC-managed enroute segment with weather deviations, instrument approach and landing at the destination airport, day or night.

Two-crew turbojet charter (PIC or SIC) with fare-paying passengers aboard: FBO ramp departure, IFR flight in the high-altitude NAS between towered airports, crew coordination and callouts, approach and landing in mixed weather, taxi to the FBO.

Air tour / sightseeing flight (helicopter or fixed-wing) with passengers, flown repeatedly over a published scenic route from a tour base or heliport, VFR day, low altitude near terrain, heavy same-operator and other tour traffic, return to the same pad.

Helicopter air ambulance flight: launch from a base helipad, interfacility transfers between hospital rooftop/ground helipads, plus off-airport accident-scene landings selected from the air, often at night or in marginal weather with wires, poles and bystanders around the landing zone.

Utility / aerial-work flying: agricultural application passes over farm fields, external-load or utility lifts, offshore platform shuttles, pipeline and survey patrol - repetitive low-level maneuvering over terrain and sites taken as found, operating from rural strips, pads or platforms.

Backcountry or bush charter: passengers or freight to unimproved gravel, dirt, beach or high-altitude strips with no ATC, no published approach, and surface, wind and obstacle conditions assessed from the air by the pilot before committing to land.

Off-airport helicopter approach and landing at an unprepared site (accident scene, remote pad, dusty/snowy LZ) in a degraded visual environment — brownout/whiteout or night with few visual cues — relying on instruments and onboard sensing for the final approach.

instances.label: Part 135 on-demand passenger charter: single- or two-pilot turboprop or light jet from an FBO at a towered airport, engine start and taxi, IFR departure and enroute clearance handling, 1-3 hour leg in mixed weather, instrument approach and landing at a destination airport, passengers aboard.

Feeder cargo/mail run in a single-engine turboprop (Caravan class) or light twin: single pilot, often night or IMC, ramp-to-ramp legs of 100-400 nm between a hub airport and small regional/non-towered airports, freight loaded in pod and cabin.

Air tour flight: helicopter or fixed-wing scenic loop of 20-60 minutes with 4-6 passengers, departing and returning to the same heliport/airport, VFR in congested tour corridors (canyon, coastline, city), repeated many times per day.

Helicopter air ambulance mission: launch on short notice, land at an unimproved scene landing zone (roadside, field) or a hospital rooftop/ground helipad, load patient and medical crew, fly to a receiving hospital pad, frequently at night or in marginal weather.

Remote-area freight/supply run: turbine helicopter or utility aircraft delivering cargo (fuel, supplies, sling loads, mail) to off-airport sites and unimproved landing zones — mine sites, camps, villages, backcountry pads — with no prepared surface or ground infrastructure.

Bush/backcountry passenger flight: floatplane or tundra-tire aircraft carrying passengers and their gear to a lake, gravel bar, or unimproved strip serving a lodge or village, judging surface, wind, and water conditions on arrival.

tasks.label: Check baggage or cargo to ensure that it has been loaded correctly.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Charter/corporate jet (e.g., King Air, Citation) at an FBO ramp: after line crew or the pilot loads passenger suitcases, golf bags and boxes into the external baggage compartment, the pilot inspects the stow — items within the compartment's placarded weight limit, nothing that can shift into the tail cone or block the fire-detection/service panels, restraint net hooked, door closed and latched — and reconciles it with the weight-and-balance sheet before accepting the load.

Part 135 cargo feeder turboprop (Cessna 208 Caravan, Beech 99, Metroliner) at a cargo ramp or freight dock: handlers stack parcels, totes, mail sacks and odd-sized freight in the cabin and belly pod; the pilot checks the load against the load manifest and zone weight limits, verifies cargo nets/straps are anchored to the correct rings and tensioned, checks for hazmat/leaking freight and clear egress, then closes and latches the cargo door.

Small piston air taxi, air tour, or sightseeing flight (C206, C182, Piper Navajo) at a GA ramp: the pilot loads and checks passenger bags, camera gear, coolers and small freight into an aft baggage compartment or nose locker, confirms the aft compartment limit is not exceeded for CG, sees that items are wedged/tied so they cannot shift in turbulence, and secures the latch.

Air ambulance or EMS/tour helicopter at a hospital helipad or airport base: the pilot checks that patient-transport gear, oxygen bottles, isolette or medical bags, plus crew and passenger baggage, are stowed in the correct bay or under a cargo net, that lateral/longitudinal limits are respected in a small cabin, and that nothing is loose near controls or doors, often under time pressure with rotors turning.

Utility helicopter, bush, floatplane or backcountry charter at an off-airport landing zone, gravel strip, dock or remote camp: the pilot checks a mixed load of fuel drums, tools, hunting/fishing gear, building materials or a cargo-hook/basket load, verifies lashings and hook attachment, judges the stack against CG limits, in wind, rain, snow, dust and uneven terrain with no ground-support infrastructure.

sources.system: ICAI airside robotics program (ramp-side baggage robotic arm, in development)
sources.developer: International Centre of Aviation Innovation (Singapore) with industry partners
sources.title: How Robotics Are Changing Airport Operations | Aviation Week
sources.claim: Industry program leaders state that putting robots inside aircraft for baggage and ... is still a long-term, technically challenging objective, and that even ramp-side interaction with the aircraft (such as opening cargo doors) is the 'next challenge' beyond today's autonomous tractors and dollies.
sources.transferJustification: Directly about the environment of this task (aircraft holds and the ramp interface). It establishes that no fielded robotic system works inside aircraft holds or opens/latches aircraft cargo doors, which the pilot's load check requires.

sources.system: ARC 1 / ARC One
sources.title: Robot Handles Every Bag in Airports | The Road to Autonomy
sources.claim: The most advanced fielded airport baggage robot is a mobile manipulator that picks, scans and places bags onto carts and into ULDs inside airport bag rooms; it works in the bag room, not at the aircraft, and its output is loading, not verification of an aircraft's load.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous baggage handling with per-bag scanning in a structured airport facility. It does not transfer: the robot never enters an aircraft compartment, does not check restraint nets/straps, weight-and-balance zone limits, or door security, which are the accepted output of the pilot's check.

sources.system: CargoCobra
sources.title: CargoCobra · The only autonomous robot for inside aircraft cargo holds
sources.claim: A robot intended to work autonomously inside narrow-body aircraft cargo holds exists only as a development project with an OEM proof of concept, and its function is loading/unloading bags rather than verifying that a load is correct.
sources.transferJustification: Closest robotic effort to working inside an aircraft hold. It is pre-deployment (POC), targets airline narrow-body holds rather than GA/charter compartments, and performs loading rather than the pilot's acceptance check.

sources.system: DTAC robot fleet (evoBOT, O3dyn, autonomous forklift)
sources.developer: Fraunhofer IML / Digital Testbed Air Cargo
sources.title: Testing robotics in live airport cargo operations - Air Cargo Week
sources.claim: Autonomous ground-handling robots have been tested in live airport cargo operations in Germany, covering container transport and ULD loading/unloading in terminals and on the apron, but as research testbed trials rather than accepted operational load-verification.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous air-cargo handling in an institution-controlled airport (E2). Does not transfer to this task: the robots move containers and pallets; none inspects a loaded aircraft compartment or issues a go/no-go acceptance on restraint and weight distribution.

sources.system: Donecle automated aircraft inspection drone
sources.title: French AviationTech startup Donecle bags €10 million to grow drone-based inspection platform | EU-Startups
sources.claim: Autonomous drones perform certified automated visual inspection of aircraft exteriors in hangars at commercial scale, showing autonomous aircraft inspection exists, but only for external surface damage, not interior load verification.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous inspection of an aircraft in a structured facility. It does not transfer: the drone images external skin for dents/lightning strikes and cannot open compartments, tug restraints, reposition bags, or evaluate a load against weight-and-balance limits.

sources.system: GMO AI & Robotics humanoid ground-handling robots at Haneda
sources.developer: Japan Airlines / JAL Ground Service with GMO AI & Robotics
sources.title: Japan Airlines to test humanoid robots for airport ground handling work - The Japan Times
sources.claim: Humanoid robots being trialled for airport ground handling, including baggage tasks beside live aircraft, are not yet autonomous; autonomous operation is a future goal of the multi-year trial.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: general ramp/baggage work by general-purpose robots. Cannot support a positive judgment because the robots are remotely operated during the trial period.

sources.system: Speedcargo CARGO EYE / CARGO ARM with Güdel gantry robots
sources.title: Speedcargo & Güdel Announce Launch of Air Cargo Automation System for ULD Palletizing | DC Velocity
sources.claim: Purpose-built robotic air-cargo cells (gantry robots with computer vision plus automated weight, dimension and X-ray acceptance lanes) build and break down ULDs inside cargo terminals; the machine builds pallets to plan rather than inspecting and accepting a load already placed in an aircraft.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated build-up/verification of air cargo units in a fixtured cell — the best candidate for an E1 counterfactual. It does not complete this task: it constructs ULDs from loose freight and never verifies an aircraft's stowage, restraint, or center-of-gravity compliance as the pilot must.

tasks.label: Conduct in-flight tests and evaluations at specified altitudes and in all types of weather to determine the receptivity and other characteristics of equipment and systems.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Post-installation/repair avionics check flight on a light single or twin (Part 135/91 fleet, air-taxi or flight-school aircraft). The pilot departs the home airport, climbs to specified altitudes, tunes and evaluates comm/nav/GPS/transponder reception and interference on various headings and ranges, checks autopilot modes and a coupled approach, then writes up squawks. Day VMC, towered or untowered airport plus the local practice area.

Equipment evaluation flight on a turbine charter aircraft or business jet at altitude: climb to assigned flight levels under IFR, frequently in IMC, verifying datalink/SATCOM/nav radio reception, RVSM altimetry, weather radar and autoflight behavior in cruise, working with ATC in controlled airspace.

Functional check flight after heavy airframe/engine or flight-control maintenance: a prescribed test-card profile with deliberate abnormal-condition checks (stall warning/protection, autopilot disconnects, emergency gear and pressurization checks, single-engine handling), requiring in-flight judgment of handling, vibration, noise and system behavior before return to service.

Helicopter check/evaluation flight after mission-equipment installation (EMS, utility, ENG or tour operator): hover and low-speed checks, track-and-balance, then low-level and off-airport maneuvering to evaluate FLIR, searchlight, hoist, radios or NVG compatibility, sometimes at night, at unimproved landing sites and over as-found terrain.

Airborne payload/sensor evaluation flights: fly prescribed lines, orbits or altitude steps to check a survey camera/lidar, radio relay, telemetry link, antenna coverage or navaid/ADS-B signal reception, over varied terrain and water, largely in uncontrolled airspace and in whatever weather is encountered.

Developmental or certification flight testing of newly installed equipment for an STC holder, OEM or defense program: fly test cards at specified altitudes and speeds with telemetry, chase support and flight-test engineers, operating from a test airport or designated test area.

sources.system: Reliable Autonomy System (automated Cessna 208B Caravan)
sources.title: Reliable Robotics Secures $17.4M Air Force Deal As FAA Approves Fully Autonomous Aircraft Testing
sources.claim: Reliable Robotics flew a Cessna ... nobody on board through a complete automated flight (taxi, takeoff, cruise, landing) at a public-use municipal airport under an FAA special airworthiness certificate, supervised remotely from 50 miles away.
sources.transferJustification: The flight was itself an FAA-approved test flight of an onboard system, flown by machine through a full profile in the same airport/terminal-airspace environment in which post-maintenance and avionics check flights are conducted.

sources.system: Reliable Autonomy System (Cessna 208B)
sources.title: Flying the pattern with robot 208B - AOPA
sources.claim: Reliable Robotics' automated Caravan is being used for a NASA-contracted flight test campaign around regional airports that evaluates routine operations plus contingency scenarios including detect-and-avoid and GPS-degraded/denied conditions; the system can fly with a safety pilot aboard or with no one aboard.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on task: an automated aircraft flies test profiles in shared airspace around regional airports while onboard equipment and system behavior are evaluated, which is the pilot role in in-flight equipment tests.

sources.system: Reliable DAA system with Sagetech, Collins and uAvionix sensors on a Cessna 208B
sources.developer: Reliable Robotics / FAA / Virginia Tech MAAP

sources.claim: Reliable Robotics completed an FAA-contracted campaign of detect-and-avoid data-collection flights in and around airport ..., assessing the alerting and maneuver-guidance performance of onboard DAA sensors and ACAS X in terminal and en route environments.
sources.transferJustification: Same task class (in-flight evaluation of the reception and alerting characteristics of installed equipment around airports), but the release does not establish that the autonomy flew the test sorties, so it is treated as context only.

sources.system: Superpilot (autonomous Cessna Caravan 208)
sources.title: Joby Completes Landmark U.S. Defense Exercise with Autonomous Flight Technology
sources.claim: Joby's Superpilot autonomy flew a Cessna Caravan 208 for 43.7 hours and 7,342 miles during a US Air Force exercise, executing cargo, inter-island and ISR (sensor) profiles across Class B, C, D and uncontrolled airspace under both VFR and IFR, with a safety pilot aboard only monitoring.
sources.transferJustification: ISR profiles are sensor-payload collection flights flown to prescribed tracks and altitudes; flying such profiles under IFR and in uncontrolled airspace is the same piloting work required for airborne equipment evaluation flights.

sources.system: Merlin Pilot
sources.title: Merlin Advances Toward Autonomous Flight Tech STC with Simulator
sources.claim: Merlin's Pilot autonomy system has been integrated on five aircraft types including King Airs and Part 135 cargo Caravans, and secured US National Airspace System integration ... after FAA-contracted uncrewed cargo trials in Alaska.
sources.transferJustification: Shows machine flight of the same class of turbine aircraft used for charter check flights, operating within the structured NAS; supports the flying half of an in-flight equipment evaluation in that environment.

sources.system: XQ-58A Valkyrie with AFRL AI agents
sources.title: AFRL AI agents successfully pilot XQ-58A Valkyrie uncrewed jet aircraft
sources.claim: AI algorithms flew an uncrewed XQ-58A Valkyrie jet for a three-hour test sortie inside a segregated military test range, the purpose of the sortie being to test the machine-learning flight-control software and its safety framework.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on task at a purpose-built setting: a machine flies a jet test sortie in cleared range airspace with ground-based test control while the performance of an onboard system is evaluated.

sources.system: X-62A VISTA with DARPA ACE AI agents
sources.developer: USAF Test Pilot School / DARPA / Lockheed Martin Skunk Works
sources.title: U.S. Air Force Secretary Kendall Flies in AI-piloted X-62A VISTA
sources.claim: AI agents flew the X-62A VISTA test aircraft through 21 flight tests at Edwards AFB, including within-visual-range maneuvering against a human-piloted F-16, as part of a campaign evaluating flight-critical autonomy software.
sources.transferJustification: Demonstrates machine-flown test-card sorties, including aggressive envelope maneuvering, in instrumented test-range airspace - the closest analogue to a pilot flying prescribed test maneuvers to characterize a system.

sources.system: Optionally Piloted Black Hawk (ALIAS/MATRIX)
sources.title: ALIAS equipped Black Hawk helicopter completes first uninhabited flight | DARPA
sources.claim: A UH-60A Black Hawk retrofitted with Sikorsky's MATRIX autonomy flew for 30 minutes with nobody on board over a US Army installation, the first uninhabited flight of the type.
sources.transferJustification: Shows a full-size helicopter flown entirely by machine, covering the pilot's flying role (takeoff, maneuvering, landing) needed for helicopter check and equipment-evaluation flights; the flights were themselves tests of the MATRIX system.

sources.system: MATRIX / SARA autonomy
sources.title: MATRIX Technology | Lockheed Martin
sources.claim: Sikorsky's MATRIX autonomy performs full-authority flight control for autonomous helicopter operation, including takeoff, route planning, obstacle ..., landing-site selection and landing, using onboard sensors for real-time 3D perception.
sources.transferJustification: Hover, low-speed and off-airport landing capability is the flying skill set a helicopter check flight requires; demonstrated on institution-controlled airfields and ranges rather than arbitrary civil sites.

sources.system: Optionally Piloted Black Hawk (MATRIX)
sources.title: Marines Explore Autonomous Flight with Sikorsky's MATRIX System | SOFREP
sources.claim: At Project Convergence 2022 the uninhabited MATRIX-equipped Black Hawk autonomously flew an 83-mile resupply mission at 200 feet across valley terrain carrying 500 pounds of cargo.
sources.transferJustification: Low-level autonomous helicopter flight over as-found terrain matches the maneuvering environment of helicopter mission-equipment evaluation flights, though it occurred inside a controlled military range.

sources.system: NLR Drone Flight Inspection (DFI)
sources.title: R&D case: ILS inspection on airports with drones - Nederlands Lucht- en Ruimtevaartcentrum
sources.claim: NLR developed a drone flight inspection system for measuring instrument landing system signals at airports; all inspection runs can be flown in ..., complementing the crewed flight-inspection aircraft.
sources.transferJustification: Flight inspection is the same work as this task's 'receptivity' checks - flying prescribed profiles to measure the signal reception characteristics of navigation equipment - here done by an automated aircraft in an airport environment.

tasks.label: Perform minor aircraft maintenance and repair work, or arrange for major maintenance.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Turnaround servicing on an FBO ramp between charter/air-tour legs: open the cowl or oil door, check the dipstick and add engine oil, drain fuel sumps and inspect samples for water/debris, check tire, strut and brake condition, top hydraulic fluid, wipe bugs off windshield and leading edges, resecure caps and panels. Outdoor apron, mixed aircraft types, variable weather, aircraft parked among ground support equipment.

Discrepancy discovered on pre-/post-flight (oil leak, worn tire, bird strike, avionics fault, unusual vibration): the pilot judges airworthiness against the MEL/regulations, enters the squawk in the aircraft maintenance record, phones the company A&P or an MRO, arranges parts, a mobile mechanic, a hangar slot or a ferry flight, and returns the aircraft to service. Ramp, hangar or operations office.

In-hangar preventive maintenance items allowed to the pilot (FAR 43 App. A): replace a landing/nav light bulb or lens, a safety belt, seat cushion or static wick; secure or replace loose inspection-panel/cowl fasteners; lubricate hinges and latches; service tires with air; replenish oxygen; replace a side window. Company hangar, standard aircraft types, tools and stands on hand.

Helicopter tour, utility, EMS or bush operation servicing away from a maintenance base 
animproing LZ, ranch or oil pad, hospital pad or gravel strip: wipe rotor blades and windows, check and add engine/transmission/hydraulic oil, inspect for leaks between cycles, resecure cowlings and fairings, clear FOD and debris, install tie-downs and covers. Layout and surface differ every site; no institution controls the setting.

Cold/adverse weather ramp work before the first leg: brush and remove frost, snow and ice from wings, tail and rotor blades, clear ice from control surfaces and inlets, install/remove engine, pitot and rotor-blade covers, arrange or perform engine preheat, check fuel for water after a temperature swing. Outdoor apron, wind, darkness, time pressure.

Post-flight exterior cleaning of the airframe at the home hangar or wash rack: wash or dry-wash the fuselage and wings, remove bug, oil and exhaust residue from leading edges and belly, clean windshield and cabin windows to the company appearance standard.

sources.system: Wilder Systems robotic aircraft washing system (RoboDK-programmed FANUC arms)
sources.title: RoboDK Software helps cut Aircraft Washing Time by 95% - RoboDK blog
sources.claim: Wilder Systems' robotic 'drive-thru' aircraft wash runs the complete wash cycle on an F-16 with the robots operating alone, replacing a four-person manual wash.
sources.transferJustification: Aircraft exterior washing and bug/residue removal is the same work as the pilot's post-flight exterior cleaning instance: same objects (airframe skin, wings, belly), same accepted output (visually clean with no damage to paint or antennas).

sources.system: Wilder Systems robotic aircraft washing cell
sources.title: Case Studies: How RoboDK is used for Automated Airplane Washing | RoboDK
sources.claim: The Wilder aircraft washing installation is a purpose-built, self-contained cell with two 6-axis industrial robots on linear axes, through which the aircraft is towed.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes the environment of the washing evidence: a purpose-built robotic cell with the aircraft brought to the machine (E1), not an ordinary hangar bay or open apron.

sources.system: Donecle autonomous inspection drone
sources.title: Donecle's €10M Inspection Drone Raise Meets America's Aircraft Mechanic Shortage
sources.claim: Donecle's autonomous drones fly laser-positioned paths around parked aircraft in MRO hangars and produce defect reports; deployed by AAR, United, Lufthansa and others.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous exterior visual inspection of aircraft in a hangar. It substantiates only finding and reporting skin defects, not fluid servicing, component replacement, or coordinating repairs with a maintenance provider.

sources.system: Aerowash AW3 / AW12X aircraft washing robot
sources.title: Air Canada Invests In New Robots To Wash Aircraft | Aviation Week Network
sources.claim: The aircraft washing robots actually fielded on airport aprons and in hangars (Aerowash) are driven by a human operator with a wireless remote control.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (aircraft exterior cleaning) in an E2 setting. Because it is operator-driven throughout, it cannot support an autonomous completion judgment at E2.

sources.system: Automated Aircraft Ground Refueling (AAGR)
sources.title: AEROSPACE: Robots and vision refuel jet aircraft | Vision Systems Design
sources.claim: AFRL's Automated Aircraft Ground Refueling prototype used a robot with machine vision to unbolt a latch panel and connect a fuel adapter to refuel a fighter — a demonstration prototype for one aircraft type, not a fielded servicing system.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic access-panel opening plus fluid servicing on an aircraft, the nearest analogue to a pilot's oil/fluid top-off. Autonomy is not established and it never left prototype status, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.system: Avinxt (MSG Aviation) de-icing, washing and inspection robot
sources.date: 2023-03 announcement; still starting construction per 2025 reports

tasks.label: Rescue and evacuate injured persons.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: HEMS scene response: helicopter air-ambulance pilot is dispatched to a motor-vehicle crash or rural trauma scene, sizes up and lands in an ad hoc landing zone set up by fire/EMS (highway, field, parking lot), often at night with wires, poles, vehicles, dust and bystanders; medical crew loads the patient; pilot flies to a hospital helipad.

HEMS interfacility transfer: pilot flies a litter patient with a flight nurse/paramedic aboard from a rural hospital helipad to a trauma-center rooftop or ground helipad, day or night, making weather/IFR go-no-go decisions and operating into congested urban airspace and confined pads.

Fixed-wing air ambulance: pilot flies a King Air/Caravan/jet airport to airport (FBO ramp to FBO ramp) with a patient loaded from a ground ambulance and a medical crew aboard; IFR in controlled airspace, longer legs, sometimes cross-country or international repatriation.

Mountain/wilderness or maritime search-and-rescue: pilot holds a precise hover over rugged terrain, a cliff face, or water while a crew member hoists or short-hauls an injured hiker or boater, in turbulence, high density altitude, or over open water, then flies the patient out.

Disaster/mass-casualty evacuation: flood, hurricane or wildfire response flying injured and stranded people out of austere, damaged sites (levees, rooftops, cut-off communities) with degraded visibility from smoke or rain, ad hoc landing zones, crowds, and improvised coordination.

sources.system: Sikorsky/DARPA MATRIX optionally piloted Black Hawk (ALIAS)
sources.title: Sikorsky and DARPA's Autonomous Black Hawk Flies Logistics and Rescue Missions Without Pilots on Board
sources.claim: An uninhabited MATRIX-equipped UH-60A Black Hawk autonomously flew a combined cargo/casualty-evacuation mission at Yuma Proving Ground: re-routed in flight, it released its sling load, landed at a nearby site where a manikin on a litter was secured in the cabin, then flew the patient out while relaying vitals.

sources.system: Sikorsky OPV Black Hawk with MATRIX
sources.developer: Sikorsky (Lockheed Martin) with DARPA and the Joint Personnel Recovery Agency
sources.title: U.S. Soldier Becomes First to Plan and Execute Autonomous Black Hawk Missions using MATRIX Technology at Northern Strike 25-2
sources.claim: At Northern Strike 25-2 (Camp Grayling, Michigan, August 2025) a National Guard sergeant trained in under an hour planned and commanded autonomous OPV Black Hawk missions, including a simulated personnel recovery with a tail-to-tail patient transfer at an unimproved landing site, commanded by tablet from inside the aircraft.

sources.system: Sikorsky OPV Black Hawk with MATRIX
sources.title: U.S. Soldier Becomes First to Plan and Execute Autonomous Black Hawk Missions using MATRIX Technology at Northern Strike 25-2
sources.claim: The same Northern Strike exercise included the aircraft holding an autonomous hover while ground personnel attached a 2,900-pound external load, showing machine-held precision hover with people working directly beneath the aircraft.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (airborne external-load hookup) transfers to the pilot's part of a hoist or short-haul rescue: holding a precise, stable hover while crew attach and lift a load. It does not substantiate hoisting a live person from a cliff or from water.

sources.system: MATRIX (OPV Black Hawk, S-76 SARA)
sources.title: US Marines test Sikorsky's uncrewed helicopters with MATRIX
sources.claim: Sikorsky's MATRIX autonomy had logged more than 700 hours of autonomous flight on the optionally piloted Black Hawk by August 2025, including uncrewed resupply and medevac missions flown for the US Marines alongside an S-76 navigating an obstacle course.

sources.system: EHang EH216-S

sources.claim: China's CAAC granted the first Air Operator Certificates for human-carrying pilotless aircraft to EHang operators in March 2025, authorizing ticketed passenger-carrying EH216-S flights from designated sites in Guangzhou and ..., supported by purpose-built automated vertiports.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (pilotless passenger flights) substantiates the carriage element of an evacuation flight: a live human is flown with no pilot aboard between prepared pads under machine control. It does not cover litter patients, medical crew, or dispatch to arbitrary sites.

sources.system: Reliable Autonomy System on Cessna 208B Grand Caravan

sources.claim: Reliable Robotics' automation flies a Cessna 208B Caravan through all phases of flight 'gate to gate' with no pilot on board; it completed a 12-minute fully uncrewed flight at Hollister Municipal Airport ... November 2023 and continues FAA-backed uncrewed and detect-and-avoid flight testing under an Air Force contract.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (uncrewed cargo flight airport to airport) transfers to fixed-wing air ambulance: same aircraft type and same flight profile (taxi, IFR departure, cruise, approach, landing at another airport), with the cabin carrying payload rather than a patient litter.

sources.system: CMU/Piasecki autonomous landing-zone selection system on Boeing Unmanned Little Bird
sources.developer: Piasecki Aircraft Corp. / Carnegie Mellon Robotics Institute
sources.title: Piasecki Aircraft-Carnegie Mellon Demonstrate Autonomous Helicopter Collision Avoidance & Landing Zone Selection System
sources.claim: A full-size autonomous helicopter (Boeing Unmanned Little Bird with the CMU/Piasecki system) flew low-altitude obstacle-avoiding approaches, evaluated and selected safe landing sites in unmapped terrain, and landed on a self-generated approach path for a simulated casualty pickup.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (autonomous landing-zone evaluation and landing in unmapped terrain) covers the scene-landing element of a HEMS scene call, but was flown on test ranges without traffic, wires, crowds, weather minima decisions, or a real patient.

tasks.label: Instruct other pilots and student pilots in aircraft operations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Primary dual instruction flight in a single-engine trainer (e.g., C172/PA-28) at a flight school: instructor rides right seat while a pre-solo student flies the traffic pattern and practice-area maneuvers (slow flight, stalls, ground reference), physically demonstrates each maneuver on the controls, gives running verbal corrections, guards/takes the controls on unsafe inputs, handles radios and traffic scan, and debriefs and logs the lesson. Variable wind, turbulence, traffic and terrain.

Ground instruction at the flight school: pre-flight and post-flight briefings at a table or whiteboard, ground-school lessons on regulations, weather, systems and aeronautical decision making, walk-around preflight demonstration on the ramp, plus checkride prep and signing logbook endorsements.

Advanced dual instruction: instrument approaches under the hood or in actual IMC, night and cross-country flights, simulated engine failures and emergency procedures induced by the instructor (pulling power, covering instruments), at unfamiliar airports and in changing weather.

Operator/company training and checking of already-certificated pilots by a charter, air-ambulance, air-tour or corporate pilot serving as instructor/check airman: aircraft-specific and line-oriented training in the actual operating environment (mountain tour routes, helicopter confined-area and off-airport EMS landing zones, autorotation practice), plus mentoring and evaluation to company standards.

Simulator or flight-training-device session at a training center or flight school: instructor sets scenarios at the instructor operating station, injects failures, coaches the crew through procedures in real time, then conducts a structured debrief and grading.

sources.system: ROBOpilot (Robotic Pilot Unmanned Conversion Program)
sources.developer: US Air Force Research Laboratory / DZYNE Technologies
sources.title: VIDEO: AFRL's robotic pilot flies Cessna for 2 hours
sources.claim: AFRL/DZYNE's ROBOpilot is a robotic actuator kit that physically flies a conventional light aircraft (Cessna 206) autonomously, showing that machines can manipulate cockpit controls in flight — but the demonstration is unmanned flight, with no student aboard and no instructional function.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: flying a light training-category aircraft. It shows robotic manipulation of the same controls a CFI uses, but instruction requires teaching, evaluating and safeguarding a human student flying the aircraft, which this system does not do.

sources.system: Pibot
sources.developer: KAIST (Korea Advanced Institute of Science & Technology)
sources.title: 'Pibot' Better Than Human Pilots Say Researchers
sources.claim: KAIST's Pibot humanoid can physically manipulate standard cockpit controls, but it is a laboratory research prototype flying itself, not a system that trains or supervises a human student pilot.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: operating cockpit controls. Transfer to instruction fails because no cited demonstration has the robot occupying an instructor seat, assessing a student's inputs, or intervening to keep a novice-flown aircraft safe.

sources.system: Merlin Pilot (Cessna 208B Grand Caravan)
sources.title: Merlin's self-flying Cessna begins testing for FAA validation
sources.claim: Merlin Pilot autonomously flies a Cessna Caravan in flight test toward FAA certification; it is an autopilot-replacement for cargo/transport flight, not a system that delivers dual instruction to student pilots.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous operation of a general-aviation airframe. It does not transfer to instruction, which requires real-time coaching, error diagnosis and control-guarding with an unqualified pilot at the controls.

sources.system: AI flight-training tools (e.g., IP GPT simulator coach, AI debrief analytics)
sources.developer: US Air Force AETC; various training vendors
sources.title: Pilot training in 2026: How AI, VR and data are reshaping the industry
sources.claim: State-of-the-art AI in pilot training as of 2026 consists of software tutors, debrief analytics and simulator coaching chatbots that assist human instructors; none is an embodied system, and trade press reports AI augments rather than replaces certified instructors.
sources.transferJustification: Directly about the task. These are software-only systems (chatbots, analytics), excluded as robotic systems, and they are positioned as instructor aids, not substitutes.

tasks.label: Fly with other pilots or pilot-license applicants to evaluate their proficiency.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Flight-school CFI/chief instructor conducts a stage check or flight review with a student or rated pilot in a single-engine piston trainer (C172/PA-28). Evaluator occupies the right seat with dual controls, briefs and runs the sequence, pulls the throttle to simulate engine failure, sets the view-limiting device, works the radios, guards/takes the controls when the applicant's maneuver becomes unsafe, and issues a satisfactory/unsatisfactory judgment plus debrief. Flown in the practice area and traffic pattern in day VFR with real traffic, terrain and weather.

Part 135 charter/cargo check airman flies a competency or line check in a light twin, turboprop or light jet in the IFR system: real ATC clearances, instrument approaches to minimums, simulated engine failure and abnormal procedures, evaluator qualified as PIC and ready to intervene, then completes company/FAA check paperwork.

Instrument proficiency check or IFR skill evaluation where the candidate flies under a hood or in actual IMC; the evaluator serves as the legally required safety pilot, maintains outside traffic scan, fails instruments/avionics by covering gauges or pulling breakers, and judges tolerances against the ACS.

Helicopter operator (tour, EMS, utility) check pilot evaluates a line pilot: hovering work, autorotations, run-on landings, confined-area and pinnacle/off-airport landing-zone approaches, power management; evaluator guards the controls throughout and must recover the aircraft instantly if entry parameters degrade.

Designated pilot examiner or company examiner administers a full practical test to a certificate/rating applicant: ground/oral portion, then the flight in the applicant's aircraft, largely observing and running scenario prompts while remaining able to take control, ending in a pass/fail decision and certificate paperwork.

Recurrent proficiency check conducted in a qualified full-flight simulator or FTD at a training center: the check airman sits at the instructor operating station or right seat, injects failures and weather, and grades the pilot's performance to company/FAA standards inside a controlled indoor training facility.

sources.system: PIBOT
sources.developer: KAIST (Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology)
sources.title: Pibot' Better Than Human Pilots Say Researchers
sources.claim: KAIST's PIBOT humanoid robot sits in a cockpit and manipulates conventional flight controls and switches, demonstrated on flight simulators; it flies the aircraft itself rather than riding along to assess a human pilot's proficiency.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = physically flying an aircraft from the cockpit. It bounds the state of the art for robot occupancy of a pilot seat, but it does not transfer to evaluating another pilot: PIBOT flies the aircraft in simulators and has no demonstrated capability to observe a human trainee, inject test failures, judge maneuvers against the ACS, or render a pass/fail decision.

sources.system: Reliable Autonomy System (Cessna 208B Grand Caravan)
sources.title: Air Force Acquiring Autonomous, FAA-Certifiable Cargo Plane
sources.claim: Reliable Robotics' autonomy system has flown a Cessna 208B Caravan gate-to-gate with no pilot aboard, from real airports in the national airspace system; the system replaces the pilot, and there is no evaluation-of-a-human-pilot function.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = autonomous operation of a GA aircraft in real airspace. It shows machine flight control is feasible, but the rated task requires supervising, testing and grading a human pilot in the other seat; no such observation, intervention-on-a-trainee, or certification-decision capability is demonstrated.

sources.system: MATRIX / ALIAS Optionally Piloted Black Hawk
sources.title: Sikorsky and DARPA's Autonomous Black Hawk Flies Logistics and Rescue Missions Without Pilots on Board
sources.claim: Sikorsky's MATRIX autonomy (DARPA ALIAS) has flown an Optionally Piloted UH-60 Black Hawk with no crew aboard, performing cargo resupply and rescue-style missions; the autonomy flies the helicopter, it does not evaluate a human pilot.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = autonomous rotorcraft flight including precision approaches to landing points. Relevant to the helicopter check instance only in that machines can fly the aircraft; it provides no evidence of a machine judging a human pilot's autorotation or confined-area technique or intervening on that pilot's behalf.

sources.system: CAE Rise
sources.title: CAE Rise | CAE
sources.claim: CAE Rise automatically detects and ... maneuvers from simulator telemetry, but the output feeds a human instructor who performs the assessment; it is software with no embodiment and does not itself conduct or sign off a proficiency check.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = grading pilot maneuvers during a training/checking session. It is software-only (not a robotic system) and explicitly supports rather than replaces the instructor's assessment, so it cannot substantiate machine completion of the evaluation instance at any tier.

sources.system: Loft Dynamics H125 VR FSTD
sources.title: FAA approves VR flight simulator from Loft Dynamics for pilot training
sources.claim: Loft Dynamics' motion-platform VR device is FAA-qualified as a flight training device for helicopter training and rating credit, but training and checking on it are conducted and graded by human instructors/check airmen.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = presenting a controlled flight environment for proficiency work inside a training facility. It shows the structured-facility version of the instance exists, but the device is a training platform, not an autonomous evaluator; the check airman's observation, failure injection and pass/fail judgment remain human.

tasks.label: Inspect airfield conditions to ensure compliance with federal regulatory requirements.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Daily/continuous Part 139 self-inspection at a commercial-service airport: ops specialist drives runways, taxiways and aprons in a radio-equipped vehicle, coordinates runway access with ATC, scans pavement for cracks/spalls/rubber buildup and FOD (picking up debris), checks hold-position and edge markings, signs, in-pavement and edge lights, safety-area grading, construction barricades and wildlife, then logs discrepancies, initiates work orders and NOTAMs.

Night airfield lighting and visual-aid inspection: driving the movement area and approach areas after dark checking runway/taxiway edge and centerline lights, threshold/REIL, PAPI angles and colors, obstruction lights, sign legibility and illumination, recording burned-out or misaligned fixtures for the electricians.

Special condition inspections triggered by events: after thunderstorms (ponding, blown debris, downed signage), winter surface condition assessment (contaminant type and depth, friction check, RCAM/FICON runway condition code determination and reporting), and post-incident or post-construction inspections before returning a surface to service.

Perimeter, safety-area and wildlife inspection: driving/walking the perimeter service road and off-pavement grass areas to check fence integrity, gates, washouts and animal burrows, vegetation height and obstructions to approach surfaces, standing water and wildlife attractants, documenting findings for the wildlife hazard management plan and Part 139 records.

Military airfield daily inspection (Air Force/Navy airfield management): checking runway/taxiway surfaces and shoulders for FOD and pavement failures, markings and airfield lighting, arresting systems and barriers, airfield signage, obstructions, construction and waiver items against UFC/service instructions, with entries in the airfield check log and coordination with tower and CE.

Periodic documented surface-condition survey of a runway or taxiway supporting regulatory/records compliance: systematic capture and mapping of pavement distresses (cracking, spalling, raveling) across a full pavement surface, delivered as a quantified condition report used for the airport's inspection records and maintenance planning; conducted during a scheduled closure rather than in real time.

sources.system: sUAS used for Part 139 airport self-inspections (generic)
sources.title: On Airport Unmanned Aircraft System Operations | Federal Aviation Administration
sources.claim: FAA policy guidance states that unmanned aircraft cannot serve as the sole means of performing the required Part 139 airfield self-inspections; they may only supplement traditional inspection methods, so a drone-only inspection would not be an accepted output.

sources.system: DRONIC / AUTOSPEX
sources.title: Airfields - Niricson
sources.claim: Niricson performs airfield pavement condition assessment using autonomous UAV flights with AI defect detection (AUTOSPEX), collecting full-surface data in about an hour and producing quantified distress maps and PCI calculations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: periodic pavement condition survey rather than the regulatory self-inspection checklist. It transfers to the pavement-condition element of airfield inspection because the objects (runway surface cracking, spalling, FOD-generating distress), the precision required (mm-scale defect mapping), and the environment (an operating airport movement area) are the same.

sources.system: DRONIC / AUTOSPEX at Toronto Pearson International Airport
sources.developer: Niricson Software (for Greater Toronto Airports Authority)
sources.title: Toronto Pearson Airport - Niricson
sources.claim: A drone survey of an active international airport runway was flown for the airport authority, capturing the 60,400 m2 runway at 2 mm resolution in 3.5 hours, with a defect-quantified 3D model delivered to the operator.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above (pavement condition assessment on an operating airfield); shows the autonomous aerial survey completed at a real Part 139-equivalent commercial airport, i.e. an E2 setting.

sources.system: DRONIC vehicle-mounted capture at Gerald R. Ford International Airport
sources.title: Gerald R. Ford International Airport Runway - Niricson
sources.claim: The same vendor's 2025 project at a US Part 139 airport used a human-driven, vehicle-mounted imaging system rather than a robot, and the AI defect maps were reviewed by human QA/QC and cross-compared with a traditional consultant inspection.
sources.transferJustification: Same pavement-condition related task; cited as a limit — the US airfield delivery relied on a human-driven vehicle and human review, not autonomous robotic inspection.

sources.claim: An autonomous ground robot was tested on the ramp at a US commercial airport, patrolling the tarmac to detect foreign object debris and alert operations staff; the developer described the machine as still under development for future commercialization.

tasks.label: Implement airfield safety procedures to ensure a safe operating environment for personnel and aircraft operation.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine airfield safety inspection/surveillance round at a Part 139 airport or military airfield: driving the movement area in an ops vehicle, requesting runway access from the tower by radio, checking pavement condition, markings, signs, lighting, safety areas, NAVAID critical areas, gates and obstructions, then logging discrepancies and initiating NOTAMs or work orders.

FOD control on paved movement areas: spotting and removing loose debris (bolts, stones, rubber fragments, paper, luggage parts) from runways, taxiways and aprons during and after inspections, disposing of it in FOD bins and logging the find.

Wildlife hazard management: patrolling grass infields, ditches and perimeter, dispersing birds and mammals with pyrotechnics, vehicle harassment or noise, checking perimeter fence and gates for breaches, collecting carcasses after strikes and documenting the event.

Safeguarding closed or unserviceable areas and construction work: placing lighted barricades, cones and runway/taxiway closure markers, verifying contractor compliance with the construction safety plan, and escorting contractor or vendor vehicles across the movement area with ATC coordination.

Winter and adverse-weather surface operations: executing snow and ice clearance of runways, taxiways and aprons during a storm (plough/sweeper/blower formation, deicer application) so surfaces meet operating standards before reopening.

Emergency, incursion and personnel-enforcement response: responding to aircraft emergencies and alerts, disabled aircraft, fuel spills, unauthorized persons or vehicles on the movement area, stopping non-compliant drivers, and delivering airfield driving/ramp safety briefings.

sources.system: Teksbotics Autonomous Patrol Car (with UISEE)
sources.developer: Teksbotics / UISEE, for Airport Authority Hong Kong
sources.title: Autonomous Patrol Cars Deployed at Hong Kong International Airport
sources.claim: Four Teksbotics/UISEE autonomous patrol cars are deployed at Hong Kong International Airport, autonomously patrolling the north and south runway perimeters, detecting abnormalities or intruders with cameras and lidar and alerting on-duty airport staff.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine airfield perimeter patrol with automated anomaly detection and reporting. It shows a driverless vehicle can run repeated airfield safety rounds on airport pavement in weather, but it checks only fence-line intrusion, not the full Part 139 discrepancy checklist.

sources.system: ANYmal (ANYmal D / ANYmal X) with inspection analytics
sources.title: ANYbotics Introduces End-to-End Robotic Inspection Solution
sources.claim: ANYbotics sells a commercial, fully autonomous legged robot that performs routine inspection rounds in industrial plants, capturing sensor data at defined checkpoints and reporting condition anomalies without an operator.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous routine inspection rounds of fixed infrastructure. Transfer holds where assets are presented at standardized, surveyed checkpoints on a fixed route (an E1-style layout), which is how ANYmal inspects; it does not cover open-ended judgement over a live airfield.

sources.system: sUAS used for Part 139 airport self-inspections (generic programs)

sources.claim: The FAA states that unmanned aircraft cannot serve as the sole means of conducting required Part 139 airport self-inspections; they may only supplement inspections still performed by traditional (human) methods.

sources.system: Trombia Free autonomous sweeper (autonomous power unit + Trombia Sweeper Attachment)
sources.title: Trombia demonstrates autonomous airport parking lot sweeper - Automated Warehouse

tasks.label: Conduct inspections of the airport property and perimeter to maintain controlled access to airfields.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine perimeter fence-line patrol at a medium/large Part 139 commercial airport: drive the perimeter service road (5-15 miles of chain-link/barbed-wire fence), scanning for cut or damaged fabric, washouts and animal digs under the fence, debris, vegetation growth, and unauthorized persons or vehicles along the boundary; findings are radioed in and logged in the daily self-inspection record.

Hands-on gate and access-point inspection: at each vehicle and pedestrian gate, physically verify the gate is fully closed and latched, test the padlock/chain or electric operator, badge the card reader/keypad to confirm it works, close and secure any gate found open or propped, and check gate hardware, warning signage and tailgating detection.

Observe-and-report sweep of airport property for access-control compliance: patrol apron edges, hangar and tenant leaseholds, cargo areas and secure non-public corridors and doors, looking for propped doors, unsecured gates, vehicles without airport identification, and people in restricted areas; anomalies are reported to the operations/security center.

Responding to a deficiency found during inspection: intercept and challenge an unauthorized person or vehicle inside the AOA, check credentials/badges, escort the person out or hold them for police, and temporarily secure a fence breach or failed gate with cones, barricade or chain while standing by for maintenance; document the incident.

Military airfield perimeter and entry-control patrol at an air base: cover the installation boundary including remote, unimproved and off-road stretches in all weather, verify restricted-area boundaries and remote gates, and report intrusions, fence anomalies and unauthorized approaches to the base defense operations center.

Small GA/reliever airport or an active airfield construction project: walk or drive an unimproved boundary through tall grass, mud and drainage ditches, past temporary construction fencing, haul-road gates and laydown yards whose layout changes week to week, checking for gaps, unauthorized access points and vehicles entering the AOA.

tasks.label: Assist in responding to aircraft and medical emergencies.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Alert II/III aircraft emergency (gear problem, smoke, hard landing): specialist drives an airfield ops vehicle across the active movement area under ATC clearance, leads/escorts ARFF apparatus and mutual-aid units to the scene, positions the vehicle, establishes and controls the incident perimeter, keeps other traffic and personnel clear, relays scene status by radio.

Medical emergency in the terminal, at a gate, or aboard an aircraft: respond on foot or by vehicle, meet and escort EMS crews through security and airside, clear a path and stage equipment, help move the patient/stretcher, render basic first aid or AED use until EMS assumes care.

Emergency worked from the airfield operations/communications center: receive the tower alert, activate the crash phone and mass-notification system, dispatch and coordinate ARFF, police, EMS, mutual aid and the airline, brief responders, and log/document the event timeline.

Post-incident airfield restoration: inspect the runway/taxiway, close it and mark the closure (lighted X, barricades, cones), locate, collect and document debris/FOD and fluid spills, coordinate disabled-aircraft recovery and reopening, pass NOTAM information.

Scheduled emergency exercise (triennial full-scale drill or tabletop): set up the scenario site and props, play the assigned role, move and account for simulated casualties, staff the triage area or mobile command post, and participate in the after-action review.

Off-pavement or off-airport response: aircraft down in the grass infield, in mud or deep snow, or just beyond the fence; unimproved terrain, no prepared surface, mutual-aid units unfamiliar with the site, access gates to be opened and guides provided.

tasks.label: Manage wildlife on and around airport grounds.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine bird-dispersal sweeps of grass infields, loafing areas and drainage margins inside the airfield fence between aircraft movements: detect gulls/starlings/pigeons settling, haze them with bio-acoustic distress calls or other non-lethal deterrents, and log species, numbers and location in the wildlife log.

Full airfield wildlife patrol as part of a Part 139 airfield inspection: drive runways, taxiways and safety areas under ATC clearance, scan for mixed species and mammals, judge which are hazardous, apply graduated hazing (vehicle presence, horn, distress-call unit, pyrotechnics/screamers), radio the tower, and record observations.

Urgent response to wildlife on or near an active runway (goose or gull flock at the threshold, deer/moose/coyote through the fence) reported by ATC or a pilot: reach the spot within minutes, clear the animals, confirm the surface is clear, and report back to the tower before the next arrival or departure.

Habitat and attractant management on airport grounds: walk/drive the perimeter fence checking for breaches and animal diggings, look for standing water, carrion, food waste and nests in signs, lights, hangars and jet bridges, remove nests and attractants, plug fence gaps, and verify grass height and vegetation against the wildlife hazard management plan.

Handling of strike remains and carcasses: locate a struck bird or dead animal on pavement or in the grass, remove and bag it, collect a feather/snarge sample for identification, dispose of the carcass, and complete the FAA wildlife strike report and internal log.

Direct control of individual persistent hazardous animals under USDA/USFWS permit: set and check live traps for raptors and relocate them, herd or remove deer, coyotes or foxes from the airfield, and carry out permitted lethal depredation with a firearm, then handle and document the animal.

instances.label: Routine scheduled airfield self-inspection drive (FAA Part 139 self-inspection or USAF airfield check): specialist drives the operations vehicle over runways, taxiways, aprons and safety areas under tower clearance, visually checks pavement condition, markings, signs, lighting, NAVAID critical areas and obstructions, picks up any FOD found, judges what constitutes a discrepancy, logs findings and initiates NOTAMs/work orders. Active commercial or military airfield with live aircraft traffic and radio coordination.

Perimeter and fence-line surveillance patrol drive on the airside service road: check fence and gate integrity, look for breaches, unauthorized persons/vehicles, wildlife incursion and general anomalies along the boundary; alert on-duty staff to anything abnormal. Fixed, mapped patrol route inside the airport restricted area.

Scheduled FOD sweep/removal on apron, flightline, hangar ramp and taxiway shoulders: cover the designated area systematically with a sweeper or mat, collect bolts, rubber, wire, gravel and litter, dispose of the debris, and record the sweep. Institution-controlled paved area, aircraft and GSE present.

Rapid response to a reported hazard on the movement area (pilot or tower reports debris, blown tire fragments, a fuel/hydraulic spill, a bird carcass, a disabled aircraft or pavement failure): drive out under ATC clearance, assess, remove or contain the hazard, decide whether the surface must be closed, and pass the result back to the tower and dispatch. Time-critical, between aircraft movements.

Wildlife hazard patrol and dispersal: drive the airfield locating flocks, gulls, raptors, coyotes or deer; disperse with vehicle presence, pyrotechnics, distress calls or handheld laser; remove carcasses from the runway; complete strike/wildlife log entries and coordinate habitat follow-up. Airfield movement area and infield grass.

Escort and airfield control work: escort contractor and non-badged vehicles across the movement area, mark and monitor construction limits, place and retrieve barricades, lighted markers and runway closure 'X' markers, and conduct night/low-visibility lighting and marker checks. Airfield with active works, mixed vehicle and aircraft traffic.

roles.title: Flight Attendants
roles.description: Monitor safety of the aircraft cabin. Provide services to airline passengers, explain safety information, serve food and beverages, and respond to emergency incidents.

tasks.label: Verify that first aid kits and other emergency equipment, including fire extinguishers and oxygen bottles, are in working order.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Narrowbody (737/A320) preflight safety-equipment check at the gate before boarding: the attendant walks to assigned stations, opens overhead bins/closets and jumpseat stowages, confirms the halon/BCF extinguisher is in its bracket with pin and seal intact and gauge in the green, checks the portable oxygen bottle gauge and attached mask, confirms the first aid kit is present, sealed and in date, checks PBE pouch seals and flashlight indicator, then signs the cabin check sheet within a ~15-30 minute turn.

Widebody long-haul preflight check with a much larger inventory: several extinguishers and portable oxygen bottles at multiple doors and galleys, AED and sealed emergency medical kit (seal number and expiry), crash axe, multiple PBEs, megaphone function, plus door/slide pressure gauges and emergency lighting checks, performed while caterers and cleaners work through the cabin.

Regional jet or quick-turn narrowbody check under time pressure with boarding already underway or gate agents and passengers moving through the aisle; reduced equipment set checked fast, and when a discrepancy appears (broken seal, low extinguisher gauge, missing or out-of-date kit) the attendant notifies the captain, writes it in the cabin logbook and coordinates a replacement item before door close.

First-flight-of-day or post-overnight full equipment audit on an empty parked aircraft: complete inventory count against the aircraft's equipment list, expiry-date audit of first aid kits, medical kits and fire extinguisher hydro dates, life-vest presence spot checks under seats, restocking and replacement of expired items, with more time and an empty, well-lit cabin.

In-flight or immediately post-use verification: after a medical event or a smoke/fire event, confirm remaining pressure in the used oxygen bottle, check what was consumed from the first aid kit, verify the discharged extinguisher is tagged out and a spare is available, restow everything securely, and log the defect so the item is replaced before the next leg.

sources.system: Spot (with Scout / automated visual inspection and gauge-reading models)
sources.title: Automated Visual Inspection | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot performs automated visual inspection rounds in industrial facilities, autonomously reading analog gauges and raising alerts when readings fall outside the desired range — the same judgment as confirming an extinguisher or oxygen bottle gauge is in the green band.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine industrial asset inspection. Transfers to reading a pressure gauge on a fire extinguisher or oxygen bottle (same analog dial, same in-range/out-of-range decision), but only in open plant walkways, not inside an aircraft cabin stowage.

tasks.label: Announce and demonstrate safety and emergency procedures, such as the use of oxygen masks, seat belts, and life jackets.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Narrowbody domestic flight without cabin video screens: during taxi, one attendant reads the PA script while others stand in the aisle holding up a demo seat belt, oxygen mask, and life vest/flotation cushion, pointing out exits and floor path lighting.

Widebody or newer narrowbody with in-flight entertainment: the pre-recorded safety video is played over screens; attendants stand at their stations, monitor passenger attention, and point out nearest exits, adding PA supplements as needed.

Boarding and pre-departure PA announcements conveying safety information without props: seat belt sign, electronic device rules, carry-on stowage, exit locations, no-smoking rules, and reminders to review the safety card.

Individual verbal briefings at the seat: exit-row passengers confirming willingness and ability to assist, passengers with disabilities, unaccompanied minors, and infants in arms — explaining oxygen mask, seat belt, and life vest use for their situation.

In-flight or non-normal situation announcements: turbulence and seat-belt commands, oxygen mask reminders after a decompression, brace and evacuation commands, and cabin-preparation instructions before an anticipated emergency landing or ditching.

tasks.label: Monitor passenger behavior to identify threats to the safety of the crew and other passengers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Walk aisles of planes to verify that passengers have complied with federal regulations prior to takeoffs and landings.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Narrow-body domestic jet (A320/737), full 150-180 seat cabin, pre-departure compliance walk after boarding: attendant moves down a ~17-inch aisle amid passengers still settling, visually and by hand verifies each seat belt is fastened, seat backs upright, tray tables and footrests stowed, carry-ons fully under the seat in front or in bins, presses overhead bins closed and re-stows bags blocking latches, tells passengers to stow large electronics and bags, then reports 'cabin secure' within a few minutes.

Same narrow-body aircraft, descent/landing preparation: cabin lights dimmed, some passengers asleep under blankets or coats (belt confirmed visually or by touch through the blanket), attendant simultaneously collects cups and trash, raises seat backs and tray tables, checks bins and closets while the aircraft is in motion and occasionally in light turbulence, then secures the galley and takes a jumpseat.

Wide-body international aircraft (777/787/A350), twin aisles and multiple cabin classes: lie-flat/business seats returned to upright takeoff/landing position with footrests and ottomans stowed, bassinets removed, IFE screens and privacy dividers stowed, bulkhead and exit-row areas cleared; attendants sweep assigned zones amid many sleeping long-haul passengers.

Regional jet or turboprop (CRJ/ERJ/Dash-8) with a single attendant: very narrow low-ceiling aisle, small overhead bins that will not take roll-aboards, gate-checked bag handling, the attendant performs the entire compliance sweep alone while also closing the door and doing the manual safety demo.

Compliance checks complicated by passengers needing individual handling: lap children and infant seats/CARES harnesses checked, child restraint installation verified, exit-row occupants re-briefed and confirmed willing and able, passengers with disabilities or wheelchairs, service animals stowed on the floor, and passengers who refuse to comply (phone use, seat back down, bag in the aisle) requiring persuasion and escalation to the purser or captain.

It shows aisle navigation is feasible only in a cleared, passenger-free cabin; the system has no manipulator and stops when people are present, so it cannot perform a compliance sweep of seated passengers.

tasks.label: Direct and assist passengers in emergency procedures, such as evacuating a plane following an emergency landing.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In-flight abnormal event short of evacuation (severe turbulence, rapid decompression, sudden diversion, rejected takeoff): the flight attendant shouts commands over the noise, orders passengers into seats with belts fastened, helps children/elderly/passengers with disabilities don oxygen masks, moves down a narrow crowded aisle in a moving aircraft, secures loose carts and galley items, and calms and redirects frightened passengers until the situation is stable.

Preparing cabin and passengers for an anticipated emergency or precautionary landing (typically 5-30 minutes of warning): demonstrating and drilling brace positions row by row, selecting and briefing able-bodied passengers to help at exits, checking every seat belt, collecting sharp objects and glasses, reseating passengers away from exits, stowing carts and bags, then giving brace commands on impact and calm deplaning instructions.

In-flight fire, smoke/fumes, or security incident in an occupied cabin: moving passengers away from the affected rows into other seats or the aisle ends, directing them to stay low or use wet cloths, retrieving and operating an extinguisher/PBE, restraining or isolating a violent passenger with help from passengers, and keeping the rest of the cabin seated and informed.

Ground evacuation at an airport (engine fire, rejected takeoff, smoke on taxiway or at the gate): assessing outside conditions through the window, operating the exit handle and deploying the slide (heavy door, high force, in seconds), standing at the exit shouting repeated commands, physically pushing/pulling passengers who hesitate or carry bags, jumping seat rows or blocking a blocked exit, and assisting mobility-impaired passengers and infants down the slide, often in smoke or darkness.

Evacuation after an off-airport forced landing or ditching: deformed or partially blocked cabin, injured or unconscious passengers, water or rough terrain outside, life vests and rafts to deploy and inflate, passengers to lift or drag through a distorted exit, then head counts and group control away from the aircraft.

sources.transferJustification: Same occupation and environment (aircraft cabin in flight); shows the state of in-cabin robotics for safety duties, which bounds capability on emergency direction and assistance.

tasks.label: Prepare passengers and aircraft for landing, following procedures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Narrowbody domestic flight, full cabin (~150 pax): after the descent PA, the attendant walks the aisle with a trash bag, takes cups/napkins/bottles handed over by seated passengers, verifies and corrects seat backs upright, tray tables stowed and latched, seatbelts fastened (often hidden under blankets or coats), laptops/large items stowed under seats, presses closed and latches overhead bins that passengers reopened, all within roughly 10 minutes while the aircraft is descending and moving.

Galley and service-equipment securing before landing: push service carts into their galley bays, set brakes and engage the cart latches, secure coffee pots, hot jugs, trash inserts and loose service items into stowage compartments, latch every compartment and oven door, confirm lavatories vacant with doors secured, then confirm the cabin/galley secure to the lead attendant.

Widebody international flight, dimmed cabin with sleeping passengers: wake passengers, collect headsets, blankets, glassware and duty-free items, return lie-flat/premium seats to the upright landing position and stow footrests, screens and IFE handsets, raise window shades, check bassinets removed, across two aisles and ~250-350 passengers before a long descent.

Non-routine pre-landing preparation: a passenger still in the lavatory during descent, unaccompanied minors and passengers needing assistance (seatbelt extenders, mobility aid stowed in the cabin closet, infant lap holding), a non-compliant or intoxicated passenger who refuses to raise a seat back or stow a bag and must be persuaded or escalated to the captain, plus required PA announcements.

Regional jet or short-haul narrowbody with one or two attendants and a shortened, turbulence-compressed prep: a single fast pass through a 50-76 seat cabin collecting trash and checking compliance, handling gate-checked bag tags and oversized carry-ons, securing a tiny galley, then strapping into the jumpseat before the seatbelt-sign deadline.
