Latching a galley compartment or oven door and placing loose items into a fixed stowage position is the same class of positioned insertion and door/latch actuation at millimetre precision, once the equipment is presented in known positions.

tasks.label: Administer first aid to passengers in distress.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Minor injury or complaint in flight: passenger cuts a finger on a can, bumps their head on a bin, or has a headache. Attendant assesses, dons gloves, cleans and dresses the wound from the onboard first aid kit, supplies an ice pack or over-the-counter analgesic per company protocol, and logs the event.

Faintness, dizziness, hypoglycemia or hyperventilation: passenger goes pale and clammy or slumps in a seat or lavatory. Attendant helps them to the floor or a galley/exit-row area, elevates legs, loosens clothing, offers juice or water, checks responsiveness and pulse, monitors until recovery, and reports to the flight deck.

Nausea, airsickness, anxiety attack, or ear/sinus pain in a seated passenger in a full cabin: comfort care with sick bag, cool damp cloth, hydration, reassurance, repositioning and cleanup, with periodic re-checks during the flight.

Respiratory distress or allergic reaction: attendant retrieves and opens the portable oxygen bottle, fits the mask to the passenger's face and confirms flow, assists the passenger with their own inhaler or epinephrine auto-injector, relays vitals to ground medical advice, and monitors, sometimes in turbulence or dim cabin lighting.

Choking, seizure, or heavy bleeding: abdominal thrusts or back blows on a standing or seated passenger in a 17-inch aisle; or protecting a seizing passenger's head and clearing hazards; or applying gloved direct pressure and dressings to a bleeding wound while managing bystanders.

Unresponsive passenger / cardiac arrest: move the passenger from the seat to the aisle or galley floor, check breathing and pulse, start chest compressions and rescue breaths, bare the chest, apply AED pads and deliver shocks per prompts, continue CPR in rotation until landing and handover to EMS.

sources.system: Automated handheld venipuncture robot (Rutgers / VascuLogic)
sources.title: New Robot Does Superior Job Sampling Blood | Rutgers University
sources.claim: An autonomous venipuncture robot performed blood draws on human volunteers in a clinical trial with the arm positioned in a purpose-built device; this is the closest demonstrated case of a robot autonomously performing a needle procedure on a person, and it is limited to a single fixtured limb in a clinic.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated venipuncture. It shows autonomous robot contact with a cooperative human body part, but only with the arm immobilized in a purpose-built station; it involves no distress assessment, no travel to the patient, and no manipulation of an uncooperative or collapsed person, which the first-aid instances require.

sources.system: Lifeline Robotics automatic throat swab robot (UR5-based)
sources.title: Throat swabbing robot developed for COVID-19 testing by Danish startup
sources.claim: A fully automatic throat-swab robot autonomously inserted a swab into the mouth and throat of a seated cooperative person in a purpose-built swabbing station, demonstrating autonomous contact near the human face inside a machine-centred cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: oropharyngeal swabbing. It is the best evidence for autonomous robot contact with a human head or face in a purpose-built station, but it requires a cooperative, seated, correctly positioned subject and performs one contact motion, not assessment, kit retrieval, oxygen delivery or wound care.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: physical nursing assistance (patient transfer). It bears directly on moving and handling a person in distress; the system's reliance on teleoperation for the patient-contact portions shows the capability is not autonomously available.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: wound dressing. It is the nearest analogue to the bandaging instance; its status as an early-stage, teleoperation-trained sub-step study indicates no system can complete wound care on a person at worker quality.

tasks.label: Check to ensure that food, beverages, blankets, reading material, emergency equipment, and other supplies are aboard and are in adequate supply.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pre-flight safety/emergency equipment check aboard a narrowbody at the gate: crew member walks the assigned zone, opens latched stowages and overhead compartments, verifies fire extinguisher gauge in the green and seal intact, oxygen bottle pressure and seal, PBE seals, first-aid/medical kit seals and expiry dates, AED, megaphone, flashlight seated and charged, life vests under seats, door slide pressure gauge, emergency lighting and PA test — all against a printed/electronic checklist before boarding.

Galley catering and beverage load verification at the aircraft during catering/boarding: crew check that the correct number of sealed meal carts, beverage carts, ice, coffee, liquor drawers and standard units are in the assigned galley positions, break/verify seals, count meal trays and special meals against the catering manifest and passenger load, and sign off or raise a shortage with the caterer before doors close.

Cabin comfort-supply check: verifying blankets, pillows, headsets and amenity kits are stowed in the assigned overhead bins/closets in the required quantity, that every seat pocket holds a safety card and the required reading material, and that lavatories carry paper towels, soap and other consumables — restocking small shortfalls from onboard reserves.

Quick-turn / continuing-flight adequacy check: after a leg, the crew count what remains in carts, drawers and stowages (soft drinks, snacks, cups, catering leftovers, lavatory and cabin supplies), judge whether the remaining stock covers the next sector's passenger load, and order a top-up or uplift from the caterer/ground staff during the turnaround.

sources.system: Spot (Boston Dynamics)
sources.title: Autonomous Detection of Combustible Gas | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot performs fully autonomous inspection rounds in a 40-acre midstream gas plant, including reading analog gauges and detecting anomalies — routine equipment-status verification in a large, institution-controlled industrial facility, but in open plant walkways, not inside closed compartments or aircraft aisles.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine inspection rounds verifying equipment condition via gauges. It shows autonomous gauge reading and checklist-style rounds in a structured facility, but does not cover opening latched stowages, verifying seals/expiry dates, or navigating a ~19-inch aircraft aisle, so it does not carry over to the cabin safety-equipment sweep.

instances.label: Routine boarding of a narrow-body domestic flight: flight attendant stands at the L1 door/entry area, greets each passenger, glances at boarding passes, points passengers aft to seats and toward open bin space, keeps the queue moving through a 20-inch aisle, answers questions, hangs coats, and watches arriving passengers for intoxication, illness, or oversized items.

Carry-on stowage assistance during boarding: lifting and turning roller bags wheels-first into overhead bins, repositioning other passengers' bags to make space, helping short/elderly passengers hoist bags, checking that bins latch closed, and tagging/handing off oversize bags for gate-check at the door.

Special-assistance passengers: pre-boarding a wheelchair user brought to the door by a wheelchair agent, assisting the aisle-chair transfer into the seat, stowing the mobility device or assistive equipment, seating unaccompanied minors, helping parents with infants/car seats/strollers, and reversing all of this as the last passengers off after arrival.

Deplaning at the gate: disarming and opening the door to the jet bridge, standing at the door to say farewell and direct passengers, retrieving bags from overhead bins for passengers who ask, keeping the aisle flow orderly, and doing a quick sweep for left-behind items and passengers needing help over the door sill.

Irregular boarding/deplaning conditions: remote hardstand with airstairs in rain, wind or cold; regional-jet valet/gate-checked bag return at the aircraft door; oversold flight with full bins requiring bag reshuffling and gate-checks mid-boarding; uncooperative, rushed or intoxicated passengers at the doorway during a delay.

sources.system: Volodya (humanoid robot cabin assistant, Pobeda Airlines / Aeroflot)
sources.developer: Pobeda Airlines (Aeroflot) with a Unitree-class humanoid platform
sources.title: Russia airline completes live test of 'flight attendant robot'
sources.claim: The only known trial of a humanoid robot working the cabin during boarding (Pobeda Airlines' 'Volodya', a Unitree-class humanoid, on a Ulyanovsk–Moscow flight) had the robot greet passengers and perform scripted/pre-programmed motions under continuous human crew monitoring; the tasks were described as basic with no plan to replace crew.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on-task (greeting passengers during boarding in an aircraft cabin), but scripted and crew-monitored, so under the autonomy rule it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.system: José (IntBot humanoid service robot)
sources.title: San Jose airport introduces AI powered humanoid robot for passenger support
sources.claim: A humanoid greeter robot ('José', IntBot) is deployed in a four-month pilot at San José Mineta International Airport Terminal B, stationed at a fixed spot to greet travellers, answer questions and give directions; it does not handle bags or physically assist passengers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: greeting and directing passengers in an airport terminal (E2). Transfer to the boarding-door instance fails: the robot is stationary in an open concourse, does not verify boarding passes, handle carry-on bags, manage a crowded aisle, or perform door-side safety monitoring.

sources.system: WHILL Autonomous Model / autonomous wheelchair service
sources.developer: WHILL, Inc. (with Envoy Air / American Airlines, Unifi)
sources.title: Unifi Launches WHILL Autonomous Wheelchair Service at Detroit Metro Airport
sources.claim: Autonomous WHILL power chairs are in commercial airport service (American Airlines terminals at LAX/MIA, Unifi at Detroit) carrying mobility-impaired passengers through the terminal to the gate, where passengers transfer out of the chair before boarding — the automation stops short of the aircraft door and the in-cabin aisle-chair transfer.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: moving a mobility-impaired passenger through a structured airport facility. It substantiates autonomous terminal transport only; the cited deployment explicitly ends before boarding, so it does not substantiate the flight attendant's door/aisle-chair/seating assistance.

sources.system: Unitree G1 humanoids in JAL Ground Service trial
sources.developer: GMO AI & Robotics with JAL Ground Service
sources.title: Japan Airlines begins humanoid robot trials at Tokyo's Haneda airport as labor shortages bite
sources.claim: Japan Airlines and GMO AI & Robotics began a multi-year trial in May 2026 using ~130 cm Unitree G1 humanoids for airport ground handling (baggage/cargo movement, later cabin cleaning) at Haneda; early phases involve pushing carts and containers with human supervisors retaining safety control.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: humanoid handling of baggage/cargo in an airline facility. It is a supervised trial in baggage/ramp areas with coarse pushing tasks, not manipulation of passengers' carry-ons in an occupied cabin, so it does not transfer to stowage or passenger assistance.

sources.system: Automated (self-boarding) gates at DFW
sources.title: Automated Gates Debut at American Airlines' DFW Hub as Carrier Pursues Digital Transformation
sources.claim: American Airlines is testing automated boarding gates at DFW where passengers self-scan boarding passes and the gate opens jet-bridge access without a gate agent — automating the gate-podium admission step in the terminal, upstream of the flight attendant's work at the aircraft door.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: verifying and admitting passengers at the boarding gate (a gate agent function). It shows machine-controlled turnstile gating in a terminal but performs none of the flight attendant's door greeting, seat direction, bag handling, or cabin-flow duties.

sources.system: Stretch (mobile case-handling robot)
sources.title: Boston Dynamics' Stretch Lab Pairs Warehouse Environments with Robotic Testing
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Stretch is commercially deployed unloading cases up to 50 lb from trailers and containers in warehouse/logistics settings, adapting its motion to different container geometries — the closest deployed capability to lifting luggage-weight items in a confined space.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: picking and placing heavy, luggage-sized objects. Transfer to overhead-bin stowage fails: Stretch uses a suction array on flat box faces at floor-to-shoulder height in an unoccupied trailer, and has not been shown grasping soft-sided/irregular suitcases, lifting them overhead into a shallow bin, latching the bin, or working among standing passengers.

tasks.label: Conduct periodic trips through the cabin to ensure passenger comfort and to distribute reading material, headphones, pillows, playing cards, and blankets.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Mainline narrow-body domestic flight (737/A320) or regional jet at cruise: attendant walks the 18–20 inch aisle every 20–30 minutes, scans rows for passenger needs, answers call lights, and hands out blankets, headsets, magazines/safety-card replacements and small comfort items to passengers in aisle, middle and window seats, often reaching across two seated people.

Long-haul wide-body flight: bulk distribution of pillows, blankets, headsets, amenity kits and reading material — placed at each seat before boarding or handed row by row after departure — plus restocking runs from galley carts and overhead-bin stowage during the flight.

Night/low-light cabin check on an overnight or long-haul flight: dim cabin, most passengers asleep under blankets; attendant walks quietly through, checks that passengers are comfortable and belts are fastened over blankets, covers sleeping children, notes anyone unwell, and quietly supplies extra blankets/pillows/water on request.

Premium (business/first) cabin comfort service: personalized rounds offering and delivering blankets, mattress pads, duvets, pillows, slippers, magazines and newspapers, hanging and retrieving coats, making up flat-bed seats, and responding to individually varied comfort requests by name.

Congested or turbulent-cabin pass: aisle partly blocked by standing passengers, carry-ons, beverage cart or a passenger's legs; light chop or a pitched cabin; attendant squeezes through, steps over obstacles, hands items over rows, and keeps items secured while moving.

sources.system: Servi / Servi Plus (Bear Robotics)
sources.title: Bear Robotics Brings Physical AI, Service Robots and Autonomous Cleaning to Restaurants and Hotels
sources.claim: Bear Robotics' Servi family are commercially deployed autonomous mobile service robots that run food and drinks to seated guests at tables in restaurants, hotels and airport lounges, with guests taking items off the robot's trays.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: running food/drinks to seated guests along aisles between tables. Comparable to a cabin pass in that light items are carried to people seated at fixed, known positions in a controlled venue and handed off for the recipient to take; no fine manipulation is required.

sources.system: Rookie
sources.title: Robotics | NAVER Corp.
sources.claim: About 100 Rookie robots autonomously deliver packages, coffee and meals to thousands of workers at their desks throughout Naver's 1784 headquarters, a building purpose-built around the robots (robot-only elevator, even flooring, cloud control).
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine delivery of small items to seated people in a facility engineered around the machine. Shows that in a purpose-built setting a fleet can repeatedly bring requested comfort items to people at fixed seats and hand them over reliably.

sources.system: Relay
sources.title: Relay Delivery Robots – Leader in delivery robots for hospitals and hotels
sources.claim: Relay autonomous delivery robots are commercially deployed in hotels, navigating corridors and elevators on their own to bring amenities (towels, toiletries, snacks) and room-service items to guests, who take the item from the robot's compartment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: distributing comfort amenities (blankets/towels/toiletries) to guests inside an institution-controlled facility. Same object class and handover mode as distributing blankets, headsets and reading material, though to a room door rather than an aircraft seat.

sources.system: Moxi
sources.title: Deploying physical AI to aid clinicians using AWS with Diligent Robotics
sources.claim: Diligent Robotics' Moxi mobile manipulator operates autonomously in 25 US hospitals, completing more than 1.3 million deliveries of supplies, medications and lab samples through corridors shared with staff and patients.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous mobile delivery with a manipulator inside a busy human facility. Establishes reliable at-scale item delivery to people in structured settings, but the deliveries are to staff stations/rooms, not to individuals seated in a narrow aisle.

sources.system: Volodya (Unitree G1-type humanoid)
sources.title: Russia's Pobeda Airlines trials humanoid robot flight attendant
sources.claim: The only publicized in-cabin humanoid trial on a commercial flight (Pobeda's 'Volodya', a Unitree G1-class robot, Ulyanovsk–Moscow, Nov 2025) performed scripted greeting and safety-briefing movements; human flight attendants performed every service and safety task, and the robot did not distribute items or serve passengers.

sources.system: Servi Q
sources.title: Bear Robotics Introduces Servi Q
sources.claim: Bear Robotics markets Servi Q, a compact service robot engineered for narrow-path navigation through cramped corridors and between-table gaps that larger service robots cannot enter, indicating the narrow-aisle envelope reached by current commercial serving robots.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: delivering items along constricted service paths in hospitality venues; relevant to whether a wheeled server could traverse an aisle-like path, though aircraft aisles (18–20 in, obstructed by feet and carts, on a moving airframe) remain outside demonstrated operation.

tasks.label: Inspect and clean cabins, checking for any problems and making sure that cabins are in order.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pre-departure cabin and safety check on a narrow-body turnaround: attendant walks the assigned zone before boarding, verifies emergency equipment (extinguisher, O2 bottle, PBE, first-aid kit) is present, sealed, in date and undamaged, confirms safety cards and life vests are in place, checks seats/belts/exits are unobstructed and nothing was left in seat pockets or bins, and reports discrepancies to the purser/captain.

Quick-turn tidy between flights (20-30 min at the gate, no cleaning crew scheduled): crew pull trash from seat pockets and floor, wipe visible spills off tray tables and armrests, close tray tables, cross seatbelts, straighten headrest covers and literature, check overhead bins are empty and latched, and confirm lavatories are stocked with paper and soap.

In-flight cabin check with passengers aboard: periodic walkthrough collecting trash into a bag or cart, tidying and wiping lavatory counters and sinks, restocking towels and paper, picking items off the floor and aisle, and noting problems such as an inoperative reading light, torn seat cover, or blocked exit path.

Post-flight / end-of-day walkthrough after deplaning: sweep the cabin for left-behind items and lost property, remove remaining trash, check bins and lavatories, inspect for damage or missing equipment, secure galley carts and doors, and write up cabin defects in the cabin log for maintenance.

Unexpected mess in flight: passenger airsickness, a drink spilled over a seat and carpet, or a soiled/overflowing lavatory; the attendant contains the mess, uses the biohazard kit or towels and disinfectant, restores the seat area or lavatory to usable condition and reblocks or reseats the passenger.

sources.system: RAY (aero hygenx)
sources.developer: aero hygenx inc. with De Havilland Aircraft of Canada
sources.title: Ravn Alaska Commences Cabin Disinfection Procedures on Dash 8 Aircraft with Autonomous UVC Disinfecting Robot Manufactured by aero hygenx
sources.claim: The only robot in routine service inside airline cabins is an autonomous UV-C disinfection robot: Aero HygenX's RAY drives itself through the cabin between flights emitting UVC. It performs no manipulation - no trash removal, tidying, restocking, or inspection and reporting of cabin defects.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (cabin disinfection) in the identical environment; cited to establish what in-cabin robots actually do today - light emission only, no manipulation or inspection - so it cannot substantiate the inspect-and-clean instances.

sources.system: Unitree humanoid robots in the JAL / GMO AI & Robotics Haneda trial
sources.developer: Japan Airlines (JAL Ground Service) with GMO AI & Robotics, Unitree hardware
sources.title: Japan Airlines to trial humanoid robots for baggage handling at Tokyo Haneda Airport
sources.claim: Japan Airlines and GMO AI & Robotics began a Haneda ground-handling trial of Unitree humanoids in May 2026; the demonstrated work was pushing cargo onto conveyors, while aircraft cabin cleaning is listed as a capability the companies plan to add later.
sources.transferJustification: Same environment (aircraft cabin) and the adjacent task of cabin cleaning, but cabin work is stated as a future plan and autonomy is unestablished, so it supports no positive judgment.

sources.system: Reconfigurable aircraft-cabin cleaning robot with GA-based coverage path planning
sources.developer: Academic research team (published in PLOS One)
sources.title: Genetic algorithm-based coverage path planning for autonomous aircraft cabin cleaning by reconfigurable robot
sources.claim: Autonomous aircraft-cabin cleaning remains at the research stage: a 2026 paper develops coverage path planning for a reconfigurable floor-cleaning robot in cabins and identifies trash, personal belongings and reclined seats as unresolved obstacles; the work covers aisles and floor areas only.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on aircraft cabin cleaning, but limited to floor coverage planning at research maturity; it does not substantiate whole-instance completion of tidying, restocking or safety inspection.

sources.system: Downer/IISRI autonomous rollingstock cleaning robots (floor robot and 6-DOF surface-cleaning robot)
sources.developer: Downer Group with Deakin University IISRI
sources.title: Downer develops the world's first fully autonomous rollingstock cleaning robots
sources.claim: The closest analogue for cleaning a passenger-vehicle interior is Downer's pair of rollingstock cleaning robots, which autonomously scrub floors and steam-clean seats and windows of passenger trains in Downer's maintenance depots; it is a proof-of-concept working alongside cleaning staff, with cleaning duration and functionality still under development.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: cleaning rows of passenger seats inside a vehicle interior. Transfer fails because it covers only surface and floor cleaning in a depot at proof-of-concept maturity, with no seat-pocket trash removal, restocking, defect write-up, or safety-equipment verification, and no turnaround time guarantee.

sources.system: Zerith H1
sources.title: Watch A New Humanoid Robot Clean A Hotel Room Like It Owns The Place
sources.claim: Humanoid housekeeping robots exist for hotel guest rooms: Zerith H1 is reported to autonomously clean floors, scrub bathroom fixtures and restock amenities in a hotel room - a static room with full-size fixtures and no time-critical safety inspection.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (room turnover cleaning inside an institution-controlled facility). Transfer fails: the objects (seat pockets, belts, tray tables, sealed emergency equipment), the whole-aircraft 20-30 minute schedule, and the 30-inch-pitch aisle differ from a hotel bathroom, and no demonstration places this robot in an aircraft cabin.

sources.system: Somatic BCR (bathroom cleaning robot)
sources.title: Somatic - Autonomous Bathroom Cleaning Robots
sources.claim: Autonomous restroom-cleaning robots are commercially deployed in institution-controlled facilities including airports, cleaning fixtures and floors and picking up trash - but they are cart-sized machines built for full-size public restrooms, not aircraft lavatories.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (cleaning and restocking a restroom in a structured facility). The machine's size and dependence on mapped full-size restrooms mean it cannot enter or work in an aircraft lavatory, and it performs none of the cabin inspection work.

tasks.label: Operate audio and video systems.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Narrowbody commercial flight: cabin crew member picks up the interphone/PA handset and delivers routine announcements (boarding, welcome, seatbelt sign, service, descent, arrival) at the appropriate points in the flight, selecting the correct PA zone/priority on the handset keypad.

Widebody or narrowbody with pre-recorded content: crew cues the pre-recorded safety briefing video and boarding music from the cabin attendant panel, selects language/version, coordinates cabin lighting and volume, and confirms all monitors/screens deployed and playing before pushback.

In-flight entertainment management: crew enables/disables the IFE from the attendant panel, launches or stops programming for a movie or announcement override, and resets a frozen seatback screen or a whole zone of the system in response to passenger complaints.

Corporate/VIP jet (e.g., Gulfstream, Global) single flight attendant: operates the cabin management system via touchscreen or tablet to run satellite TV, movies, moving map, audio zones and window shades at principal passengers' request, and troubleshoots when content will not load.

Regional jet or older aircraft with minimal A/V: crew makes all announcements live over the PA because there is no video system, adjusting content for delays and gate information, and uses the megaphone or shouted commands if the PA is inoperative.

Irregular operations and emergencies: crew uses the PA/interphone for turbulence, diversion, medical-emergency 'is there a doctor onboard' calls, and evacuation commands, coordinating with the flight deck over the interphone under time pressure and noise.

tasks.label: Answer passengers' questions about flights, aircraft, weather, travel routes and services, arrival times, or schedules.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Collect money for meals and beverages.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Domestic narrowbody main cabin, buy-on-board beverage/snack service from a moving cart in a 17-inch aisle: passenger orders, attendant rings the item on a handheld POS tablet, passenger taps or inserts a card, attendant confirms the approval, hands over the item and a receipt/email, then moves to the next row, all while the cart blocks the aisle and other passengers wait.

On-demand single sale after the main service: a passenger uses the call button or flags the attendant, who takes the order, fetches the item from the galley, walks to the seat and processes a card payment at the seat, often reaching across seated passengers in a dim cabin.

Cash sale onboard (foreign carriers, charters and regional operators that still accept cash): attendant receives banknotes from the passenger, counts and returns change from a cash pouch, records the sale, and reconciles and bags the cash at the end of the flight.

Long-haul duty-free / multi-item cart sales: several items per transaction, catalogue lookup and pricing, card or cash (sometimes more than one currency), printed receipt, and stock/settlement records at the end of the sales run.

Payment exceptions and service judgment: card declines and offline authorization, a passenger disputing a charge, comping or discounting an item for service recovery, verifying a pre-purchased or complimentary entitlement, and walking an unfamiliar or elderly passenger through the cashless process.

sources.system: Briggo Coffee Haus robotic barista kiosk
sources.title: Briggo Lands its Robot Barista at the SFO Airport Next Month – The Spoon
sources.claim: Briggo's Coffee Haus is a fully ... robotic beverage kiosk deployed in airport terminals (Austin-Bergstrom, then SFO Terminal 3) where the customer buys the drink at the machine itself and the machine prepares and dispenses it.
sources.transferJustification: Same act as the rated task: taking a customer's payment for a beverage and handing over the drink. Transfer holds because the objects (card/phone tap, single beverage, receipt) and precision are the same; the difference is that the customer comes to the machine rather than the seller going to the seat.

sources.transferJustification: Same act (unattended sale of a beverage including payment capture) in a travel setting; shows the kiosk form is a current, scaled commercial deployment rather than a one-off demo.

sources.system: NCR FastLane SelfServ Checkout Release 6 (with note/coin recyclers)
sources.title: NCR Launches Next Generation Self-Checkout System with Flexible, Convertible Design
sources.claim: Commercial self-checkout units accept cash from the customer and return change automatically, recycling multiple note and coin denominations, and are sold as standard equipment for grocery and food retail lanes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is retail checkout for food and drink: the machine physically validates banknotes and coins, counts them, and dispenses correct change — the same money-handling the flight attendant performs, with equal or better error rates, for multi-item baskets of meals and beverages.

sources.system: ADAM robot barista/bartender
sources.title: Richtech Robotics' ADAM serves drinks at Kennedy Space Center - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Richtech's ADAM two-armed robot prepares and serves drinks to paying customers at fixed stations in commercial venues (a Las Vegas cafe with more than 16,000 drinks served, stadiums, casinos, hotels), with customers ordering at a self-order station.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is paid beverage service: the customer orders and pays at the station and the robot completes the sale by making and handing over the drink, showing the paid transaction closes end-to-end at a purpose-built station without a human seller.

tasks.label: Heat and serve prepared foods.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Long-haul or transcontinental economy hot meal service: flight attendant pulls foil-covered entrées from catering carts, racks them in the galley convection oven, times the heating cycle, unloads hot casseroles, dresses trays with cold items, loads the meal cart, then works the aisle offering a choice ('chicken or pasta'), handing hot trays over seated passengers in a moving cabin.

Short/medium-haul heated snack or buy-on-board hot item: individual paninis, breakfast sandwiches or pizzas heated to order in the galley oven during a short cruise window, wrapped/plated, and hand-delivered to a specific seat row along with payment handling.

Premium cabin (first/business) plated service: heat entrées and bread in the galley oven, plate on china with sides and garnish, deliver course by course to individually timed passengers, and re-heat or re-plate on request.

Special-order and crew meals: identify pre-labeled special meals (kosher, gluten-free, vegan, child/infant), follow their separate heating instructions and sealed-package rules, verify the label against the seat manifest, and deliver to the correct passenger before the general service.

Second/pre-arrival service under degraded conditions: heat and distribute a light hot item (warm breakfast, hot sandwich, warmed cookies) in a dimmed cabin with sleeping passengers, intermittent turbulence, and a tight window before descent.

sources.claim: Circus SE's CA-1 is a fully automated food production robot that dispenses ingredients, cooks and serves hot meals with about one hour of human input per day; it went live for end customers in REWE supermarkets in Germany in October 2025.

sources.claim: Yo-Kai Express autonomous hot-meal machines heat frozen prepared meals on demand in 45-90 seconds and dispense them to customers; roughly 50 units were installed across US airports, hotels, hospitals and universities, serving 200,000+ meals.

sources.claim: Miso Robotics' Flippy 2 robot arm works an entire fry station without a human in the ... in White Castle kitchens: vision identifies the prepared frozen food placed in its bin, cooks it in the correct basket and moves it to hot holding for serving.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: cooking portioned frozen prepared foods to serving temperature and transferring them to hot holding. Same heating step as galley oven work, with comparable objects (portioned prepared foods), comparable precision (basket loading/unloading, hot transfer) in a dedicated station where the work is presented to the machine.

sources.title: Breaking: Chef Robotics raises $43m Series A to scale AI-enabled robotics in meal assembly | AgFunderNews
sources.claim: Chef Robotics' robotic arms autonomously portion and assemble cooked foods into meal trays on production lines at food manufacturers such as Amy's Kitchen, Sunbasket and Cafe Spice, having assembled tens of millions of meals commercially.

sources.system: Servi / Servi Plus / Servi Q
sources.title: Bear Robotics Brings Physical AI, Service Robots and Autonomous Cleaning to Restaurants and Hotels
sources.claim: Bear Robotics' Servi robots autonomously run food to tables and bus dishes in restaurants, hotels and airport lounges, but they only transport trays that humans load and that guests unload; they do not heat food or plate and hand items to individuals.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: delivering prepared food through an occupied human facility. It is the closest demonstrated analogue to aisle meal distribution, and shows that deployed service robots transport only — they do not heat, plate, or hand meals to seated people — so the whole instance is not covered at E2.

sources.system: Humanoid robot flight attendant trial
sources.title: Russia's Pobeda Airlines trials humanoid robot flight attendant | Aerospace Global News
sources.claim: A humanoid robot trialled in the passenger cabin by Pobeda Airlines in November 2025 performed a limited, scripted role and did not handle food or beverages; robot deployments inside passenger cabins remain rare.

tasks.label: Inspect passenger tickets to verify information and to obtain destination information.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Assist passengers in placing carry-on luggage in overhead, garment, or under-seat storage.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Narrow-body economy boarding rush: flight attendant stands in the aisle/at a row and hoists passengers' 20–40 lb rollaboards from the floor or from a passenger's hands into the overhead bin, turning them wheels-in on their side, then latching bins — done in a 30-inch aisle with a queue of passengers pressing past, under jet-bridge departure time pressure.

Assisting a specific passenger who cannot lift the bag (elderly, short stature, injured, parent with infant, passenger with disability): taking the bag handed over, sometimes reaching over a seated passenger or across a row, hoisting it above shoulder height and settling it in the bin without striking anyone or damaging contents.

Consolidating a partially full bin during boarding: repositioning bags already stowed by other passengers, standing coats and laptop bags upright, judging whether one more bag fits, and deciding a bag must move to another bin or be gate-checked; done while owners watch and object.

Under-seat stowage: taking a purse, backpack, or personal item, placing and pushing it fully under the seat in front behind the restraint bar, and verifying compliance on the pre-departure cabin walk.

Premium cabin / garment closet: hanging passengers' garment bags, suit jackets and coats on the closet rail or hooks, and stowing bulky carry-on items in the forward closet or first-class bins, often while other passengers board past the galley area.

Non-standard or oversized items: folding strollers, car seats, musical instruments, mobility-aid components, duty-free boxes — securing them in a closet, a designated bin, or an empty seat area per airline and FAA stowage policy.

sources.system: Vanderlande BAGLOAD robotic loading
sources.title: Our vision for automating the handler processes at airports - Vanderlande
sources.claim: Vanderlande's BAGLOAD robotic loading systems perform fully automated loading of passenger bags from the baggage-handling system into airline containers in airport baggage halls.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: loading loose passenger luggage into a confined airline container. Same object class (soft/hard cases up to ~30 kg, variable shape), same act of lifting and placing into a box-like compartment with planned placement, which is the physical core of stowing a carry-on in an overhead bin when the bag is presented to the machine.

sources.system: Vanderlande/Grenzebach robotic baggage loading (Schiphol South baggage hall, Heathrow)
sources.title: Towards a fully automated baggage hall - Vanderlande
sources.claim: Robotic loading of bags into containers/carts has been in routine operation for years in the baggage halls of Amsterdam Schiphol and London Heathrow.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated loading of passenger bags into ULD containers and ramp carts. Demonstrates sustained worker-quality reliability and throughput for grasping and placing luggage into a constrained compartment, the same manipulation required to place a carry-on into a fixtured bin.

sources.system: Grenzebach automated baggage loading cell (robot with telescopic gripper)
sources.title: Automated Baggage Loading - Airport Technology
sources.claim: The automated baggage loading cell picks each bag from the conveyor and sets it down at a pre-calculated position inside the container or ramp cart, roughly one bag every 12–15 seconds, until the container is full.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: sequenced placement of luggage inside a container. Placement is planned against the current fill state and the bag is deposited in a chosen spot, which is what stowing a carry-on into an overhead bin requires once the bin and bag are presented as in a purpose-built cell.

sources.system: SICK sensor-equipped robotic baggage loading cell
sources.developer: SICK AG (with airport baggage loading robot integrators)
sources.title: Baggage Loading per Robot - Airport Technology
sources.claim: Sensor systems on the loading robot measure the contours of baggage weighing up to 30 kg and the current fill status of the container to plan each placement.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: perception-driven loading of heavy passenger bags. Confirms the cited loading cells handle the weight range of carry-on and checked bags a flight attendant lifts, supporting the heavy-lift instance when the bag is presented to the machine.

sources.system: Chongqing Jiangbei airport baggage-sorting robotic arms
sources.developer: Chongqing Jiangbei International Airport (with Chinese automation supplier)
sources.title: Intelligent 'helpers' deployed at international airport in SW China's Chongqing to enhance travel convenience - People's Daily Online
sources.claim: Two robotic arms at Chongqing Jiangbei International Airport autonomously grasp and load checked luggage into baggage carts at 180 pieces per hour, replacing manual sorting for four chute zones.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: vision-guided grasping of arbitrary passenger luggage and placement into a cart. Same object variability and careful-placement requirement as stowing a carry-on, in a fenced, purpose-built handling area.

sources.system: airport baggage robotics (industry overview incl. Chongqing arms, ramp-side robotic arm development)
sources.title: How Robotics Are Changing Airport Operations | Aviation Week
sources.claim: Trade coverage of airport robotics reports that robotic arms now load bags into carts at Chongqing, while deploying robotics inside aircraft for baggage loading remains technically challenging and undeployed.
sources.transferJustification: Directly bears on the in-cabin (E2) counterfactual: even robotic loading inside an empty aircraft hold is not yet fielded, so no cited system works inside an occupied passenger cabin.

sources.system: Volodya humanoid robot flight attendant
sources.title: Russia's Pobeda Airlines trials humanoid robot flight attendant
sources.claim: The only humanoid robot flown as cabin crew (Pobeda's 'Volodya') performed scripted movements and greetings while human flight attendants handled all service and safety tasks; it did not handle passenger luggage.
sources.transferJustification: Shows the state of in-cabin robotics: a scripted promotional presence, not autonomous manipulation of carry-on baggage, so it cannot support an E2 (aircraft cabin) judgment.

tasks.label: Take inventory of headsets, alcoholic beverages, and money collected.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: End-of-flight liquor/beverage count in the aircraft galley on a domestic mainline flight: flight attendant opens the beverage cart drawers and bar inserts, counts remaining miniature spirit bottles, beer and wine, tallies against the starting kit or POS sales record, records counts on the liquor inventory sheet/handheld, then re-locks or re-seals the cart. Done in a cramped galley during descent prep, sometimes with turbulence and passenger interruptions.

Onboard sales/money reconciliation: at the end of the flight the attendant totals card and cash sales on the POS handheld, counts the bills and coins collected for buy-on-board food, drinks or seat upgrades, reconciles the cash against the sales record, fills out the sales/remittance envelope and signs it for handoff to the purser or ground finance.

Pre-flight provisioning/inventory check at the gate: attendant verifies that catering and liquor cart seals are intact and match the numbers on the catering paperwork, counts meal/beverage kits, soda, water, coffee and snack stock in carts and galley stowage against the boarding manifest, and reports shortages or broken seals to catering before doors close under time pressure.

Headset, amenity and merchandise inventory: counting collected/returned headsets and remaining sealed headset stock, amenity kits, pillows/blankets and onboard retail merchandise stowed in galley compartments and overhead bins, and recording remaining quantities on a stock/restock report for the next leg.

International/premium-cabin bonded liquor and duty-free inventory: breaking the customs seal on a bonded cart, counting duty-free merchandise and bonded alcohol before and after sales, re-sealing the cart with numbered customs seals, and recording seal numbers and item counts on customs/inventory documentation for the arriving station.

sources.system: Tally (Simbe Robotics)
sources.title: Harmons Deploys Simbe's Tally Inventory Robot In Stores Following Pilot Success
sources.claim: Simbe's Tally is an autonomous shelf-scanning robot deployed commercially in US grocery chains, using computer vision and barcode scanning to count on-shelf stock and reconcile it with the retailer's inventory system.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: retail shelf inventory counting. It is the same act as the flight attendant's stock tally - machine identification and counting of packaged consumer goods (including bottles and boxed merchandise) with the counts written to an inventory record - but it works only on open, front-facing shelf stock, not items latched inside galley carts.

sources.system: Tally (Simbe Robotics)
sources.title: BJ's Gains Efficiency from Robotic Inventory Management
sources.claim: Tally robots have been rolled out chainwide at BJ's Wholesale Club (237 clubs), imaging shelves and pallets and reconciling counts with the inventory management system.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: retail inventory auditing at scale. Demonstrates reliable, worker-quality item counting of diverse packaged goods in a facility, transferring to counting beverages/merchandise when the goods are presented on shelving or trays.

sources.system: Sparrow
sources.title: Amazon introduces Sparrow—a state-of-the-art robot that handles millions of diverse products
sources.claim: Amazon's Sparrow is a robotic arm in fulfillment centers that autonomously detects, identifies and handles individual products from mixed totes using computer vision, covering a large share of Amazon's item catalogue.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: item-level singulation and identification in a fixtured picking cell. Counting a liquor kit or headset stock brought to a machine requires the same competence - recognising and enumerating small packaged items (bottles, boxed headsets) presented in totes/trays - at industrial reliability.

sources.system: Sparrow
sources.title: Amazon's Sparrow is leaving the nest: Trailblazing warehouse robot is ready for a wider rollout – GeekWire
sources.claim: Sparrow has been operating in Amazon fulfillment centers picking individual products out of mixed totes and placing them into trays, and was cleared for wider rollout.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: singulating mixed small goods in a purpose-built cell; establishes that the counting/handling of galley-sized items is done at production reliability when the work is fixtured and presented to the machine.

sources.system: Glory CASHINFINITY CI-500X / CI-100X cash recyclers
sources.title: GLORY Announces Next Generation Retail Cash Recycling Solutions
sources.claim: Glory's CI-500X back-office cash recycler automates counting, end-of-day cash processes and store reconciliation; Glory recyclers are installed at scale in retail (e.g., 285 units rolling out in Waitrose stores).
sources.transferJustification: Related task: end-of-shift cash count and till reconciliation in retail. The physical act is identical to a flight attendant's money count - notes and coin fed into a machine that validates, counts, stores and reconciles against POS sales records - and is a deployed, purpose-built machine.

sources.system: Glory CI-100X
sources.title: GLORY Confirmed as Global Leader in Retail Cash Recycling Solutions by RBR Data Services
sources.claim: Glory retail cash recyclers are being installed in large numbers across retail chains, confirming commercial deployment of automated cash counting and reconciliation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated cash handling/reconciliation deployed at scale; supports that the money-counting portion of the inventory task is completed by a machine when cash is presented to it.

sources.system: Verity inventory drones
sources.title: Verity inventory drones surpass 100 warehouse sites, including UPS
sources.claim: Verity's autonomous inventory drones perform cycle counting in warehouses at over 100 customer sites, flying set routes and reconciling scanned locations against the inventory system with high accuracy.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous stock counting in an institution-controlled facility. It shows machine inventory counting replacing human cycle counters, but only for labelled/tagged locations on open racking - it cannot open latched carts or handle cash.

sources.system: Cognex vision systems (tamper/safety seal inspection)
sources.title: Tamper-Proof and Safety Seal Inspection - Food and Beverage | Cognex
sources.claim: Cognex machine vision systems are commercially used on packaging lines to verify tamper-evident and safety seal integrity against programmed limits, rejecting non-compliant units.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated tamper-seal verification and code reading on a line. Checking that a catering or bonded-cart seal is intact and matches a recorded number is the same inspection act when the cart is presented to the machine.

sources.system: Unitechnik automated catering logistics system at LSG Sky Chefs
sources.title: LSG Sky Chefs: Europe's most modern catering operation
sources.claim: Airline catering operations already run automated logistics plants where returned trolleys are emptied, washed, machine-conveyed to loading stations and restocked with duty-free items, headphones, drinks and food - i.e. the galley carts are physically brought to a purpose-built machine environment.
sources.transferJustification: Context only, not decisive: shows that the E1 counterfactual can arise - carts, liquor kits and headset stock are routinely conveyed to an automated catering facility where contents could be presented to counting machines.

tasks.label: Sell alcoholic beverages to passengers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Domestic narrowbody main-cabin beverage cart service: two attendants work the 17-19 inch aisle with a rolling cart, take drink orders row by row, sell a beer, mini-bottle of wine or a spirit with mixer, visually check ID if the buyer looks young, pour over ice into a plastic cup, tap the passenger's card on a handheld POS reader, and hand the drink across one or two seated passengers, all with the aircraft in motion.

Individual mid-flight order: a passenger presses the call button or comes to the galley; the attendant prepares one alcoholic drink at the galley counter, runs the card on a handheld terminal, and either hands it over at the galley or carries it on a small tray down the aisle to the passenger's seat, stepping around standing passengers and carts.

Premium-cabin / paid-upgrade drink service: wine or a mixed cocktail poured into glassware, delivered to a seat with a napkin, refills offered, charged to the passenger's card or drink voucher; requires opening bottles, careful pouring, and placing the glass on the passenger's tray table or console.

Regional jet or single-attendant flight: sell canned beer or single-serve wine plus a cup from a small cart on a short segment, with a compressed service window, restricted galley space, card-only payment, and frequent interruption by turbulence and the seatbelt sign.

Responsible-service judgment: a passenger orders another round after several drinks (or has been drinking personal alcohol); the attendant assesses speech, coordination and behavior, decides to limit or refuse the sale, communicates the refusal, and coordinates with other crew about the passenger for the rest of the flight.

sources.system: Bionic Bar (Makr Shakr)
sources.title: Robot Bartenders at the Bionic Bar on Royal Caribbean - Cruise Critic
sources.claim: The Bionic Bar by Makr Shakr, deployed commercially on Royal Caribbean ships since 2014, uses two robotic arms to autonomously mix and dispense cocktails ordered by passengers on tablets — i.e., it completes an alcoholic-beverage sale to passengers inside a purpose-built robotic bar unit.
sources.transferJustification: Same task in a different setting: selling and serving alcoholic drinks to fare-paying passengers; objects (spirits, mixers, ice, cups) and measured-pour precision match in-flight drink service.

sources.system: Bionic Bar (Makr Shakr)
sources.title: Bionic Bar: Royal Caribbean's cruise ship robot bartenders | Royal Caribbean Blog
sources.claim: At the Bionic Bar the sale transaction itself is machine-handled: the guest swipes a SeaPass card at the tablet, the charge posts to the guest account or drink package, and alcohol is only served to guests of legal age, with entitlement tied to the card.
sources.transferJustification: Covers the payment and age-entitlement half of the same task (selling alcohol to passengers), executed by the machine rather than a human server.

sources.system: Bionic Bar (Makr Shakr)
sources.title: Get Cocktails Made by a Robot at the Bionic Bar - Cruise Spotlight
sources.claim: The Bionic Bar verifies the buyer's identity at pickup and physically presents the finished drink: the guest taps the SeaPass at the bar and the machine slides the correct cocktail to them.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (handing a purchased alcoholic drink to the verified buyer), showing machine-side identity check and hand-off in a fixtured bar unit.

sources.system: Toni (Makr Shakr)
sources.title: Robots in action at Changi Airport to curb theft, prepare cocktails and perform other duties - Focus on Travel News
sources.claim: Makr Shakr's 'Toni' dual-arm robotic bartender is permanently installed and operating in Lotte Duty Free stores at Singapore Changi Airport Terminals 2 and 3, serving cocktails to travelers from a self-contained robotic bar unit.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (mixing and serving purchased alcoholic drinks to air travelers), demonstrating the fixtured robotic-bar approach works in a travel setting with the customer coming to the machine.

sources.system: Volodya humanoid robot flight attendant
sources.title: Russia's Pobeda Airlines trials humanoid robot flight attendant
sources.claim: The only airline trial of a humanoid robot in the cabin (Pobeda's 'Volodya', Ulyanovsk–Moscow, Nov 2025) used scripted movements; human flight attendants performed all service work, including food and beverage sales, showing no robot completes in-aisle drink sales aboard aircraft.

roles.title: Ambulance Drivers and Attendants, Except Emergency Medical Technicians
aliases: CPR Ambulance Driver (Cardio Pulmonary Resuscitation Ambulance Driver)
EMS First Responder (Emergency Medical Services First Responder)
roles.description: Drive ambulance or assist ambulance driver in transporting sick, injured, or convalescent persons. Assist in lifting patients.

tasks.label: Place patients on stretchers, and load stretchers into ambulances, usually with assistance from other attendants.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine non-emergency transport pickup at a skilled nursing or assisted-living facility: two attendants roll a frail, partly cooperative resident with a draw sheet from the bed onto the wheeled cot, position pillows and blankets, fasten three to four body straps and side rails, wheel the loaded cot down corridors and through doors to the ambulance at the entrance, and load it into the patient compartment.

Hospital or dialysis-center interfacility transfer: patient moved from a hospital bed, gurney, or treatment chair onto the ambulance cot in a room or bay, with IV lines, oxygen tubing, drains, or a cardiac monitor to keep untangled; cot raised, patient secured, wheeled to the ambulance bay and loaded, then unloaded and transferred to a bed at the receiving facility.

Private residence pickup for non-emergency or convalescent transport: patient in a bedroom or recliner in a cluttered home with narrow hallways, doorways too tight for the cot, possibly steps or a porch; attendants lift or use a stair chair/slide sheet to move the patient, transfer onto the cot outside the room or at the door, secure them, negotiate thresholds and the driveway, and load into the ambulance.

Field or public-place response: patient lying on the ground, floor, sidewalk, or seated in a vehicle at a roadside, workplace, or public venue; attendants log-roll onto a scoop/backboard or lift with a sheet, place onto the cot, secure straps in variable weather, uneven ground, traffic and bystanders, and load into the ambulance.

Bariatric or high-acuity patient in a facility: 350-600 lb or unresponsive/contracted patient requiring three or more attendants or a lift assist, a bariatric cot, coordinated lifting and repositioning, careful spine and limb handling, then powered loading into a bariatric-capable ambulance.

sources.system: ALTA Platform
sources.title: Able Innovations Deploys Robotic Patient Delivery Platform in the U.S.
sources.claim: Able Innovations' ALTA Platform is a commercially deployed robotic device that automates lateral transfer of a supine patient between a bed, imaging table, or stretcher, but each transfer is set up and initiated by a staff member at the bedside; it does not autonomously locate, position, secure or transport patients, nor load a cot into a vehicle.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hospital lateral patient transfer bed-to-stretcher, the closest mechanized analogue of 'place patients on stretchers'. It shows the state of the art is an operator-driven power-assist device confined to flat, aligned surfaces, not autonomous patient handling.

sources.system: RIBA-II
sources.title: A Patient Transfer Apparatus Between Bed and Stretcher (RIBA-II discussion)
sources.claim: RIBA-II, the leading research robot able to lift an adult from the floor and place them on a wheelchair or stretcher, is explicitly not autonomous: a caregiver guides every motion via tactile sensors, and it never left the laboratory.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: lifting a human body from floor/bed onto a wheelchair or stretcher — the same physical act as placing a patient on a stretcher. The source establishes the act is performed only under continuous human control.

sources.system: ROBEAR
sources.title: The strong robot with the gentle touch | RIKEN
sources.claim: ROBEAR, the successor nursing-care robot able to lift a patient from a bed, remained an experimental prototype; as of its announcement no such lifting robots had been deployed in care facilities, and it was never commercialized.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: lifting a patient from a ... onto another surface. Even this best-known prototype was experimental and human-guided, indicating no cited system performs the transfer autonomously.

sources.system: Power-LOAD Cot Fastener System (model 6390)
sources.title: Power-LOAD | Stryker
sources.claim: The widely fielded EMS loading aid, Stryker's Power-LOAD cot fastener, is a powered fastener that lifts and lowers the cot ... while the crew rolls the cot up, engages it, and controls the cycle; it automates only the lift portion of loading and does nothing to place a patient on the cot.
sources.transferJustification: Directly relevant to the 'load stretchers into ambulances' half of the task: the only mature machine for it is an operator-controlled power-assist fastener, not an autonomous system, and it presupposes a crew that has already placed and secured the patient.

sources.system: Rovi
sources.title: Clearwater health system studying how robots can help move patients | Business Observer
sources.claim: Rovex's Rovi is an autonomous mobile robot ... existing hospital stretchers and drives them through corridors, doors and elevators; in an April 2026 pilot at Morton Plant Hospital it began by retrieving empty stretchers. It moves stretchers but does not transfer patients onto them or load them into vehicles.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: wheeling a stretcher through a healthcare facility. It shows autonomy in hospitals today is limited to navigation with a stretcher in tow; no patient-to-stretcher transfer or vehicle loading is claimed.

sources.system: UNEX UGV
sources.title: U.S. Army Tests UNEX UGV for Medical Evacuation Training in Lithuania | UST
sources.claim: Robotic casualty evacuation systems fielded and tested with the US Army (ABRIS UNEX UGV in Project Flytrap, Lithuania, 2026) carry casualties over terrain, but the casualty is placed aboard by soldiers; autonomy covers driving, not patient handling.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: field casualty evacuation, the outdoor analogue of loading a patient for transport. The demonstrated autonomy is vehicle mobility; loading the casualty remains a human act, so it cannot substantiate placing a patient on a litter/cot.

tasks.label: Replace supplies and disposable items on ambulances.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Start-of-shift rig check and restock at the EMS station: working from a par-level checklist, the attendant pulls gloves, gauze, dressings, IV start kits, ECG electrodes, syringes, airway adjuncts and linens off station supply-room shelves, carries them out to the ambulance in the apparatus bay, opens the patient-compartment cabinets, drawers and sliding-door bins, fills each labeled location to par, and pulls expired stock.

Post-call restock at the hospital: after a transport, the crew draws used disposables from the ED's EMS restock room or exchange cart, walks them to the rig in the hospital ambulance bay, and reloads cabinets, wall pouches and the stretcher (sheets, blanket, straps) between calls, signing the hospital restock log.

Refilling jump bags/airway kits and exchanging sealed modules: opening zippered trauma and airway bags, replacing used pouches and single-use items pocket by pocket, swapping a sealed drug box or narcotics pouch at the pharmacy window, re-sealing with numbered tamper tags and documenting seal numbers.

Replacing oxygen cylinders and bulky/heavy items at the station: swapping portable D cylinders out of their brackets and straps in the side compartment, checking/replacing the main O2 supply, and restocking backboards, straps, folded linen, sharps containers and biohazard bags.

Restock after a contamination event or deep clean: once the compartment has been decontaminated, replacing every opened or exposed disposable, re-lining the bench and stretcher, swapping the sharps container and rebuilding the rig to service-ready condition before it returns to the road.

Field/roadside replenishment: mid-shift or at a multi-patient scene, transferring supplies from a supervisor's SUV, logistics unit or cache into the ambulance while posted in a parking lot or at the curb, in weather, on uneven ground, with no fixed layout.

sources.system: Amazon Sparrow
sources.title: Amazon introduces Sparrow—a state-of-the-art robot that handles millions of diverse products
sources.claim: Amazon's Sparrow robotic arm autonomously picks and places individual products of widely varying shape and packaging out of bins in fulfillment centers, at commercial scale.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: item-level bin picking and placement in a fenced fulfillment cell. It is the physical core of replacing disposables once the work is presented as an E1 setting would present it (stock in totes, destination bins fixtured), because the objects (boxed, bagged, blister-packed goods) and placement precision are comparable.

sources.system: RightPick 4
sources.title: RightHand Robotics Introduces the RightPick 4 System
sources.claim: RightHand Robotics' RightPick 4 performs autonomous piece-picking of diverse items including pharmaceutical products; RightPick systems are installed at pharmacy fulfillment operations such as Apotea.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: order/kit picking of individual pharmaceutical and general-merchandise items into destination totes in a fenced cell - the same grasp-and-place operation used to bring an ambulance supply tray back to par when the tray and replenishment stock are presented to the machine.

sources.system: BoxPicker Automated Pharmacy Storage System
sources.date: 2026-04 product page; commercial product for years
sources.title: Automated Pharmacy Storage System - Swisslog BoxPicker
sources.claim: Swisslog's BoxPicker is a robotic storage-and-retrieval unit installed in hospital pharmacies that fully automates picking of individually boxed medications for restocking and dispensing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated retrieval and refill of boxed medical consumables inside a purpose-built enclosure. Comparable objects (small boxed medical items) and comparable accuracy requirement (right item, right location, barcode-verified) to restocking sealed drug modules and disposable stock.

sources.system: Omnicell XR2 Automated Central Pharmacy System
sources.title: How Pharmacy Automation Transformed Our Hospital's Workflows & Bottom Line
sources.claim: Omnicell's XR2 central pharmacy robot autonomously picks, scans and bags roughly 700 medication packages an hour around the clock and is installed in US hospitals.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: barcode-verified picking of individual medical packages to a list inside a purpose-built machine enclosure - the same select-verify-place cycle as restocking an ambulance drug module or disposable bin when the containers are presented fixtured.

sources.system: TX SCARA
sources.title: Restocking robots deployed in 300 Japanese convenience stores
sources.claim: Telexistence's TX SCARA autonomously restocks refrigerated beverage shelves in hundreds of Japanese convenience stores, with rare remote intervention; it is a rail-mounted arm behind one standard cooler handling uniform bottles and cans.
sources.transferJustification: Closest deployed shelf-restocking system inside a human work facility; it marks the limit of E2 restocking - fixed rail, one standard shelf geometry, uniform cylindrical SKUs - rather than a mobile robot entering a vehicle to fill latched cabinets with heterogeneous medical disposables.

sources.system: Moxi
sources.title: How Diligent's Robots Are Making a Difference in Texas Hospitals
sources.claim: Diligent Robotics' Moxi mobile manipulator autonomously picks supplies out of hospital supply closets and delivers them to patient rooms; over 100 units operate in 30+ hospitals.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: item retrieval from supply rooms and transport in a structured facility (E2). It covers only the fetch-and-carry half of ambulance restocking; no source shows Moxi or any deployed mobile manipulator entering an ambulance and filling its cabinets, bags and brackets to par.

sources.system: Operating Room Bot (ORB)
sources.title: ORB: Operating Room Bot, Automating Operating Room Logistics through Mobile Manipulation
sources.claim: A CMU research mobile manipulator (ORB) autonomously retrieved and restocked item-level operating-room supplies, reporting 80% retrieval and 96% restocking success - below worker-level reliability and in a research setup.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: item-level medical supply restocking by a mobile manipulator in a hospital, the nearest E2 analogue to ambulance restocking; it remains a research prototype with sub-worker retrieval reliability, so it cannot support an E2 positive judgment.

sources.system: Stretch
sources.title: DHL Group signs MOU with Boston Dynamics for additional 1,000-robot deployment
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Stretch autonomously unloads floor-loaded cases from trailers and containers at up to 700 cases per ... is commercially deployed by DHL across multiple countries.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: handling heavy cases inside a vehicle body in a logistics facility. Supports bulk-case handling but only for regular boxes on a floor stack, not placement of items into cabinets, brackets and bags inside an ambulance.

sources.system: Robotic cylinder handling system (AF-CHR-AU)
sources.title: Robotics cylinder handling system - LPG Solutions
sources.claim: MAKEEN Energy sells a robotic cylinder handling system that automatically handles gas cylinders in filling plants, moving 324 cylinders in under 15 minutes across cylinder types.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated grasping, lifting and seating of heavy gas cylinders in a purpose-built plant. Objects and weights match ambulance oxygen cylinder swaps; substantiates cylinder handling only where the cylinder and its receptacle are presented to the machine.

sources.system: FANUC-tended ROBODRILL cell (integrator APT Manufacturing Solutions)
sources.title: Why robotic arms are now being integrated with CNC machines
sources.claim: Robotic machine-tending cells commercially load and seat parts into fixtures and chucks with high repeatability, running unattended production shifts in fenced industrial cells.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: repeatable insertion of rigid objects into fixtures inside a fenced cell; substantiates the E1 counterfactual mechanics of seating cylinders, boards and rigid modules into presented holders, not any in-vehicle work.

tasks.label: Accompany and assist emergency medical technicians on calls.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential 911 call: the attendant follows the EMT into a private house or apartment taken as found (stairs, narrow halls, clutter, pets, distressed family), carries in the jump bag/oxygen/monitor, helps position and reassure the patient, assists the EMT with vitals and packaging, moves the patient by stair chair or draw sheet to the cot, and helps roll and load to the ambulance.

Call at a nursing home, assisted-living facility, dialysis center or clinic (including scheduled interfacility transfers): the attendant brings the cot through controlled corridors and elevators, assists the EMT with a bed-to-cot lateral transfer of a heavy or immobile patient, collects belongings and paperwork from staff, secures straps and monitor lines, and helps load the cot.

En-route assistance in the ambulance patient compartment: while the vehicle moves, the attendant hands the EMT equipment, applies oxygen or a blood-pressure cuff, holds IV lines, suctions, braces or repositions the patient, assists with CPR or mechanical CPR device placement, and records times, responding to whatever the EMT calls for.

Public or outdoor scene taken as found (motor-vehicle crash, sidewalk, park, workplace, sporting venue): the attendant helps with scene safety and traffic, carries the backboard/scoop and gear over curbs, grass, gravel or ice in weather, assists with spinal motion restriction and a multi-person lift onto the cot, and helps move the patient to the ambulance.

Hospital emergency department arrival and turnover: the attendant unloads the cot, wheels the patient through the ambulance bay and ED, assists the EMT with the lateral transfer onto the hospital bed and with handoff of belongings, then remakes the cot, decontaminates and restocks the unit for the next call.

sources.system: Moxi
sources.title: Diligent Robotics completes 300,000 pharmacy deliveries with Moxi - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Moxi is an autonomous mobile manipulator deployed in dozens of U.S. hospitals; it fetches and delivers supplies and medications along corridors and rides elevators, but it does not touch, lift, or handle patients or assist clinicians at the bedside.
sources.transferJustification: Closest deployed hospital-mobility system; cited to show that state-of-the-art autonomy in a controlled medical facility is limited to supply logistics, with no autonomous patient contact, so it cannot substitute for an EMT's assistant on a call.

sources.system: ALTA Platform
sources.title: Able Innovations Deploys Robotic Patient Delivery Platform in the U.S.
sources.claim: The ALTA Platform performs powered lateral patient transfers between beds, stretchers and imaging tables in acute-care hospitals, but it is a device driven by a human staff member for a single transfer step, not an autonomous crew member.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: bed-to-stretcher patient lifting, the physical core of instances 1, 2 and 5. Cited to show the best available patient-lifting machine still requires a human operator to bring it, position it and run it, so it cannot complete the instance.

sources.system: LUCAS 3 chest compression system
sources.title: Robot paramedic used for first time to carry out chest compressions in ambulance
sources.claim: The LUCAS 3 mechanical CPR device delivers automated chest compressions to patients in ambulances, freeing crew for other tasks, but it is applied and monitored by the crew and performs only one narrow sub-step of in-transit assistance.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-ambulance assistance with resuscitation. Cited to show that machine assistance en route is confined to a single fixed, pre-positioned function and does not cover the varied fetch-hold-position-assist work the attendant performs for the EMT.

tasks.label: Earn and maintain appropriate certifications.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Renewing CPR/BLS (and often advanced first aid) certification: registering for a refresher course at a training center or employer in-service, sitting through instruction, completing the written test and a manikin skills check, and receiving/filing the new card.

Completing required continuing education / refresher training hours (online modules, employer in-service sessions, driving-safety or ambulance-operator courses) and logging the completion certificates for the employer and state agency.

Renewing the state ambulance driver certificate or license endorsement: filling out the renewal application, paying fees, scheduling and passing a DOT/DMV medical examination, submitting fingerprints or background-check paperwork, and mailing or e-filing the packet before expiration.

Initial certification for a newly hired attendant/driver: enrolling in and completing the required ambulance attendant / first aid / driver-training course, passing the written exam, and obtaining the initial certificate before starting solo shifts.

Ongoing maintenance and record-keeping: tracking expiration dates for multiple credentials, responding to employer or state compliance audits, uploading copies of cards to the HR/credentialing system, and rescheduling anything about to lapse.

tasks.label: Drive ambulances or assist ambulance drivers in transporting sick, injured, or convalescent persons.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine scheduled non-emergency transport drive inside a metro/suburban service area: with the patient aboard the van-ambulance or ambulette, drive from a nursing home or clinic to a dialysis center, hospital, or residence over ordinary city streets in daylight/normal traffic, smoothly enough for a rider in back, pulling up at the facility's standard patient-loading entrance. (Placing the patient on the stretcher and loading is O*NET task 8608, not this task.)

Serving as the second crew member/attendant rather than the driver: riding in the patient compartment during the transport, watching the patient, steadying the cot and equipment over bumps, talking with the patient/family, relaying to dispatch and the receiving unit, navigating for the driver and spotting while the rig backs into the receiving bay.

Emergency/urgent drive: responding code 3 with lights and siren to a scene (residence, roadside, workplace) through traffic, red lights and oncoming lanes, finding and positioning at unpredictable scene access, then a priority run to the ED ambulance bay where minutes matter.

Transport drive with unstructured access or degraded conditions: pickups at private homes, apartment complexes and trailer parks up narrow driveways, unlit rural roads, gravel or unplowed lots, night, rain/snow, addresses that are new to the driver.

Interfacility transfer drive: patient already secured on the cot, extended run between hospitals, often on freeways and sometimes out of the metro area to a tertiary center, delivering to the receiving hospital's ambulance entrance.

sources.system: Waymo Driver / Waymo One
sources.title: From the road — June 24, 2026 (Waypoint, the official Waymo blog)

Conveying a seated or reclining human passenger in a minivan/van-class vehicle over the same public streets, to the same medical destinations, is the same driving task an ambulance driver performs on a non-emergency transport; vehicle class (Pacifica/Zeekr vans) and road environment are comparable.
