It shows that inside a structured facility a machine can carry a mobility-impaired person to a destination at commercial service quality.

tasks.label: Administer first aid, such as bandaging, splinting, or administering oxygen.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: During a non-emergency interfacility or dialysis transport, the attendant sets up and applies supplemental oxygen in the ambulance/ambulette patient compartment: selects nasal cannula or simple mask, connects tubing to the onboard regulator, sets flow, seats the cannula in the nares or fits the mask over a conscious, sometimes confused elderly patient's face, and adjusts it during a moving ride.

At pickup or drop-off inside a nursing home or hospital, the attendant cleans and bandages a minor wound (skin tear, abrasion, dislodged dressing, small bleed from an IV site) on a frail patient: opens gauze/tape, holds pressure, and wraps or tapes the dressing on an arm, leg, or head without tearing fragile skin.

At a private residence pickup, the attendant finds a patient who has fallen or is bleeding in a cluttered bedroom, bathroom, or hallway: controls bleeding by direct pressure, applies a dressing/bandage, and places an oxygen mask if the patient is short of breath, working in poor light and confined space around family members and pets.

Assisting on an emergency call at a roadside, worksite, or public place, the attendant helps immobilize a suspected fracture: supports the limb, positions a padded board/vacuum or SAM splint, secures it with cravats or straps, and checks distal circulation on a patient who may be in pain, uncooperative, or lying on the ground.

Assisting an EMT/paramedic at an emergency scene (public building, sidewalk, event, or crash site): under direction, applies trauma dressings and pressure to bleeding wounds, holds a non-rebreather mask on a struggling patient, and manages equipment while the crew works around a patient on the ground or on a stretcher.

sources.system: UCSD dVRK-based robotic wound redressing framework (tape initial detachment + tape placement)
sources.developer: University of California San Diego (Yip lab) / Cornell
sources.title: Towards Autonomous Tape Handling for Robotic Wound Redressing (arXiv:2510.06127)
sources.claim: State of the art in robotic wound care is an autonomous framework for a single subtask of wound redressing (adhesive tape detachment and placement), validated in lab experiments on anatomical surfaces/phantoms; the paper states wound care is still performed exclusively by clinicians.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: applying and securing dressings with tape, the closest published robotic analogue to bandaging. It automates only a subtask in a lab on phantoms, so it does not substantiate completion of a whole bandaging instance at worker quality.

sources.system: Novel anesthesia airway management robot (two continuum snake arms + mask-fastening module)
sources.developer: Ma et al. (China), published in Sensors
sources.title: Development of a Novel Anesthesia Airway Management Robot
sources.claim: A robot designed to hold a ventilation mask on a patient's face and lift the jaw was validated only on a mock person and controlled by a joystick unit; it has not been used on humans.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: placing and holding an oxygen/ventilation mask on a human face, the closest robotic analogue to administering oxygen by mask. It is joystick-controlled and manikin-only, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.system: Rethink Robotics Sawyer in simulated ICU patient room
sources.developer: Academic health-care robotics feasibility study (IISE Transactions on Healthcare Systems Engineering)
sources.title: Robotics in Simulated COVID-19 Patient Room for Health Care Worker Effector Tasks: Preliminary, Feasibility Experiments
sources.claim: In a simulated COVID-19 ICU room, a Sawyer arm was hand-programmed to reach an oxygen flow knob; the robot was fixed in place and the motion was pre-programmed rather than autonomously perceived and planned.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: operating oxygen-delivery equipment. Even this single knob turn was scripted with the robot fixed in a mock ICU room, far short of applying oxygen to a patient in an ambulance.

sources.system: DARPA MASH (Medical Swarm Robotics for Extraction and Life-Saving Interventions) program solicitation
sources.title: Medical Swarm Robotics for Extraction and Life-Saving Interventions: STTR | DARPA
sources.claim: As of 2025-2026 DARPA is soliciting research to create robot swarms that could autonomously stop bleeding and stabilize fractures in the field, indicating such autonomous field first-aid robots do not yet exist.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: field hemorrhage control and fracture stabilization (bandaging/splinting). This is a program objective, not a demonstrated system, so it substantiates no positive judgment.

sources.system: Moxi
sources.title: Diligent Robotics Unveils Moxi 2.0, Advancing The Largest Fleet of Deployed AI-Powered Mobile Manipulation Robots
sources.claim: The largest deployed fleet of hospital mobile manipulators performs logistics tasks - delivering medications, supplies and lab samples - and no hands-on patient first aid.
sources.transferJustification: Shows what autonomous robots actually do today in the most structured patient-care facilities (E2): item transport, not patient-contact procedures such as bandaging, splinting, or applying oxygen.

tasks.label: Remove and replace soiled linens or equipment to maintain sanitary conditions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine cot turnaround after a patient transport, done in the ambulance patient compartment at the hospital ambulance bay: strip the used flat sheet, pillowcase and blanket off the stretcher mattress, drop them in the soiled-linen bag, wipe the mattress and rails with a disinfectant wipe, apply a fresh sheet and pillowcase, and refasten the straps before going back in service.

Replacing used equipment and consumables to keep the unit sanitary: swap out used oxygen masks/tubing and a used suction canister, exchange a soiled backboard/straps for clean ones, discard trash and sharps into the correct containers, and restock linens, gloves, gauze and pads into the ambulance cabinets from the station or hospital supply room.

Cleanup after a heavily soiled call (vomit, blood, urine or feces): don PPE, bag grossly contaminated linens as regulated biohazard waste, scrub and disinfect the cot, bench seat, floor and walls of the compartment with the required contact/dwell time, and replace all disposables before the unit is returned to service.

Linen handling at the pickup point — a private residence or a nursing-home room: lay a clean sheet and absorbent pad on the cot before the transfer, and remove a soiled draw sheet or incontinence pad from under a convalescent patient during or after the move, bagging it and placing a clean one.

End-of-shift turnover in the EMS station garage: strip all linens from the cot and spare kits, haul soiled-linen and waste bags to the laundry exchange cart, restock clean linen from the supply room, and sweep/mop and disinfect the patient-compartment floor.

sources.system: Figure F.03 with Helix-02 VLA policy
sources.title: Helix 02 Bedroom Tidy
sources.claim: Two Figure F.03 humanoids running a single learned Helix-02 vision-language-action policy autonomously reset a staged bedroom in under two minutes, including collaboratively making a bed by lifting, unfurling, spreading and smoothing bedding, plus taking out trash and hanging clothes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: making a bed. Spreading and smoothing large bedding over a mattress is the same class of large-fabric manipulation as putting a fresh sheet and blanket on a stretcher mattress; a fixtured E1 cot cell is more structured than the staged bedroom used here.

sources.system: DYNA-1 (dual stationary arms)
sources.title: Dyna Robotics Unveils DYNA-1: The First Commercial-Ready Robot Foundation Model Offering Fully Autonomous, Round-the-Clock Dexterity
sources.claim: A pair of stationary robotic ... running the DYNA-1 model autonomously folded over 800 napkins ... run at production-grade quality (~99.4% success, 60% of human throughput) at customer sites.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: commercial linen folding at a fixed workstation. It establishes that fabric pick-separate-manipulate cycles can run unattended at production reliability when the work is presented to a fixed station, which is the E1 presentation assumed for a fixtured cot linen swap.

sources.system: Bed-making robots (Toyota HSR, Fetch) with learned pick-point networks
sources.developer: UC Berkeley AUTOLAB (Seita, Goldberg et al.)
sources.title: Deep Transfer Learning of Pick Points on Fabric for Robot Bed-Making
sources.claim: Mobile manipulators (Toyota HSR and Fetch) autonomously located pick points on blankets and pulled them to cover a bed, reaching 92% blanket coverage versus 95% for human supervisors on a quarter-scale twin bed.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: laying bedding over a mattress. Peer-reviewed evidence that grasping and spreading bed-sized fabric onto a known bed frame can be done autonomously, though only near-human coverage in a lab, supporting E1-level (fixtured) but not facility-level performance.

sources.system: JENSEN/Inwatec soiled-side sorting robots (Thor separator, Odin scanner, Futurail bag handling)
sources.title: Laundry automation | JENSEN-GROUP
sources.claim: Industrial laundry robotics from JENSEN/Inwatec automate the soiled side of hospital-linen processing — separating, identifying and sorting individual soiled linen items from bulk and feeding them to washers — inside purpose-built laundry plants.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: handling used, wet and wrinkled linen. Shows that machines can grip and route soiled linen items reliably at production rates when the linen is presented to them, which is the removal/disposal half of an E1 cot linen swap.

sources.system: TX SCARA
sources.title: Telexistence to Install AI Restocking Robots in 300 Convenience Stores Across Japan
sources.claim: Telexistence's TX SCARA restocking robot was mass-deployed to 300 FamilyMart convenience stores, autonomously picking and placing drink bottles and cans into refrigerated display shelving, with a remote operator intervening only in rare failure cases.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: shelf restocking. Removing depleted/used stock and placing known SKUs into fixed shelf positions is the same pick-and-place problem as swapping used consumables and equipment into fixtured holders, at comparable object size and precision.

sources.system: Somatic BCR (bathroom cleaning robot)
sources.title: Somatic - Autonomous Bathroom Cleaning Robots
sources.claim: Somatic's bathroom cleaning robot autonomously cleans and disinfects fixtures and floors and picks up trash in restrooms at hospitals and airports during normal facility operation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: spraying, wiping and vacuuming a small enclosed space to a hygiene standard. Supports the surface-disinfection and floor-cleaning portion of sanitizing a compartment, but the demonstrated environment is a pre-mapped fixed-layout restroom, not a contaminated patient compartment.

sources.system: TIM-E
sources.title: Hotel Tech-in: The robot lightening the load for housekeepers
sources.claim: TechForce Robotics' TIM-E autonomous service robot was installed at a California hotel where it transports hundreds of pounds of ... through the property with minimal human input.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: moving soiled linen and waste inside a facility. Covers only the haulage step of station turnover (bags to the laundry cart); it does not strip or apply linens.

tasks.label: Report facts concerning accidents or emergencies to hospital personnel or law enforcement officials.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Clean and wash rigs, ambulances, or equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine exterior wash of the rig/ambulance at the station apron, garage wash bay, or a fleet/commercial wash: soap, brush or high-pressure rinse of body, graphics, lightbar, mirrors, wheels; rinse and dry.

Routine cleaning of the patient compartment between calls at a station or hospital bay: bag and remove trash and used disposables, strip and replace cot linens, wipe bench seat, walls, handrails and cabinet fronts with disinfectant, sweep or mop the floor, restore compartment to ready state.

Deep decontamination after a contaminated or infectious call: remove and bag biohazard waste and soiled linen, scrub bodily fluids from floor, cot and walls, apply disinfectant with required contact time, unit out of service until dry.

Washing/hosing durable, non-powered equipment in the decon bay or utility sink: backboards, scoop stretchers, stair chair and cot frames, splints, KED, reusable bins and carry bags; scrub, rinse, disinfect, dry, return to rig.

Wipe-down and disinfection of the powered cot and sensitive equipment: power-cot mattress and rails, cardiac monitor and cables, BP cuffs, suction unit, oxygen regulators, radios, tablet - germicidal wipes, no immersion.
Cab housekeeping and detail: tidy and wipe the driver cab, clean interior glass and mirrors, clear debris from footwells, spot-clean wheels and step wells between full washes.

sources.system: InterClean Ultra Gantry / drive-through vehicle wash systems
sources.title: Truck Wash Systems - Designed for Commercial and Municipal | InterClean
sources.claim: InterClean's Ultra Gantry and drive-through wash systems automatically wash large, irregularly shaped fleet vehicles in a purpose-built wash bay; the driver parks and exits and the machine runs the wash cycle, with chassis/wheel wash and blower drying options.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (washing a rig's exterior) on comparable objects: box-bodied municipal/emergency-service vehicles with mirrors and irregular contours, of which an ambulance is one.

sources.system: Westmatic Super / Tornado touchless wash system
sources.title: Touchless Vehicle Washing Systems | Westmatic
sources.claim: Westmatic's touchless heavy-vehicle wash uses robot-controlled high-pressure arches whose arms self-adjust to the vehicle's shape to wash front, back and sides of large irregularly shaped vehicles.
sources.transferJustification: Same task on comparable vehicles: self-adjusting robot arches handle the protrusions (mirrors, lightbars, irregular profiles) that make ambulance exteriors awkward to wash.

sources.system: KKE 501 / KKE fleet wash systems
sources.title: Automatic Bus - Truck Wash Systems | Fleet Cleaning Equipment - KKE Wash Systems United States
sources.claim: Commercial automatic fleet wash systems are sold specifically for ambulances alongside buses and trucks, in friction, touchless and combination configurations installed in fixed wash bays.

sources.system: Steelco LC 80 / LC 80 BOT trolley washer-disinfector
sources.title: LC 80 - Steelco
sources.claim: Steelco's LC 80 trolley washer-disinfector automatically washes and thermally disinfects bulky patient-care items - hospital furniture, transport trolleys, bed frames, wheelchairs - in a purpose-built chamber, with optional automatic loading and unloading.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated wash-and-disinfect of bulky non-electronic patient-handling equipment. EMS backboards, stair-chair and cot frames, splints and bins are the same class of rigid plastic/metal items requiring the same soil removal plus disinfection, in the same kind of purpose-built chamber.

sources.system: Steelco/Miele trolley washer-disinfectors (CSSD cart washers)
sources.title: Trolley Washer Disinfectors | Medical Equipment | ARES Scientific
sources.claim: Trolley/cart washer-disinfectors installed in hospital sterile-processing departments are used for thermal disinfection of patient transport ... and other bulky transport equipment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: reprocessing of stretchers and transport equipment in hospitals maps onto washing EMS carry and immobilization equipment - same objects, same accepted cleanliness standard, load presented to a fixed chamber machine.

sources.system: Tesla robotaxi hub cleaning robot
sources.title: Tesla readies its autonomous Cybercab and Robotaxi cleaning service | Teslarati
sources.claim: Tesla installed a fixed robotic arm with interchangeable attachments at its Austin robotaxi hub to vacuum and clean vehicle interiors between rides, shown in a company video and confirmed by a state building permit; it addresses loose debris and left-behind items in a passenger cabin, not linen changes, biohazard handling or validated disinfection.
sources.transferJustification: Nearest related task to ambulance interior cleaning (automated cleaning of a vehicle cabin brought to a fixed machine); cited to show the closest available capability, which stops short of soiled-linen replacement, biohazard removal and disinfection to EMS standard.

sources.system: Bioquell BQ-EMS; Zimek Z-vac Micro-Particle Evacuator
sources.title: Safeguard EMS personnel with advanced ambulance decontamination practices and products | EMS1
sources.claim: Automated ambulance decontamination products used by EMS (Bioquell BQ-EMS hydrogen peroxide vapor, Zimek disinfectant misting) run an unattended cycle that kills pathogens on compartment and equipment surfaces, but they are fixed vapor/mist appliances applied after gross soil, trash and linens have been removed by hand.
sources.transferJustification: Cited for the disinfection sub-step of ambulance cleaning; it substantiates only terminal disinfection, not the cleaning (soil, trash, linen removal) the task requires.

tasks.label: Perform minor maintenance on emergency medical services vehicles, such as ambulances.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Start-of-shift rig check in the ambulance station apparatus bay: walk-around of the unit, open the hood and check engine oil, coolant, brake, power-steering and washer fluid levels, check belts/hoses and battery terminals, check tire condition and pressure, start the engine and verify gauges, headlights, brake lights, emergency warning lights and siren, wipers and horn, then sign the vehicle checklist and report defects.

Fueling the ambulance during or at the end of a ... at the agency's fuel island or a commercial station: park at the pump, open the fuel door and cap, insert the nozzle, dispense diesel or gasoline to full, replace the cap, and record fuel and mileage.

Washing the ambulance exterior at the station wash rack or apron: soap, scrub/spray the box, cab and undercarriage, rinse, clean windows and mirrors, dry the body and light bars so the unit is presentable and salt/road grime is removed.

Small in-bay servicing between calls: topping off engine oil, coolant or washer fluid, swapping worn wiper blades, replacing a burned-out bulb or blown fuse, inflating a low tire, jump-starting or putting a battery on charge, tightening a loose compartment latch or mirror, and tagging bigger problems for the fleet mechanic.

Field or roadside minor fixes away from the station: changing a flat tire on the shoulder, jump-starting the rig at a hospital ramp or scene, adding coolant or oil after a warning light, scraping ice/snow off the windshield and emergency lights, in traffic and weather with no fixed layout.

sources.system: Robofuel (SCOTT Automation)
sources.title: Autonomous refuelling solution for mining trucks from Universal Field Robots - International Mining
sources.claim: Scott Automation's Robofuel robotic arm autonomously refuels heavy diesel mining trucks at unmanned refuelling stations and is reported in use at several mine sites, including with an autonomous Komatsu 930E ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic diesel refuelling of a heavy vehicle. The physical act is the same as fueling an ambulance - locate the filler on a parked vehicle, insert a commercial fuel nozzle, dispense to full, withdraw - at comparable precision, but done at a purpose-built unmanned fuel station.

sources.system: Robofuel (SCOTT Automation)
sources.title: Scott | Autonomous Truck Refueling - The Robot Revolution
sources.claim: Robofuel uses vision sensing to locate the truck's fuel tank and couple the nozzle, and the vendor states it works with standard commercial fuel nozzles and receivers without vehicle-side equipment.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above; establishes that the robotic refuelling is machine-controlled (vision-guided coupling) and does not require modifying the vehicle, supporting transfer to a conventional emergency vehicle presented in a purpose-built fuel bay.

sources.system: InterClean automatic drive-through truck wash systems
sources.title: Vehicle Wash Systems – State-of-the-Art Wash Systems for Every Vehicle (InterClean)
sources.claim: InterClean sells and installs fully automatic drive-through wash systems for truck and large-vehicle fleets: the driver drives the vehicle into the ... the machine performs the full wash cycle, including chassis wash and spot-free rinse, in under three minutes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated exterior washing of trucks and buses. An ambulance box/cab is the same class of body panel surface at the same scale, so machine washing transfers directly to washing the rig; the wash bay itself is built around the machine.

sources.system: KKE drive-through bus/truck wash systems
sources.title: Automatic Bus - Truck Wash Systems | Fleet Cleaning Equipment - KKE Wash Systems United States
sources.claim: Drive-through bus and truck wash systems installed in fleet depot wash bays sense the vehicle and sequence the wash arches automatically as the vehicle passes, with no cleaning crew required.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated fleet vehicle washing in depot wash bays; confirms the wash cycle is machine-controlled and routine in fleet facilities, transferring to washing an ambulance of similar body size.

sources.system: UVeye heavy-duty inspection scanners
sources.title: UVeye for Heavy Duty Vehicles - UVeye
sources.claim: UVeye's drive-thru AI scanners perform an automated 17-point condition inspection of trucks and buses, detecting worn tires, underbody leaks, rust and cracks and exterior damage, but the scan covers only exterior, tire and underbody condition - not under-hood fluid levels or functional tests of lights and sirens.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated pre-trip/condition inspection of heavy vehicles at fleet facilities. It bounds what automation covers for an ambulance rig check: condition scanning of tires/underbody/exterior, with no fluid-level checking, no lamp/siren functional test and no corrective top-off.

sources.system: UVeye drive-thru scanners at Mesilla Valley Transportation
sources.title: UVeye and Mesilla Valley Transportation Bring Automated Inspections to Trucking
sources.claim: UVeye drive-thru scanners are deployed in commercial trucking operations (Mesilla Valley Transportation), performing full 360-degree scans of heavy-duty vehicles in seconds and issuing digital condition reports at the fleet yard.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated fleet vehicle inspection in a human work facility (truck yard). Shows the E2-capable automation is limited to scanning/reporting, not the physical checks and top-offs in an ambulance rig check.

sources.system: Rocsys autonomous charging robot
sources.title: Charging up the Robotaxi revolution | Electric Vehicle Charging & Infrastructure
sources.claim: Rocsys robotic hands-free charging is being supplied to the APM Terminals Maasvlakte II container ... to autonomously plug in and charge electric automated terminal trucks around the clock.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous energy replenishment of a fleet vehicle inside a structured facility (container terminal, an E2 setting). It transfers only partly: it inserts a standardized charge connector into automated terminal tractors, not a fuel nozzle into a conventional gasoline/diesel ambulance filler with a cap.

tasks.label: Restrain or shackle violent patients.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Interfacility behavioral-health transport: at a hospital ED or psychiatric facility, the attendant helps secure an agitated but currently controllable psychiatric patient onto the ambulance cot before departure — positioning limbs, applying soft wrist/ankle limb holders and chest/lap straps at the correct tension, checking distal circulation, and re-checking as the patient pulls against them.

En route in the moving ambulance patient compartment: a transported patient becomes combative (delirium, hypoglycemia, intoxication, psychiatric crisis). The attendant, in a cramped compartment, physically holds and controls thrashing limbs, calls for the driver to pull over, and applies or re-secures limb restraints while protecting the airway and avoiding prone positioning.

Scene response at a private residence: a combative, altered or intoxicated patient in a cluttered home, sometimes on the floor or in a bathroom. Attendant works with a partner and/or police to take hold of the patient's limbs, control the head, move the patient to the cot, and apply restraints amid furniture, pets, and family members.

Public place or roadside: combative patient on a sidewalk, in a bar, at a shelter, or in a parked car, often with police already applying handcuffs. Attendant physically controls the patient during transfer to the cot, replaces or supplements law-enforcement hardware with medical restraints, and secures the patient for transport in a crowd with bystanders.

Nursing home, group home, or dialysis clinic pickup: a confused dementia or developmentally disabled patient resists being moved, grabs rails, or strikes out. Attendant uses gentle hands-on control, redirection, and applies safety straps/limb holders on the cot or wheelchair per facility and agency policy.

sources.system: ALTA Platform (Able Innovations)
sources.title: Able Innovations Deploys Robotic Patient Delivery Platform in the U.S.
sources.claim: The most advanced deployed hospital patient-handling robot performs lateral transfers of cooperative or immobile patients under a staff member's operation; it does not grasp limbs, control a resisting person, or apply restraint straps.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic patient handling/transfer in a hospital. It does NOT transfer to this task — the platform moves a passive, cooperative patient between flat surfaces with a human operator present, and has no capability to seize thrashing limbs, apply soft limb holders, or maintain control of an actively resisting human.

sources.system: Knightscope Autonomous Security Robots (K5/K3)
sources.title: Roaming Robots in Public? Knightscope Moves with Precision and Purpose
sources.claim: Deployed autonomous security robots operating in human facilities and public spaces explicitly do not make physical contact with or physically apprehend people; they patrol, sense, and report only.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic control of potentially violent people in public and institutional settings. The closest fielded systems are explicitly non-contact, confirming that no deployed robot physically restrains a resisting human.

sources.system: Police force-deploying robots (remotely operated ground robots)
sources.developer: various law enforcement agencies / robot vendors
sources.title: The Rising Call for Regulating Police Robots
sources.claim: Where robots are used against people by public safety agencies, they are remotely operated by a human rather than autonomous, and their use is contested and restricted; no system autonomously applies physical restraint to a person.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic physical intervention against an uncooperative person. Even in this closest domain the machines are continuously teleoperated and deliver force rather than safely restraining a patient, so nothing carries over to applying medical restraints at worker quality.

emergingTasks.label: Evaluate patient condition by checking vital signs before and after transport.
emergingTasks.status: Proposed for future data collection; not treated as established task evidence

roles.title: Driver/Sales Workers
aliases: Automotive Parts Delivery Driver (Auto Parts Delivery Driver)
roles.description: Drive truck or other vehicle over established routes or within an established territory and sell or deliver goods, such as food products, including restaurant take-out items, or pick up or deliver items such as commercial laundry. May also take orders, collect payment, or stock merchandise at point of delivery.

tasks.label: Drive trucks to deliver such items as food, medical supplies, or newspapers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Prepared-food/restaurant delivery: driver loads 2-5 hot orders at a pizzeria, chain restaurant or ghost kitchen, drives residential and commercial streets in mixed traffic (day, night, rain), parks at the curb or in an apartment lot, and hands the order to the customer at the door or lobby (or leaves it). Many stops per shift, tight time windows.

Direct-store-delivery food route: step van or 26-ft box truck, 10-25 stops per day at supermarkets, convenience stores and restaurants; driving city/suburban streets between stops, backing to a dock or double-parking, then hand-trucking cases/trays inside, checking in with a receiver and obtaining a signature.

Consumer home delivery of groceries, convenience/retail goods or bottled water from a store or local depot: van or car, residential streets, multi-stop route, carrying totes/cases from the curb to the porch or doorstep.

Single-destination bulk shuttle run: full load of ambient/refrigerated/frozen food or supplies driven from a distribution center, commissary or dark store to one retail store or outlet over a fixed, repeated route including highway and surface streets; the receiving site's staff unload at the dock.

Medical supplies / pharmacy / lab courier route: van driven daily among clinics, nursing homes, dialysis centers, hospitals and some patient homes, carrying temperature-sensitive medications, specimens and supply totes, with signature or ID verification at handoff.

Newspaper/publication route: pre-dawn, personal vehicle, several hundred stops on residential streets, bagged papers tossed to driveways and porches from the moving vehicle, plus bundle drops at racks, stores and boxes; all weather, no supervision.

sources.system: Gatik Driver (26- and 30-ft autonomous box trucks)
sources.title: Gatik launches fully driverless commercial trucking operations - FreightWaves
sources.claim: Gatik operates fully driverless (no driver or safety observer) medium-duty box trucks in daily revenue commercial service on public roads in Texas, Arkansas and Arizona, hauling ambient, refrigerated and frozen goods from distribution centers to retail stores over routes up to 400 miles on highways and surface streets.

sources.system: Gatik Driver autonomous trucks (PepsiCo deployment)
sources.title: PepsiCo and Gatik launch commercial driverless trucking deployment - FreightWaves
sources.claim: Gatik's driverless food-and-beverage deliveries are live commercially at multi-state scale under a PepsiCo partnership, indicating sustained rather than pilot operation.

sources.system: Waymo Driver (Jaguar I-Pace) on DoorDash Autonomous Delivery Platform

tasks.label: Collect money from customers, make change, and record transactions on customer receipts.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Prepared-food (pizza/restaurant takeout) delivery to a private residence: driver meets the customer at the door, takes cash or a card, counts and returns change from a personal bank of bills and coins, and hands over the printed ticket/receipt or a signed card slip, often at night, in weather, with the food in one hand.

Prepared-food or catering delivery to a business, office suite, hotel, or hospital: payment taken at a reception desk or loading area, usually a card tapped on a handheld terminal or a company check, with a receipt printed/emailed and a signature or department code recorded.

Direct-store-delivery route sales at a supermarket or convenience store: driver totals the delivered/returned quantities on a handheld, presents the invoice to the receiving clerk or manager in the back room, collects a check or cash for a COD account, makes change, obtains a signature, and leaves the receipt copy.

Commercial laundry / uniform / linen route stop at a business (restaurant, shop, clinic): driver swaps garments or mats, prints or writes the invoice, collects a check or cash from the office manager, makes change if needed, and records the payment on the handheld and the customer's receipt copy.

Mobile vending or residential route sales (ice cream truck at a curb, bottled-water, propane, or beverage home route): cash taken from consumers on a public street or at a doorstep, change made from an apron or cash box, and a handwritten or handheld-printed receipt given; multiple small transactions in quick succession outdoors.

sources.system: Glory CASHINFINITY CI-10X point-of-sale cash recycler
sources.title: GLORY Announces Next Generation Retail Cash Recycling Solutions
sources.claim: Glory's CI-10X point-of-sale cash recycler automates the whole cash transaction at the point of payment, including validating notes/coins taken in and mechanically dispensing the correct change, integrated with standard POS software.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: collecting a customer's payment at point of sale. It transfers because the objects (US banknotes and coins), the required output (correct change plus a POS-recorded transaction and printed receipt) and the accuracy standard are the same as a driver's collection; the only difference is that the customer presents the cash to a machine slot, which is exactly the E1 presentation assumption.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: taking payment from a customer and giving change at a retail point of sale. Same currency handling, same reliability requirement, and the money-in/change-out/receipt record is the identical accepted output; it is a fielded deployment rather than a demo.

tasks.label: Maintain trucks and food-dispensing equipment and clean inside of machines that dispense food or beverages.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Vending route driver servicing snack and cold-drink machines in customer break rooms, school and hospital corridors, and factory lunchrooms: unlocks and opens the machine, wipes shelves, spirals, glass and delivery bin, removes spilled/leaking product and crumbs, wipes coin/bill validator area and door gaskets, checks the refrigeration deck and drain, closes and tests.

Route driver cleaning food/beverage dispensing equipment at customer sites: office bean-to-cup and fresh-brew coffee machines (remove brew group, whipper bowls, mixing funnels, milk lines; wash in a sink; sanitize; descale; wipe drip tray and cabinet) and c-store fountain, juice or frozen-slush machines (disassemble tap valves, spiral blade, bowl gaskets; wash, sanitize, reassemble).

Daily truck upkeep at the depot yard: DOT pre-/post-trip walk-around, check and top off oil, coolant, washer fluid, check tire pressure and tread, lights, brakes, liftgate and refrigeration unit, fuel the truck, clean out the cab, and write up defects for the shop.

Washing the exterior of the delivery/route truck at the fleet depot wash rack or a commercial truck wash at the end of the shift so the branded food-delivery vehicle stays presentable and free of road film and salt.

Cleaning out the cargo body of a bread, dairy, beverage or restaurant-supply truck at the depot: pull out empties, dunnage and trash, sweep crumbs and broken product, then wash and sanitize the box floor, walls and shelving (reefer bodies to FSMA sanitation standards).

Food truck / mobile canteen operator cleaning the truck's food-dispensing and holding equipment after service — beverage dispensers, coffee urns, holding cabinets, prep surfaces and sinks — in the cramped galley, usually at the commissary at the end of the day.

It transfers to a route truck's cargo-box clean-out because the surfaces (box floor, walls, shelving), the sanitation standard (FSMA food-contact cleanliness), and the purpose-built depot wash bay are the same.

sources.system: Mobile Cleaning Device 4.0

sources.transferJustification: Related task: jet-cleaning food-processing equipment surfaces. It does not transfer to cleaning inside vending or beverage dispensers, which contain electronics and require opening the machine, removing parts and wiping rather than high-pressure spraying; it also remains a research prototype.

tasks.label: Arrange merchandise and sales promotion displays or issue sales promotion materials to customers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Supermarket / mass-merchandiser sales floor: a bread, snack or beverage route driver wheels product in on a hand truck and arranges it on the assigned shelf section and racks - placing bags, boxes, trays and bottles in their planogram slots, fronting and facing labels, rotating older stock forward, pulling stales - during store hours with shoppers and carts moving through the aisle.

Convenience store, gas station or small independent account: the route driver restocks and arranges bottles and cans in the reach-in/walk-in cooler and on countertop and rack displays, fronting product so rows are full and facing out, in a small standard-layout store.

Building or refreshing a sales promotion display in a retail store: erecting a corrugated shipper or wire rack, stacking cases into a floor stack or end-cap pyramid, filling the display, and attaching header cards, price signs and shelf talkers per the promotion plan.

Issuing sales promotion materials at a business account: at the delivery, handing the store manager, restaurant owner or office contact coupon books, flyers, new-product sell sheets, catalogs or product samples, and leaving the stack at the counter or back office.

Residential or small-office route stop (home food/bakery delivery, bottled water, uniform/laundry route): the driver hands the customer, or leaves at the door with the order, promotional flyers, menus, catalogs, coupons or a free sample.

tasks.label: Collect coins from vending machines, refill machines, and remove aged merchandise.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Office/corporate building breakroom bank of 2-4 machines (snack spiral machine + cold-drink machine). Driver badges in, wheels a hand truck of totes from the truck, unlocks each machine with a key, pulls the bill stacker and coin box and secures the cash, reloads spirals and drink racks with 40+ SKUs of bagged snacks, candy, cans and bottles, rotates and pulls dated product, wipes the front and restarts the machine.

Manufacturing plant, warehouse or distribution center: several machine banks spread across a large facility (snack, cold drink, frozen/fresh-food and coffee machines), dock entry with a pallet jack or cart, cash and card revenue collected from each machine, high-volume restock, and mandatory pull of dated sandwiches/fresh food with credit logging.

School, university or hospital site: machines in corridors, cafeterias and staff lounges, escorted or badge access, students/staff passing during service; unlock, empty coin box and bill stacker, restock snacks and drinks, pull expired product, comply with dating/nutrition rules.

Small public-facing or outdoor placements taken as found: hotel lobbies and ice/vending alcoves, gas stations, laundromats, apartment laundry rooms, car washes, car dealerships, parks and rest stops. Cramped or exposed positions, weather, vandalism and jammed coin mechs; cash-heavy machines; unlock, collect coins/bills, restock and pull aged product.

Micro market / unattended cashless retail in a breakroom: restock open gondola shelves, glass-door coolers and freezers with hundreds of SKUs, face and rotate stock, pull and credit expired items, service the self-checkout kiosk (empty its bill acceptor if fitted) and tidy the space.

Card-only (cashless) cold-drink machine at a high-traffic campus or transit site: no coin box to pull; driver opens the machine, tops up serpentine/rack columns from cases of cans and bottles brought on a hand truck, rotates stock and closes up. Long-dated product, so aged pulls are rare.

sources.system: TX SCARA
sources.title: AI Flying Off the Shelves: Restocking Robot Rolls Out to Hundreds of Japanese Convenience Stores
sources.claim: Telexistence's TX SCARA, a rail-mounted robot arm installed in convenience-store back rooms, autonomously picks bottles and cans and places them into the refrigerated display shelves, succeeding automatically more than 98% of ..., with remote operators taking over only for exceptions; deployed to 300 FamilyMart stores.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: refilling a chilled beverage display cabinet. It transfers partially to 'refill machines' for drink vending — same objects (cans/bottles from cases), similar insertion into narrow lanes of a fixed cabinet — but the robot is a fixed rail installation in an engineered work envelope; it does not travel a route, unlock machines, handle cash, or pull dated product.

sources.system: TX GHOST

sources.transferJustification: Related task: stocking beverages into store display shelves. Nearest deployed analogue to 'refill machines' for drinks, but confined to a fixed installation stocking one product class; it performs no cash collection, no date-based removal, and no route service of vending equipment.

sources.system: RightPick 4
sources.title: 5 questions about the new RightPick 4 picking system with RightHand Robotics

It shows autonomous grasping of such items in a purpose-built cell, but placement is into open totes, not into spiral coils or racks inside a machine, and the system does no machine opening, cash-box extraction or date inspection.

tasks.label: Write customer orders and sales contracts according to company guidelines.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Review lists of dealers, customers, or station drops and load trucks.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: DSD snack/bread/dairy route: at the depot before dawn, the driver reviews the route's customer order list on a handheld, pulls mixed cases and trays for each stop from staging racks and floor stacks, and hand-stacks them into a step van/box truck in reverse stop sequence.

Beverage/beer route: at the distribution-center dock, the driver checks the load manifest against pre-picked pallets or bays staged by warehouse selectors, then loads a bay truck or trailer with a pallet jack or forklift, confirming counts and adding extra product for anticipated sales.

Restaurant take-out/prepared-food driver: reviews the ticket queue at the expo/warming rack, matches bagged and boxed orders (drinks, hot entrees, sides) to each customer, verifies contents, and carries them out to load level into the vehicle's insulated bag or cargo area.

Commercial laundry/uniform route: at the plant, the driver reviews the day's account list, matches bundled garment packs, mats and bagged linen to each account, and rolls carts/bundles into the truck grouped by stop.

Station-drop route (newspaper bundles, vending/parts totes, magazine drops): the driver reviews the drop sheet with per-station counts, pulls the correct bundles/totes from the dock staging area, and loads the van in drop order.

tasks.label: Sell food specialties, such as sandwiches and beverages, to office workers and patrons of sports events.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Mobile canteen / lunch truck route: driver drives an established route on public streets, parks in office-park and industrial-site lots at fixed break times, opens service windows, sells prepackaged sandwiches, pastries, snacks, sodas and urn coffee to a rush of 20-40 workers in a few minutes, takes cash and cards, restocks between stops.

tasks.label: Inspect loads to ensure that cargo is secure.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Dry van / enclosed trailer at a shipper dock or distribution center yard: after loading, driver checks freight placement and weight distribution, verifies pallets are braced (load bars, straps, dunnage) or that the load will not shift, closes and seals the doors, and signs off before pulling out.

Flatbed / step-deck loaded with steel coils, lumber, pipe, or machinery at a mill or plant yard: driver walks the load, counts and tugs chains/ratchet straps, checks binders, edge protection, webbing abrasion and working-load-limit adequacy, re-tensions loose devices, and checks tarps before departure.

In-transit re-inspection required by FMCSA 392.9 (within the first 50 miles and roughly every 150 miles/3 hours) and after hard braking: performed on a highway shoulder, ramp, rest area, or crowded truck stop lot, often at night, in rain/snow/heat, with traffic passing; loose straps are re-tightened and shifted freight re-blocked.

Intermodal chassis or tank/bulk work at a port, rail ramp, or terminal: verify container is seated and the chassis pins/twist locks are locked, container doors closed and seal intact and matching paperwork; for tankers/pneumatics verify hatches, dome lids, valves closed and hoses/equipment stowed.

Tow / heavy recovery driver: after winching a disabled or wrecked vehicle onto a wrecker or rollback at a crash scene, shoulder, or private lot, check that wheel straps, safety chains, and tie-downs are tight and correctly routed, steering/parking brake handled, and re-check at first stop.

tasks.label: Check vehicles to ensure that mechanical, safety, and emergency equipment is in good working order.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Daily pre-trip inspection of a tractor-trailer at the carrier's terminal or yard before dispatch: seven-zone walkaround (lights, reflectors, tires/wheels, brake chambers and slack adjusters, air lines, suspension, fifth wheel and coupling, leaks), hood-up check of fluid levels/belts/hoses, in-cab check of gauges, horn, wipers, mirrors, seat belt, applied and leak-down air-brake tests, and verification of emergency equipment (fire extinguisher charge, warning triangles, spare fuses); defects logged on a DVIR.

The same full daily pre-trip performed away from base by an over-the-road driver - in a truck-stop or rest-area parking row, or a shipper/receiver lot where the driver parked overnight - often before dawn, in rain, heat or snow, with the rig boxed in between other trucks and no shop support.

End-of-day post-trip inspection and written DVIR at the terminal or a drop yard: walkaround of service and parking brakes, steering, lighting devices and reflectors, tires, wheels/rims, horn, wipers, mirrors, coupling devices and emergency equipment, plus noting damage or defects found during the run for the shop.

En-route condition check of a dry-van or reefer combination at a fuel island or rest stop: looking over tires and wheels for wear, cuts, low inflation and missing lug nuts, scanning the underbody and driveline for fluid leaks or hanging components, and checking body/trailer damage before continuing.

En-route check on a flatbed, tanker or hazmat load (required within the first 50 miles and periodically after): re-tensioning straps, chains and binders, checking tarps, hoses, valves and placards, and confirming emergency kit items, usually on a shoulder, ramp or gravel pull-off.

Vocational or tow-truck equipment check before a shift or before a recovery: winch and cable condition, hooks, chains, straps, wheel-lift and boom hydraulics and hoses, PTO, dump-gate or tank fittings, light bar and beacons, plus fire extinguisher, triangles and spill kit, at the operator's shop yard or at the scene.

tasks.label: Crank trailer landing gear up or down to safely secure vehicles.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Drop-and-hook at a carrier terminal or large distribution-center yard: paved, marked parking rows, controlled access. Driver lowers the two-speed landing gear to set down a loaded or empty dry van before pulling out, or cranks the gear fully up after backing under and coupling a trailer.

Coupling/uncoupling at a shipper or receiver's site (warehouse dock apron, plant yard, grocery DC, retail back lot): premises controlled by the customer, generally paved but sometimes sloped or potholed; driver cranks gear down to drop, or up after hooking, judging nose height so the trailer sits level and the fifth wheel takes the load.

Drop or hook on an unpaved or uncontrolled surface: gravel/dirt drop lot, truck stop, staging area, or street-side spot. Driver must judge leg height on uneven ground and often place boards or dunnage under the sand shoes so the gear does not sink or the trailer shift.

Field/job-site work with flatbed, lowboy, dump, or tank trailers at construction sites, oilfield lease roads, farms, or logging landings: unimproved, muddy or sloped ground, blocking required, trailer may be loaded heavy on the nose.

Degraded or difficult cases in any setting: rusted or bent crank handle stowed in an odd position, seized or damaged gearbox needing a cheater bar or hammer, heavily nose-loaded trailer requiring low-gear cranking and repeated height adjustment, done in rain, snow, ice, or darkness.

sources.system: Outrider System / TrailerConnect robotic arm
sources.title: Outrider Adds Robot Arms Using Deep Learning to Autonomous Yard Trucks - Robotics 24/7
sources.claim: Outrider's TrailerConnect robotic arm autonomously locates and connects/disconnects trailer brake and electric lines on semi-trailers while autonomous yard trucks hitch and unhitch trailers in customer distribution yards.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic trailer coupling at the trailer nose. It shows autonomous perception-guided engagement of standardized trailer hardware in real yards, the closest demonstrated manipulation to seizing and turning a landing-gear crank; it does not show multi-turn torque cranking, so it supports only a fixtured (E1) presentation of the crank shaft.

sources.system: ISEE trailer auto-coupling system

sources.claim: ISEE's auto-coupling system uses a six-axis robotic arm on autonomous yard trucks to autonomously couple trailers and connect airlines on unmodified trailers at customer sites, trained on over 10,000 operational moves.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous trailer coupling in distribution yards. Same workpiece (arbitrary semi-trailers) and same environment class, but the arm handles air/electric lines only; it demonstrates no landing-gear cranking, so it substantiates capability only where the crank is presented in a known, fixtured position.

sources.claim: AIRman's automated landing gear deployment/retraction unit, a 15-lb electrically driven device fitted to the trailer's crank shaft, fully retracted both landing gear legs in 29 seconds in a public demonstration; it replaces manual cranking with a switch.
sources.transferJustification: Same task, but machine-actuated on human command rather than autonomous, so it cannot by itself support a positive judgment; it establishes that the mechanical demand of raising/lowering loaded landing gear is met by a small motorized drive on the crank shaft.

sources.claim: Outrider's autonomous yard trucks use a lifting fifth wheel that raises the trailer so its landing gear clears the ground, i.e. yard automation moves trailers without ever cranking the landing gear.

instances.label: Fuel stop: driver pulls the tractor onto a truck-stop or fleet diesel island, swipes a fuel card, pulls the nozzle, fills one or both saddle tanks (and DEF if low), replaces caps, squeegees the windshield, and takes the receipt. Varied truck makes, cap types, hose reaches; other trucks and people moving around the island.

Fluid top-off/check at a terminal yard or fuel island: driver tilts the hood or opens access panels, pulls the dipstick, adds a quart or two of engine oil, tops the coolant surge tank, adds windshield washer fluid and DEF from jugs, wipes up spills, checks for leaks.

Minor repairs and adjustments found during pre-trip or on the road: swapping a burned-out marker/tail lamp or fuse, replacing a torn glad-hand seal or air-line, re-hanging a mud flap, changing a wiper blade, tightening a clamp, checking and airing up tires, jump-starting, or hanging tire chains. Done in a parking lot, at a dock, or on a shoulder in whatever weather and lighting exist.

Washing the tractor and trailer at a commercial truck wash or fleet terminal wash bay: pulling into the bay, running the wash (automatic drive-through or self-serve wand), and touching up mirrors, grille, wheels and fuel tanks to fleet appearance standard.

Vocational/tow-truck specific upkeep at the shop yard: greasing the fifth wheel and wrecker boom/pivot points, topping hydraulic fluid for the wrecker or PTO, draining air tanks, inspecting and lubricating winch cable, checking chains, straps and hooks, and adding fuel/oil to auxiliary equipment.

tasks.label: Couple or uncouple trailers by changing trailer jack positions, connecting or disconnecting air or electrical lines, or manipulating fifth-wheel locks.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Yard spotter/shuttle driver at a distribution center, carrier terminal or plant: dozens of hook/drop cycles per shift with a yard tractor (lifting fifth wheel), backing under standard dry vans, engaging the fifth-wheel lock, connecting/disconnecting glad hands and the 7-way cord, moving trailers between dock doors ... on a paved, institution-controlled yard.

Over-the-road or regional driver doing a drop-and-hook at a large DC or carrier terminal in benign conditions: pull the fifth-wheel release, crank the landing gear down/up, disconnect/connect air and electrical lines, verify kingpin lock with a tug test; paved, lighted, marked yard, standard 53-ft van trailer.

Same drop-and-hook but in adverse conditions: night, rain/snow/ice or mud on a gravel or rutted section of yard, rusty or bent landing gear needing high crank force, trailer nose sitting too low or too high so fifth-wheel height must be worked, frozen or torn glad-hand seals needing a swap.

Intermodal drayage: hooking or dropping a chassis (often with a loaded container) at a rail ramp, marine terminal or customer yard - pool chassis of mixed age and configuration, chassis landing gear cranking, worn air line couplers and pigtail sockets, lock/pin checks, tight lanes with other trucks around.

LTL doubles work at a breakbulk terminal: coupling/uncoupling pup trailers with a converter dolly - pushing/positioning the dolly, backing the lead trailer, engaging the dolly fifth wheel on the second pup's kingpin, hooking safety chains, running two sets of air and light lines, cranking dolly and trailer jacks.

Coupling or uncoupling away from a controlled facility: dropping or picking up a trailer at a street-side customer, a truck stop parking row, or a farm/construction/oilfield site - unpaved or crowned ground, no lighting, no institutional control of the surroundings, sometimes needing boards under the jack pads.

tasks.label: Maneuver trucks into loading or unloading positions, following signals from loading crew and checking that vehicle and loading equipment are properly positioned.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Distribution center / warehouse / LTL terminal: driver arrives at a paved, striped, guard-controlled trailer yard and backs a 53-ft tractor-trailer 45-90 degrees into an assigned dock door, sometimes guided by a spotter or dock crew hand signals, then checks trailer squareness to the dock bumper, dock plate/leveler and wheel chocks/restraint before setting brakes.

Retail, grocery, convenience-store or restaurant delivery: maneuvering a tractor-trailer (or pup) into a tight strip-mall lot, alley, or street-side receiving door with parked cars, shopping carts, pedestrians and public traffic; often blind-side or multi-point backing while a store employee waves the driver in.

Industrial or bulk facility: positioning a tanker, hopper, flatbed or van inside a plant, mill, terminal, port or grain/cement facility - spotting under a loading spout or silo, alongside a crane or forklift bay, or on a scale - inching forward/back on hand or light signals from the loading crew until the fill point or lifting gear lines up.

Quarry, aggregate plant or mine: positioning a dump truck under a wheel loader/excavator bucket or at a crusher hopper on unpaved but operator-maintained ground inside a geofenced pit, following the loader operator's signals, then confirming the body/tarp and load position before pulling out.

Active construction, roadwork or field site: backing a dump truck, flatbed or mixer to the placement point on unimproved, changing ground amid other trades, overhead lines and soft spots, guided by hand signals from a ground crew or flagger; layout differs at every site and changes hour to hour.

Tow/wrecker work: positioning the wrecker relative to a disabled or crashed vehicle at the roadside, in a ditch, or in a customer lot - lining the boom/wheel-lift up with the casualty vehicle in live traffic or a cramped lot, often taking signals from a partner or police officer.

tasks.label: Check conditions of trailers after contents have been unloaded to ensure that there has been no damage.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Dry-van trailer live-unloaded at a warehouse or distribution-center dock: after the lumpers/forklifts finish, the driver climbs into the 53-ft box, walks it end to end looking for forklift punctures in walls and liner, gouged or broken floor boards, torn e-track/logistics posts, damaged ceiling bows and door seals, kicks out debris and broken pallets, closes and latches the doors, and notes any damage on the bill of lading before pulling off the dock.

Delivery to a retail store, grocery back dock, small manufacturer, or 3PL customer facility: cramped dock, sometimes unloaded by a store crew or by hand, driver checks the emptied trailer interior and rear frame/doors for damage caused during unloading (dock plate gouges, door panel dents, bent hinges), photographs anything found and reports it before departure.

Yard/terminal drop-and-hook: driver drops the emptied trailer or picks up an empty in a carrier terminal or shipper yard, does a walk-around (sides, roofline, lights, mudflaps, tires, landing gear, doors) plus an interior look-in and sweep-out, and tags or reports any damage found so the trailer is not sent out damaged.

Refrigerated trailer emptied at a grocery DC or food plant: driver inspects interior floor grating/duct, walls and air chute for pallet-jack and forklift damage, checks door seals and gaskets, confirms the box is clean and undamaged for the next food load, and records condition.

Flatbed or step-deck unloaded by crane or rough-terrain forklift at a construction site, lumberyard, steel service center, or farm: after the load is off, the driver inspects the deck boards, stake pockets, rub rails, headache rack and coil racks for gouges or cracks, checks straps, chains, binders and tarps for cuts and damage, outdoors in whatever weather and ground conditions exist.

Tank, pneumatic/hopper, or dump trailer after discharge at a plant or terminal: driver checks hoses, valves, gaskets, discharge gates, hopper interior/tank manway and hydraulics for damage or leaks caused during the unload before closing up and leaving.

tasks.label: Drive trucks to weigh stations before and after loading and along routes in compliance with state regulations.

instances.label: OTR/regional tractor-trailer trip: driver runs a loaded interstate route past state weigh stations; weigh-in-motion screening or a PrePass/Drivewyze transponder clears the truck, or the station is closed, so the driver stays on the mainline and continues the route legally.

Same interstate trip, but the station is open and the truck is directed to exit: driver decelerates down the scale ramp, queues behind other trucks, stops squarely on the static platform (or creeps across the WIM lane), reads the light board/officer signal, and merges back onto the highway.

Truck is directed off the scale into the inspection bay: driver parks, hands over CDL, medical card, ELD logs, permits and bill of lading, accompanies a Level 1/2 inspection, and cannot leave until cleared or defects are corrected.

After loading at a shipper, driver detours to a public truck-stop CAT scale to verify gross and axle weights: pulls into the busy lot, positions steer/drive/trailer axles on the three platforms, uses the intercom or scale app, then collects the weight ticket.

Bulk/vocational hauling (frac sand, aggregate, grain, waste, cement): truck crosses the facility's certified weighbridge empty before loading and loaded after, at the quarry, mine loadout, elevator, landfill or plant, stopping in the marked position and taking an electronic or attendant-issued ticket.

Local vocational street work (dump truck, tow truck, tank truck): driver takes the loaded truck on city/rural streets to a municipal or customer scale, or is waved onto a portable roadside scale set up by enforcement, in unmapped and variable local conditions.

instances.label: Live load/unload at a distribution center, LTL terminal, cross-dock or manufacturer's shipping dock: trailer backed to a dock door with leveler; palletized or floor-loaded cases moved in/out with a forklift or electric pallet jack; driver does the work or works alongside dock staff, then bars/seals the load.

Delivery to a chain retail/grocery store or restaurant-supply site that has a receiving dock or level door: driver rolls palletized freight off the trailer with an electric pallet jack and stages it in the receiving area for check-in.

No-dock street-level delivery (foodservice, beverage, appliance, building supply, small jobsites): liftgate or ramp, two-wheeler or cart, over curbs, thresholds and steps, through back doors and hallways into coolers/backrooms, in traffic and weather.

Flatbed/heavy-haul: load placed by the shipper's forklift, crane or overhead gantry at a mill, lumber yard, steel service center or jobsite; driver positions dunnage/coil racks, then chains, binds, straps, edge-protects and tarps the load to securement standards.

Bulk tanker or pneumatic trailer: spot at a loading rack/plant/retail station, ground the unit, open hatches or connect bottom-loading arms and vapor-recovery lines to multiple compartments, run the pump/PTO transfer, then break down and stow hoses.

Aggregate/dump cycle inside a quarry, mine or large controlled earthmoving site: spot precisely under the shovel/loader for loading, haul on site haul roads, and raise the body to dump at the crusher, stockpile or fill.

instances.label: Lamp/bulb failure found on pre-trip or flagged en route: driver stops on a shoulder, truck-stop lot or shipper lot, unscrews a lens or pulls a grommet-mounted marker/clearance/tail/turn lamp, swaps the bulb or sealed lamp, checks the circuit and function. tasks.label: Remove debris from loaded trailers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Dry van/reefer at a DC, plant or cross-dock: after loading, the driver clears loose debris from inside the trailer around and under the load — stray stretch film, broken pallet slats, cut banding, crushed cartons, spent dunnage bags, loose nails — before closing the doors. Indoor dock, load stays in place.

Flatbed/step-deck in a mill, steel service center or lumber yard: bulky loose debris left on the deck around the secured load — scrap blocking and dunnage, cut steel banding, broken pallet pieces, offcuts — thrown off by hand before tarping and leaving the yard. Outdoor, institution-controlled yard, weather varies.

Open-deck or open-top load with loose particulate debris only — bark, sawdust, wood chips, gravel, dust, dirt — on the deck, rails and load top; swept or blown off at the shipper's site before highway travel so nothing blows off in transit.

Dump/end-dump, grain hopper or aggregate trailer at a quarry, asphalt plant or elevator: loose spillage knocked or hosed off the tailgate, top rails, frame rails, catwalk and fifth-wheel area right after loading, before the loaded truck enters the public road.
Snow and ice cleared from the roof of a loaded van/reefer/container at a terminal yard or truck stop before departure, to comply with state snow-and-ice removal laws.

At a customer delivery/pickup site taken as found — construction site, retail back lot, farm, roadside pull-off: the driver clears whatever has accumulated on the loaded trailer (mud, broken pallet, spilled product, road debris caught on the deck, strap and film remnants) with only the tools on the truck.

tasks.label: Secure cargo for transport, using ropes, blocks, chain, binders, or covers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Dry van / reefer at a warehouse or DC dock: after pallets are loaded, the driver secures the freight inside the trailer — inserting load bars/decking beams into E-track, running ratchet straps over the rear tiers, placing dunnage bags and blocking/bracing so the load cannot shift or fall out when the doors open. Indoor dock, standard 53-ft trailer, mixed pallet heights.

Flatbed/step-deck at a shipper's yard, mill, or plant: driver throws 3/8" G70 chains and ratchet or lever binders (or 4" straps with corner protectors) over machinery, steel, pipe, coils, or building materials, sets dunnage/blocking, works out the required number of tiedowns/WLL, climbing on and around an irregular load outdoors in whatever weather.

Tarping a flatbed load: driver drags 60–120 lb lumber/steel tarps onto the top of the load, unfolds and spreads them over irregular freight (lumber, drywall, crated machinery), tucks corners and secures with bungees, rubber straps, and rope, often on a windy outdoor lot beside the loading area.

En-route re-securement: within the first 50 miles and at every stop, the driver re-tightens binders and ratchets, re-hooks chains that have gone slack, re-fastens flapping tarp corners and bungees, and adds tiedowns if the load has settled — done on a highway shoulder, truck stop lot, or weigh-station apron in traffic, wind, dark, or rain.

Open-top bulk hauling (end dump, hopper bottom, chip, refuse transfer): driver covers the loaded body with a tarp before leaving the quarry, grain elevator, asphalt plant, or transfer station, as required by state spill/cover law, and re-checks the cover before entering the highway.

Tow/recovery: operator secures a casualty vehicle to a rollback carrier or under a wheel lift — running chains/straps through wheels or frame points, ratcheting tie-downs, adding safety chains and axle straps — at a crash scene, highway shoulder, or private lot with damaged, non-standard vehicles.

tasks.label: Follow appropriate safety procedures for transporting dangerous goods.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Over-the-road placarded hazmat run (e.g., a tank trailer of flammable liquid or a van of packaged corrosives) on public highways: verify shipping papers and emergency response info are in reach, confirm placards match the load, obey designated hazmat routes and tunnel/bridge restrictions, stop for the required en-route cargo-tank/tire checks, and park only where the load may be attended or safely left.

Bulk fuel or liquid chemical delivery to a customer site (retail fuel station, farm, contractor yard): set brakes and chock wheels, verify the receiving tank and product, bond/ground the tanker, connect and secure hoses, keep the extinguisher and spill kit ready, attend the vehicle throughout the transfer, and prevent overfill or spillage.

Bulk chemical or fuel pickup/delivery inside an institution-controlled industrial site (refinery, chemical plant, loading rack, tank farm): follow site hazmat rules and PPE, position at the rack, ground the unit, complete controlled loading with overfill protection, and check for leaks before departure.

Local/LTL multi-stop hazmat route in city traffic and at customer docks: check packages for damage or leakage at each stop, keep incompatible classes segregated and blocked/braced, add or remove placards as the load composition changes, and keep paperwork current for each shipment.

Incident and emergency handling en route: discovering a leaking valve, fitting or package, or being involved in a crash — stop in a safe place, shut down ignition sources, keep the public away, consult the Emergency Response Guidebook, notify the carrier and responders, and hand shipping papers to emergency personnel.

sources.system: Highly automated transportation systems (regulatory status, HM-266 ANPRM)
sources.title: Federal Register :: Hazardous Materials: Modernizing Regulations To Facilitate Transportation of Hazardous Materials Using Highly Automated Transportation Systems
sources.claim: US DOT's hazmat rules were written for human-driven vehicles; PHMSA opened an ANPRM in Dec 2025 asking how shipping papers, attendance, loading/unloading and incident response should work when no person is aboard — indicating no established driverless hazmat highway operation.
sources.transferJustification: Context for the road-transport instances: it establishes that the hazmat-specific procedural duties (papers, attendance, leak detection, incident response) are unresolved for driverless vehicles, so no cited system performs them on public roads.

It shows unmanned trucks can drive public routes, but the freight is general cargo and none of the hazmat-specific safety procedures (placard verification, en-route cargo tank inspection, attendance, ERG response) are performed, so it cannot substantiate this task at E3.

sources.system: Automated storage/retrieval systems and AGVs in hazmat warehouses (no specific system named)

tasks.label: Inventory and inspect goods to be moved to determine quantities and conditions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: LTL or dry-van driver at a distribution-center/warehouse dock: physically counts pallets, cartons or handling units being loaded or unloaded against the bill of lading, walks the trailer, looks for crushed cartons, torn wrap, leaking or wet freight and leaning pallets, and records exceptions before signing. Labeled, barcoded palletized freight; indoor dock and trailer interior.

Truckload driver picking up at a shipper's plant or DC: verifies piece/pallet count as the trailer is loaded (or counts before the seal goes on), checks that goods are undamaged, properly stacked and stable, notes shipper-load-and-count discrepancies, verifies seal number. Indoor dock plus trailer interior at a company-controlled facility.

Flatbed/heavy-haul driver at a steel service center, lumber yard, pipe yard or plant yard: counts coils, bundles, crates, pipe or machinery pieces, checks dimensions and weight distribution, documents pre-existing dents, rust, broken banding or gouges before securing. Outdoor, weather-exposed but institution-controlled industrial yard.

Bulk/tanker or agricultural hauler at a terminal, elevator or plant: confirms product identity and quantity (gauge, meter ticket, scale), checks product condition — moisture, temperature, contamination, foreign material — and inspects seals and hatches before hauling.

Driver delivering to a customer's premises — retail back door, restaurant, construction jobsite, or residence: counts pieces off the truck with the receiver, inspects cartons/bundles/furniture for damage, notes shortages or damage on the delivery receipt and gets a signature. Layout differs at every stop; conditions taken as found.

Tow truck driver at a roadside breakdown, crash scene, impound or repossession: inspects the vehicle to be moved, documents existing damage and condition (photos, condition report), checks whether wheels roll/steer and what gear is needed before hookup. Uncontrolled roadside or lot.

tasks.label: Follow special cargo-related procedures, such as checking refrigeration systems for frozen foods or providing food or water for livestock.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Refrigerated van load of frozen/fresh food: at the shipper dock or carrier terminal the driver confirms the trailer is clean and pre-cooled, sets the unit to the bill-of-lading temperature and continuous/cycle mode, runs and reads the unit's pretrip test, checks reefer fuel level, air chute and door seals before/after loading.

Reefer run in progress: at each fuel/rest stop the driver checks the unit display (return-air temp vs setpoint), confirms the unit is running and fueled, logs readings, clears or responds to alarms, and at the receiver produces the temperature record/download (occasionally pulp temperatures of product).

Flatbed/heavy-haul special cargo: tarping lumber, steel coils or machinery, applying chains/straps/edge protection per commodity rules, and re-checking securement within the first 50 miles and every 150 miles thereafter at roadside pull-offs, in wind, heat or rain, across varied shipper yards.

Tanker/hazmat load: placarding, verifying manhole covers, valves and emergency shutoffs, bonding/grounding, connecting hoses or loading arms, monitoring pressure/product temperature (LPG, hot asphalt, chemicals, fuel) during loading and delivery at bulk terminals and customer sites, carrying shipping papers and emergency response info.

Livestock haul (cattle/hogs): bedding the trailer, opening/closing side-slat ventilation for weather, checking animals through the slats at stops for downed or distressed animals, and providing water/feed on hauls approaching the 28-hour limit, at farms, feedlots, stockyards and rest areas.

Dry bulk pneumatic or other specialized freight: connecting blower and discharge hoses for cement, flour or plastic pellets and monitoring line pressure through the blow-off; auto-hauler chaining and deck adjustment; hazardous-waste containment and manifest checks at plants and customer sites.

tasks.label: Install or remove special equipment, such as tire chains, grader blades, plow blades, or sanders.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Chaining up: at a designated chain-up pullout or highway shoulder during a winter storm, the driver drags 40-80 lb steel triple/single chains out of the side box, drapes them over the drive tires, crawls under the tractor in slush to hook the inner fastener, drives forward, then tightens cams and rubber tensioners on 4-8 tires in wind, darkness, snow and passing traffic.

Chaining off / field repair: at a chain-removal area past the control point, the driver unhooks tensioners and cams, pulls chains off drive (and sometimes trailer) tires, shakes off snow and coils them back into the chain box; occasionally splices a broken cross-link or re-tensions a slapping chain on the shoulder.

Plow hookup/removal: in a municipal or state DOT maintenance garage or fenced yard, the driver aligns the truck to a front plow (or wing) resting on its stand, engages the quick-hitch, drops the pins/latches, connects hydraulic quick-couplers and the electrical harness, checks blade lift and angle, and reverses the process at end of season.

Sander/hopper spreader install or removal: in the agency shop, the driver, with a hoist, gantry or forklift, sets a hopper or tailgate spreader into the dump body or on the tailgate, chains or bolts it down, connects hydraulic hoses, spinner motor and control cable, and tests the auger before the shift.

Blade/edge changeout: in the shop, the driver rolls the plow moldboard or underbody/grader scraper blade over, breaks loose 12-20 salt-corroded carriage bolts (impact gun, sometimes torch or chisel), removes the worn cutting edge, positions a new 100-200 lb steel edge, aligns the holes and torques new hardware.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: hooking equipment to a heavy truck. Connecting pressurized service lines and an electrical harness to truck-mounted equipment is the connector step of mounting a plow or spreader; the fittings, insertion forces and outdoor truck-side geometry are comparable.
