tasks.label: Pick up passengers at prearranged locations, at taxi stands, or by cruising streets in high-traffic areas.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: App- or radio-dispatched prearranged pickup at a street address on a public road: a house, apartment building, office, restaurant or bar in a city or suburb. Driver navigates mixed traffic, finds the address and a legal curb space (often double-parking briefly), waits for the rider, and the passenger self-boards with a small bag. Day and night, rain, other traffic and pedestrians present.

Airport pickup: enter the airport roadway system, hold in the designated taxi/rideshare staging lot until called forward, pull to the assigned terminal arrivals curb or rideshare zone, identify the fare, and load passengers and luggage under airport-police curb-clearing pressure.

Waiting at a taxi stand on controlled private/institutional property - hotel or casino porte-cochere, convention center, arena, train station forecourt - where walk-up passengers with bags board at a marked stand, often coordinated by a doorman or starter.

Cruising dense downtown streets in high-traffic areas looking for street hails: spotting an arm raised at the curb, a doorman's wave, or a crowd at bar-close/event let-out, pulling across lanes to the hailer, negotiating the destination through the window, and picking up before another cab does.

Prearranged pickup where the passenger needs physical assistance: an elderly or mobility-impaired rider on a medical/paratransit trip escorted from the door to the car, a folding wheelchair or walker to be stowed in the trunk, or several heavy suitcases the driver loads.

Prearranged pickup under degraded or unmapped conditions: heavy snow/ice or storm, an exurban or rural address off the mapped grid, or a pickup point cut off by construction, road closure or police-directed traffic at a large event.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Airport terminal taxi rank/curb: ambulatory passenger with 2-3 checked suitcases; driver lifts bags from the sidewalk or cart into the trunk, closes it, and at the drop-off (hotel or home) lifts them out and sets them on the ground or carries them to the door.

Hotel porte-cochere or downtown venue curb: passenger with one or two rolling bags, garment bag or boxes; driver opens the rear door, stows bags in the trunk or on the back seat, and retrieves them at the destination curb, often in traffic and weather.

Ordinary street hail or residential/driveway pickup: passenger with a backpack, shopping bags, a stroller or a bag of groceries; driver takes the items, places them in the trunk or footwell, opens/closes the door, and hands the items back at the destination.

Able-bodied passenger with no luggage at a street or venue curb: driver's assistance amounts to opening the passenger door on the curb side, making sure the passenger is seated clear of the door, and closing it, then opening it again at drop-off.

Elderly or mobility-limited passenger at a private home, senior residence or clinic entrance: driver offers an arm or hand, steadies the passenger while they lower into the seat and swing their legs in, buckles or hands over the belt, and folds and stows a walker, cane or folded wheelchair.

Wheelchair-accessible taxi: driver deploys the ramp or lift, guides/pushes the chair aboard, anchors it with four-point tie-downs and an occupant belt, then reverses the process at the destination curb.

tasks.label: Report to taxicab services or garages to receive vehicle assignments.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Start-of-shift check-in at an urban taxi fleet garage: at shift change the driver presents at the dispatcher/cashier window, shows the hack license, signs the lease/trip sheet, is assigned a specific numbered cab, takes the keys, finds the car in the company yard, does a quick walk-around, and puts it into service. Indoor office plus a company-controlled paved yard, crowded with other drivers and cars at shift change.

Taking custody of an assigned vehicle that is not at the base: the cab sits at a satellite lot, at a relief-driver handoff point, or parked curbside near the garage, so the driver travels through city traffic to collect it and/or bring it back to the base. Public streets, mixed traffic, weather and parking conditions as found.

Airport or hotel-fleet staging: the driver reports to the airport taxi holding-lot dispatch booth (or a hotel/casino stand) to be logged in, get queue position and vehicle/medallion confirmation, then joins the line for the terminal curb. Institution-controlled staging lot with marked lanes and a starter/dispatcher.

Mid-shift vehicle swap: the assigned cab develops a fault (warning light, tire, meter/camera failure, minor collision damage), so the driver drives it back through traffic to the garage, reports it to the dispatcher/mechanic, and is issued a replacement vehicle to finish the shift.

Small suburban or regional taxi/livery company: the driver reports to a small office or fenced lot, takes keys from the board or a lockbox, picks up fuel card, radio and paperwork, checks fuel and fluids, and pulls out. Low traffic, few vehicles, familiar fixed layout.

Owner-operator or long-term lease driver who keeps the cab overnight: periodically reports to the base/garage for vehicle rotation, meter and camera checks, decal/equipment work, or the annual safety inspection, and is reassigned the same or a different vehicle.

tasks.label: Test vehicle equipment, such as lights, brakes, horns, or windshield wipers, to ensure proper operation.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Start-of-shift check at a taxi company garage/yard: fleet driver takes over a leased cab, switches on headlights, tail, brake and turn signals and walks around to confirm each illuminates, sounds the horn, runs wipers and washers, presses the brake pedal for feel/travel and sets the parking brake, then reports any defect to dispatch or the shop.

Owner-operator or independent livery driver checks the vehicle before the shift in a home driveway or on-street parking: same lights/horn/wipers/brake-pedal checks, alone, in whatever weather and lighting exist, often using reflections in windows or a wall to see rear lamps.

Rolling functional check in the first minutes of the shift on public streets: light brake application at low speed to feel for pull, grab or long pedal travel, checking dash warning lamps, running wipers/washer and defroster in rain, and deciding whether to keep the car in service or return it.

Ad hoc mid-shift check in an airport taxi holding lot or company staging area after a warning light, a passenger comment or a suspected burned-out lamp: cycling the suspect lights, testing horn and wipers, and calling the check in.

Verification check at the fleet garage before presenting the cab for a regulatory taxi inspection or after shop work: driver systematically confirms all exterior lamps, horn, wipers/washers and service and parking brakes operate before the vehicle is signed out or driven to the inspection station.

tasks.label: Turn the taximeter on when passengers enter the cab, and turn it off when they reach the final destination.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Street-hail metered trip in a city medallion/licensed cab: passenger flags the cab at the curb and gets in, the driver engages the meter (button or lever) to start flag-fall and distance/time accrual, then switches it off on arrival so the fare and any surcharges display for payment.

Dispatched or phone/app-ordered metered trip: driver arrives at a pickup address, may start the meter per local waiting-time rules once the passenger boards, and stops it at the drop-off address, closing out the trip record on the meter/TPEP unit.

Flat-rate, voucher, or airport/out-of-town trip: the driver still engages the meter (or selects a flat-rate/contract mode on it) at pickup so the trip is recorded and receipts print, and shuts it off at the destination.
Multi-stop or wait-and-return trip: the meter is left running on the waiting rate at intermediate stops while the passenger runs an errand, and is only switched off at the final destination.

App-based/e-hail trip where the 'meter' is a driver smartphone app or in-car tablet: the driver taps 'start trip' when the passenger boards and 'end trip' at the destination, with fare computed by the software.

tasks.label: Vacuum and clean interiors and wash and polish exteriors of automobiles.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: End-of-shift interior clean at the taxi company's garage/yard or at a car wash's free-vacuum area: pull out and shake floor mats, vacuum carpets, seats and seat-track crevices, wipe dash, console, door panels and grab handles, clean inside glass, empty seat-back pockets. Cab is parked in a normal stall or vacuum stall.

Exterior wash by taking the cab through a commercial automatic wash — conveyor tunnel or in-bay automatic — paying at a kiosk, driving in and letting the machine soap, scrub/spray, rinse and blow-dry the vehicle.

Hand wash of the exterior with hose, bucket and brush/mitt at a self-serve wash bay or in the driver's own driveway or a curbside parking spot: pre-rinse, soap wheels and body, scrub bugs and road film, rinse and towel-dry, clean exterior glass and mirrors.

Quick mid-shift tidy at a taxi stand, airport hold lot or curbside between fares: pull out trash and food wrappers left by the last rider, brush or handheld-vacuum crumbs and sand off the rear seat and floor, wipe a small spill and smudged rear windows, straighten mats. Done in a few minutes, outdoors, in whatever weather.
Periodic exterior wax/polish of the cab at the fleet garage or a wash/detail bay: apply wax or sealant, machine-buff or hand-buff panels to a shine, touch up dull or scuffed paint areas, dress trim.

Deep remediation clean after a sick passenger or major spill: soak up vomit/liquid, shampoo and hot-water-extract upholstery and carpet, scrub seat belts and trim seams, disinfect and deodorize the cabin, remove and clean mats, before the cab can go back in service.

sources.claim: FANUC six-axis robots running 3M's Finesse-it system sand and polish painted car bodies on a moving assembly line at GM's Spring Hill plant, guided by an automated vision inspection system.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic machine sanding and polishing of automotive painted exterior panels — same surfaces, same rotary abrasive/polish tooling and finer precision than a taxi wax-and-buff, performed in a purpose-built line cell.
